And if the head of that cock is fried /fol. 31v./ in good oil and you set that oil aside, that oil gives great benefit, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if a woman applies it upon a wad of cotton, and she suffers from haemorrhage, it benefits her, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate) 299 times and carry that writing and enter into the fray of battle, no weapon shall work upon you, no harm shall befall you, and everyone who meets you shall flee from before you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if al-Raḥīm is written upon a sheet 21 times and hung upon one afflicted with headache, it departs from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write His name al-Raḥīm upon the palm of one seized by a fit (maṣrūʿ) and speak it into his ear 7 times, he comes to himself on the instant, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write the blessed Name al-Raḥīm upon 7 almond kernels with a needle of brass on Friday in the hour of Venus — which is the first hour, at the rising of the sun — and if you write the noble Name according to its number upon those almonds and feed them to the one you desire, he will love you with a love so intense that there is no increasing upon it. And if you write the name al-Raḥīm in this form [figure not reproduced in the edition]. And if it is written upon a piece of leopard-skin or cheetah-skin and one faint of heart carries it, his heart is emboldened and his resolve strengthened, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you write His name al-Raḥīm thus [figure not reproduced in the edition]. And if it is written upon a new mirror on Monday at the rising of the sun and one afflicted with facial palsy (al-laqwa) gazes into it much, God, exalted is He, cures him of it. And if he writes it thus — al-Raḥīm — in this form: — upon a ring

— of silver, its weight two dirhams: God, exalted is He, bestows upon its bearer love, awe, and obedience, by the leave of God, blessed and exalted. And this is the form of the signet, and it is as you see.
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source — each row and each column contains, once each,(bism),(Allāh),(al-Raḥmān),(al-Raḥīm), and (fulān, "So-and-so"). Cells given in source order:]

And for the cutting off of tyrants and the arrogant: write the table of the basmala on a piece of lead, and place the name of the person sought, as mentioned, in the table of the signet; suffumigate it with asafoetida (ḥiltīt) and red garlic; then bury the signet in a place close beside a fire that burns perpetually. And beware of letting the fire reach the lead, for then the one against whom that is done perishes and dies, and you are the one answerable for him on the Day of Resurrection. This is its form. And these are the names which you say over the aforementioned signet: O God, I ask You by the right of Your mighty Name, which is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", before which faces are humbled, to which necks bow down, before which voices are hushed, and in dread of which hearts quake — I ask You to bless /fol. 32r./ and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to his family and his companions, and to grant peace; and that You fulfil my need concerning So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. O God, if You know that he will turn back from that which he is in, then guide him and grant him success; and if You know that he will not turn back from that which he is in, then send down upon him Your affliction, Your wrath, and Your displeasure, and destroy him — O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), O God, O God — seven times. And you make this invocation seven hundred times; for the one against whom it is done, God destroys him or guides him. So fear God, exalted is He. And God is the granter of success in what is right.

And if you write the noble basmala, as I shall draw it for you, in the middle of a circle, and write within the circle and around it Muḥammad is the Messenger of God; and those who are with him are severe against the unbelievers (Q 48:29) to the end of the sura, and suffumigate it with everything of sweet fragrance at an auspicious time, and carry it — then you become awe-inspiring, magnified, and honoured in the sight of everyone; and none sees you but he loves you and seeks your company and your companionship, so much so that women incline toward you and toward intimacy with you. So fear God, exalted is He, in secret and in the open. And God is the granter of success. And this is the form of the circle, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

And if you write the basmala in its entirety — the moon being in Pisces and the ascendant auspicious — upon gazelle parchment, and he carries it with him after he has recited it over the parchment to the count of its number: then if he lives, he lives happy, and if he dies, he dies a martyr, and he will never see anything hateful befall him, through the blessing of the noble basmala.

Know, O you — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that bism is the concealed Name; that Allāh, exalted is He, is the Greatest Name; and that by al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm He describes Himself, for He is the All-Merciful of this world and the Compassionate of the hereafter. And al-ḥamdu li-llāhi rabbi l-ʿālamīn ("Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds") stands opposite "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate": so bism Allāh stands opposite al-ḥamdu li-llāh; rabb stands opposite al-Raḥmān; al-ʿālamīn stands opposite al-Raḥīm. And know that all of that is taken into account in His saying Master of the Day of Judgement (Q 1:4) — by "Judgement" He intends the manifestation of Lordship. So He is Malik (King) and Mālik (Master) and Malīk (Sovereign): by the illumination of the intellects and of the subtle lights on the Day of Judgement with the attribute of kingship, so that He is Malik; and He manifests Himself to the souls with subjugating power and dominion, so that He is Mālik yawm al-dīn (Master of the Day of Judgement); and He manifests Himself to those possessed of mercy in the worldly abode by way of possession, so that He is Mālik al-mulūk (Master of kings); and He manifests Himself to those brought near by way of al-Malīk, according to His saying, exalted is He: in a seat of truthfulness, with a Sovereign Omnipotent (Q 54:55).

So understand the secret of these divine subtleties. And all of this is within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". The bāʾ that is in the Name serves to convey the good from all the worlds to the True King, and it raises up the call by the tongue through the instrument of utterance. So bism Allāh is an ascent that has no limit, and al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm is a descent to the final issue, just as bism Allāh is a rising up to the First Beginning. In it, then, is the secret of the beginning and of the end; and in it are the degrees of the affirmation of divine unity, because bism stands opposite shahida ("[God] bears witness"), and Allāh opposite Allāh, and "the angels" opposite al-Raḥmān, and "those possessed of knowledge" opposite al-Raḥīm. And likewise by relation to the quadratic world, which is His saying, exalted is He: Those are with those whom God has favoured — of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous (Q 4:69). "The prophets" is a relation from bism to Allāh; "and the truthful" is a relation from Allāh to bism, which are the degrees of the prophets; "the martyrs", from All-Mercifulness (raḥmāniyya) to Compassionateness (raḥīmiyya); and "the righteous", from Compassionateness to All-Mercifulness. That, then, is the succession of the steps in the ascent to the secret of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". For the beginning of the circle of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is like its end, and its inward like its outward. By it God set up the tree of the created beings, and by it He made manifest the secret of engendering, and how the worlds became separated out from "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate".

And in the noble hadith: ((Whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" in his scroll eight hundred and twelve times — and that is the number of the letters of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" after the dropping of their repetitions, their number being four hundred and six, and its double, eight hundred and twelve times — and is a believer, certain of His Lordship, God frees him from the Fire and admits him into the Garden, the abode of permanence.)) Then God, blessed and exalted, said to Jesus son of Mary — peace be upon him: ((O Jesus, let "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" be at the opening of your recitation and of your prayers; for whoever sets it at the opening of his recitation and his prayer, neither Munkar nor Nakīr shall terrify him. And if he dies upon that, God makes light for him the agonies of death and the narrowness of the grave, and the mercy of God is /fol. 33r./ upon him; and He makes his grave spacious for him, and illumines it for him as far as his sight can reach, and brings him forth from his grave on the Day of Resurrection with body made white, his face gleaming with light; and He reckons with him an easy reckoning, and makes his balance heavy, and grants him the perfect light upon the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) until he enters the Garden; and He commands the herald to call out over him in the open courts of the Resurrection with happiness and forgiveness. Jesus — peace be upon him — said: O Lord, is this for me alone? He said: It is for you and for whoever follows you in particular, and takes as you take and speaks as you speak; and that shall belong to Aḥmad and to his community after you.))

So Jesus — peace be upon him — informed his companions of that. And when Jesus — peace be upon him — was raised up to heaven, the disciples passed away and others came after them, and they went astray and led astray, and altered and substituted, and exchanged religion for this world. So the verse of faith was taken away from the breasts of the Christians and the monks, and it remained in the breasts of the people of the Gospel, until God, exalted is He, sent our Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and sent it down upon him in Sūrat al-Naml, and it was an opening. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — gave command, and it was written at the heads of the suras and of the registers and at the heads of letters. And the Lord of Might swore by His might that no believing servant should pronounce it over anything without His blessing it for him.

And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever recites "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" and is a believer, the mountains and the celestial spheres glorify God together with him, save that he does not hear their glorification.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace —

said: ((When the believing servant says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", the Garden says: At Your service, and at Your good pleasure! O God, Your servant So-and-so has said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; O God, draw him far away from the Fire and admit him into Your Garden.)) And it is related from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((There are among my community a people who will come on the Day of Resurrection saying "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and their good deeds will weigh heavier than their evil deeds.)) And the nations will say: Glory be to God! How the good deeds of the community of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — outweigh! And their prophets will say to them: It is only the Name of God, exalted is He, that has come to them. And that is because the beginning of their speech was three of the mighty names of God, exalted is He — were they set in one pan of a balance, and the heavens and the earths and all that is in them and all that is between them set in the second pan, they would outweigh them — and they are "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". Then he said: ((And He has made it a security against every affliction, a remedy for every malady, and a protective charm against every accursed satan. And this community has been made safe from being swallowed up by the earth, from being pelted, from metamorphosis, and from drowning, through its blessing. So hold fast to reciting it, and draw near by means of it to the Possessor of Majesty and Honour.))

And al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said concerning His saying, exalted is He, And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qurʾān, they turn away upon their backs, recoiling (Q 17:46): he said, that means [their recoiling] from "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And it has been said concerning His saying, exalted is He, And He bound them to the word of pious reverence (kalimat al-taqwā), and they had the better right to it and were its rightful people (Q 48:26), that it was "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And whoever writes it /fol. 33v./ and writes it finely, in reverence for it, is recorded with God among those brought near.

And it is related from ʿIkrima that he said: ((God, exalted is He, was, and nothing was with Him. Then He created the creation of the light; then from the light He created the Tablet and the Pen. Then God, exalted is He, commanded the Pen to run over the Tablet with all that would come to be until the Day of Resurrection. And the first thing the Pen wrote upon the Preserved Tablet was "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So He made it a security for His creation so long as they hold to reciting it; and it is the recitation of the people of the seven heavens and of the people of the pavilions of glory among the angels — the cherubim, those ranged in ranks, and those who glorify. And the first thing that was sent down upon Adam — peace be upon him — was this verse, which is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And he said: I have come to know that my believing progeny will not be chastised with the Fire so long as they hold to it. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of the Friend [of God], Abraham — peace be upon him — and it was sent down upon him while he was in the mangonel, and God, exalted is He, delivered him by it from the fire. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of Solomon son of David — peace be upon them both — and it was sent down upon him; and the angels said: Now has God completed your kingdom, O Solomon son of David! And God, exalted is He, commanded him to proclaim among all the tribes (asbāṭ), the ascetics, and the devotees: Lo, whoever wishes to hear the verse of security, let him gather to Solomon son of David — peace be upon him — in the prayer-niche of his father. So they gathered to him, and Solomon — peace be upon him — arose and ascended the pulpit and recited to them the verse of security — and in some copies, the verse of faith — and it is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And when they had learned it they came forward rejoicing and said: We bear witness that you are truly the Messenger of God, O son of David. Then it was taken up after him, until the time of Moses — peace be upon him — and it was sent down upon him; and by it he subdued Pharaoh and his hosts, and Qārūn and his hosts and his partisans, and Hāmān and his partisans. Then it was taken up after Moses, until the time of Jesus — peace be upon him. And God revealed to him, saying: O son of Mary, do you not know what verse has been sent down upon you? He said: Yes indeed, O Lord. He said to him: O Jesus, there has been sent down upon you the verse of security — and it is said, the verse of faith — and it is "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". So hold fast to reciting it in your night and your day, in your going forth at morning and your coming, in your sitting and your standing, in your eating and your drinking, and in all your states. For whoever comes on the Day of Resurrection with eight hundred and twelve times of it in his scroll — and the hadith has already been given.

And it is related of one of the righteous that he came to one of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) to visit him and to seek his supplication and his blessing. He found the people gathered at his door, awaiting his coming out; and a rainbow (qaws quzaḥ) was set upright over his door. While things were thus, behold, the master had opened the door and come out. Then he set his foot upon the rainbow and said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and passed over it and walked on until he came down on the other side, while the people looked at him and marvelled at him. Then the man who had come to visit him — he was called al-Shaykh al-Malījī — when he saw what the master did, said: Alas! /fol. 34r./ And he was stirred, and said: Thus do [true] men outstrip [others]; and thus shall we be, if God, exalted is He, wills. Then the shaykh [al-Malījī] set himself to earnestness and striving until he joined the solitary ones (al-afrād). And the man who passed over the aforementioned rainbow was Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rajrājī — may God be pleased with him.
So look, my brother, at what is in "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; and listen, and lend both your ears to the saying of

God, exalted is He: It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves above me, but come to me in submission (Q 27:30–31) — how Bilqīs became obedient to Solomon, and faith entered her heart, and this came about through the blessing of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And in it, of secrets and acts, of the attracting of hearts and bodies, and of that whereby hearts are gladdened and souls are made to rejoice, there is a wondrous matter. And know, my brother, that "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is nineteen letters, as has already been stated. In it are ten that are unrepeated, and they are:(bāʾ),(sīn),(mīm),(alif),(lām),(hāʾ), (rāʾ), (nūn),(yāʾ). In it the mīm is repeated three times, the lām (ḥāʾ), four times, the rāʾ twice, and the ḥāʾ 2 times; the bāʾ is not repeated, nor the nūn, nor the yāʾ likewise, nor the hāʾ, nor the sīn likewise. And the repeated among them are five letters, and they are these:. Of these the mīm is repeated in it 3 times, and the alif likewise, and the lām four times, and the rāʾ twice, and the ḥāʾ 2 times. So it results from this that the root of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is ten unrepeated letters. Among them is the bāʾ, which serves to convey the good; and it is a cold letter, and therefore I always begin with it in the verse of security. And the letter bāʾ is among the letters that remain on the Day of Resurrection, and it is a hidden secret. That is because the odd (al-witr) is the secret of the indications in respect of the Essence, save that it is an indication of the Reality, and it is from you to Him.

And know that it stands at the head of the scrolls of Abraham — peace be upon him — these names, which are "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; and likewise in the scroll of Noah — peace be upon him; and likewise in the scroll of Solomon son of David — peace be upon him. Then likewise at the beginning of the revelation to the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in His saying, exalted is He: Recite in the name of your Lord, who created man from a clot (Q 96:1–2). So He began with the secret of the bāʾ, which conceals the secrets of the divine realities. It is from you to Him, and they are the concealed contents of the Essence, by the secret of self-disclosure (tajallī), according to His saying: "Through Me you have known Me". And when He created the bāʾ, He created together with it eighty-one angels, who glorify God, exalted is He, and hallow Him.

And among the occult properties of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" is that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever says, when he rises in the morning, three times: "In the name of God the Mighty, with whose Name nothing in the earth or in heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing" — no sudden calamity and no affliction shall befall him until evening; and whoever says it when evening comes, three times, no sudden calamity and no affliction shall befall him until morning. And in one transmission: no paralysis shall befall him; and in another transmission: nothing shall befall him.)) And so Khālid ibn al-Walīd — may God be pleased with him — came to the poison and drank it down. That was when the great one of the Byzantines — that is, the king of the Christians — sent to him and said to him: If you are truthful in what you say, that poison does no harm together with these words, then drink it. He said: So our master Khālid — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — took the poison in the presence of the envoy whom he had sent, and in the presence of a company of the Companions and others, and placed it in his palm and said: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; "In the name of God, with whose Name nothing in the earth or in heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Then he drank it down, and it did him no harm at all, save that he broke out in a sweat, by the leave of God, exalted is He. So look at this gracious Name, and how it wards off poison. And by this noble Name /fol. 34v./ the ark of Noah — peace be upon him — ran its course, and he was delivered, through His saying, exalted is He: In the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring (Q 11:41). And by it God, exalted is He, delivered the Friend [of God], Abraham — peace be upon him — from the fire of Nimrod, and God, exalted is He, made it coolness and peace for him. And by it is deliverance when you enter your house and when you go out, according to his saying — upon him be blessing and peace: ((And say, when you enter your house and when you go out: "In the name of God we have entered, in the name of God we have gone out, and upon God we rely." And you say it also at the shutting of the doors; for Satan does not open a lock over which the Name of God, exalted is He, is invoked, nor does he come near it.)) And among its occult properties is that, when you go to your bed, you say: "In the name of God, and upon the religion of the

Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace." And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((There is no ablution for him who does not pronounce the Name.)) And from Abū Dāwūd: ((And whoever eats with a leper and says "In the name of God, in trust in God and in reliance upon Him", nothing shall harm him.)) And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may God be pleased with him — did this with Muʿayqīb al-Dawsī, who was a leper, when the food was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may God be pleased with him — and he was present. ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — said to him: Eat with us. "In the name of God, in trust in God and in reliance upon Him." So he drew near and ate with him.

And by this noble Name healing is sought from the evil eye: you strike with your hand upon the breast of the one struck by the eye and say: "In the name of God; O God, take away its heat and its sickness." And you say it when a man sets his foot in the stirrup intending to travel: he says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", and no hateful thing shall ever reach him. And when the believing servant says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", Satan shrinks until he becomes like a fly. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — used to say it to whoever went forth as a traveller and to whom he wished to bid farewell; and he would say, when he mounted: ((In the name of God, and by God, and upon the religion of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace.)) And with it the Messenger of God used to make his opening upon his journey, saying: ((In the name of God; I take refuge with God from the hardship of travel, from a sight that brings gloom, and from an evil return in respect of family, property, and child.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said to Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, when his hand was struck and his fingers were cut off: ((Truly, had you said "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", the angels would have raised you up while the people looked on.))

So consider this Name, which the angels raise up — that is, the one who utters it; and at whose mention the satans shrink; and at whose mention poison is cut off. The lord of mankind has made known to you its worth, and the Lord of the Throne has granted you its secret and its excellence — so wherever you seek it, you find it — and its glory. So make no movement and keep no stillness save with its mention; for by it you are given provision, and made happy, and kept safe, and delivered. And all of that is folded within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And with "In the name of God" Jesus — peace be upon him — used to perform healing recitation (ruqya) and have it performed against pains and against every kind of harm.

And some of the masters said: whoever writes the form of the bāʾ on a Friday, having fasted on the Thursday and given alms, and hangs it upon his right upper arm — God, exalted is He, expands his breast, removes sloth from him, makes blessing manifest upon him, shows him the secret of the bāʾ that subsists by it, and he sees the lights of the angels when their forms appear, the celestial and the terrestrial. It appears as an upright form, perfect in shape, sweet of scent; the noble ones among the great ones see that, save that it speaks with the bāʾ, and it is fixed in light, its light does not change. And when the name of the bāʾ is invoked, its light appears upon its essence. And it is one of /fol. 35r./ the treasured Names. And this letter, when it is in one of the names of God, exalted is He, and someone invokes it, he is treated with kindness. And it is fitting that the name containing the bāʾ be written for every dry pain and for every difficult matter, for God makes that matter easy. And it is among the names of God, exalted is He: in His name, exalted is He, al-Barr (the Benign), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Bāqī (the Abiding), and al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead); and in them is the secret of subsistence (baqāʾ). For that reason God, exalted is He, bestowed it as a favour within "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". That is because the upright alif is the head of the bāʾ, and it is the outspread one that has spread out within the essence of the bāʾ — thus:.And the bāʾ has appeared also in His name al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), and in His name al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), and in His name al-Bāṭin (the Hidden). In every name there is a meaning proper to it: thus al-Barr is for the people of piety (birr), aiding in the works of piety and in filial devotion to parents.

And whoever mentions it two hundred and thirty-three times every day, after he has mixed it with the name of the one to whom he wishes to show kindness — and that is, that you take, for example, the name ʿAmr, thus:; then you take the first letter from the name al-Barr and set it at the head of the first line; then you take the first letter from the name ʿAmr and set it after it, thus, to the end of the two names, thus:
. Then you take it and break it (taksīr) until the two names come back and appear as they were the first time, thus:

[Table: five lines of eight letters, cells as in the source; within each line the letters are printed in reading order, the first letter in the leftmost cell. The source run carries one glyph too many — a straystanding before the third line; the taksīr sequence (positions 8, 1, 7, 2, 6, 3, 5, 4 of the preceding line) confirms line 3 as [

The figure: the first [line] has come round last. Drop the last, and there remain four mixed lines. Write them upon whatever you wish, and put them in your bosom, and speak over them with this speech, saying: O Lord of lords, Nurturer of all, by the subtlety of Your Lordship hasten to me a flowing forth of Your subtlety, that I may be drowned in a sea from among the seas of Your power and rejoice in the sweetness of that sea — a sweetness that makes sweet the spirits of those who find rest in the understanding of Your secrets. And grant me a name from among the names of Your power, such that whoever arms himself with it is guarded from the evil of what He has scattered abroad in the earth, and the evil of what comes forth from it, and of what descends from heaven and what ascends therein. Truly You are al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing). And as for His name al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), it is for the healing (ibrāʾ) of pains and sicknesses; and as for al-Bāqī (the Everlasting) and al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), they have occult properties which will come in their proper places, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Let us now return to what we were about and engaged upon. As for the letter sīn: when God, exalted is He, created it from the world of His command, He sent down with it nine thousand eight hundred and thirty angels. It is the first letter that received from the bāʾ the secret of its bringing-into-being, and it is one of the letters of the outward aspect of the Greatest Name. Now the Greatest Name has an outward and an inward: by its outward the heavens were established, and by its inward were established the things of the upper world — the Footstool and the Throne. For that reason the sīn falls at the beginning of al-samāwāt (the heavens) and in the third rank of al-kursī (the Footstool). And since the bāʾ is attached to power — and it is the concealed of the concealed things — and the hāʾ, because the hāʾ is from you to Him /fol. 35v./: so you say Huwa Huwa ("He, He"), and He says bī bī ("by Me, by Me"). And in Sūrat Yā-Sīn there are names from among the names of wisdom. Whoever lights upon them and writes them and effaces them with pure water, facing the qibla, for as many days as the number of the names — God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom. And it is the middle of the sura, and the number of its letters is sixteen letters, of which two letters are dotted above and two letters dotted below; and it is five words, the first of which is the letter sīn and the last the letter mīm. And this letter has appeared in His name al-Salām (the Peace), His name al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), and His name al-Sarīʿ (the Swift). Al-Samīʿ is the name of those who are insistent in supplication especially, for often the answer comes swiftly to him; and likewise al-Sarīʿ: whoever mentions it and asks for an answer obtains it. And whoever desires some need of God, exalted is He, that he may attain it, let him inscribe it upon his two palms and raise them up and make entreaty by the name, multiplied by the days, and let him bring its number to the full; for the answer will come to him from God, exalted is He, after the aforementioned count. And its number multiplied by the days is four thousand two hundred and seventy-seven. And whoever desires the vision of the spirits, let him make entreaty by it to God, exalted is He, that He unveil for him the eye of certainty; then he will speak with them and ask about what he wishes, and they will answer him. In it are hidden secrets and manifest operations. So search out and operate: you will arrive and attain. As for His name al-Samīʿ: whoever adjoins to it al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing) and says "Yā Samīʿ, yā Baṣīr", and writes them at a favourable time, and casts the writing upon one who has fainted — he comes to at once. And this has been beheld with their own eyes by the masters of the secrets; for when they came to it they found at its gate

Ibrāhīm b. Jārūkh, who had fallen into a swoon. So the wafq was inscribed for him and cast upon him, after the two names had been recited seven hundred and fifty-four times; and he came to, and what he was suffering departed from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if the two are inscribed upon gold and a person carries them, he hears the tongues of the jinn and sees them, and he exercises authority over the spirits in whatever he wishes. And if he persists in the litany of remembrance by means of them, he is granted unveiling of the secrets of created beings, and he informs them of what is in their inmost thoughts, and the states of all the servants become manifest to him. And this has been witnessed many times. As for His name al-Salām: it is for the seeking of safety and the seeking of security. And it is the litany of remembrance of our master the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — on the Day of Resurrection and on the day his community passes over the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ); he says: "Yā Salām, sallim" (O Peace, grant safety!). And in another transmission, that he — God bless him and grant him peace — says: "Sallim, yā Salām" (Grant safety, O Peace!).

As for the letter mīm of bism: the mīm is one of the diameters (aqṭār) of the letters; and the diameters of the letters are every letter whose beginning is like its end, namely the wāw, the mīm, and the nūn. And the mīm points to gathering, because of the encompassment it contains, and it points to stillness, because of the awe it contains. It is one of the letters of the Tablet. And when God, exalted is He, created it, He created it as a light /fol. 36r./, round, blotted out with light. And it is one of the letters of the intellect, because of its encompassing; and from it the sun in the fourth sphere draws its sustaining supply. And by its secret God, exalted is He, established the kingdom and the dominion; and the manifestation of knowledge is by the mīm, so that it is an aid in the operations, by the secret of the light of the mīm. And it is the last rank of bism. In it is the secret of the attainment of full strength, according to His saying, exalted is He: until, when he reaches his full strength and reaches forty years (Q 46:15). And the numbers that fall to the mīm are forty. And God, exalted is He, has appointed over it ninety angels from among the angels of the Tablet. And it is the secret which God, exalted is He, deposited in the name of His Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — at its beginning, and that by the secret of the dominion (malakūt); and in its middle, by the secret of the kingdom (mulk). There is gathered for him the innermost reality of the world of dominion and the world of the kingdom. So whoever gazes upon the form of the mīm forty times every day while reciting His saying, exalted is He, Say: O God, Master of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will— up to His saying, exalted is He — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27) — God, exalted is He, will make easy for him the means of this world and of the hereafter. That is to say, the eightfold figure (al-muthamman), the description of which and the discussion of which will come; and it belongs to Mercury, on Wednesday. So whoever inscribes its numerical secret — after fasting forty days, maintaining ritual purity continuously, and the remembrance of God, exalted is He

— upon pure parchment, facing the qibla, in the purity of the complete ablution, the moon being in Saʿd al-Suʿūd and the hour being that of the sun: then no blameworthy thought will occur to its bearer, and God, exalted is He, will grant him an opening through the reception of the realities of faith and the holy lights. And the one who wears it is secure from every harm, and God, exalted is He, bestows awe upon him. And whoever supplicates by it on Friday, while fasting and constant in the litany of remembrance, and supplicates by it concerning a righteous need — God, exalted is He, fulfils his need. And likewise whoever carries it while he is engaged in pursuing his means of livelihood — God multiplies his good, and God, exalted is He, makes easy the means of his provision and provides for him whence he does not reckon. And in it also there is, of the joining of hearts and their inclining and their turning toward the one who seeks them, that which is a blessing and more, for whoever contemplates them and to whom God, exalted is He, has given understanding of its secret. And its figuration and its representation will come in its proper place, when the discussion of it arrives. And the manner of supplicating by it for a need is that you gather, from the Most Beautiful Names of God, exalted is He, all its numbers, as I shall represent it for you together with its figures; and I shall expound to you how you may draw hearts to you, and their affection toward you, and their turning about in the phases of love for you, and their submission to you — such as you will not find in any book, nor light upon in any register. So take care to keep it hidden and to guard it, for it is the red sulphur, the greatest treasure, and the most renowned magnet.

And know, O my brother, that whoever has been granted an opening onto the secrets of the mīm, its encompassing, its closing round upon itself, and the worlds it contains, has witnessed the wonders of the engendered worlds. And likewise whoever wishes God, exalted is He, to make memorization easy for him: let him write this numerical secret on Thursday, in a state of purity, facing the qibla /fol. 36v./, and with it the name of the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — forty times; then let him efface it and drink it with water and bees' honey, and say: O God, by the blessing of what I have drunk, make memorization and understanding easy for me. And let him persist in that for forty days: God will grant him an opening, outwardly and inwardly. This is for whoever understands the secret of the mīm, until he beholds what is in the power of its inward, of every world, in the secret by which He established the mīm. By this aspiration the opening comes. As for its literal figure, it is among the treasured secrets. And that is: whoever writes it upon pure parchment on Monday, in the hour of the moon, and suffumigates it with storax (aṣṭarak), and conceals some matter within himself and wishes to see its outcome, and fasts that day of his purely for God, exalted is He — and let him break his fast upon a little bread, and let him perform his litany (wird), and let him sleep in the purity of the ablution, and let him sleep upon his right side, and let him recite Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1) with it beneath his head, and let him not speak with anyone after it, and let him sleep — then God, exalted is He, will apprise him of the outcome of his affair according to the measure of the portion he intended. And that is fitting only for the people of purity of hearts and bodies and the people of spiritual discipline (riyāḍa). And likewise whoever writes it in a glass cup and drinks it — God, exalted is He, makes wisdom easy for him. And whoever hangs it upon himself — God, exalted is He, makes understanding easy for him and causes him to speak with wisdom. And whoever writes it, and with it lā ilāha illā Allāh ("There is no god but God") eighty times, and hangs it upon his right upper arm, or writes it upon a garment and wears that garment — God, exalted is He, bestows upon him awe and compassion.

And if he keeps to a single unbroken course and practises spiritual discipline, there is no doubt that God, exalted is He, will apprise him of the world of the jinn, after you write what I describe to you. And likewise, if you wish to take brethren from among the believing jinn who will fulfil your need for you and strive for your good pleasure, you begin with the fast on Wednesday until

— Saturday, the fourth day of it, after you have performed the full ablution (ghusl); and you wash your clothes on each day of these days — I mean, you perform the full ablution, since the full ablution is indispensable. And you recite Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ1,000 times, and Sūrat Yā-Sīn once, and Sūrat al-Dukhān likewise, and Tanzīl al-Sajda (Sūrat al-Sajda) and Tabāraka lladhī bi-yadihi l-mulk (Sūrat al-Mulk), once. Then, when it is the afternoon of Saturday — and that is the tenth [hour] — you withdraw from people in a pure and empty place, in a clean spot, and you take seven warrants (barāwāt) of paper (kāghad). And you write upon the first His saying, exalted is He: And He it is who gives life and gives death — to His saying — the day (Q 23:80); and His saying, exalted is He: And when He has decreed a matter, He but says to it "Be", and it is (Q 2:117); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the second His saying, exalted is He: Truly your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then mounted the Throne — to His saying, exalted is He — so blessed be God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 7:54); and His saying, exalted is He: /fol. 37r./ and He has encompassed everything in knowledge (Q 65:12), and He has numbered everything in counting (Q 72:28), God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the third: and a messenger to the Children of Israel — to His saying — by the leave of God (Q 3:49); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the fourth: Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you come forth (Q 30:25); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the fifth: and at once they are hastening forth from the graves to their Lord (Q 36:51); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the sixth: And the Trumpet is blown, and at once they are standing, looking on (Q 39:68); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And you write upon the seventh: On the day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as though they were racing toward a standard set up (Q 70:43); God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137) — this after you have prayed four rakʿas: the first with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Yā-Sīn; the second with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Sūrat al-Dukhān; the third with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Tanzīl al-Sajda; and the fourth with the Mother of the Qurʾān and Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion, and He is powerful over everything (Q 67:1). And you say in the last prostration: Glory be to Him who has clothed Himself in might and spoken by it. Glory be to Him who has enwrapped Himself in majesty and shown Himself noble by it. Glory be to Him who has numbered everything in His knowledge. Glory be to Him to whom alone glorification is due. Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, has but to say to it "Be", and it is. Glory be to Him: what He wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. Glory be to the Possessor of favour, grace, and blessings. Glory be to the Possessor of knowledge and forbearance. Glory be to the Possessor of abundant bounty and grace. Glory be to the Possessor of the Throne, the Tablet, the Pen, and the Light. Then you raise your head and say: O God, I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and by the utmost reach of mercy from Your Book; I ask You by Your name, the Magnificent, the

Greatest, and by Your countenance, the Generous, the Most Generous, and by Your perfect words, that You make subservient to me a helper from among the righteous believing jinn, that he may aid me in what I desire of the needs of this world and the next. For seven persons of their nobles and their great ones will appear to you, and they will take visible form before you. And they will be [present]: before you recite the names, you will already have hung upon yourself seven warrants upon a thread, like a ṭarṭūr (a tall conical cap), and hung them upon your head; and that is to be before you begin the prayer. And you are to have wax with you. Then, when they are present before you, you take the first warrant of the seven warrants which you wrote and recited in the prayer, and you recite it over them and say: Which of you is the owner of this warrant and the owner of this note? And one of them will say: I am its owner. Then you say: What is your name? And he will say to you: My name is So-and-so son of So-and-so. So you write his name at the top of the note. Then you say to him: Hand over your seal. And you take /fol. 37v./ the thread and the wax and seal the bottom of the note as one seals a deed (ṣakk) — that is, the written document. Then you return his seal to him. And you say the like of that to each one of them, until you come to the seventh. Then you say: I conjure you by the names that are in these notes, that you present yourselves and answer my call whenever I call you, in obedience. Then you say: Depart; may God bless you, and [His blessing be] upon you. Then you lay away the deeds — that is, those warrants and those sealed documents — in a pure place, until some need appears to you: of food, or drink, or knowledge of some thing, or some buried treasure, or some hidden thing, or other than that. Then you call upon them, and they answer you swifter than lightning and wind, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And beware, my brother, of performing that while you are not strong of heart and firm of resolve. So if you are firm in your intellect, of lofty aspiration, steady of brain and strong of heart, and you are practised in the sciences, then set about this operation of yours if you have need of it. But if you are not firm of heart, and are heavy of head, then beware of their presence, for you will harm your spirit — for they are mighty destroyers. And guard yourself against beholding them, for [thereby] the veil of the heart is stripped away. And if you confine yourself to the eightfold signet (al-muthamman) mentioned above, that is a healing sufficiency, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And whoever writes the signet upon gazelle parchment and hangs it upon one who suffers bodily pains — such as fevers, chills, and the like — and [uses it] for the operations of concord (iʾtilāf) and for looking into the outcomes of affairs: God, blessed and exalted, does not fail to show him wonders in that. And that is because the secrets of the numbers possess an intellective power; for the numbers point to the letters by way of reception, and the letters point to the numbers by way of ascent; and the numbers point to the spiritual world, while the letters point to the corporeal world — and within it there is a spiritual [world]; and the letters become manifest through the subtleties of the corporeal things, while the numbers become manifest through the subtleties of the spiritual things. So whoever understands the secret of the mīm, to him is disclosed the secret of the ringing of the bell, by which comes the revelation of the sending-down (al-waḥy al-tanzīlī). And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — was asked: How does the revelation come to you, O Messenger of God? And he — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((It comes to me at times like the ringing of a bell; and at times the angel takes visible form for me in the likeness of a man, and speaks to me, and I retain what he says.)) And the bell (jaras) is the jaljal. Do you not see, when they are gathered together upon the necks of the horses, upon their manes and their [trappings?], and the horses stir in their going, how there arises for the bell a resounding that is heard at a far distance? Such, then, is the manner of the revelation in the ringing of the bell. And the Prophet — blessings and peace be upon him — said: ((And that is the hardest of it upon me; then it leaves off from me, and I have retained what he said.)) And the likening of the letter mīm to the bell came about only because of its roundness, its closure, the gravity of its affair, and its dreadfulness. Do you not hear his saying — blessings and peace be upon him — concerning the description of Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — /fol. 38r./ and the immensity of his frame, his strength, and his obedience; and how upon his shoulder rests one of the legs of the Throne, for all its immensity; and then the Preserved Tablet is between his eyes, for all its immensity and the greatness of its bulk; and then the Trumpet, which is in breadth a journey of five hundred years — and it is said that it has many branches likewise. And he has set the Trumpet in his mouth, and has put one foot forward and set a foot back; the other of his two feet would surely pierce the seven earths to their utmost bounds. So consider his saying: ((He has taken the Trumpet into his mouth)) — how the mīm stood in the last position in [the word] iltaqama; for by the Trumpet come the terror, the swooning, and the raising [of the dead]. And he stands with his gaze fixed upon the Throne, awaiting when he shall be commanded to blow the Trumpet. And the blowing issues forth only by the closing of the two lips, and the mīm issues forth by the closing of the two lips; and one who pronounces it cannot bring it forth otherwise than by the closing of the two lips. For that reason it stood in the likening to the ringing of the bell; and the ṣalṣala is the force of the sound. And know here the difference between the ringing of the bell and the dragging of the chain over the smooth rock — the [revelation] of the sending-down, the Israelite, the Mosaic: for the sensation of the ringing is a spiritual motion, whereas the dragging of the chain is a corporeal motion. And the mīm has two aspects: a celestial aspect, which is the first mīm, and a terrestrial aspect, which is the second mīm, in the relation of detailed exposition — thus:. And since the mīm has a secret in the celestial spiritual things and in the terrestrial corporeal things, the numbers too have a relation within the celestial things, and their letters have secrets within the terrestrial things. And it is a hot letter in general, and within it there is a moisture between two heats, in detail — and that is the letter yāʾ; and the two heats are the two mīms, the first and the last, thus:. And from these two heats came its closing and its agitation. And were it not for the moist yāʾ that separates the two heats, the two Akhshab mountains would close together. So know [this]. And by the letter mīm was completed the concealed Name, the exalted, the most exalted — and it is bism. And now we shall expound the three noble and mighty names, which are Allāh, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. As for His name Allāh, exalted is He, it is the Greatest Name, comprehending all the [other] names; and for that reason He began His Book with it and sealed His Book with it, and by it He made His servants worship, and to it He pointed, and by it He made Himself known. And that is by reason of His saying, exalted is He: He is God (Q 59:22) — glorified be He. So He is the one pointed to in His names.

And whoever writes the letter mīm, and its figure and its wafq, and recites over it the words and the verses that follow, and carries it, and goes in with it upon kings and governors and the judges of Islam, is accepted in their sight and his word prevails; and awe accrues to its bearer, so that were he to confront lions with it, they would abase themselves before him and stand in awe of him. And if its bearer enters into war, he subdues the enemies and crushes the adversaries, and no enemy draws near him but God, exalted is He, gives him victory over him. And he will be beloved among the people, held in esteem and honoured; everyone who sees him loves him and inclines toward him. And it has mighty occult properties. /fol. 38v./

And some of the imams have indicated that whoever makes his striving (mujāhada) and his discipline (riyāḍa) sincere, and frees himself from the hand of appetite and of anger and of base characteristics and evil deeds; and sits in an empty place, and closes off the road of the senses, and opens the eye of the inward and its hearing; and sets the heart in correspondence with the world of the Dominion (ʿālam al-malakūt); and strives, and says "Allāh, Allāh" continually with the heart and not with the tongue, until he comes to have no existence of himself, and remains not seeing

— anything but God, exalted is He, there is opened for him an aperture through which he looks, and he beholds in waking what he beholds in sleep. So there appear to him the spirits of the angels and of the prophets, and beautiful, comely forms; and the Dominion (malakūt) of the heavens and the earth is unveiled to him, and he sees what it is not possible to expound nor to describe — as the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((The earth was drawn together for me, and I saw its easts and its wests.)) And God, exalted is He, said to His Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — in His Mighty Book: And remember the name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him with utter devotion (Q 73:8). Its meaning is: the severing [of attachment] from everything, and the purifying of the heart of everything, and the imploring of Him with one's whole being. And this is the way of the Sufis in this age.

And know that among the occult properties of Lordship is the knowledge of His Most Beautiful Names and of His supreme, exalted attributes — and especially, among them, the Greatest Name of God. For He is God, who alone is singled out by this name, by His majesty and His glory; and He is the God to whom divinity belongs from Himself, by Himself; and He is God, who has no child and no parent: God is only one God (Q 4:171). And for that reason one of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) said to one of the aspirants: Do you wish to learn a benefit of which you are capable? He said: Yes. So he said to him: Persevere in saying "Allāh, Allāh, Allāh" for seven days, mentioning none but Him; and fast your day, and rise [in prayer] in your night as much as you are able; and persevere in this litany of remembrance, not parting from it by night nor by day, and speak to no one; and withdraw into retreat away from people for seven days — and the wonders of the earth will be shown to you. Then continue in that for another seven days — and the wonders of the heavens will be shown to you. Then likewise for another seven days — and the wonders of the highest Dominion will be shown to you. And if you attain to forty days, God, exalted is He, will manifest to you charismatic marvels (karāmāt), and will grant you free disposal (taṣarruf) in existence.

And it is related from the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((When the believing servant says: Yā Allāh (O God) — God, exalted is He, says: At your service, My servant! I am God; what is your need?)) God knows God best; none knows the innermost reality (kunh) of God's greatness but God. He is the Lord of all, and He is Knower of all things. And people have spoken concerning the innermost reality of God, exalted is He — whether it is knowable to human beings or not. He who accepts that it is not knowable to human beings says: because a thing is known by direct sight when it is present, and by likeness when it is absent; whereas God, exalted is He — the like of whom there is nothing (Q 42:11) — and He is not attained by direct sight, because of His saying, exalted is He: Sight does not attain Him, but He attains all sight (Q 6:103). And one of the masters among the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn) said: since His pre-eternity, exalted is He, is established without beginning /fol. 39r./ and His perduring without cessation, and His unicity is not [a unicity] of number, and His attributes fall outside the attributes of creation, it necessarily follows that those who describe cannot reach the innermost reality of His attribute; for were it so, there would appear for it a limit and a likeness, and limit and likeness lead to passing away and annihilation, and that, in respect of God, exalted is He, is impossible. So said al-Muḥāsibī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him. And it is related that Gabriel — peace be upon him — came down upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — with the Greatest Name upon a leaf from the leaves of the Garden, sealed with a seal of musk, on which was written: O God, I ask You by Your Name, the treasured, the concealed, the pure, the purified, the All-Holy, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the Possessor of Majesty and Honour. Anas said: A woman said: Teach it to us, O Messenger of God! And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((We have been forbidden to teach it to women and children.)) And one of the excellent ones wrote to one of the righteous imams, [asking] that he gather for him formulae with which he might supplicate in the weighty matters of his affairs. So he wrote out for him this supplication, saying: O God, I ask You by Your Name; and by [the truth] that You are God in the realities of pure realization; and by [the truth] that You are God in every state among the states of majesty and equitable ordering; and by [the truth] that You are God, sanctified by the properties proper to oneness (aḥadiyya) and to self-sufficiency (ṣamadiyya), above [having] an opposite, a peer, a contrary, or an equal; and by [the truth] that You are God, the like of whom there is nothing, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (Q 42:11) — that You bless our master Muḥammad, and the family of Muḥammad, and everyone who loves Muḥammad; and that You bless him; and that You fulfil all my needs, every one of them, with a fulfilment wherein there is for me the good of this world and of the hereafter — preserved by [Your] watchful keeping, preserved from calamities, regarded with the special properties of [Your] providential care. O You who return again and again with good things! O You who are in reality worthy of pious reverence and worthy of [bestowing] good things! O God, this is the request of a servant of the might of Your Lordship, in the making manifest of his request, by [the truth] that You are the Knower of the unseen realms, and the Witness of the realities of the things sought before ever they come into contact with hearts. So bring it to completion with a beautiful ending, O best of all that is sought. And may God bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, the beloved of hearts. And it is said that this supplication contains the Greatest Name of God, just as has been transmitted concerning "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate". And know that between it [the basmala] and the Greatest Name of God there is only what lies between the black of the eye and the white of it.
Chapter 6 (al-bāb al-sādis): On spiritual retreat (khalwa) and what pertains specially to the practitioners of the devotional seclusions (iʿtikāf) that give access to the celestial realms [75]

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that by this chapter, mighty in import, one attains to the name al-ʿAzīz al-Raḥmān (the Mighty, the All-Merciful). A certain one of the righteous, of the imams of the religion, made devotional seclusion (iʿtikāf) in the preaching-chamber of the congregational mosque of Aleppo. It was like a grave, having in it no opening for the light except from the door; so when the door was shut, it remained like a grave, in narrowness and in darkness. He would pray with the congregation, and would go out backwards at the time of the standing for prayer; and when the prayer was finished, he would enter in his [former] state, facing the qibla, and would not look at anyone. /fol. 39v./ And the greater part of his humble entreaty and of his asking of God, mighty and exalted, at all his times, was that God should teach him the Greatest Name. And while he was thus one night, seated, striving earnestly in fervent supplication to God, exalted is He, with the litany of remembrance (dhikr), lo, there was a tablet of light that had taken form before his eyes, and upon it figures depicted. He turned away from it, lest looking at it should divert him from his turning toward God, exalted is He. Then he was struck with it in the face, and it was said to him: "Take what will profit you." Thereupon he opened his eyes and turned to the tablet, contemplating it.

And behold, it was four lines: a line above, a line below, a line on the right, and a line on the left; and in the middle a circle; and inside the circle another circle; and between the two circles the measure of a gap (fatḥa). And in the middle of the small circle is a line that cuts it into two halves; and in the upper half is the meeting of two other lines with the cutting line, [forming] a triangular figure; and written in the middle of it, from the pole of the circle: Nay, rather He is God (unidentified quotation; not a Qurʾānic verse); and a jīm in the angle of the two lines. And on the end of the right-hand line that meets the diameter of the circle is the letter dāl; and written near the letter is the name al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), its beginning from the line of the triangle and its end close to the circle. And at the angle of the diameter from the circle is the letter alif; and the name al-Wāḥid (the One), exalted is He, is in front of the name al-Ṣamad, and behind it the name al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), and behind the name al-Qahhār, behind it; and al-Qahhār is at the top of the line from the circle. And from inside the line — I mean the line of the triangle — is the letter yāʾ; and on the end of the left-hand line that meets the diameter of the circle is the letter hāʾ; and on the diameter, from the angle upon the line that meets the circle, are the name al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) and the name al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), from the line of the triangle to the circle; and behind it the name al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving). And within the triangle, upon the diameter, is the letter ṭāʾ. And the lower half, upon the diameter, is a line of a quarter of the circle: a letter khāʾ added upon its diameter, a quarter of the circle, running to the circle; and another line issuing from it that ends at the half of the circle; and within this line is written mutajallī ("manifesting"); and within the other line from the diameter is written in light, at its end that faces the circle, the letter zāy. And outside this line, which is a quarter of the circle, is written qad atāka ("there has come to you"). And on the left half of the half-circle — that is, its quarter — are two lines: in one of them, namely the one that adjoins mutajallī, is written mukhtār ("chosen"); and in the other line is written bi-l-hudā ("with guidance"); and outside it is written ʿabd lanā ("a servant of Ours"). And from inside the other two lines, up to the half of the circle, is written the wāw; and there is written Those are ten complete (Q 2:196), running to the half of the pole. And written at the head of this diameter, upon the outer circle, is Alif-Lām-Mīm. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 3:1–2), in disconnected letters. And this Alif-Lām-Mīm faces the jīm that is inside the triangle; and the lām-alif of lā ilāha illā huwa ("there is no god but He") faces the alif that is at the end of the pole on the left side; and al-Ḥayy faces the letter wāw that is at the bottom of the circle; and the mīm of al-Qayyūm faces Alif-Lām-Mīm. And the lines whose mention has already been made are before you. And the circle, at its edge, has written on the outside and God encompasses them round about (Q 85:20); and on the other side, outside the circle, is written Nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:21–22). And in the lower line, outside the circle: Those who have denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers — they shall come to know (Q 40:70). And when I had firmly fixed its form in my mind well, by means of the figure, the form vanished from me. Then, when I had prayed the dawn prayer and had sat down, I began the recitation /fol. 40r./ of my litany (wird), and a drowsiness of sleep came over me. And while I was asleep I saw in it the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, ennoble his face and be pleased with him — and he said to me: "Where is the tablet that you were given?" And it was [still] depicted with me; so I handed it to him, and he deemed it mighty. And he said to me concerning its meaning things which I did not understand, nor did I grasp of them anything save a single word. That was that the Commander of the Faithful placed his finger upon the letter jīm that is in the angle of the triangle in the upper half of the circle, and said: "From Huwa ('He') the Name of Majesty issues forth." So I knew that it was the Greatest Name of God, and that the names point to it, and that it points to the transcendence (tanzīh) of the names of the holy Essence.

So I said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have not understood what you have said to me." He said to me: "Muḥammad b. Ṭalḥa will expound it to you, if God, exalted is He, wills." Then I awoke and completed my litany, and went to Ibn Ṭalḥa — for between me and him there was a covenant of brotherhood in God — and I recounted the story to him. He praised God, exalted is He, and set about expounding it. Now he had supposed in his mind that no one would attain to it; and when he heard that from me, he asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, for that, and set about it, and named it al-Durr al-munaẓẓam fī ism Allāh al-aʿẓam ("The Well-Ordered Pearl, on the Greatest Name of God") — and it is [also] said, fī al-sirr al-aʿẓam ("on the Greatest Secret").

Then, after that, I saw the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in another vision, and he was seated in the prayer-niche (miḥrāb), and the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — was present; and he was making mention of that tablet in the presence of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace. And ʿAlī — may God ennoble his face — said: "The holy Name does not depend upon any other than itself for its signification." And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: "By the truth of the Truth, thus did Gabriel — peace be upon him — the Trustworthy Spirit, teach it to me." And when I recovered from my sleep, I came to the master (shaykh) and informed him of the vision; and he fell silent for the space of a full hour, then stretched out his hand behind his back and brought forth a slip of paper on which was written this very expression — I mean, "The holy, greatest

Name does not depend upon any other than itself for its signification." And when I saw that, I said to him: "Why do you not put it into the commentary?" He said: "I supposed that no one would come to know of it but myself, because of what had befallen me." Then he asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, for that, as we mentioned at the first, and appended it to the commentary as we have set forth, and named it as we have described. And it is a secret among the secrets of God, exalted is He, which none attain save the truthful, who stand guard upon godfearing. For it is a mighty name and a noble secret: if you come to know the indication of its operative deployment (taṣrīf), mankind and the jinn will obey you, and the treasures will be opened to you — the treasures of knowledge and the treasures of the earth. So guard it from him who is not fit for it, and touch it not save when you are in a state of purity.

And this is its form, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, glorified and exalted, wills. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 40v./

Know that the letters set in its angles are the letters of the triangle, and they are the completion of the nine numbers, which are the first letters of abjad, thus:(alif),(bāʾ),(jīm),(dāl),(hāʾ), (wāw), (zāy), (ḥāʾ),(ṭāʾ),(yāʾ) — and the yāʾ, the tenth of them, is in it for the vocative. So you say: Yā Allāh (O God), Yā Bāʿith (O Raiser of the dead), Yā Jalīl (O Majestic), Yā Dāʾim (O Everlasting), Yā Hādī (O Guide), Yā Wāḥid (O One), Yā Zakī (O Pure), Yā Ḥāfiẓ (O Preserver), Yā Ṭāhir (O Undefiled) — nine names that gather the nine letters. And [with them] what has already been given of the supplication, whose beginning is "O God, I ask You by [the truth] that You are God", to the end of it; and it is the supplication of this greatest figure.

And it is this noble supplication: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You by [the truth] that You are God, sanctified by the properties proper to oneness (aḥadiyya) and to self-sufficiency (ṣamadiyya), above [having] an opposite, a peer, a contrary, or an equal; and by [the truth] that You are God, of whom there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (Q 42:11). I ask You to bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, and to the family of Muḥammad, and to everyone who loves Muḥammad; and to fulfil my need and all my needs, every one of them, and whatever holds for me the good of this world and of the hereafter, [I being] encompassed by [Your] watchful keeping, preserved from calamities, with the special marks of the [good] outcomes. O You who return again and again with good things! O You who are in reality worthy of pious reverence, worthy to forgive, and worthy of [bestowing] good things! O God, this is the request of a servant of the might of Your Lordship, in the making manifest of his request — for You are the Knower of the unseen realms, and the Witness of the reality of the seeker before /fol. 41r./ ever it comes into contact with hearts. So bring it to completion with a beautiful ending, O best of all that is sought. And may God bless our master Muḥammad, the beloved of hearts, and his family and his Companions, and grant them abundant peace." And this is the supplication of this greatest figure.

So draw the analogy and derive from it whatever you wish; and whatever you desire in it you will find, and you will attain your request in all that is hoped for. Sufficient is it as an utmost end! For it is the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar) and the greatest theriac (al-tiryāq al-akbar). So whoever understands its secret attains thereby what he desires, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Another section of the same. He — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: I was in spiritual retreat (khalwa), and I saw a figure, namely a circle, and within the circle the Name of Majesty, which is Allāh. And there had branched off from it every name in which there is an ʿayn — and they are nineteen weighty names, which you see drawn in the figure, completing 20 with the Name of Majesty. And when this figure had become fixed in my mind, and that state had parted from me, and the luminous figure had been lifted away, I represented it upon paper. Then my thought returned to me, and I said: it is possible that I should bring forth from this name the ninety-nine names by way of branching. So I set about that, and a seizure took hold of me, and it was said to me:

— "Therein is thanksgiving for the making-known, together with the granting of success." So I asked forgiveness of God, exalted is He, and praised Him, and turned back from that thought which had occurred to me. These, then, are nineteen names that issued from the Name of Majesty (al-jalāla), and the Name of Majesty out of which they issued is the twentieth, which seals them. They possess benefits — things not to be doubted by anyone who knows how they are to be employed and has seen their efficacious influence. Among these: there is no matter, worldly or otherworldly, whose attainment a man desires — whereupon he purifies himself, faces the qibla, and prays two rakʿas in a clean place, in seclusion, with good intention and with fine recourse to God, exalted is He, at midnight or in the last part of it, and invokes these twenty names with presence of heart, in such a way that his thought is not occupied with anything other than the matter he is engaged upon, and recites them one thousand six hundred and seventy-three times (and if you wish to restrict yourself to fewer than that number, let it be one hundred and eighty-one times), and then asks God, glorified and exalted, for his need immediately after the supplication — but that God, exalted is He, makes its means easy for him; especially if he asks of God that some branch of knowledge be made easy for him, for God — mighty and majestic, exalted is He — opens for him from His mighty Name a road to his objective, and he sees therein marvels: some of them such as may be uttered, and some of them such as may not be uttered. Among these also: when a man writes this circle and places it among his goods, at home and on a journey, he is guarded, by the leave of God, exalted is He, from corrupters finding any way to him. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon his right upper arm and walks with it among his enemies, God, exalted is He, preserves him from them and forsakes them. And whoever goes in upon one of the tyrants whom he fears — that man is humbled before him and submits, and God, exalted is He, overturns his tyrannical might before him, and he is humbled before him and submits, and his soul is given over to what he desires, and he grants him his requests; and, by the leave of God, exalted is He, he is spared the evil of all that, because of the wondrous and majestic secrets contained in it. And if you write the noble names with rose-water, musk, saffron, and fine camphor, and give them as a draught to one in whose body there is a bodily ailment or a psychic ailment /fol. 41v./, it removes it and lightens it; and it gives its bearer strength in his soul, his body, and his spirit, and the names give him awe-inspiring presence and majesty, such that he witnesses that with a witnessing concerning which he has no doubt. And if a man invokes them every day after the dawn prayer seventy-seven times, and they become part of his litany, he will see, from the blessings of that, good things in his religion, his worldly life, and his soul — wondrous things, so much so that his aspiration scarcely ever attaches itself to any of the creatures, and the creatures are made subservient to him upon his completing them, and their love for him [is procured for him too]; and he loves them and they love him with an intense love. And if one of the tyrants wrongs a man, or overpowers him, or harms him, and he wishes to take vengeance upon him, let him recite this supplication and these names, saying: O God, O al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), O al-Sarīʿ (the Swift), O al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), O al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), O al-ʿAdl (the Just), O al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might), O al-Faʿʿāl (the Doer of what He wills) — in the first hour of Saturday, for the whole of it; and let him invoke against the one who wronged him and harmed him. For God, blessed and exalted, will take vengeance for him upon that man before the week comes round, and he will be granted victory over the one who wronged him.

And if you want it for love and for reconciliation between two who bear hatred toward each other, then the twenty names are written, and you write together with them the name of the one whom you wish to love you and to be subject to your command and your prohibition: so write his name and your name, dissolve them in water, and give the two who hate each other to drink of that water — they will come to love one another, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And likewise, if you give the names as a draught to whomever you wish, he will love you with an intense love and will never again wish to be parted from you. The writing is to be done in the daytime of Sunday, in the hour of the Sun or in the hour of Mercury, after you have suffumigated with a fragrant suffumigation such as aloeswood, nadd, ambergris, benzoin (jāwī), musk, nadd, and mastic. And that will come to pass, if God — exalted and glorified is He — wills.
And these are the twenty names alluded to. You say: O God, O al-Samīʿ, O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-Sarīʿ, O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-

Embracing), O al-ʿAdl, O al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Mutaʿāl (the Most High), O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Bāʿith, O al-Faʿʿāl, O al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Rafīʿ (the Sublime), O al-Maʿbūd (the Worshipped), O al-Māniʿ (the Withholder), O al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of benefit), O al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer), O al-Badīʿ. And this is the form of the Greatest Signet alluded to, and it is as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He, His be the praise — wills. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 42r./
[Circular diagram (the Greatest Signet): as in the source — ]

And this is the supplication of the circle. You say: In the name of God, and with His name is the beginning made. In the name of God. O Lord, I ask You by Your name with which You opened the world of creation and of command, by the self-disclosure to the Real which makes manifest the relations of the sending-down; and [I ask You] by the One transcendent in command, in existence, and in an intelligible hiddenness — that being for whomever You have strengthened, nay, known to whomever You have granted witnessing, unknown to whomever You will — by reason of that in it which is ambiguous: a multiplicity that does no injury to the oneness of that which You have made firmly established of a firm decree. O al-ʿAlīm, O al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), O God, O Lord, I ask You, O God: O al-Samīʿ, O al-ʿAlīm, O al-Sarīʿ, O al-Wāsiʿ, O al-ʿAdl, O al-Mutaʿāl, O al-ʿAzīz, O al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), O al-Bāʿith, O al-Shahīd (the Witness), O al-Rafīʿ, O al-Maʿbūd, O al-Māniʿ, O al-Muʿīd, O al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser), O al-Mundafiʿ [so in the base text; perhaps read al-Mudāfiʿ, the Defender], O al-Jāmiʿ, O al-Badīʿ. I ask You, O God, by the secret of the relation (iḍāfa) that binds together the Presence of Necessity. I ask You, O God, by that which You have spread out in the malakūt (realm of dominion) of Your jabarūt (realm of omnipotence), and by that which You have made plain in the jabarūt of Your malakūt, and by that which You have kept to Yourself in the worlds of the holiness of Your lāhūt (realm of divinity), and by that which You have hidden from the apprehension of the intellects in the secret of the bahamūt of Your mercy, and by that which You have folded into the secret of Your secret in the ground of the well-proportioned existentiation, and by the symbols and the intimations which You have set out in detail among the kinds of the treasured modality within the inmost of the inmost depths of the descent: that You guard me with
