Your impregnable guarding from the voices of Satan, his tunes, his promptings, and his slanders — for he makes good into evil, and land into sea, and sea into land /fol. 42v./, and benefit into harm — and from the ill-omen of his guile. I ask You, O God, that You bestow upon me, by Your all-pervading kindness and Your immense generosity, the rank of the kings luminous in bestowed graces (ʿawārif) and in operative deployment within the kingdom of acts; and honour me with Your perfect words in life and in death, that I may attain the glory of the paths of those bestowed graces; and bestow upon me from Yourself gnosis (ʿirfān), O Ḥannān (the Tender), O Mannān (the Bounteous), O Lord of the worlds.

Another faṣl belonging to it. It is that by which our master Jesus — upon him be peace and blessing — used to bring the dead to life, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and it is the Greatest Name. So know what has come to you of its good, that you may be made happy by it; for its secret is rare and its effect is wondrous. It is the name of God — the Mighty, the Great, the Greatest, the Good, the Pure, the Undefiled, the Complete, the Treasured, the Hidden — by which all the Most Beautiful Names are made to shine. Asad b. Mūsā transmitted it from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: This treasured, hidden Name — whoever writes it while fasting and with clean garment, on Sunday at sunrise, and suffumigates it with Indian aloeswood and red sandalwood, upon gazelle parchment or clean paper, and hangs it upon his forearm — good things hasten to him, and he witnesses of its blessing wondrous things not to be doubted. And this is the Name with which God sent Moses —

peace be upon him — to Pharaoh, when He said to him: Indeed I am God; there is no god but I, so worship Me (Q 20:14). And by this Name Zubayda held sway over Hārūn al-Rashīd, and he would do nothing save by her counsel and her opinion. And if you write it and suffumigate it close by the fire, and the writing is hung facing the sun, where it rises upon it and sets, and its rays do not leave it the whole day long, it becomes for him a means of acceptance among people.

And this is the supplication of the letter-circle, the expounded one, whose mention and whose excellence have gone before. You say: O God, I ask You — O God, O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O al-Qāʾim (the Upholder), O al-Qadīr (the All-Powerful), O al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Qadīr, O al-Qarīb (the Near), O al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing) — You are the One who gave might to Your friends through Your prophets, and perfected Your prophets through the bearing of Your affliction, and crushed the wretched by the spreading out of the sovereignty of the dominion of Your power and of Your overmastering. I ask You by Your impregnable, momentous might, and by Your immense, all-powerful generosity, and by Your right over Your creation, over the exalted among them and the lowly, that You make me mighty among created beings through independence of them and neediness toward You; and honour me with Your life diffused within the secrets of their innermost selves, so that I may take refuge by it and turn toward You; and grant me a might drawn from Your ennobling of Your friends, in the final issue and in the present state, at Your drawing of them to Yourself; and make me mighty at the door of the Real through steadfastness and witnessing, that I may be one possessed of true selfhood (inniyya) before You; and spread out my might within the hearts of the people of faith, that I may attain the secret of Your compassion at the manifestation of the proof and the demonstration. O Ḥannān, O Mannān, You are the One who manifests in the hearts of those who love You the secret of the opening and of the self-disclosure. You hear what is subtler and more hidden, and with Your eye that neither sleeps nor slumbers You see the creeping of the black ant upon the solid rock, beneath the layers of the dust-coloured earth, in /fol. 43r./ the darkest night. O God, I ask You by the subtleties of what You have folded into hearing and sight; and by the fine things of what You have bestowed upon sight; and by the realities of what You have gathered together between hearing and sight; and by the fine points of what You have concealed within sight, that it might fall out in the place of hearing; and by the precedences of what You have hidden within hearing, that it might stand in the place of sight: that You grant me secrets folded into the encompassment of sight, and the witnessing of lights established at the containing of hearing and sight; and grant me, by Your luminosity and by the crowning of the secret of Your signs, the perpetuity of watchful vigilance over what descends from Your most high holiness, and the apprehensions of the All-Encompassing that gathers the names; and strengthen me to understand the calling of the soul to account with exacting reckoning. For You are the gatherer of every good and the repeller of every harm, O Lord of the worlds. I ask You, O God: O al-Qāhir, O al-Qahhār, O al-Qarīb, O al-Quddūs, O al-Qāʾim, O al-Qayyūm — I ask You to bless and grant peace to our master

Muḥammad and to the family of our master Muḥammad, and to fulfil my need entire: what I ask for and what I do not ask for, of that wherein You have good pleasure, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And this is the end of what has been set down of the faṣl. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.
Chapter 7 (al-bāb al-sābiʿ): On the names by which our master Jesus — peace be upon him — used to bring the dead to life, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted [83]

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that these names are of mighty import. The Imām al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: I sought the Greatest Name for seven years, and I found it with none but a man of the people of China. He had gathered together of these names a mighty matter, and I found them written in his keeping in the Ḥimyarī script, so that none should know them save their [rightful] people.

And ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: Whoever fasts for them seven days, then, when the seventh day comes, let him write these names upon gazelle parchment with musk, saffron, and rose water; then let him invoke by the names of the angels of the seasonal quarter (thāqūfa) in which that operation is performed — the thāqūfa being the quarter of the year — and let him adjure by the names of the winds, according as Abraham, the Friend of the All-Merciful — peace be upon him — named them. Then after that you mention your need and ask for it. And if it be possible for that to be over running water, it is better. And you hang it up toward the sun and mention what you desire, and you recite over it the names of the angels of the thāqūfa and its helpers, and the winds and the planets that belong to it.

Al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: When he met with the Chinese master mentioned above, when he asked him about the Greatest Name, he said: O my son, know that every name of the names of God, exalted is He, is mighty. I said: Yes, but I have already come to know many of them. Then the master questioned me about the thāqūfa of Balʿām b. Bāʿūrā and the thāqūfa of Joseph, and I informed him of them both; for the master had supposed that I had not gained access to the treasured names. Thereupon the master said: Draw near to me — by God, no comer has come to me dearer than you. I said: Yes. So I drew near to him, and we did not cease conferring together /fol. 43v./ concerning the names. Then I asked him about the names that were upon the staff of Moses — peace be upon him — but he did not know them. Al-Khwārizmī said: And he it was who dictated to me the Greatest Name. He said to me: O my son, know that the most exalted of the names of God, exalted is He, and the greatest of them, are these names, if God, exalted is He, wills. And these ancient names were written in a foreign tongue, and some of them in Hebrew, so that none should know them. And they are the majestic names. And their excellence and their blessing is what Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — related from Ḥumayd b. Abī Thābit from Abū Khālid — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: I heard a man of the people of knowledge say: The excellence of these names over all [other] names is like the excellence of the Night of Power over all other nights, and like the excellence of Friday over all other days.

The Imām al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: I found them written in the Ḥimyarī script in a place called Qazwīn. So whoever understands their excellence, it is incumbent upon him that he guard them well, and then that he fear God, mighty and exalted. And they are beneficial for one afflicted with anguish or with terror, or for one who has trembling, or griping [of the bowels], or palpitation of the heart. And Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: If one fasts for them three days, then writes them upon a clean, white gazelle parchment with saffron, then hangs it upon one afflicted with the wind, or with the evil eye (naẓra), or with black bile, or with something other than that — it departs from him in the swiftest time that may be. And it is said, in [another] transmission: you write them on Saturday for whatever you desire; you fast that day of yours, and you write them upon gazelle parchment after you have ascertained the house of the Moon — whether it be the best of the good, or the contrary of that. And it is said that Jesus — upon whom be blessing and peace — used to bring the dead to life by them, and to heal by it the man born blind and the leper, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And they are written in the lowest heaven. They are to be written on Friday. The people of knowledge have agreed upon their interpretation, and it is that upon which the Commander of the Faithful al-Maʾmūn gathered the jurists, the scholars, and the sages, until, in his presence, their interpretation was verified. And whoever is assiduous in the mention of them and is in accord with God, exalted is He — God, exalted is He, rends for him the customary order of things, and the objects of desire and the benefits come within his reach. So beware of treating them with contempt; make them the greatest of your concern; hold fast to them all your life long; make them your stored treasure; and make them your litany (wird) by day and by night — you will win the station of sainthood (wilāya), and attain the ranks of the God-fearing.

And from Abū l-Hudhayl — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: When Jesus — upon whom be blessing and peace — desired to bring the dead to life, he would pray two rakʿas, reciting in the first the Mother of the Book (the Fātiḥa) and Alif-Lām-Mīm al-Sajda, and in the second the Mother of the Book and Blessed is He in whose hand is the kingdom, and He is powerful over everything (Q 67:1). Then, when he had finished his prayer, he would prostrate himself before God, mighty and exalted, and praise Him. Then he would invoke by the seven names whose invocation is answered, and these are the names: /fol. 44r./ O Qadīm (Eternal), O Ḥayy (Living), O Dāʾim (Everlasting), O Fard (Single), O Aḥad (Unique), O Wāḥid (One), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge). Muqātil b. Sulaymān — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: I kept seeking the names by which our master Jesus — peace be upon him — used to bring the dead to life, for forty years, until I found them with a man of the people of knowledge and religion; and they are these names mentioned above. And Muqātil b. Sulaymān — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: Whoever invokes by them after the dawn prayer one hundred times and asks for whatever need he desires — if he is not answered, then let him curse Muqātil, be he alive or dead. And they may also be invoked for the destruction of the wrongdoers and of the tyrants, and for other things besides that. So when you have prayed the dawn prayer, say, while seated, before you speak with anyone, one hundred times: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. O Qadīm (Eternal), O Qāʾim (Subsisting), O Dāʾim (Everlasting), O Fard (Single), O Witr (Odd-numbered), O Aḥad (Unique), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting), O Karīm (Generous), O Raḥīm (Compassionate), O Sanad (Support), O You unto whom is all reliance, O You who did not beget and were not begotten, and to whom none is equal (Q 112:3–4), O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." Then, when you have completed the hundred times, ask for your need, whatever it may be. And if you are not answered, then curse Muqātil, be he alive or dead. And as for these names: when you invoke by them, beware of invoking by them against anyone, lest the invocation turn back upon you. And if you invoke and ask, then ask for what befits you of the affair of your livelihood, in a matter of this world or of religion, or the teaching of knowledge from which benefit is had, and the like of that — for they are mighty, noble, majestic names.

And when you desire the operative deployment (taṣrīf) of the Greatest Name, then make a circle like the circle of the sun, the names being within it, and suffumigate it with aloeswood and ambergris and the like of that. And this is the form of the circle, as you see.
[Circular diagram of the Greatest Name: as in the source — ]

And this is the invocation of the Greatest Name. You say: O God, I ask You by that whereby Gabriel — peace be upon him — asked You when he prostrated himself beside Your mighty Throne, and by the right of Your name Allāh Allāh, that You subject to me Your angels, and the servitors of Your Throne and the Presence of Your dominion: Kasfiyāʾīl, and

Dardiyāʾīl, and Samḥiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾīl, and Rūqiyāʾīl, and Nūriyāʾīl, and Samkiyāʾīl, and Ṭahṭahāʾīl, and Jibriyāʾīl, and Darʿiyāʾīl, and Samsamāʾīl, and Ṭāṭāʾīl, and Ḥarmiyāʾīl, and Ṭayṭiyāʾīl, and Isrāfīl, and ʿAzrāʾīl, and Mīkāʾīl, and Karmāʾih, and Karshāʾih, and Sarfiyāʾīl, and ʿArqiyāʾīl, and Thaṭbiyāʾīl, and ʿAyniyāʾīl. Answer me, by the noble angels and the good spirits — peace be upon them — who are brought near to God by [the affirmation of] His oneness; by the right of the name of God, the One, the Magnified, the Light most holy, which You have preferred above all the names entirely — the mighty of them and the impregnable of them, the majestic of them and the great of them — [I ask nothing] save that You subject to me these noble angels, that they may fulfil my need, which is such-and-such, and which is a thing wherein God, mighty and exalted, has good pleasure. And beware of what is not lawful; for Balʿām b. Bāʿūrā had good command of the Greatest Name, and when he invoked by it against the people of Moses — upon whom be blessing and peace — the invocation was turned back upon him, and God, exalted is He, stripped him of the Greatest Name. And refuge is with God, exalted is He, from that. And God, exalted is He, has said: And recite to them the tiding of him to whom We brought Our signs, and he stripped himself out of them, whereupon Satan pursued him and he became one of the errant. And had We so willed, We would have lifted him up by them; but he sank down toward the earth and followed his own whim. His likeness, then, is the likeness of the dog: if you drive at it, it pants; and if you leave it be, it pants. That is the likeness of the folk who denied Our signs. So narrate the accounts, that they may perhaps take thought (Q 7:175–176). God, God, concerning this Greatest Name! And beware of making light of it, for it turns back upon you and upon whoever deploys it in acts of disobedience to God, exalted is He. Guard it from those who are not its [rightful] people, and preserve it, and you will be happy; for it is God's secret [entrusted] to His friends and to His elect. Many of the scholars and the righteous have busied themselves with it and have attained by it their desire and their object of search. And we have abridged the discourse; and God guides whom He wills to a straight path. And know — may God grant me and you success in the understanding of His noble names — that whoever writes this treasured, hidden, noble, blessed wafq and carries it, being pure in garment and in body, God, exalted is He, establishes his affair outwardly and inwardly, aids him unto obedience, and provides him with strength and with victory over his enemies. No tyrant's glance falls upon him but he holds him in awe and magnifies him. And whoever places it upon his head, every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan is abased before him; and God, exalted is He, gives life to his outward and his inward, and strengthens his heart for the outward works and the inward. And no one has carried it and contended with his enemy but that he overcame him, subdued him, and gained the victory over him, by the blessing of God, exalted is He, and the blessing of this blessed wafq. And whoever enters into war having it with him is granted victory over his enemies, and no harm ever reaches him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if a king carries it, his troops obey him, and love him, and hold him in awe, and
he is victorious and divinely supported. /fol. 45r./
Chapter 8 (al-bāb al-thāmin): On the four seasonal quarters (thawāqīf) and the revolving seasons that pertain specially to them

The master — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him — that this chapter is the pivot of this book, and that in it are recondite secrets. So when you wish to operate with these names and with the blessed and majestic seasonal quarters (thawāqīf), and with the names of the angels who govern time, and the names of the winds and the planets — know then that the year is twelve months, divided into four divisions, each division of them being three months; and the seasons are four: among them the season of summer, among them the season of autumn, among them the season of winter, and among them the season of spring. And each season of these four seasons is called a thāqūfa. The first thāqūfa is that of the season of spring, and its beginning is the twenty-fourth of Māris (March) to the twenty-fourth of Yūniya (June). The second thāqūfa is that of the season of summer, and it is the twenty-fourth day of [June] to the twenty-fourth day of Ishtanbīr (September). The third thāqūfa is that of the season of autumn, and it is from the twenty-fourth day of September to the twenty-fourth day of Dujanbīr (December). The fourth thāqūfa is that of the season of winter, and it is from the twenty-fourth day of December to the twenty-fourth day of March.

The names of the kings who govern time — it is said, the times: /fol. 45v./ the lord of the east, his name is Danyāʾil; and the lord of the west, his name is Dardiyāʾīl; and the lord of the qibla, his name is Anyāʾīl; and the lord of the south, his name is Ṣarfiyāʾīl. And the lord of the qibla is for the season of spring; and the lord of the east for the season of summer; and the lord of the south for the season of autumn; and the lord of the west for the season of winter.

The distribution of the helpers over the four cardinal directions. The helpers of the lord of the east are Darḥamiyāʾīl, Ḥarqiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾīl. And the helpers of the lord of the west are Ḥabrīqīl, Qaṣmāʾīl, and Shūʿiyāʾīl. And the helpers of the lord of the qibla are Farghūʾil, Ṭākhīl, and Allūl. And the helpers of the lord of the south are Qamiyāʾīl, Marḥiyāʾīl, and Ḥarmakiyāʾīl.

And now there have been gathered together for you the four invocations, with their names, their angels, and their helpers, and the name of the sun and the moon and the four winds, and the name of the heaven and the earth, and everything you have need of. So lick the honey, and do not ask the honeycomb about its bees, for it has come to you white and pure. So if you are in the season of spring and have a need, then call upon the lord of the qibla. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Anyāʾil, and your helpers Farghūʾil, Ṭākhīl, and Allūl; and the winds ʿAqdadūn, Māshūl, Māsūrā, Samʿā, and Ṭabʿatayn; and the sun and the moon: Yāḥaft, Saʿsamyāh, Yūnār, Miyārij, Jarjalfah, Baṣād and her sisters, and Basīlīṣ. In the name of God, and by His name, the name with which beginning is made, Lord of the hereafter and of this present world, who has no goal and no end. [His is] what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them and what is beneath the soil. God is mighty, everlasting in bounties, most merciful of the merciful, powerful and not subject to power, subduing and not subdued, and just on the Day of Resurrection. There is no god but He, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. He is God, other than whom there is no god: the King, the All-Holy, the Peace, the Granter of Security, the Overseer, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supremely Great. Glory be to God above what they associate with Him. He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner. His are the Most Beautiful Names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise (Q 59:23–24). I ask You, O God, O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), that You grant me in this station of mine a mercy from Yourself, and that You fulfil my need in such-and-such a matter. Truly You are powerful over everything. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. I ask You, O God, O Lord, by Your perfect Name — O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). I bear witness that everything apart from You is vain. O God, I have believed in You; there is no god but You. O Lord, there is no lord besides You. I ask You by Your mighty Name, which You have preferred above all Your names entire, that You make subservient to me the lord of this season, and the lord of the hour, and of the thāqūfa, and of the four regions, so that they may be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need, by Your leave, O God. O my God, You decree with truth, and no decree is passed against You. I adjure you, O company of spiritual kings, that you fulfil my need — by the right of Him to whom belong might and omnipotence, and by the right of the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Everlasting who does not die, who — there is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing; who has a name that is not forgotten, and a light that is not extinguished, and a Throne that does not pass away, and a Footstool that does not move; who sent down the Book /fol. 46r./ upon His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. I ask You, O God, O God, O God: You are He beside whom there is no god, the Master of this world and of the hereafter. I ask You to fulfil my need, and to make subservient to me the spiritual being that serves these names. Truly You are powerful over everything.

And if you are in the time of summer, then call upon the lord of the eastern thāqūfa. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Danyāʾīl, and your helpers Darḥamiyāʾīl, Ḥarqiyāʾīl, and Samʿiyāʾil; and the winds Kaydaḥ, Masahīmūn, Masahmiyūn, Marmūd, and ʿĀdūd; and the sun and the moon: Abājūn, Nājūn, ʿAjramīsh, Barjalās, Sīlsūf, Bahwān, Balḥān, and Nīnādrūḥ. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, and by God; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. O God, I ask You, O Lord, in that You are living and do not die; overcoming, and are not overcome; creating, and are not created; seeing, and do not doubt; hearing, and are not uncertain; all-subduing, and are not subdued; everlasting, and are not exhausted; near, and are not far; witnessing, and are not absent; a god, and are not harmed; subduing, and do not do wrong; an eternal refuge, and are not fed; self-subsisting, and do not sleep; veiled, and are not seen; compelling, and are not oppressed; mighty, and are not to be assailed; knowing, and are not taught; strong, and do not grow weak; faithful, and do not fail; just, and do not act unfairly; rich, and do not become poor; a treasure that is not exhausted; forbearing, and do not act unjustly; inaccessible, and are not subdued; known, and are not denied; a trustee, and are not held in contempt; odd, and are not made even; single, and are not doubled; bestowing, and do not refuse; swift, and are not distracted; bountiful, and do not begrudge; mighty, and are not abased; knowing, and are not ignorant; preserving, and are not heedless; everlasting, and do not perish; known, and are not denied; answering, and do not weary; abiding, and do not wear away; one, and are not likened to any; omnipotent, and are not contended with. Thus it stands in this recension; but in others there is a second recension, which says: O God, I ask You, O Lord: O Living who does not die; creating, and are not created; self-subsisting, and do not sleep; truthful, and do not fail; just, and do not do wrong; veiled, and are not seen; inaccessible, and are not subdued; known, and are not denied; a trustee, and do not weary; swift, and are not distracted; bountiful, and do not begrudge; mighty, and are not abased; preserving, and are not heedless; everlasting, and do not perish; one, whom nothing resembles. There is no god but You, O Lord of the worlds. I ask You by Your might that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me all the spiritual beings, by the right of Your majesty and the light of Your noble face. Truly that is easy for You. I adjure you, O company of spiritual beings, by God the Mighty and by His treasured, concealed Name, that you be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need, by the right of the Lord of the lofty edifice — that you assuredly answer in that to which I summon you. So hear and obey what I have commanded you, by the right of that by which I have adjured you among the mighty names of God. Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you.

And if you wish to call upon the lord of autumn, then call upon the lord of the south. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Ṣarfiyāʾil, and your helpers Qamiyāʾil, Marḥiyāʾīl, and Ḥarmakiyāʾīl; and the four winds Qandīd, Yafʿūn, Maysūr, and Kāfūn; and the sun and the moon: Sabās, Taʿābil, Huwayfīm, Mahūlāḥ, al-Nūḥ, Mithāl, Sabā, and Badūraḥ. I ask you to descend into my presence, and to comply with all /fol. 46v./ that I have commanded you and with all that I request of you. I ask You, O God, O Light of light, O Disposer of affairs, O Knower of secrets. You are God, the King, the All-Subduing; there is no god but You, and no object of worship besides You. O God, O God, by the right of these mighty names: God, God, the High, the Mighty; God, God, the Forbearing, the Generous; God, God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting; God, God, the Single, the Eternal Refuge; God, God, who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal. I ask You by Your might, and by Your establishing Yourself upon Your Throne, that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me the lord of this day, and of the hour, and of the thāqūfa, and of the four regions. Truly You are powerful over everything, for You decree with truth and no decree is passed against You; and that they be a help to me in such-and-such. O God, O

God, You are God: there is no god but You. I have believed in You and have put my trust in You. You are God: of You stands in fear all Your creation, and to You it submits itself in humility. You are the light of the heavens. You are He who has veiled Himself, so that You are not seen and Your light is not comprehended. O God, O God, O God, You are God, the Subduer. Lofty is Your majesty! You are exalted above Your Throne, and none of Your creation can describe Your greatness. O Light of light, the people of Your heavens and the people of Your earth have been illumined by Your light. O God, O God, You are too exalted to have any associate, and too magnificent to have any opposite. O Light of light, every light is quenched before Your light. O King, and every king passes away, while You are the Abiding, the Everlasting, who neither changes nor ceases. O God, O God, O God, You are the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Have mercy upon me with a mercy whereby You extinguish from me Your wrath and Your displeasure, and whereby You grant me felicity from Yourself, and whereby You admit me into Your Garden, in which You have settled the choicest of Your creation. O God, O Most Merciful of the merciful — for I ask You that You fulfil my need, and that You make subservient to me the spiritual beings, that they may be my help in such-and-such. O God, O God, O God, O Lord of the worlds! Hasten, O Shamhūrish!

And if you are in the time of winter, then call upon the lord of the west. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. I adjure you, O Dardiyāʾīl, and your helpers Jabrīqīl, Qaṣmāʾil, and
Sūghiyāʾīl; and the winds from the earth Mujarrad, Darʿādūm, Maʿmūr, and Jarīdūm; and upon

— the sun and the moon: Jād and Jayādīm and Jālītad and Sayyīn and Lātūn and Nīshāriḥand Mudhhabāyin and Samīdrīs. I ask you to fulfil my need, by the right of that by which I speak over you. O God, I ask You by Your might, O Light of lights, O Knower of secrets! You are the King, the Compeller, the Mighty, the All-Subduing. To You belong praise, laudation, glory, and bounties. I have believed in You; there is no god but You. I ask You: O God, O Lord, O al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Malik (the King), O al-Muḥīṭ (the All-Encompassing), O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-Qadīr (the All-Powerful), O al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), O al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), O al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing), O al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), O al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), O al-Kāfī (the Sufficient), O al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), O al-Shākir (the Thankful), O Ilāh (God), O al-Wāḥid (the One), O al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), O al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), O al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), O al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Walī (the Protecting Friend), O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), O al-Qāʾim (the Upholder), O al-Sarīʿ (the Swift), O al-Raqīb (the Watcher), /fol. 47r./ O al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), O al-Shahīd (the Witness), O al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner), O al-Mughīth (the Succourer), O al-Wakīl (the Trustee), O al-Fāṭir (the Originator), O al-Qāhir (the Subduer), O al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), O al-Qādir (the Powerful), O al-Khabīr (the All-Aware), O al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), O al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), O excellent Patron and excellent Helper, O al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), O al-Qarīb (the Near), O al-Mujīb (the Answerer), O al-Qawī (the Strong), O al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), O al-Wadūd (the Loving), O Faʿʿāl li-mā yurīd (Doer of whatsoever He wills), O al-Kabīr (the Great), O al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), O al-Mannān (the Bounteous), O al-Khallāq (the Creator of all), O al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), O al-Wārith (the Inheritor), O al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Ḥaqq (the Truth),

O al-Mubīn (the Evident), O al-Nūr (the Light), O al-Hādī (the Guide), O al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), O al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), O al-Ghāfir (the Forgiver), O al-Qābil (the Accepter), O Dhū al-baṭsh al-shadīd (Possessor of the mighty assault), O Dhū al-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty), O al-Razzāq (the Provider), O Dhū al-quwwa al-matīn (Possessor of strength, the Firm), O al-Barr (the Benign), O al-Malīk (the Sovereign), O al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), O al-Bāqī (the Abiding), O Dhū al-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O al-Awwal (the First), O al-Ākhir (the Last), O al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), O al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), O al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), O al-Salām (the Peace), O al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), O al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Jabbār (the Compeller), O al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), O al-Khāliq (the Creator), O al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), O al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper), O al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Aḥad (the

Unique), O al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), O You who have not begotten and have not been begotten, and to whom none is equal, O God, O God, O God! There is no god but You. I ask You, O Lord, by the right that these names have with You and by the might they possess in Your sight, that You make subservient to me the spiritual being of the lord of the day, and of this hour, and of this seasonal quarter (thāqūfa), and of the four regions — truly You are powerful over all things. I adjure you, O spiritual beings, that you be a help to me in the fulfilling of my need. Answer, O Khaylahūn, and rend the veil that is between me and you, by Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, both of you, obediently or under compulsion! They said: We have come obedient (Q 41:11).
The four seasonal quarters (thawāqīf) are now complete, together with their names; and in God lies success. And they have a signet proper to them.

As for His name al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, these are two majestic, mighty names, and the remembrance (dhikr) by means of them is mighty and noble. It profits those in dire straits and is a security for those who fear. Whoever engraves them on a Friday, in the last hour of the day, upon a signet-ring, and seals with it, will never see anything he finds hateful. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of them is treated with gentle kindness in all matters. al-Raḥmān is derived from raḥma (mercy), and al-Raḥīm likewise. And it is related that God, exalted is He, says concerning the womb (al-raḥim): ((I am al-Raḥmān, and it is the womb (al-raḥim); whoever joins it, I join him, and whoever severs it, I sever him.)) And if you look and ascertain, you will find al-Raḥmān and al-Raḥīm gathered together in Alif-Lām-Mīm and Alif-Lām-Rāʾ and the seven Ḥawāmīm. And God knows best.

And His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān: whoever writes it eight times in a clean vessel, with the Moon in its exaltation, and washes it off with rainwater, and one who has hardness in his heart drinks of it — that [hardness] departs from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And it has a square of four by four: if it is written in water and the one afflicted with burning fever is given to drink of it, it departs from him, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And this is its form, as you see.

His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥīm: whoever sets it down, with the Moon in its exaltation, is secure from the calamities of time; and whoever sets it in a signet-ring of silver and seals with it is safe from all calamities and afflictions, and from the evil of all hateful things. And this is its form.

His name, exalted is He, al-Malik (the King): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — the tyrants (al-farāʿina) become compliant to him, for his protection and for the fulfilling of his need. His name, exalted is He, al-Salām (the Peace): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, keeps him safe from all calamities; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it overcomes him, and then takes hold of a snake or a scorpion, it does not harm him. And it has a square of four by four: if the king carries it with him in war, he is kept safe from the assaults of calamities. And this is the form of its square, as you see.

His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it 132 times, God, exalted is He, grants him security from the evil of the plague. His name, exalted is He, al-Muhaymin (the Overseer): whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring five times, with the Moon in its exaltation, and seals with it, is protected from /fol. 48r./ the evil of the satans of humankind and of the jinn. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has therein a munition against the enemies of God. His name, exalted is He, al-Jabbār (the Compeller): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes awe-inspiring in the sight of all people. His name, exalted is He, al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his word takes effect among the secondary causes. His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Khāliq (the Creator): whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring of silver, with the ascendant one of the signs of the fiery triplicity (al-muthallathāt al-nāriyya), and seals with it, and then has intercourse with his wife — she conceives by him, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāriʾ (the Maker): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon wondrous secrets and subtle traces. His name, exalted is He, al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — the spiritual forms descend upon him within the corporeal forms. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved in wars from the onslaughts of [hostile] eyes. His name, exalted is He, al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it subdues his carnal appetites. His name, exalted is He, al-Wahhāb (the Bestower): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it asks God, exalted is He, for nothing but that He gives it to him. His name, exalted is He, al-Razzāq (the Provider): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes the means easy for him and provides for him whence he does not reckon. His name, exalted is He, al-Fattāḥ (the Opener): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God opens for him the avenues of good things, outwardly and inwardly. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom. His name, exalted is He, al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him awe-inspiring presence among all the worlds. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his inmost secret is expanded. His name, exalted is He, al-Khāfiḍ (the Abaser): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and calls down [imprecation] upon a wrongdoer is answered, if he remembers it under the [requisite] conditions. His name, exalted is He, al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, raises his standing and elevates his degree. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him might in this world and in the hereafter. His name, exalted is He, al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, abases the tyrants before him. His name, exalted is He, al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has his supplication answered. His name, exalted is He, al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and writes it a hundred times upon a signet-ring of glass, washes it off with rainwater, and drinks it at the breaking of the fast — his mind grows keen and his understanding strong. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥakam (the Judge): it is fit for [obtaining] the effectiveness of one's word before rulers. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAdl (the Just): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, inspires him in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Laṭīf (the Subtle): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it while an illness presses hard upon him, God, exalted is He, makes deliverance from that easy for him. His name, exalted is He, al-Khabīr (the All-Aware): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, engraves it upon a gemstone in the first hour of Friday, and places it upon his mouth — the distress of thirst does not reach him; and if he puts it into a water-jug and drinks from it, God, exalted is He, hastens for him the quenching of thirst, and he does not seek water after that. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it /fol. 48v./ is safe from agitation when hardships descend. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes great in the eyes of people. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving): God, exalted is He, guards him from the evil of what he fears and is wary of. His name, exalted is He, al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, elevates his standing. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is preserved from the evil of the evildoers in all his movements and his stillnesses. His name, exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it feels no pang of hunger. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has his need fulfilled. His name, exalted is He, al-Jalīl (the Majestic): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it finds increase in all his states and his sayings. His name, exalted is He, al-Karīm (the Generous): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one whose invocation is answered. His name, exalted is He, al-Mujīb (the Answerer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it falls into no hardship but that he finds a way out of it. His name, exalted is He, al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, causes the springs of wisdom to burst forth from his heart upon his tongue. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥakīm (the Wise): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes beloved among people, in the sight of everyone. His name, exalted is He, al-Wadūd (the Loving): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, being a king — God, exalted is He, enlarges his kingdom. His name, exalted is He, al-Majīd (the All-Glorious): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is impelled toward every good. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him witness watchful vigilance (murāqaba) in his spiritual retreat (khalwa) and in all his affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Shahīd (the Witness): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes his word subduing and prevailing. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥaqq (the Truth): it has a square of five by five. Whoever engraves it upon a stone of marble, with the ascendant Scorpio (al-ʿAqrab), and places it in a house — there remains in it no snake and no scorpion but that it goes out from it, and likewise the noxious creatures, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

His name, exalted is He, al-Qawī (the Strong): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — his spirit is strengthened and his love endures. His name, exalted is He, al-Matīn (the Firm): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is safe from weakness of strength. His name, exalted is He, al-Walī (the Protecting Friend): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — God takes charge of him and gives him charge. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and writes it upon a signet-ring according to its number

— and washes it off with water and gives it to drink to one who has an illness, God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. His name, exalted is He, al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is secured from evil deeds. His name, exalted is He, al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator): it is suitable for whoever wishes to make a beginning in some affair among affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʿīd (the Restorer): when it is set in a square with the ascendant one of the movable signs (al-burūj al-munqaliba), and it is hung up in the path of the wind, and the person keeps on reciting the Name the whole night long over a runaway slave or a traveller, he returns to the place from which he went out, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart with the light of gnosis. His name, exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, puts to death whatever stirs in him of his dark desires. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḥayy (the Living): whoever writes it 120 times upon the door of a house, with Venus in her exaltation — then the one dwelling in it is preserved from melancholic afflictions and from evil /fol. 49r./ afflictions, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it finds within his inmost being ample sciences and gnoses of the divine oneness. His name, exalted is He, al-Wājid (the

Finder): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God brings into being in his heart faith and pious reverence. His name, exalted is He, al-Mājid (the Glorious): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, raises his standing high, and he flees from the world. His name, exalted is He, al-Wāḥid (the One): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it grows estranged from multiplicity. His name, exalted is He, al-Aḥad (the Unique): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes singular in the sciences. His name, exalted is He, al-Fard (the Sole): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, no other enters in upon him, and he feels no pang of hunger at all. His name, exalted is He, al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him a spiritual power and a gnostic strength. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes easy for him all circumstances. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqaddim (the Advancer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God bestows upon him free disposal (taṣarruf) in the world of secondary causes. His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer): a secret whose door is locked and whose veil-covering is let down. His name, exalted is He, al-Awwal (the First): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one who presses onward toward good things. His name, exalted is He, al-Ākhir (the Last): a well-guarded secret, and its knowledge is concealed. His name, exalted is He, al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes him privy to what is right and to the hidden aspects of affairs. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāṭin (the Hidden): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — he does not come to anyone but that he answers him and fulfils his need. His name, exalted is He, al-Wālī (the Governor): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes awe-inspiring in the sight of everyone. His name, exalted is He, al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him a luminous might and an awe befitting the Eternal Refuge (ṣamadāniyya). His name, exalted is He, al-Barr (the Benign): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness. And it has a square of four by four: whoever draws it upon his palm and calls upon God by it — He turns to him in relenting. His name, exalted is He, al-Muntaqim (the Avenger): whoever writes it in a vessel, washes it off with rainwater, and gives it to drink to one who has a love for the drinking of wine — he comes to loathe it. His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner): whoever fears a punishment from a king or from another, and remembers it according to its number, is secured from what he fears. His name, exalted is He, al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God is ever-gentle with him, and no tyrant's gaze falls upon him but that [God] turns his heart toward him. His name, exalted is He, Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it while he is seeking a kingdom, God, exalted is He, grants it to him. His name, exalted is He, Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it asks God, exalted is

He, for nothing but He gives it to him. His name, exalted is He, al-Muqsiṭ (the Equitable): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is characterized by [spiritual] poverty (faqr) and justice in all his states. His name, exalted is He, al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it when a slave of his has run away or a stray of his has gone missing, God restores to him that stray, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Mughnī (the Enricher): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the means of wealth and the means of this world grow abundant for him, and its provisions become ample for him; and whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself, his trade turns a profit. His name, exalted is He, al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient): whoever multiplies > /fol. 49v./ His name, exalted is He, al-Māniʿ (the Withholder): whoever multiplies < the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him independent of created beings. His name, exalted is He, al-Māniʿ (the Withholder): whoever writes it upon the wall of a city, running all around it, in 161 places, while the preacher is upon the pulpit on Friday — God, exalted is He, guards it from the assaults of the wicked. Some of the sages set it upon a wall on the citadel of Mārdīn, and no enemy was able to take it, by the leave of God, exalted is He. His name, exalted is He, al-Ḍārr (the Bringer of Harm): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and then asks God, exalted is He, for a need [that requires] the harming of a wrongdoer, sees in the sea of its operative deployment a means, and in the land of its operative deployment a wonder. His name, exalted is He, al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit): in it is a healing for every sick man and a restoration to health for every poor wretch. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it in a state of harm, God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. And if he be one possessed of a truthful [spiritual] state, and he persists in its remembrance until some of its worlds come into accord with him, he does not pass his hand over one who has been harmed but that God wipes away his harm. And so it is that whoever sets it in a square upon a signet-ring of silver, with the Moon in its exaltation — no one afflicted with an illness is sealed with it but that God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. Do you not see that it points to His name, exalted is He, Muʿāfī (the Restorer to Health), and that the names of its letters point to two majestic names, namely Ilāh (God) [readingfor the edition's]and Shāfī (the Healer)? And this is its form, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

His name, exalted is He, al-Nūr (the Light): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, illumines his heart. And when His name, exalted is He, al-Nāfiʿ is joined to it, it is a healing for every sickness and pain that arises from coldness. And when the Name is set in the square of the figure and water is poured over it, the one who suffers from coldness derives from it a far-reaching and manifest benefit; and it is preferable that the water be cast [upon it]. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best what is right. And this is the form of the square, as you see. [Wafq: cells as in the source — ] His name al-Hādī (the Guide) is a majestic name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the light of his heart increases and God guides [Fig. 26] his innermost secrets to knowledge of Him. And whoever is hard pressed by some affair among the affairs of this world, outward or inward, let him perform the ablution and pray two rakʿas with the Throne Verse and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, and let him make remembrance until his breath is cut off; then he is guided to what he seeks. His name, exalted is He, al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not cease to be an originator of the divine sciences and the secrets of religion. [His name al-Wārith (the Inheritor)]: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and desires to inherit from one of his kinsmen or of his family, God, exalted is He, gives him to inherit what he seeks. His name, exalted is He, al-Bāqī (the Abiding): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, his final outcome is praised in all /fol. 50r./ his movements and his stillnesses. His name, exalted is He, al-Ṣabūr (the Patient): whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him steadfastness in hardships, in weighty affairs, and in strange calamities, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And God, exalted is He, knows best.
Chapter 9 (al-bāb al-tāsiʿ): On the occult properties of the openings of the firmly established (muḥkamāt) suras of the Qurʾān and of the clear verses

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — that among the occult properties of the letters of the alphabet that stand at the openings of the suras, and of the letters of the alphabet in their entirety, and of what attaches to them of their effects in the matters of operative deployment (taṣrīf), is what certain of the scholars — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — said concerning His saying, exalted is He, Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād (Q 7:1): its meaning is "I am God, I decide." And al-Ḥasan said: the alif is the alif of pre-eternity (azal); the lām is the lām of post-eternity (abad); the mīm is "from Him unto Him"; and the ṣād is the joining of whoever joins himself to Him and the severance of whoever severs himself from Him. Yet in reality there is neither joining nor severance. These expressions run according to the [spiritual] states, and the mines of the Real are guarded from utterances and expressions. Every name among the names of God, exalted is He, brings you to a rank among the ranks; but His name Allāh, exalted is

He, brings you to all the ranks, for it is the name of the Essence qualified by the holy attributes, and all the names go back to it. And whoever is made privy to its meaning is made privy to the meanings of the hidden names, which are the individual letters (al-ḥurūf al-mufrada). So understand the indications, and do not halt at the expressions — you will be among those possessed of certainty. And the first of the hidden names is Huwa (He), a name composed of two letters; and it is the locus set for the divine indication (al-ishāra al-ulūhiyya), to which the hidden and the manifest names all return.

Fāʾida (a useful point). When God, exalted is He, created the letters, He appointed for them the ranks of the secret in Adam — peace be upon him — and did not lodge it in the angels. So the letters ran upon the tongue of Adam — peace be upon him — in the diverse modes of running and in the kinds of languages. And God, exalted is He, set the form of all the letters within the heart as a spiritual reality, and it is that which appears in the utterance of the soul and in corporeal script. So there are letters in the breast, letters upon the tongue, and letters in the bodily [members]. To that points His saying, exalted is He: Ṣād. By the Qurʾān, possessor of the Remembrance (Q 38:1); Qāf. By the majestic Qurʾān (Q 50:1); Nūn. By the Pen and what they set down in lines (Q 68:1). And the letters point to the verses of the Book, a reminder for those possessed of understanding. Every letter has three stations, according to the three vowels: the fatḥ (a), the ḍamm (u), and the khafḍ (i). And the letters of prolongation and softness (ḥurūf al-madd wa-l-līn) [derive] from them, after the likeness of the elements: each letter is the counterpart of an element. The worlds are three: of the visible kingdom (mulkī), of the Dominion (malakūtī), and of the Omnipotence (jabarūtī); and each one of the three is corporeal, psychic, and spiritual — so they are nine. The numbers are nine, the celestial spheres are nine, and the natures and the senses are nine. So the correspondence became manifest. Search out, then, the secrets of number and of the letters, and you will light through them upon sublime gnoses in [their] conjunctions and separations, according to what is required by the All-Mercifulness (raḥmāniyya) and the Compassionateness (raḥīmiyya) /fol. 50v./ of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate"; for it is from "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" that the cosmos takes its nourishment, and eats and drinks. So consider the suras of the Qurʾān: you will find them to arise from the multiplication of six by nineteen, the result being sixty and fifty-four. For the sixty added to the fifty is one hundred and ten, and with the four the total came to one hundred and fourteen, the number of the suras of the Qurʾān. And the six is the perfect number, corresponding to the number of the days in which God, exalted is He, created the heavens and the earth and what is between them. And these three are divided out into nineteen: the heavens are nine, together with the Throne and the Footstool; and the earth is ten, [with] the elements and what is composed of them — mineral, plant, animal, jinn, and angels. And the letters that are the openings of the suras are arranged in five ranks: single, twofold, threefold, fourfold, and fivefold. As for their sum, it is seventy-eight, which the number of fourteen letters comprises after the removal of what is repeated.

Faṣl. The letters are of two divisions: dotted and undotted. The dotted is of the visible kingdom (mulkī), and the undotted is of the Dominion (malakūtī). Then the mulkī is of two divisions: dotted with two and dotted with three. Those dotted with three are the shīn ()and the thāʾ (:)the shīn indicates the assemblage that is dispersed, and the thāʾ indicates the assemblage that is gathered. Those dotted with two are the tāʾ ()and the yāʾ (:)the yāʾ is a manifestation in the kingdom of His felicity (yumn), and the tāʾ appeared in the Dominion. Those dotted with one are the qāf ()and the nūn (): the qāf appeared in everything whose place of manifestation is from Him, as in al-Qādir (the Powerful) and al-qalam (the pen); and the nūn appeared in everything that makes manifest, and everything that makes manifest encompasses that which is made manifest by it — as the light of the sun, and instruments, and the nūn of the pen, and the ink of the book whereby the secret of its matter is made manifest. And the thāʾ likewise is a gathering by which the subsistence of everything comes about, for it is everything through which there is subsistence. And the shīn likewise is an announcement of evil, as it is in al-sharr (evil). And the shīn is the fruit of what lies between the two relations, for every growing offspring, as in al-tamr (dates) and al-turāb (earth). And the shīn is the manifestation of complete differentiation in outward beauty, and in all [of these]: al-shanaʾān (hatred) and al-shatāt (dispersion) and al-shabāb (youth) — which is a branch of madness — and al-ashghāl (preoccupations); or else it is doubled with what is congruent to it among the letters, as in al-ʿishq (passionate love), al-shaʿaf (ardent love), al-shighār (exchange-marriage), al-ghishāwa (the covering film), al-ghashm (oppressive wrongdoing), and the like of that. And the nūn — its meaning is a manifester that makes clear, as the light of sense-perception, the light of the sun, the light of knowledge, and the ink of books whereby their secrets are made manifest; and the water of the rain-cloud (al-muzn), which brings to light the foremost of creation — that the position of the nūn in His word might be preserved. The essences have enfolded it: their outward, their inward, and what lies between the two. And likewise it is distinguished in its form by three marks, as is the case with the name that gives notice of the thing it names, and with the journey that gives notice of the characters of men, and the like of that.

And al-Ḥasan — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: In the Qurʾān is the knowledge of everything; and the knowledge of the Qurʾān is in the letters that stand at the openings of the suras; and the knowledge of the letters is in lām-alif; and the knowledge of lām-alif is in the alif; and the knowledge of the alif is in the point; and the knowledge of the point is in the primordial gnosis; and the knowledge of the primordial gnosis is in pre-eternity; and the knowledge of pre-eternity is in the [divine] volitions; and the knowledge of the volitions is in the unseen of the Ipseity (al-huwiyya); and the knowledge of the unseen of the Ipseity is in the like of whom there is nothing (Q 42:11).

And it is said concerning Yā-Sīn (Q 36:1) that it is a name among the names of God, exalted is He, like the rest of the letters of the alphabet that occur at the openings of the suras. And these are the luminous letters, fourteen letters, unrepeated, and they are these:(alif), (ḥāʾ), (rāʾ),(ṭāʾ),(kāf),(lām),(mīm), (nūn),(ṣād),(ʿayn), (qāf),(sīn),(hāʾ),(yāʾ). And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he used to say: The openings of the suras are taken from the names of God, exalted is He.

And Abū l-ʿĀliya said: There is not a letter among them but that it is the key to a name among the names /fol. 51r./ of God, exalted is He. So the alif is from Ilāh (God); the lām from Laṭīf (the Subtle); the mīm from Malik (the King); the ṣād from Ṣādiq (the Truthful); the rāʾ from Rabb (the Lord); the kāf from Kāfī (the Sufficient); the hāʾ from Hādī (the Guide); the yāʾ from ʿAlīm (the Knowing); the ʿayn from ʿĀlim (the Knower); the ṭāʾ from Ṭayyib (the Good); the sīn from Samīʿ (the All-Hearing); the ḥāʾ from Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy); the qāf from Qadīr (the Powerful); and the nūn from Nūr (the Light). And this is their form, according as Abū l-ʿĀliya arranged them:

He made the middle letter a letter of indication — namely the hāʾ and the yāʾ — and he placed first the letters of Alif-Lām-Mīm, Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād, Alif-Lām-Rāʾ, Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, and Ṭā-Sīn; and the ḥāʾ from Ḥā-Mīm; and the qāf from Qāf. By the majestic Qurʾān (Q 50:1); and the nūn from Nūn. By the Pen (Q 68:1).
And Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — said concerning the meaning of Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1): its meaning is

"I am God, I know"; and Alif-Lām-Rāʾ (Q 10:1): "I am God, I see." So the alif conveys "I" (anā); the lām conveys the name Allāh; the mīm conveys "I know" (aʿlam); and the rāʾ conveys "I see" (arā). And this is their order: Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1), Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād (Q 7:1), Alif-Lām-Rāʾ (Q 10:1), Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ (Q 13:1), Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ṭā-Hā (Q 20:1), Ṭā-Sīn (Q 27:1), Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm (Q 26:1), Yā-Sīn (Q 36:1), [Ṣād](Q 38:1), Ḥā-Mīm (Q 40:1), ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:2), Qāf (Q 50:1), Nūn (Q 68:1). Then what was repeated among them fell away, and there remained fourteen letters, unrepeated; for their letters are established in these fourteen suras, and the fourteen luminous letters came forth from these fourteen suras — the ones whose mention has preceded — and it is to them that Abū l-ʿĀliya pointed. Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: The openings (fawātiḥ) of the suras — they are the Greatest Name of God.

Fāʾida. The names in their entirety are the number of the degrees of the Garden. From them knowledge was separated out, and to them it returns; and from them the existent things appeared. So the existent things are a sign pointing to the Most Beautiful Names. The names have coursed through them as the spirits course through bodies, and have taken within them the place that the Command holds in relation to creation. So there is no existent thing, minute or great, high or low, but that the names of God, exalted is He, encompass it, in entity and in meaning. And what the name of Divinity (al-ulūhiyya) requires is comprehensive of the meanings of all the [other] names; and the names in their entirety expound its meaning and give expression to it. So it is the greatest of the manifest names in this respect. The alif, then, is an upright letter: from it the letters arose, from it they draw their supply, and it is their matter; so it is the counterpart of the Intellect, the Pen, the Throne, and the Tablet. Next after it comes the lām, which is the letter that joins the highest to the lowest, and its counterpart is the Tablet, the Footstool, and the Soul. And next after the lām comes the mīm, which is the letter that indicates completion, and its counterpart is the body. For the Intellect is the first created thing, and the body is the terminus of created things. And all the [other] meanings of the letters are contained within the alif; and in the alif is the meaning of gathering and of summary comprehension, just as the letters are summarily comprehended in the Pen. So understand the meaning of summary comprehension and of mutual interpenetration, and there will gleam forth for you precious spiritual secrets, the sciences of which reach [only] to inward finding (wijdān). So understand. Faṣl. Know that the friends of God (awliyāʾ) — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — spoke concerning the science of the letters and of the names out of radiant lights that were made to flow upon them from the wellspring of [divine] election, upon the attainment of certainty in their hearts and of sincerity. So they were singled out, in the science of the names, above all others by three things. The first is that they were given to understand, of the meanings of the ninety-nine, by [divine] confirming support /fol. 51v./ and by inspiration, what others did not know by speculation and demonstration. The second is that they knew hidden names beyond these ninety-nine. The third is that they were singled out by being made privy to the Greatest Name of God. As for the prophets — peace be upon them — they knew of the meanings of the ninety-nine names, by the light of revelation, what the friends of God did not know by inspiration; and likewise they knew of the sciences of the hidden names and of the knowledge of the Greatest Name of God. And every name among these names — none knows it as it truly is save He who has named Himself by it and is qualified by its meaning, and that is God alone. And beyond all these names that God, exalted is He, has taught to His prophets and His friends —

— that behind which God, exalted is He, has veiled Himself in the world of the unseen: He has made none privy to it, neither a prophet sent [as messenger] nor an angel brought near. They said: The first thing with which God, exalted is He, singles out the servant, when He wills to take him under His patronage and to teach him the God-given science (al-ʿilm al-ladunnī) so that he becomes a knowing friend of God (walī), is that He should single him out, from the knowledge of the ninety-nine names, by [certain] special properties (khaṣāʾiṣ), so that there is opened to him from them, of knowledge, what is not opened to the [ordinary] scholar by the path of speculative reasoning. Then He raises him to the knowledge of the hidden names, the first of which is Huwa (He) — a name compounded of two letters, a locus for the divine indication to which the names, hidden and manifest, revert in their entirety, just as the manifest names reverted to the name Allāh, exalted is He. And after his knowledge of that, he learns the hidden names, which are the single letters, namely the fourteen letters that occur in the Qurʾān in the luminous openings of the suras, whose mention has already been made. And after he has understood them, God, exalted is He, bestows upon him the Greatest Name — that by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. And the Greatest Name is taken only from al-Khaḍir — peace be upon him — according to the most widespread of the reports. Yet the friend of God may also receive it by inspiration, which is cast into his inmost being (rawʿ) when the breeze of mercy blows upon the servant. And the manner of its being received among the friends of God varies; the book would grow long with the exposition of it. And thereupon the earth is folded up for him, and he walks upon water, and he ascends through the air, and entities are transmuted for him, and other things besides among the charismatic marvels (karāmāt) with which the friends of God have been specially favoured. And all this is not a knowledge [drawn] from written pages; rather it is a special gift between a man and his Lord: whomever God, exalted is He, makes privy to it, He has taught it to him. And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((All existence stands only by the names of God, exalted is He, the hidden and the manifest, the sanctified; and the alphabetic hidden names of God, exalted is He, are the root of everything among the affairs of this world and the next. They are the treasury of His secret and the concealed store of His knowledge; from them branched forth all the names of God, exalted is He; and they are those by which He decreed all affairs and which He deposited in the Mother of the Book.)) And Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — was asked about Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), and he said to the questioner: Were I to inform you of its interpretation, you would walk upon the water without your two feet being submerged.

And Sahl b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: /fol. 52r./ A man came to Ibrāhīm b. Adham and said to him: What do you say concerning Yā-Sīn (Q 36:1)? He said: Truly, in Yā-Sīnthere is a name — whoever knows it and calls upon God, exalted is He, by it is answered, be he righteous or dissolute; and when it is called upon for some matter, it is his own special possession. And it will come hereafter, if God, exalted is He, wills, in this book of ours.

Faṣl. And each letter of these fourteen letters that are in the openings of the suras has a meaning and a secret; when God, exalted is He, makes the servant privy to it, he attains a charismatic marvel from His own presence, or else he meets al-Khaḍir — peace be upon him. And it is soundly established in the hadith, from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said to his Companions: ((When you meet the enemy tomorrow, let your watchword be Ḥā-Mīm: they shall not be given victory.)) And Ḥā-Mīm (Q 40:1) is among the hidden, treasured names of God, exalted is He. Whoever attaches himself to its light, God, exalted is He, rends for him the customary order of things, and he attains benefits from its secrets. And Sahl b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: The noblest of all the letters are the nine letters; from their light the letters were clothed in beauty and splendour. And they are these: And the manifest bodies point to them and to their nobility, and they are the seven heavens, the Footstool, and the Throne; and these are the nine corporealized [realities] to which God, exalted is He, alluded in the Qurʾān in His words, exalted is He: Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1), Alif-Lām-Mīm-Ṣād (Q 7:1), Alif-Lām-Rāʾ (Q 10:1), Qāf (Q 50:1), Nūn (Q 68:1), Ḥā-Mīm (Q 40:1), ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:2), Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ṭā-Sīn (Q 27:1). And they are the fourteen letters. And it is said that they are the Greatest Name, the manifest and the hidden. And that which the masters among the people of realization, and the leading scholars among the people of the Law and of the Reality, have intimated is that the Greatest Name is Allāh among the manifest names, and consensus has all but been concluded upon it.

And the explanation of this Greatest Name is that it brings things forth from nonexistence into existence. The alif in it is an indication of the Noble Essence; and the hāʾ is a letter of encompassment, [fitted] for the reception of the secret, and it is the secret of the breast, since the breast is the secret of knowledge, in sum and in detail. And through it was the favour conferred upon the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in the words of the Real, exalted is He: Did We not expand your breast for you, and lift from you your burden?(Q 94:1–2). So the hāʾ is the secret of the expansion of the breast.

And since the alif is too exalted to be described by motion or by rest — on account of its separateness in the primordial things, and since to it belongs the terminus of all ends, so it is in the last [state]; for motion is bound up with the four aspects, ḍamm, naṣb, khafḍ, and sukūn, by way of a kind of determination, whereas it stands in no need of determination — it brought forth the first lām at rest, out of its own relation; then [the first lām] took on motion from the relation of what joined to it of the second lām, so as to receive the secret of its rest through motion. And the hāʾ receives it with a secret from the secret of the alif's rest, for as long as its powers endure; and the second lām receives that secret, and the second lām brings it forth, and it takes on motion from the relation of what joined to it of the second lām, by the secret of motion — for the second lām is its reality — and the second lām transmits it by the secret of its elevation. [Such is] its encompassment; and there are gathered in it the secret of motion and the secret of rest; and for this reason it was the hidden of the hidden, as God, exalted is He, said: He is God (Q 59:22), He is the Living (Q 40:65).

So the hāʾ is the secret of the expansion of the breast. /fol. 52v./ And the alif is the indication of the Essence; and the first lām is for the covenantal reference (al-ʿahd al-mīthāqī), by virtue of the secret of the alif's mediation contained in it. Then the second lām is for the reference of the cosmic regions (al-ʿahd al-quṭrī), by virtue of the secret of the alif contained in it. Then the second lām is for the compact of faith on the day of this world, for the acceptance of the obligation imposed by the Law, by virtue of the secret of the alif's mediation contained in it. Then the hāʾ is for the completion of the matter on the day of the last arising, for the gathering of the first and the last. So by this lordly wisdom there revolved a circle of fourteen letters, whose beginning is like its end and whose end is like its beginning, because the alif both precedes it and comes after it. The demonstration of that is that the alifs and the lāms are four; you multiply them by three, and it comes to twelve; and the hāʾ has a share of two; the total is fourteen, thus spread out. And they are these:— as he said, God bless him and grant him peace: ((He is the Manifest: there is none above Him; and He is the Hidden: there is none below Him.)) And since it is composed of fourteen letters, the seven heavens and the seven earths, and what is within them and what is between them of kingdom (mulk) and dominion (malakūt), subsist by a secret from among the secrets of the name of God, majestic is His remembrance. Thus in every atom of the atoms of the world, and in what is lesser than it, there is a secret from among the secrets of the name of God, exalted is He; and by that secret it understands from Him and bears witness to Him with [the confession of] the divine oneness. God, exalted is He, said to His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace: Do you know any namesake for Him?(Q 19:65). And He said, exalted is He: Say: "God!" Then leave them (Q 6:91).

And the imām, the gnostic of God, exalted is He, the erudite Fakhr al-Dīn al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, sanctify his spirit — said, in the sacred precinct of Mecca, in the year six hundred and seventy: Whoever knows God, exalted is He, by the name that exerts its efficacious influence upon his state and his station has come to know the

Greatest Name that is proper to him — just as He was Arḥam al-Rāḥimīn (the Most Merciful of the merciful) for Job — peace be upon him — when he said: Affliction has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful (Q 21:83); and when He was al-Wahhāb (the Bestower) for Solomon — peace be upon him — when he said: My Lord, forgive me, and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not befit anyone after me; truly You are the Bestower (Q 38:35); and just as He was Khayr al-Wārithīn (the Best of inheritors) for Zechariah — peace be upon him — when he said: My Lord, leave me not solitary, and You are the Best of inheritors (Q 21:89). So God, exalted is He, granted him John — peace be upon him — and granted Solomon a mighty kingdom, and restored Job to health from his affliction. So whoever knows the name that corresponds to his need and asks God, exalted is He, by it — He answers him and brings him to his desire.

And it was the practice of certain masters that, when a disciple came in upon him seeking the way of wayfaring (sulūk), he would seat him before himself and recite over him the ninety-nine names, while he looked upon his face as he uttered the names; and thereby the name suited to the disciple would become clear to the master, and he would command him to keep constantly to it, until through it a door of mercy would be opened to him from the name whose remembrance he had commanded him — for his name is the odd one (al-witr) within it, and by it the efficacious influence occurs in every person. And this is his aim.

And the knowledge of the Greatest Name of God is among the noblest of the sciences. The Greatest Name is a well-guarded pearl, kept safe from those who are not its people; it lies hidden among the most precious of treasures and stored up for the [secret] hoards. Over it have been pitched the pavilions of Might; before it has been let down the veil of Awe; around it has been extended the protected preserve of the Dominion (malakūt); and about it has been made to revolve the sacred precinct of the Omnipotence (jabarūt). So I set forth for it a similitude: the difficult questions of religion, which none attain /fol. 53r./ save the stalwarts among the divinely supported scholars. And among its grandeur, by which it is expounded, among the kinds of its nobility and its honour, is that those descriptions that are lofty and those noble epithets should be sent forth for it, and that there should be joined to it praiseworthy litanies of remembrance and glorious eulogies; and though their kinds differ, yet in declaring [God] transcendent and holy lies their gathering. And enough of good for you is the hearing of them, according to what the transmitted reports have brought concerning that, so that it may be the more magnificent in its remembrance, and greater for whoever hears it or recites it, and more precious to whoever repeats it and seeks it out.
