[Wafq: reproduced as a figure in the source — ]

And this is the supplication of the noble verse. You say: O God, You are the True King; there is no god but You — the One, the Unique, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the King, the Witness, the Bountiful, the Sustainer of everything, the Singular, the Eternal, the Preserver, the Exalted, the Magnificent. Grant me an awe drawn from Your majesty, by which You may veil harms from me and by which I may acquire benefits. And by the secret with which Adam — peace be upon him — used to call upon You, and by Your having taught him the names, all of them: pour out upon me, O God, of Your bounties, what shall stand between me and the wrongdoing folk. You are my Master and I am Your servant, and "He" is said of none but You, O God. O Living One, Your life — by it life is spread abroad and shines resplendent in every living thing. O Living One, give me life, a goodly life in which no hateful thing shall ever befall. O Living, O Self-Subsisting (Yā Ḥayy Yā Qayyūm), all the worlds stand upright by Your subduing might. Here am I, before the hands of Your self-subsistence, upon the carpet of fear, wrapped in the mantle of shame, veiled with hope, casting upon my back the load of ill-doing, leaning upon the expectation that You have said — and Your word is the truth — Call upon Me, and I will answer you (Q 40:60). I seek none but You, being certain that none shall deliver me from what I am in save You, showing forth the outward of sincerity from Your self-subsistence. O Subduer, subdue whoever desires my subduing, with a subduing that denies him the disposal of his own self, as a bounty from You to me. O You whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes: whoever intends evil against me, veil me from him, and deny him slumber and sleep, and straiten the earth upon him for all its breadth; let no ease gladden him, but rather let adversity harm him; and occupy him with the evil of the evildoers. And what is hidden is not hidden from You. O God, O God, O God! O Owner of the heavens and the earth, and of what is in them and what is between them! Do not give me over, O God, into the possession of my enemies, nor of anyone who would harm me thereby. I am a wronged servant, Your servant, the poor, the weak. Pour out, O God, and let down over me from Your bounties a covering by which I may enter, together with Your friends, upon the carpet of Your holiness and Your intimacy. O You with whom none intercedes save by His leave: I have sought intercession by my spirit upon the tongue of the prophets — blessings and peace be upon them — and that He grant me protection in all hateful things. O You whose Throne-seat has encompassed the heavens and the earth, and the guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255): O God, turn away from me what grieves me of wrong and of vicissitudes, and mend my heart with a victory from You, O Mender of broken hearts. And blend the blending with joy in my particularity and in my universality. O Strong One, strengthen my heart after weakness, and raise over my head a banner to which the world shall bear witness, that I am wronged. Grant me, O God, the reward of the wronged. Indeed You know what we do not know. O Rich One, repel from me the poverty that holds me back. O God, O God, O God! O Exalted One, O Magnificent One, You are exalted with a great exaltation. And magnify me with Your mighty greatness, and deliver me from the wrongdoing folk, and sustain me with Your angels brought near, and make subservient to me the hearts of all Your servants, by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful. And the guarding of them does not weary /fol. 94v./ Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). O God, I ask You, O

God, O Ḥaqq (the Real), O Mubīn (the Manifest), O Ḥayy (the Living): deliver me, and whoever takes refuge with me, from the wrongdoing people; and admit me into the treasuries whose locks are "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", whose key is "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds", "There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God".

And this is a mighty supplication belonging to the noble verse. It is this: when you are in a place of fear, or among peoples whose evil and whose harm you fear, you recite the noble Throne Verse eleven times, and then after it you say this supplication: O God, guard me with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter me with Your support that cannot be assailed, and forgive me by Your power over me, that I may not perish; and You are my hope. We have entered upon evening within the treasuries of God, chained fast with the remembrance of God. Its door is "There is no god but God"; its wall is "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God"; its roof is "There is no power and no strength save in God". "In the name of God" is light, and "In the name of God" is joy, and the Throne Verse revolves about us as the wall revolved about Muḥammad the Messenger. It has neither lock nor key, from the evening until the morning, by the leave of the King, al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), the Cleaver of the dawn — by a thousand thousand "There is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty". You are He to the might of whose Name necks have been abased, and before whose awe the towering mountains have been ground to dust. Yours is the lofty sovereignty and the exalted dominion, and the kingdom and the heavenly kingdom; and Yours are might and omnipotence. You have wrapped Yourself in the mantle of bounties, and all created things have yielded obedience to Your greatness, and the angels brought nigh, and the spiritual beings, and the cherubim have trembled in awe. O Lord of the first and of the last, I ask You, O God, that You preserve me, and guard me, and watch over me, and keep me, and look upon me with a look of mercy; for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. I have hidden myself from my enemies by God, and entered into the shelter of God, and clothed myself in the mantle of God, and taken hold of the most firm handhold, which never breaks. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing (Q 2:256). And God encompasses them from behind (Q 85:20). Nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved tablet (Q 85:21–22).

And likewise a supplication of the Throne Verse, which follows upon the other supplication. You say — and you recite the noble Throne Verse in its entirety and its completeness: I ask You, O God. You are God, there is no god but You, al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Aḥad (the Unique), al-Fard (the Single), al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes. I ask You that You bestow Your bounty upon me, and give me from what is with You and in the treasuries of Your mercy — of good, and of provision, and of blessing — by Your favour, and Your generosity, and Your beneficence; and that You make me rich by Your favour, [independent] of all besides You. O God, O God, O God! O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful! O Living, O Self-Subsisting! O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth! O Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion)! O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour)! I ask You, O God, by the light of Your noble Face, which has filled the pillars of Your mighty Throne; and by Your power, by which You have power over all Your creation; and by Your mercy, which embraces all things. There is no god but You; glory be to You! Truly I have been among the wrongdoers, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. I ask You /fol. 95r./ and I call upon You that You make lasting upon me the blessing, and the good, and the provision, and that which soars high; and that You give me from Your ample treasuries that whereby You make me independent of all besides You. O You who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say to it "Be", and it is (Q 36:82) — truly You have power over all things. O God, O God, O

God! O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful! There is no god but You, al-Muʿṭī (the Giver) of the treasuries of blessings, al-Muḥsin (the Beneficent), al-Mutafaḍḍil (the Bountiful), al-Karīm (the Generous), and al-Wahhāb (the Bestower). Grant me, O God, abundant wealth, and a soaring blessing, and provision, and might, by Your ample favour. O Fayyāḍ (Ever-Effusing), O Fayyāḍ, O Mufawwiḍ (Entruster): commit unto me the blessing and the good, and enrich me with a wealth after which there is no poverty, ever. For You are God, [beside] whom there is no god [but] You, al-Muʿṭī, al-Wahhāb, al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Mujīb (the Answerer), al-Fayyāḍ. O God, You are the Sustainer of all things, al-Qadīm (the Eternal), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), al-ʿAẓīm (the Mighty). So magnify me with Your greatness, mighty and magnified, O You who are greater than every great one! I ask You, O God, by the right of Your Name, the mighty, the greatest, the magnified, by which, when You are called upon, You answer, and by which, when You are asked, You give; and by the right of all Your Most Beautiful Names, those of them that I know and those that I do not know; and by the right of the Torah and what is in it; and by the right of the Gospel and what is in it; and by the right of the Mighty Qurʾān and what is in it; and by the right of the Name by which You established the seven heavens and what is in them; and by the right of all Your prophets, and Your friends, and Your chosen ones; and by the right of Your angels brought nigh; and by the right of Your Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and his family and his companions all together. O Lord of the worlds! And I call upon You that

You supply me with abundant good, and soaring provision, and ample blessing: by Your favour, O Mutafaḍḍil; and Your generosity, O Jawād (Munificent One); and Your beneficence, O Muḥsin; and by Your generous bounty, O Karīm; and by Your giving, O Muʿṭī of lavish blessings. O God, O God! I ask You, O Sustainer of all the worlds by Your manifestation, O Sustainer of the heavens and the earth! Everything has come obediently to Your self-subsistence, wrapped about with life, veiled with hope. I ask You, O God, for truly You are al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander); and You are the most truthful of speakers, since You said in Your Mighty Book: Call upon Me, and I will answer you (Q 40:60). I ask You, O God, and I call upon You, that You supply me with soaring wealth and ample blessing, out of lavish provision. O God, O God, O God! O Munʿim (Bestower of blessings), O You great in goodness! O God, by the right of the Night of Power and of the Throne Verse, that You provide me with provision that is goodly, ample, abundant, wholesome, and blessed, from whence I neither know nor am aware; truly You have power over all things. O God, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate! Here am I, seeking the answer, openly avowing the outward tokens of sincerity, [asking] of the Sustainer of Your self-subsistence. O Subduer: subdue whoever intends me hurt or evil — subdue him with Your subduing might, until You keep him away from me; for neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You. And straiten the earth for him, for all its breadth: no ease to gladden him, but rather adversity to harm him. O God, O God, O God! O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful, O All-Merciful! O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth! O Mālik al-Mulk! O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām! I ask You, O God, that You fulfil my need, and that You pour out /fol. 95v./ upon me, from Your bounties, the secret of the celestial [order] among Your servants, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him — that the letters of the Throne Verse are one hundred and seventy letters; and as for its words, they are fifty; and its sections are twenty-eight, and it is said twenty, and it is said five. And it is said: whoever recites it at the beginning of the day is in safety from Satan and from the ruler, and likewise at the beginning of the night. Whoever recites it in the dead of night, facing [the qibla], far removed from all sounds, the number of its letters, and asks God, exalted is He, for his need — He fulfils it for him. And whoever recites it the number of the messengers, 313, or [the number] of the people of Badr, or of the companions of Ṭālūt, or its reckoning from the name of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and asks God, exalted is He, for his need, whether of the affair of this world, or of religion, or of the hereafter, it is fulfilled. And whoever fears his enemy and desires his destruction, and the destruction of a wrongdoer, or the ruin of his house, let him recite it that number of times and add to it: "O Subduer, O You severe in assault"; and you say: O God, just as You have been subtle with what is above Your Throne, and the whisperings of breasts are with You as things openly declared, and the open utterance of speech is as the secret within Your knowledge, and everything has yielded obedience to Your greatness, and every possessor of authority has bowed low before Your authority, and the affair of this world and of the hereafter has come to be in Your hand and in the hand of none other than You — grant me, out of every care in which I have entered upon morning and upon evening, a gladness and a way out. O God, truly Your pardon of my sins and Your passing over my transgression are of that wherein I have fallen short. I call upon You in security, and I ask You in intimacy; for You are the one who does good to me, and I am the one who does evil to myself in what is between me and You. You endear Yourself to me with blessings, while I make myself hateful to You with acts of disobedience; yet trust in You has borne me on to boldness toward You. So extend to me Your favour and Your beneficence toward me, and turn to me in forgiveness; for truly You, toward me, are al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate).

And this is the adjuration of the Throne Verse. > I ask You < O God, truly I ask You by the diffusing fragrance of the breeze of the sweet basil of the spirits of the penetration of the lights of the secrets of Your greatest Name — by whose self-disclosure parched livers have been given profit, and the basin of Your beneficence has slaked those who make for the all-glorified [depths] of Your secret. O You to whom belongs the Greatest Name! O You whose loftiness is prior to pre-eternity, and He is the more ancient! O You who have no limit that might be known, and He is the more knowing! I ask You, O God, by Your Name, the mighty, the greatest, and by the light of Your Name, the noble, the most noble, and by that with which the pen has run, that You bless our master Muḥammad and his family and grant them peace, and that You make subservient to me all that You have created, what I know of it and what I do not know. For I have called upon You by Your Name, by which he was saved who was saved and by which he perished who perished. There is no god but You. Blessed and exalted are You, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām!

And this is another supplication belonging to this noble verse. O God, O Living, O Self-Subsisting! O You the subsistence of whose existence is by Himself, and the subsistence of the existence of all else is by Him! There is no power and no strength save in You. I have raised up my destitution to You, and spread out my palm before You; so do not disappoint my hope in You, for You are the most generous of the generous. And how should that not be so, when to none besides You belongs the existence of Your bounties? For truly You are the One in truth; there is no god but You — nay, there is no existent besides You: the existence of Your bounties. And bring me into being through what is in the secret of Your Name, of the existence of Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. Three times. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family, the good and the pure, and grant them peace. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. /fol. 96r./
This is the invocation of the noble Sūrat al-Anʿām and the conditions of reciting it

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that this noble sura: when you wish to work with it, you begin with ablution, and with cleanliness of garment, and with leaving aside, absolutely, whatever does not concern one; and likewise talk of this world — you do not converse with anyone in the course of the recitation. And you hold fast to self-abasement and brokenness before God, exalted is He, mighty and majestic. And the beginning of the operation is to be on Sunday, after the noon prayer. You pray two rakʿas for the fulfilment of needs and the sufficing of pressing matters, reciting in them the Fātiḥa and Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad (Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ) three times. And he writes down his need and sets it in front of him, beneath his prayer-mat, turning toward the qibla; and he does not look to the right nor to the left, nor does he ever speak talk of this world, from the very first beginning of it to the end of it. In this ordering God, exalted is He, fulfils his need, and forgives his sins, and [the sins] of seventy of the people of his household, and makes provision ample for him. And before he recites he says: "O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and grant benediction and peace, by the number of the things You know" — forty-one times. Then he says: And I commit my affair to God; truly God is Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44). And sufficient for me is —

God, and excellent is the Guardian — eleven times. Then he recites the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb three times, and the Throne Verse ten times. Then he takes the muṣḥaf in his hand, and forms the intention for his need, and makes his intention good. Then you recite this blessed supplication.

He says: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. This is the speech of our Lord and the attributes of our Lord. Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and we have followed the Messenger, so write us down among those who bear witness (Q 3:53). O God, in truth You sent it down, and in truth it came down. O God, make great my desire in it, and make it a light for my sight and a healing for my breast. O God, open my tongue by it, and adorn my form by it, and beautify my face and my body by it, and provide me with the reciting of it without ostentation and without seeking of repute, and upon Your obedience through the watches of the night and at the ends of the day. And make it a proof for us and do not make it a proof against us, and rouse us from the slumber of the heedless before death, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful." God, exalted is He, fulfils his need, without doubt and without uncertainty. Then give alms from what is lawful. Then you say [it]. You begin with the aforementioned sura, and it is the noble Sūrat al-Anʿām. And when you reach His word, exalted is He, and that is the manifest triumph (Q 6:16), you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) 41 times. Then you say: O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad and grant them peace, by the number of everything known to You — 41 times. Then you recite; and when he reaches His word, exalted is He, you call upon Him in humility and in secret (Q 6:63), he says You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5) 41 times. Then he says And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) 41 times. Then he says: O God, bless Muḥammad, and grant benediction upon

Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, and grant peace, by the number of everything known to You — 41 times. Then you recite; and when he reaches /fol. 96v./ His word, exalted is He, then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it (Q 6:89), you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) 41 times. Then he says: O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and grant benediction upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, and grant peace, by the number of everything known to You — 41 times. Then he recites, until when he reaches His word, exalted is He, the like of what the messengers of God were given (Q 6:124), he says And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) 41 times. Then he says Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down and we have followed the Messenger, so write us down among those who bear witness (Q 3:53).

Then he recites this blessed supplication, saying: My God, who is there that called upon You and You did not answer him? And who is there that asked You and You did not give him? And who is there that sought protection with You and You did not protect him? And who is there that sought enrichment of You and You did not enrich him? And who is this that put his trust in You and You did not suffice him? Oh, my succour! Through You, O God, O God, O God — with You I have sought succour. O Succourer, succour me — 3 times. And do what You are worthy of and deserving of, for You are the One worthy to be feared and worthy to forgive (cf. Q 74:56). Then he asks and requests his need, for it is fulfilled on the spot, if God, exalted is He, wills. Then he says: And provide me, and all Muslim men and Muslim women and believing men and believing women, the living among them and the dead, by the sanctity of this blessed sura, with the good of this world and of the hereafter; and turn away from us and from them, by the sanctity of the Mighty Qurʾān and by the sanctity of Sūrat al-Anʿām, and guard us from the evil of this world and of the hereafter and from the evil of all Your creation, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and grant benediction and peace, by the number of everything known to You — three times. And when he reaches His word, exalted is He, And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy (Q 6:133), he says: I am the poor one, the possessor of need — 18. Our Lord, truly You are the Gatherer of mankind for a Day about which there is no doubt; truly God does not fail the appointed promise (Q 3:9). Our Lord, and appoint for us from Your presence a protector, and appoint for us from Your presence a helper (Q 4:75) — 98. And when he completes the sura, he says: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O Swift in reckoning, O Severe in punishment, O Forgiving, O Compassionate, O Creator of everything, O Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Cleaver of the daybreak, O Causer of causes, O Opener of doors, O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, O Abundant in good deeds, O Patron of good deeds, O Remitter of stumbles, O Reviver of the dead, O Light of the heavens and the earth, O Forgiver of faults, O Veiler of shameful things, O Remover of evil deeds, O Repeller of afflictions, O Fulfiller of needs — fulfil my need in this hour, O God, O All-Merciful, O God of the first and the last, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" — 3. His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say to it "Be", and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). Then he prostrates and requests his need, for it is fulfilled on the spot, if God, exalted is He, wills. And when he completes the sura, he recites this supplication a thousand times, /fol. 97r./ saying: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You for the things that necessitate Your mercy and the resolves of Your forgiveness, and for the gain of every act of righteousness and safety from every evil. O God, leave me no sin but that You have forgiven it, nor any worry but that You have relieved it, nor any sick man but that You have healed him, nor any debt but that You have discharged it, nor anything corrupt but that You have set it right, nor anything scattered but that You have gathered it, nor anyone absent but that You have brought him back, nor any need among the needs of this world and of the hereafter but that You have fulfilled it — with facilitation from You, and ease, and well-being, O You whose forgiveness is vast, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful." Then you say after every hundred times: Fulfil my need, O Fulfiller of needs, O God of the first and the last, O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And may God bless our master Muḥammad, the best of all His creation, and his family and his companions, and grant them peace.
Bāb: On the renowned spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) of Say: it has been revealed (Q 72:1)

Know, O brother in God, exalted is He, that when you desire that, then fast three days, the first of them Tuesday, then Wednesday, and Thursday, which is the last of them; and that is a fast [broken] upon what is not possessed of a soul. And you suffumigate with grains of frankincense (ḥaṣā lubān) and benzoin (jāwī), by night and by day, while you sit in an empty, pure place, clean of body and of garment. Then you recite the noble sura during the three days 1000 times within that aforementioned period; and you recite each day 333 times or more, the aim being to complete it to 1000 times within that aforementioned period. And strive that your completion of the reciting of it be on the eve of Friday, in the middle third of the night. For its servant-spirit will present himself to you; and he is a short man with long arms. He will sit down before you and say to you: Peace be upon you. So make your heart firm, for upon him is a mighty awe; and he is one of the kings of the believing jinn who submitted at the hand of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace. And you will see behind him three men standing. If you hold yourself firm, your need is fulfilled; and if you fear, or fall to imagining, or falter in your speech, then they depart from you and your labour comes to nothing. So it is incumbent upon you to embolden your heart and not to fear. For his name is Abū Yūsuf. So say to him: O Abū Yūsuf, my right over you has become binding, and you see what I am in of destitution and straitness; and I want of you at this hour something of what is permitted and lawful, that I may be helped by it to my subsistence and the maintenance of my dependents, and be helped by it to the pilgrimage to the sacred House of God; and your reward is with God, exalted is He.

And know, my brother, that if you strengthen your heart and speak that speech to which we have alluded, he turns to one of the three men who are behind him and commands him with something, and he brings it swifter than lightning; and it is that which God, exalted is He, has apportioned to you from pre-eternity. So take what reaches you, and thank them, and pray for them, for they will depart. And peace. And it is related of the righteous shaykh, the ascetic, the devout worshipper, Ḥusayn b. Manṣūr, that he /fol. 97v./ did that, and the servant-spirit brought him ten thousand dinars. And it is also related that a disciple of Yaḥyā performed it; and when the servant-spirit of the noble sura presented himself to him, he feared him with a severe fear, and his teeth chattered and his tongue was struck dumb, so that he could not manage to speak to him; and whenever he opened his eyes he found him before him. And when the matter had gone long with him and he did not speak, the servant-spirit departed from him, and there befell him from it neither harm nor evil. And peace. So take to yourself, O seeker, strength of heart and steadfastness of spirit; for the servant-spirit of the sura, as we have mentioned, is of the believing jinn, and for that reason he does not harm the seeker. And the conjuration and the invocation are the noble sura Say: it has been revealed (Q 72:1), to its completion and its entirety, as we have mentioned in the exposition; and likewise the suffumigation.

And know, O you who have attained to this noble invocation, fear God in secret and in the open, for it is among the treasured secrets. So know its worth, and the worth of what has reached you and come to you, and conceal it from those unworthy of it; and know what has come to you and ponder it, for it is among the hidden secrets, for it is from the books of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) and their secrets — may God, exalted is He, profit us by them and by their secrets. And it is this blessed invocation. You say: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Say: it has been revealed to me (Q 72:1). O God, I ask You, O You who sent down the revelation upon Your Messenger from above the seven heavens, that You make easy for me what I am aiming at and seeking, and that You make subservient to me the servant-spirits of this noble, blessed sura, that they may obey me in all that I desire; truly You are powerful over everything. O God, O You to whom those who flee take flight, and O You in whose pardon the hopeful set their hope: truly a company of the jinn listened (Q 72:1). O God, I ask You, O You who hears and sees and is not seen, and who is at the highest vantage: and they said, truly we have heard a wondrous recitation, guiding to right direction, so we have believed in it (Q 72:1–2). O God,

I ask You by the right of those of the believers who believed in their prophets, and in Your Prophet, and in You, and by the wayfarers, that You make subservient to me the servant-spirits of this noble sura, that they may be a help to me in what I desire. And we shall never associate anyone with our Lord; and that He — exalted be the majesty of our Lord — has taken neither consort nor child (Q 72:2–3). O God, I ask You, O You who has taken neither consort nor child, that You cause my heart and my tongue to speak with wisdom, and that You be for me a help and a helper, and that You make subservient to me the hearts of all Your creation. And that there were men among humankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, and they increased them in oppression; and that they thought, as you thought, that God would never raise anyone up (Q 72:6–7). O God, I ask You, O Raiser of the heavens, and O Creator of created things, and O Bringer-into-being of the beings, and O Governor of time, and O You who sent down the Torah and the Gospel and the Furqān and the Psalms, and O

Favourer of the children of Adam above all created things; O Ḥayy (the Living), O Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting) who does not sleep; O You who has made the jinn subject to mankind, and has made men among humankind seek refuge with men among the jinn, so that they increased them in oppression: I ask You, O God, that You subject to me all Your creation and all things, and that You make my name renowned in what is good. O Ḥayy who does not sleep! O God, truly I ask You by the Greatest Name and by the /fol. 98r./ noble Light, that You subject to me the spiritual beings of these names, so that they may answer me and be a help to me in what I desire. Truly I have sought access to You through You, O You who are the Doer of what He wills.

I adjure you, O spiritual spirits, mighty and magnified, by the splendid names, and by the name that was written upon the heart of Adam — peace be upon him — and by the name whereby God, exalted is He, has favoured you above many of His creation among the angels: there is no god but He, the Lord of created beings. Answer, O spiritual spirits, pure, undefiled, belonging to the divine Dominion, that you be a help to me in what I desire, so that none among the terrestrial ones be able to oppose my command. Aid him who has sought aid of you, O angels of the Lord of the worlds! O God, make Your help to me excellent, and be for me a helper, for I am Your servant and the son of Your servant, and I have sought help of You. So help me, and succour me, and grant me victory, for I have no helper and no giver of victory but You; and I ask You, and I ask no one besides You. O God, truly I ask You by the verses and the wise Reminder, that You subject to me the spiritual beings of Your angels and the servant-spirits of this noble sura; truly You are powerful over what You will. Answer, O angels of the Lord of the worlds, by the right of what I have recited to you of the names of God, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and by the right of this invocation and the wise Reminder.

I adjure you, O angels of my Lord: answer, obedient to the names of God, for I have sought help against you from God, the Lord of the worlds, and by "Praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds". Answer, O Rūqiyāʾīl, by the right of the name written upon the heart of the sun, and by the right of the magnificent, greatest Name. Answer, O Mudhhib, by the right of the Lord of the worlds and by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Rūqiyāʾīl. Present yourself, you and your tribes and your army and whoever is with you under your rule. Answer, O Jibrāʾīl, by the right of the name written upon the heart of the moon, and by the right of the One, the Overpowering. Answer, O Abū l-Nūr, O Abyaḍ, by the right of the appointed king whose command prevails over you, Jibrāʾīl. Present yourself, you and your tribes and your clans and all who are under your rule. Answer, and be a help to me in what I desire, by the right of what I have recited to you of the name of God, the Magnificent, the Greatest. Be for me a help and a helper. I adjure you, O Samsamāʾīl, by the right of the lord of this lofty edifice, and by the right of God, the High, the Most High, the Magnificent: answer, and be a help to me in what I desire. Answer, O Aḥmar, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Samsamāʾīl. Answer, you and your helpers and your clans and your tribes and your soldiery and all the people of your obedience. Answer, all of you, and do for me what I have commanded you and what I desire of you, by the right of Subbūḥ (2 times), Quddūs (2 times), Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Answer, and be obedient to God and hearkening to His names. Answer, O Mīkāʾīl, by the right of the verses and the wise Reminder, and by Him who created the heavens and the earth and who is Knower of all things. Answer, O Burqān, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Mīkāʾīl. Answer, you and your helpers and your tribes and your clans, by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly/fol. 98v./ (Q 41:11). Answer, O Ṣarfiyāʾīl, by the right of the King, the Powerful, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and by the right of the five prayers, and by the right of God, the High, the Magnificent. Answer, O Samhūras, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Ṣarfiyāʾīl. Answer, you and your helpers and your clans and the people of your obedience. Let not one of you forsake these mighty names and the magnificent Name — Allāh (5 times). O God, be for me a help and a helper. Answer, O ʿAyniyāʾīl, by the right of Friday and by the right of Him who is the Gatherer of mankind upon a day in which there is no doubt. Answer, O Zawbaʿa, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, ʿAyniyāʾīl. Answer, you and your helpers and your tribes and whoever is under your rule. Answer, O Kasfiyāʾīl, by the right of the clouds made subservient between the heaven and the earth, and by the right of the King, the All-Holy, the Requiter, and by the right of God, exalted is He. Answer, O Maymūn, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Kasfiyāʾīl. Present yourself, you and your helpers and your tribes and your clans and whoever is under your rule. Answer, O companies of the spirits, the spiritual and the terrestrial, obedient to this invocation and the wise Reminder. Answer, O companies of the celestial spirits, and be a help to me in what I desire of the lower, terrestrial spirits. Answer, by the right of what you know of the worth of the names of God, exalted is He. Answer obediently, and obey, and hear my address, and deploy yourselves operatively in what I desire, O companies of the terrestrial ones, by the right of the spiritual kings. Answer — [come] to this place! Haste (3 times)! Speed (3 times)! This very hour (3 times)! It is but a single cry, and behold, they are all brought before Us (Q 36:53). Present yourselves, and answer, and obey; and whoever among you holds back, the angels shall burn him with the piercing flames. And we touched the heaven and found it filled with mighty guards and flaming meteors (Q 72:8); and we used to sit there in seats to listen, but whoever listens now finds a flaming meteor lying in wait for him (Q 72:9); and we do not know whether evil is intended for those who are upon the earth, or whether their Lord intends right guidance for them (Q 72:10); and among us are the righteous, and among us are those below that; we are divided ways (Q 72:11); and we thought that we could never thwart God upon the earth, nor could we thwart Him by flight (Q 72:12); and when we heard the guidance we believed in it; and whoever believes in his Lord fears neither loss nor oppression (Q 72:13); and among us are those who submit, and among us are those who deviate; and whoever submits — those have sought out right guidance (Q 72:14).

I adjure you, O spiritual spirits: answer by the right of what I have recited to you. Let not one of you hold back, and let not one of you set another in his place. Answer, and hear, and present yourselves, and give welcome among all the terrestrial ones. Answer, O companies of the terrestrial spirits, by the right of what I have recited to you. Answer, by the right of the names of God, exalted is He. Answer, hastening, obedient, hearkening to the names of the Lord of the worlds. Answer, and do not hold back, and let not one of you hold back. And as for those who deviate, they are firewood for Hell (Q 72:15). Answer, O companies of the terrestrial spirits, obedient and hearkening, by the right of that by which I have adjured you. And truly it /fol. 99r./ is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76); and if they had gone straight upon the way, We would have given them abundant water to drink (Q 72:16); that We might try them thereby; and whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will drive him into a mounting torment (Q 72:17). Answer, and obey, and let not one of you hold back, by the right of that by which I have adjured you. And the places of prostration belong to God, so call not upon anyone along with God (Q 72:18); and when the servant of God stood calling upon Him (Q 72:19); say: I call only upon my Lord, and I associate none with Him (Q 72:20); say: I have no power to bring you harm, nor right guidance (Q 72:21); say: none shall protect me from God, and I shall find no refuge apart from Him (Q 72:22); only a delivering from God and His messages; and whoever disobeys God and His Messenger — for him is the fire of Hell, they abiding therein for ever (Q 72:23); until, when they see what they are promised, they shall know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number (Q 72:24); say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a term (Q 72:25); Knower of the unseen — He discloses His unseen to none (Q 72:26); save to a messenger whom He has approved; and truly He dispatches before him and behind him a guard (Q 72:27). O God, truly I ask You by the ṭāʾ of Your largesse (ṭawl), and by the bāʾ of Your everlastingness (baqāʾ), and by the qāf of Your power (qudra), and by the tāʾ of Your blessedness (tabarruk), and by the thāʾ of the fixity (thubūt) of Your kingship and the breadth of Your Footstool. O You whom conjectures do not touch within His kingdom, and O You with whom every thing seeks protection — and there is nothing of all His creation but that it seeks protection with Him — and against whom none is granted protection within His kingdom: I ask You, O God, for I have no power over harm or benefit for myself save by Your leave. O God, truly I ask You by the right of the promise which You promised to Your prophets and by which You guided Your friends aright. I ask You, O God: O Jalīl (the Majestic) (3 times), O ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent) (3 times), O Quddūs (the All-Holy) (3 times), O Allāh (3 times), O You to whom belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, O You who knows and of whom none knows but Himself. O God, truly I ask You by the ḥāʾ of Your judgement (ḥukm), and by the ʿayn of Your knowledge (ʿilm), and by the ghayn of Your forgiveness (ghufrān), and by the fāʾ of Your bounty (faḍl), and by the kāf of Your grandeur (kibriyāʾ), and by the lām of Your kindness (luṭf), and by the yāʾ of Your certainty (yaqīn), and by the alif of Your divinity (ulūhiyya), and by the ḍād of Your radiance (ḍiyāʾ). O God, truly I ask You by the zāy of Your adornment (zīna) and by the sīn of Your sublimity (sanāʾ), O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm.

Save to a messenger whom He has approved; and truly He dispatches before him and behind him a guard (Q 72:27); that He may know that they have delivered the messages of their Lord; and He encompasses what is with them, and He has numbered every thing in count (Q 72:28). O God, truly I ask You by the right of the places of prostration that belong to God, and by the right of those who prostrate, and by the right of Your righteous servants, and by the right of those who bow and prostrate, and by the right of those who supplicate; for You are God the Generous — O Generous One! — and by the right of him who has called upon You: subject to me my desire, and be for me a helper. O God, truly I ask You by him who associated none with his Lord, that You make [it] easy for me and light for me, and that You help me, and that You prepare for us right guidance in our affair. O God, O You whose speech this speech is, I ask You by Your mighty speech, and by the sura Say: it has been revealed to me (Q 72:1), and by the wise promise, and by Your firm knowledge. Truly I have sought help and sought an opening by the verses and the wise Reminder. O God, O You who has numbered every thing in count, and has made the sea to flow as a supply, and who causes the creatures to pass away while He endures for ever: I ask You, O You whom the describers cannot describe /fol. 99v./ and who is not described by standing or by sitting, that You subject to me the servant-spirits of this sura and of the names, that they may serve me and obey me; truly You are powerful over all things. Answer, O servant-spirits of this invocation, of the spiritual and of the terrestrial, hearkening and obedient; and let not one of you hold back, by the right of the invocation and the wise Reminder.

I adjure you, O companies of the spiritual beings appointed over the celestial spheres, whom God created from His light and settled beneath His Throne: [I adjure you] only that you answer, obedient to His name, and that you deploy yourselves operatively in what I desire. Answer, O servant-spirits of this invocation, by the right of Arfūsh Arqūsh Kalhūsh Baṭaṭhūsh Kamaṭhūsh Bahūsh Afānūsh. I adjure you, O Rūqiyāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of the sun, by the right of God, of whom there is no god but He; every thing perishes save His face; His is the judgement, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 28:88). I adjure you, O Rūqiyāʾīl, by the presence of Mudhhib. Answer, O Mudhhib, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you

Rūqiyāʾīl, and by the right of Yāh Yāh: [I adjure you] only that you answer, and speed, and do what I have commanded you. I adjure you, O Samsamāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of Mars, by the right of Him whose command lies between the kāf and the nūn — His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it "Be", and it is (Q 36:82). Answer, O Samsamāʾīl, by the presence of al-Aḥmar. By the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Samsamāʾīl, and by the right of Damlīkh: [I adjure you] only that you answer, speed, and do what I have commanded you. I adjure you, O Mīkāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of Mercury, and by the right of Him of whom Sight does not attain Him, but He attains all sight, and He is the

Subtle, the All-Aware (Q 6:103) — al-Sattār (the Veiler). Answer, O Mīkāʾīl, by the presence of Burqān. By the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Mīkāʾīl, and by the right of Ahyā Sharāhiyā: [I adjure you] only that you hasten, and speed, and answer, and do what I have commanded you. I adjure you, O Ṣarfiyāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of Jupiter, by the right of God is the light of the heavens and the earth (Q 24:35). Answer, O Ṣarfiyāʾīl, by the presence of Shamhūrish. I adjure you, O Shamhūrish, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Ṣarfiyāʾīl, and by the right of Warmīsh: [I adjure you] only that you answer, and hasten, and speed, and do what I have commanded you. I adjure you, O ʿAyniyāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of Venus, by the right of Him who knows what every female bears, and what the wombs diminish and what they increase (Q 13:8). Answer, O ʿAyniyāʾīl, by the presence of Zawbaʿa. Answer, O Zawbaʿa, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, ʿAyniyāʾīl, and by the right of Subbūḥ, Quddūs, Lord of the angels and the Spirit: [I adjure you] only that you hurry, and hasten, and speed, and do what I have commanded you. I adjure you, O Kasfiyāʾīl, the king appointed over the sphere of Muqātil [that is, Saturn], by the right of Him who knows the secret and what is more hidden (Q 20:7). Answer, O Maymūn, by the right of the king whose command prevails over you, Kasfiyāʾīl, and by the right of Azalī Arzāl Arziyāl. /fol. 100r./ I adjure you, O angels of the Lord of the worlds, by the right of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate":

[I adjure you] only that you answer, hearkening, obedient, responding, by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11); by the right of the Worthy One, the Trustworthy King, who brings man forth from every strait; and by the sanctity of Muḥammad and of his companion al-Ṣiddīq (the Veracious): [I adjure you] only that you make subject to me these terrestrial ones, that they may be a help to me, obedient to me, complying with my command — by the right of Ahyā (2 times), Ahyānūsh, Bakmūsh (2 times), ʿAkash (2 times), Kashlakh (2 times), and by the right of the Single, the Eternal Refuge, who did not beget, and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal (Q 112:3–4): [I adjure you] only that you speed and answer, and that not one of you be left behind. Haste! Haste! Speed! Speed! This very hour! This very hour! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you. Answer, and do what I have commanded you, by the right of that by which I have adjured you — and truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76).
The blessed spiritual discipline is completed, with praise to God, exalted is He. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
*I mention the spiritual discipline (riyāḍa) of Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm, and the supplication belonging to it, and the adjuration, and the suffumigation*

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that if you wish to work with this invocation and this spiritual discipline, then let him who desires that go into retreat in a place empty of people, far away from people; and let him be pure of garment and of body; and let him fast for the duration of the retreat and the discipline, and break his fast only upon raisins, oil, barley flour, and vinegar, if that be possible. And the duration of the retreat is seven days, the first of them Sunday and the last of them Saturday. And if you desire the lesser [course], then your discipline is 3 days, the first of them Tuesday and the last of them Thursday. And when it is the night of Friday, you being [all the while] reciting the two noble names — and they are Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm (O Generous One, O Compassionate One) — every day continually, without number, and you do not slacken in their remembrance, ever. And every day, following the dawn prayer, you recite the sura Say: O you disbelievers (Q 109:1) 21 times, and after it you recite the adjuration in particular 3 times. Then you keep constantly to the recitation of the two generous names, Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm; do not slacken in that. And when it is the night of Friday, you being [all the while] reciting the two noble names — according to the sound opinion — you invoke blessing upon the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, 1000 times; and you are to have invoked blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — beforehand. And before the recitation of the two names you pray two rakʿas; then you sit after them in a state of purity, in the place of your prayer-station, facing the qibla, and you recite the adjuration whose mention follows. And when you reach His word, exalted is He, and to Him they prostrate themselves (Q 7:206), you prostrate yourself to His noble Essence and recite the supplication in that prostration of yours; and that is to be at midnight. And according to the second opinion — the seven days — you do what has been mentioned above: the recitation of the two names, the praying of the two rakʿas, the recitation of the adjuration, the reading of the supplication, and the invocation of blessing upon the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace. And when it is the night of Sunday, at midnight, /fol. 100v./ there comes to you one who comes, in your sleep or in your waking, and says to you: What do you want, and what do you seek, O servant of God? And you say to him: I want, of your bounty and of the bounty of God, exalted is He, that you bring me every day a dinar of gold. And he says to you: Yes. And he lays down conditions upon you, among them the visiting of the dead on every Saturday by day, and the recitation of the two mighty names after every prayer according to the number that falls to them, and almsgiving to the poor and the destitute and the needy. So consent to them in that, and say to them: May God reward your effort, and forgive us and you. Depart, rewarded! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you. For from that night onward you will find beneath your head a dinar of gold. So recognize what has come to you, and fear God, exalted is He. And the suffumigation for that operation is Qāqullī aloeswood (ʿūd qāqullī) and benzoin (jāwī); and it may serve as your suffumigation for as long as you continue in your discipline and your recitation.

And know that the servant-spirits (khuddām) of these two noble names are among the believing angels, and that they do not take on forms before the possessor of this invocation, nor turn him aside, nor present themselves in bodily shape to him, nor cast phantoms before him, nor do him harm. And you must hold to the fear of God in secret and in the open. And beware of vengeful gloating (tashaffī), for you will lose what has come to you. And God, glorified is He, knows best. And this is the form of the blessed adjuration. You say: O God, truly I ask You by the most towering Towering One, the High over every open plain. I call upon you, O Jibrāʾīl: command a herald to call out on your behalf by the names Shatūt Shatūt — no servant has heard you but that he became humble and submitted, nor any tyrant but that he was shaken, nor any king but that he submitted. Present yourself [reading for the edition's ,]by Him who adorned the sun in the horizon of the heaven! And truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76). Answer, O Maymūn, by the right of those who are with your Lord: they are not too proud to worship Him, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate themselves (Q 7:206). Then he prostrates himself and recites this blessed supplication. He says: O God, truly I ask You by the first of Your firstness, which has no beginning, and by the last of Your lastness, which has no end. O Generous One! O Possessor of the abundant generosity that is never cut off, ever! O Possessor of the all-embracing mercy that admits of no modality! O You whose gaze is upon the inmost thoughts, the promptings, and the passing notions — nothing eludes Him. All-Seeing: He gives sight to the people of inner discernment and guides them to His greatness, and He has set them to work, and inspired them to His remembrance, and granted them success, and taught them the secret of His noble name, and opened for them the door of mercy. So they called out: O Generous One, O Compassionate One! And they stood firm upon the uprightness of intimate colloquy. And in the watches of the night the herald of response called out to them: when you were calling upon your Lord for help, and He answered you (Q 8:9). My God, my Master, my Lord! Lift from our hearts the veil of heedlessness, and from our sights that which has veiled them from the Unseen [readingfor the edition's ,[ so that we may know, of Your knowledge, what You have taught us, and may deploy it operatively with the operative deployment of the spiritual ones, by the secret of Your name. O You who created the fires for the people of disobedience to You, and adorned the gardens for the people of obedience to You! I have sought access to You, O God, by the right of Your Most Beautiful Names and Your perfect words, /fol. 101r./ that You fulfil my need; and that You make subject to me the servant-spirit of these two noble, generous, mighty names — and they are Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm — and that he bring me every day a dinar of gold from what is licitly permitted of the earth, which I shall find beneath my head, so that I may seek help by it in my needful affairs. O God, truly I ask You by the right of this supplication and by what it contains of the noble verses and the mighty names. O God: a provision that prevails and is not overcome, that seeks and is not sought! O God, if my provision is in the heaven, then send it down; and if it is in the earth, then bring it forth; and if it is far, then bring it near; and if it is near, then make it easy; and if it is non-existent, then bring it into being; and if it is withheld, then make it firm; and if it is little, then make it much; and if it is much, then bless it for me, O God. And bring it to me from Yourself, and take charge Yourself of my affair in it. And make my hand the upper one in giving, and do not make it the lower one in seeking favours — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful! O Fattāḥ (Opener), O Razzāq (Provider), O ʿAlīm (All-Knowing), O ʿAẓīm (Magnificent), O Karīm (Generous), O Raḥīm (Compassionate)! Answer my supplication, by Your bounty and Your generosity. Truly You are powerful over every thing, and toward Your servants Subtle, All-Aware. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Magnificent. And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them peace.
*The spiritual discipline of Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm in another manner*

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that if you wish to work with this blessed invocation, then the beginning of your work with it is to be in a month whose first [day] falls on the daytime of Saturday. And you discipline yourself by abstaining from every ensouled creature and from whatever issues from an ensouled creature; and you recite the two noble, generous, mighty names Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm every day as much as you are able; and after every prayer you recite them 1000 times; and you persevere in that for a period of seven days. And when you are within the second seven days, you keep constantly to it as we have indicated, and you fast the White

Days, which are the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the fifteenth; and it comes to be the night of Friday. And when that night comes, you perform the full ablution and put on clean garments, and you fumigate yourself with such sweet-scented suffumigation as is possible. And when night has come and you have prayed the last evening prayer, then you sit facing the qibla, and you make remembrance of God, exalted is He, as much as you wish, and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — 1000 times, and you recite the two generous names Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm 1000 times, and you seal with the invocation of blessing upon the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — 1000 times. And the manner of the invocation of blessing upon the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — is: "Bless our master Muḥammad, and the family of our master Muḥammad, and his companions, and grant them peace." And when you have completed your recitation, you recite the Throne Verse (Q 2:255) and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ3 times, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-muʿawwidhatān), each one once. And beware lest you sleep at the time of your reciting /fol. 101v./ — for [then] your operation is spoiled and your labour goes to waste. And at the end of your blessing upon the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, you say: O God, grant him the means of access (al-wasīla), and the excellence, and the high and lofty degree; and raise him up to the station which You promised him; and bring us to his pool, and give us to drink from his hand a draught, pleasant and wholesome, after which we shall never thirst again. And after every prayer you recite the conjuration (ʿazīma) seven times; and it is this. You say: I ask You, O God, by Yūqālīm. O Shūnāhīl, O Shahrīn! I ask You by the sanctity of Kashhīl, Bardīm, Bahrānīl, ʿAjājīl, ʿArāsīl. I ask You by the sanctity of Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl, and by the sanctity of Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace, and by the right of Yā Karīm, Yā Raḥīm, that You provide me every day with a dinar, by which I may be helped to my subsistence and to the pilgrimage to the sacred House of God. And when the time of the dawn prayer comes, then pray it, and sit, and invoke blessing upon the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace. Then sleep will overcome you and you will sleep; and the servant-spirit of the two noble names will come to you and will say to you: O you, do you want this world without the hereafter? So say to him: I want this world that I may be helped by it toward the hereafter. Then he will take a covenant from you upon the visiting of the dead every Friday, and the major ablution, and the reciting, after every prayer, of the two noble names — Yā Karīm, Yā Raḥīm — according to their number. So consent to him in that. Then he will give you a dinar, and will say to you: Every day you will find a dinar beneath your head. So conceal your secret, and you will attain your object; and whenever you tell anyone, the dinar is cut off from you. So be among the thankful, and do not forget the poor and the destitute.
I mention the noble invocation of Sūrat al-Kahf

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in understanding His secrets — that when you desire to attain to the red sulphur and the radiant grey ambergris, and to the opening of the door of this talismanned treasure, and the unlocking of its cryptic symbols, and the nullifying of its impediments and its [wards?] (kufūz; , reading uncertain), then betake yourself to a pure, clean place, far from sounds and from movements. And you mark out for yourself a prayer-niche (miḥrāb) in the ground, and spread beneath your head fine sand. Then you perform the major ablution and put on garments all of them white, and fumigate yourself with the most excellent suffumigation, and purify your belly of unlawful foods and of everything in which there is doubt. Then you enter upon the spiritual discipline (riyāḍa), and you eat nothing that possesses a soul, nor anything that has come forth from a soul, for a period of 14 days. And let the beginning of your entry into the discipline be in a month whose first day is a Friday, and you enter the spiritual retreat (khalwa) after the Friday prayer. Then fumigate the place with sweet suffumigation, such as nadd, Qāqullī aloeswood (ʿūd qāqullī), benzoin (jāwī), and ambergris, if it be possible. And you recite Sūrat al-Kahf after every prayer once, and in the dead of night seven times; /fol. 102r./ and every time you recite the sura you set the suffumigation going, until the end of the aforementioned period. And when the eve of Friday comes, you sit upon your knees and invoke blessing upon the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, 1000 times. Then you begin the recitation of the noble Sūrat al-Kahf 40 times, and between every two suras you pray two light rakʿas with the Fātiḥa and al-Ikhlāṣthree times, and you invoke blessing upon our master Muḥammad ten times. And when you have completed the recitation, you ask forgiveness of God, exalted is He, and praise Him, and say the enduring righteous [words] (al-bāqiyāt al-ṣāliḥāt) 100 times. And when you rise in the morning and have prayed the dawn prayer, you praise God, exalted is He, with all the praises of Him that are in the Mighty Qurʾān; and after the praising you supplicate humbly to God, glorified and exalted, and call upon God with what you wish of righteous invocations. And when you have completed your supplication, then rise and walk, remembering God, exalted is He, until you go out beyond the wall of the city. Then the servant-spirit of the noble sura will come toward you in the form of a handsome youth of sweet fragrance, and he will greet you with peace. So return the greeting to him, and behave courteously with him; for he will hand over to you a purse in which are 1000 dinars, and he will lay conditions upon you, among them the visiting of the dead every Friday, and that you not forget the poor and the destitute, and that you not commit fornication. So say: Yes; and give thanks to God, exalted is He, and express your thanks to him. Then the servant-spirit will say to you: O servant of God, if you recite it and do that every month, you will be provided with 1000 dinars. Then dismiss the servant-spirit, and say to him: May God reward your endeavour, and forgive us and you; depart, rewarded, with good. So conceal your secret, and you will attain your object.
I mention the noble invocation of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in understanding the secrets of His names — that this sura is the key to the door of wealth. The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said: ((Ten things ward off ten things. Sūrat al-Fātiḥa wards off the wrath of the Lord; and Sūrat Yā-Sīn, the reciting of it wards off the Resurrection; and Sūrat al-Dukhān, the reciting of it wards off the terrors of the Resurrection; and Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa, the reciting of it wards off poverty; and Sūrat al-Mulk, the reciting of it wards off the punishment of the grave; and Sūrat al-Kāfirūn wards off unbelief at the death-agony; and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, the reciting of it wards off hypocrisy; and Sūrat al-Falaq, the reciting of it wards off the envy of the envious; and Sūrat al-Nās, the reciting of it wards off the insinuating whisperings.))

And know that this invocation has many occult properties. Among its occult properties is that whoever persists in reciting it after the five prayers, it becomes for him a safeguard against poverty and destitution. And among its occult properties is [its use] for entering in upon kings, viziers, and governors: one recites /fol. 102v./ the noble sura before you meet those whom we have mentioned. And you say when you go out: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, of binding the tongue of him who is such-and-such, by the right of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa which is binding upon you. And you say And truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76). Take charge of So-and-so — and you name whom you wish. And you say: Your good is between your eyes and your evil beneath your feet. And voices are humbled before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a hushed whisper (Q 20:108). Take charge, O servant-spirits of this invocation and this noble sura, by Mahmahūb (2 times), Mahūb (2 times), possessor of a hidden subtlety (2 times); by

Ṣaʿṣaʿ (2 times), Ṣaʿṣaʿ (2 times), possessor of a resplendent light (2 times). They do not speak, save him to whom the All-Merciful has given leave, and who says what is right (Q 78:38). Make me, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, one whose word and speech take effect with So-and-so son of So-and-so, that he may hear my word and obey my command, and that my need and all that I desire be fulfilled, by the right of this noble sura. They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded (Q 66:6). For it will accomplish your interests with him, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among its occult properties is [its use] for love and affection between two persons within what is lawful — for the speech of God is not put to operative use save in what is lawful. But as for one who — God, exalted is He, be our refuge — does it in what is unlawful, it harms his spirit, and he is not answered, and his labour goes to waste. So when you desire love between two who bear hatred toward each other, you recite the sura over something edible, and say at the end of the sura: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this sura, of intimacy and love and affection between such-and-such and such-and-such, by the right of Hahṭūb Hahṭūb Lamʿūb Lahūb. Answer, by Ṣamʿaṣūn, possessor of splendour and beauty. Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, of lasting love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of this sura which is binding upon you, and of your obedience which is with you. Then present the food to her; and when the two have eaten, they will be reconciled and will not part save after death.

And among its occult properties is that if you recite it after the afternoon prayer 15 times, and the Most Beautiful Names of God the like of that — the recitation being the sura once and the Most Beautiful Names of God once — and you persist in the recitation every day in this manner, and you recite after your recitation the supplication in this manner, for a count of 40 days, then you will gain possession of the servant-spirit, and he will be a help to you in everything you desire. And it is not possible to speak more plainly than this. So understand. And its suffumigation is grains of frankincense (ḥaṣā lubān), liquid storax (mayʿa sāʾila), sandarac (ṣandarūs), and black cumin (ḥabba sawdāʾ). And this is the supplication of the noble sura. You say: O God, I ask You, O Allāh, O Allāh, O Wāḥid (One), O Wāḥid, O Fard (Single), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O Witr (Odd One), O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting), O Badīʿ (Wondrous Originator) of the heavens and the earth, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O Bāsiṭ (Expander), O Ghanī (Rich), O Mughnī (Enricher) — by Mahmahūb Mahmahūb, possessor of a hidden subtlety; by Ṣaʿṣaʿ, possessor of a resplendent light; Saʿsaʿūb. God, to whom belong greatness and grandeur. Ṣamʿaṣūn, possessor of splendour and beauty. Ṭahūb, possessor of might /fol. 103r./ that is lofty; Yāh Mahlahūb. God, who by His light has made subservient every light — by Ṭahṭahūb Ṭahṭahūb Lahūb. Answer, O servant-spirits of these names, servant-spirits of the mighty, greatest Name of God, with the subjugation of the hearts of created beings and the attraction of provision; and set in motion for me the spiritual force of love, with lasting love. In the name of God, whose light has pierced through the veils, before whose greatness necks are abased, before whose awe the mountains are ground to dust, and whose praise the thunder glorifies, and the angels, from awe of Him. He is God, there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne. O God, I ask You by Your uplifted Name, which You have given to whom You willed of Your friends (awliyāʾ), and inspired to Your chosen ones among Your beloved. I ask You, O God, that You bring me a provision from Your presence, whereby You enrich my poverty, and mend my brokenness, and sever thereby the attachments of Satan from my heart. For You are God: al-Ḥannān (the Ever-Tender), al-Mannān (the Bounteous), al-Sulṭān (the Sovereign), al-Dayyān (the Requiter), al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), al-Ḥāfiẓ (the Preserver), al-Rāfiʿ (the Exalter), al-Muʿizz (the Honourer), al-Mudhill (the Abaser), al-Ghanī (the Rich), al-Mughnī (the Enricher), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Muʿṭī (the Giver), al-Razzāq, al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Shakūr (the Ever-Thankful), Possessor of bounty and of blessings and of munificence and of generosity. O God, I ask You by Your right, and by the right of Your right, and by Your generosity, and Your bounty, and Your beneficence — O Eternal in beneficence, O You whose beneficence is above every beneficence, O Master of this world and the hereafter, O True in promise: there is no god but You; glory be to You! Truly I have been among the wrongdoers. O God, make easy for me my provision by lawful means, and make it a portion for me. O God, answer my invocation, by the right of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa, and by the right of Your mighty, greatest Name, and by the sanctity of our master and our prophet and our beloved Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and of his family and his companions all together; and by the right of Faqaj Makhmat: Fattāḥ, Razzāq, Qādir (Powerful), Muʿṭī, best of providers, Enricher of the destitute poor, Tawwāb (Ever-Relenting), who does not call to account for crimes. O God, make easy for me a provision lawful and goodly, and bring me and it together from what is lawful of Yours, and make it my portion within what is lawful, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām, in this very hour. O Allāh, O Kāfī (Sufficer), O Kafīl (Guarantor), O Wakīl (Trustee): enrich me by Your hidden subtlety, O Karīm, O Raḥīm. O God, enrich me by what is lawful of Yours [so that I need not] what is unlawful of Yours, and by obedience to You [so that I need not] disobedience to You, and by Your bounty [so that I need not] any besides You. O Allāh, O All-Merciful of this world and Compassionate of the hereafter, O Lord of the worlds! Answer, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, in all that I have commanded you and that with which I have charged you, by the right of Ahyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt Āl Shadāy. I ask You, O God, that You bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad and his companions, and grant them abundant peace. So understand.
that, and you will be rightly guided. And God speaks the truth and He guides to the way. /fol. 103v./
*I mention a majestic spiritual discipline (riyāḍa), and it is: Yā Ḥāfiẓ (O Preserver), Yā Bāsiṭ (O Expander), Yā Wadūd (O Loving), Yā Muʿīn (O Helper)*

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that when you desire the spiritual retreat (khalwa) and the discipline for these noble names, then betake yourself to a clean place, empty of sounds, and sit in it, and set the suffumigation going — and it is nadd aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), and dry storax (mīʿa). Then you begin with the reciting of the aforementioned names for 14 days; and if you desire speed, then let the period be 7 days — this, while you recite the names after the prayers, by their numbers. And when the days are complete, there enter in upon you 15 angels, and they greet you with peace; so return the greeting of peace to them. And beware of fearing them, for if you fear, your spirit is struck and your labour is lost. They will say to you: Peace be upon you. So return the greeting of peace to them. Then they sit down before you and ask about your need, and they say to you: We will fulfil it for you, so ask of us what you wish. But beware of answering them. And when the sitting has grown long for you, they depart from you. So strengthen your heart, and rouse your companion-spirit (qarīn), and strengthen your suffumigation. And when an hour or two hours have passed, there enter in upon you again 15 angels, beautiful of face and sweet of fragrance, and they greet you with peace; so return the greeting of peace to them. And in that hour you shall have made your suffumigation dry tragacanth (kathīrāʾ), male frankincense, qamārī aloeswood, and wild lupine. And when you have done that, strengthen your heart, for they will make a sign to you with their hands, and you will find your spirit in the former place. So do not speak to them, even though they speak to you. And when the matter has grown long, they depart from you. Then after that there enters in upon you an angel alone, and a throne-seat is set up and he sits upon it. Then he greets you with peace; so return the greeting of peace to him, and comport yourself with courtesy before him. For he will ask you about what you desire. So do not fear him, for he is the servant-spirit of these noble names. He says to you: What do you seek, O creature of God? So strengthen your heart and say to him: I want of you the covenant, and the servant — a servant from among your servant-spirits who will comply with my command in everything I ask of him. Thereupon he gives you the covenant, and gives you a sign for when you desire the presence of the servant-spirit, and he brings him. Then he gives you things of this world; so take them from him, then dismiss him, and he departs. And give thanks to God, exalted is He, for the blessings He has conferred upon you; and conceal your secret, and you will attain your object. And peace.
*I mention the spiritual discipline of the Name of Majesty (al-jalāla) and its retreat, and it is: Allāh, Allāh, Allāh***

And its adjuration is this noble verse, namely His word, exalted is He: God is the light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light…(Q 24:35) — the verse [to its end]. And it is that you go into retreat for it 14 days, with the conditions of the retreat: fasting from eating everything possessed of a soul and whatever issues from a soul; and withdrawal from created beings; and prayer. And you hold fast to the Name of Majesty after each /fol. 104r./ prayer 1000 times, and to the aforementioned verse 50 times. And let your suffumigation be male frankincense. And you recite the Name of Majesty every day, apart from the reciting [that follows] the prayer, 10,000 times, and in the night the like of that; and likewise the verse — you recite it in the daytime 1000 times and in the night 1000 times. All this, with the suffumigation kept working. And when the fourteenth day comes, you will see the retreat filled with light, or you will see amid that light phantom shapes. So strengthen your heart and do not fear. And you will see the Name of Majesty take shape out of the light, until you see your spirit as though you were plunged in a sea of light. So strengthen your heart and make your heart steadfast; and you will not cease to be in that state for the measure of 3 hours. Then the servant-spirit of the names comes to you, until he fills the place upon you with his bulk. So do not fear him, for he is blessed; and beware of fearing him. Return the greeting of peace to him, and comport yourself with courtesy toward him, for he is a man of mighty station and majestic worth. And you will find him uttering the Name of Majesty and the noble verse every day after the prayers. And he appoints a servant-spirit to your obedience, who will comply with your command. So give him thanks, and say to him: May God reward your endeavour, and forgive us and you, by His favour and His generosity.
Depart, rewarded; may God recompense you with the Garden, by His generosity and His favour; truly He is powerful over what He wills. And peace.
*I mention the invocation of Laṭīf (the Subtle)*

Know — may God grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that when you desire to recite it for some matter or other, then pray two rakʿas with the intention of what you want, whether the relieving of anxiety and distress, or the release of a prisoner, or whatever you want. And when you desire one of the operations, then pray two rakʿas with the Fātiḥa and Have We not expanded your breast for you?(Q 94:1). And when you have finished the prayer, you say Laṭīf 16,641 times, and that is the great number. And if you want it for the relieving of anxiety or distress or the like of that, you say it the aforementioned number, and then you supplicate for what you want; and it will be answered for you, if God, exalted is He, wills. And if you want it for the destruction of a wrongdoer, then you recite the name Laṭīf the aforementioned number, and after that you supplicate with this cry for succour (istighātha). You say: O God, You are al-Qādir (the Powerful), al-Qāhir (the Subduer), possessor of subjugation and of severe assault. My God, a servant from among Your servants has transgressed against me and behaved tyrannically, and You are the Judge, the Just. I have brought suit against him before You, and I have put my trust in You for the lifting of the wrong done me by him. So send down upon him an affliction which the people of the heavens and the earth are powerless to repel, until he knows the worth of Your blessing and of Your granting of well-being to him. And fix fast upon his crown the fixing of the stones of baked clay upon the Companions of the Elephant; and overturn him, and confound him, and cleave him asunder, and destroy him, and cast him down headlong, and seize him. So God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God (Q 40:21). Then you say /fol. 104v./
They sacrificed a grey-haired man who bore the mark of prostration upon him, one who would cut through the night with glorification and Qurʾān.
You shall surely hear a clamour in their houses: God is greatest! O vengeance for ʿUthmān!

and the women who wail over him. God destroyed them, and for the disbelievers are the likes thereof (Q 47:10). So they became such that nothing was to be seen but their dwellings (Q 46:25). God destroyed them (Q 47:10). Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the Companions of the Elephant?(Q 105:1) Did He not make their scheming go astray?(Q 105:2) And He sent against them birds in flocks, pelting them with stones of baked clay (Q 105:3–4) and made them like devoured chaff (Q 105:5). And after that you say: God is subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty (Q 42:19). You recite it 129 times. And after it you say Yā Laṭīf, with the yāʾ of address, 100 times. And you say also Yā Laṭīf 29 times upon a single breath. And you are to be in a state of ablution from the beginning of the operation to its end; and do not speak to anyone during the time of your operation and your reciting until you finish. And if you do speak, you repeat the operation from the beginning, step by step. And beware of saying: "I wonder — will it come out right or not?" For if you say that, you will never profit by it. And let your intention be good, being certain of God, exalted is He, as to the swiftness of the answer.
