And when you have done that, your need succeeds and is fulfilled, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you add to it this blessed supplication, that is better. And this is what you say: O God, I ask You, O Subtle One above every subtle one, O You whose subtlety embraces the people of the heavens and the people of the earth. O God, I ask You that You show subtlety toward me out of the hidden [depth] of Your hidden subtlety (3 times), that [subtlety] which, when You show it toward any of Your creation, suffices him (3 times). For You have said, and Your word is the truth: Does He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware (Q 67:14). God is subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty (Q 42:19). And you say this supplication 129 times. And this is the form of the wafq of Laṭīf.

I mention the spiritual discipline of "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty"

And the manner of its discipline: you recite [it] after each prayer 544 times, except at the night prayer (ʿishāʾ), where the number is 547; so that the completion of the aforementioned number for the five prayers is 2723 times. Then, after finishing the litany (wird) following the night prayer, you recite this supplication whose mention now follows 3 times, together with constant adherence [to it] on Friday. And it is this blessed supplication. You say: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. By it may my tongue be made pure and my heart be made steadfast. I ask You, O Provider for the creeping things, Anchorer of the mountains, Mover of the winds, Setter of the seas in their course. O Light of light, O Light before every light! I ask You by Your mighty bounty, O radiance of every light, One, Eternal Refuge, Everlasting for ever. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He does not disclose /fol. 105r./ His unseen to anyone (cf. Q 72:26, conflated with the standing formula ʿālim al-ghayb wa-l-shahāda, "Knower of the unseen and the witnessed", Q 6:73 etc.). And He has not taken a child (Q 25:2). I have called upon You by Your Name — Sarīʿ (Swift), Qarīb (Near). Thanks be to God. O ʿAynyāʾīl, by the way of guidance; and worship belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, the First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden, the Knower of every soul and of its guidance. O ʿAynyāʾīl, you are of the noble angels, and I am of humankind, the more excellent by the bounty of God; and prostration belongs to God. I adjure you by the blessing of the Throne, and by the Lote-tree of the Boundary, and by the face of ʿAzrāʾīl, the seizer of the creation of the heavens and the earths. I adjure you by Him who knows the belly of the sea and what is in it, and the wind and what it drives along, and the clouds and what comes upon them, and the dust of mercies and all the pools, that you make subservient to me a servant-spirit from before you who will obey my command — from among those who course through the folds of the earth, the most finely wrought of them in nature and the fairest of them in address, that they may address me. They worship none but God, and I put my trust in Him, One, Unique, having no partner in His dominion. O servant-spirits of the Tree, whose beginning is 40 branches divided out of 4 boughs, whose fruits are glorification, sanctification, and the profession of divine oneness; whose glorification is: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty." You hold fast to that for 21 days; and if he does not come, then 40 days — and the object sought has been attained. And peace.
*And likewise I mention after it the invocation of Ḥayy Qayyūm (the Living, the Self-Subsisting)*

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him — that as for this invocation: when you desire to work with it, you recite the two noble names 1000 times, and after that you recite the blessed supplication 3 times or 7 times. And then you supplicate for what you want — the easing of provision, and the understanding of a science, and the understanding of a secret, and other than that wherein God has good pleasure. And it is this blessed supplication. You say: O Ḥayy (Living One), O You to whom life is ascribed, and there is no object of worship besides Him among what He has ascribed to Himself! Your names have been magnified — glory be to You — and have been declared free of the things named; and Your Essence has been magnified above likeness, and partner, and peer, and consort, and vizier. So You are the Living for ever, the Eternal Refuge in Your everlasting life; and life has spread forth from Your life. You are the Abiding: to You belongs the everlasting subsistence after the passing away of created things.

And just as subsistence belongs to You while Your servants are those who perish, so Your command, O my God, is effective, and Your judgement has none to oppose it. For the singular ones have passed away, and the opposites have been routed, and the heretics have been subdued by the existence of Your subsistence and the perpetuity of Your life. O Living, O Self-Subsisting, I ask You by this everlasting life that You give me life with a life joined to blessings, and that You give life to my soul amid the world with a life from which I shall have sustaining supply and good fortune; and make me fortunate with a granted success from among the subtle strands (raqāʾiq) of Your name al-Ḥayy al-

Qayyūm (the Living, the Self-Subsisting); and conceal me by a subtle strand from among the subtle strands of Your name Allāh al-Ḥayy (God, the Living), until You efface from me the name of wretchedness and cause me to enter into the name of felicity, the circle of good fortune. /fol. 105v./ God effaces what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book (Q 13:39). O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O You by whose command the heavens and the earth stand fast, O You whose self-subsistence upholds the people of the heavens and the earth in length and in breadth, and by what we know, and by what we do not know, and by that of which You are the Knower — by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful. And if you wish to add to this supplication, you say: O God, if my provision is in the heaven, then send it down; and if it is in the earth, then bring it forth; and if it is near, then make it easy; and if it is far, [then bring it near; and if it is little,] then make it abundant; and if it is abundant, then bless it, O God, and convey it to me wherever I may be, and do not convey me to it wherever it may be; and bring it to me out of Your bounty and Your generosity, by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them peace.
*A supplication of Laṭīf, in another mode*

You say Laṭīf 129 [times]. Then after it you recite this blessed supplication; and it is recited after the dawn prayer. And he says "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" seven times. Then you say "God is Subtle with His servants" (cf. Q 42:19) seven times. And you say: O God, O You who has made subservient the seven heavens and the seven earths and whoever is within them and whoever is upon them, make subservient to me every thing of Your servants, of what is in Your dry land and in Your sea, so that there be nothing in existence, moving or at rest, silent or speaking, outward or inward, but that You have made it subservient to me, by the blessing of Your name al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), the treasured. O God, O Living, O Self-Subsisting. His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say "Be", and it is (Q 36:82). My God, Your munificence has guided me to You, and Your beneficence has brought me near to You. I complain to You of that which is not hidden from You, and I ask You for that which is not hard for You, since Your knowledge of my state dispenses with my asking. O You who relieves the distressed of his distress, relieve me of what I am in. O You who is not absent, that I should await Him, nor asleep, that I should wake Him, nor heedless, that I should remind Him, nor incapable, that I should grant Him respite. O Knower of the whole, O One who has no need of the detail: Your knowledge suffices in place of speech, and suffices in place of asking. Hope is cut off save from You; expectations are disappointed save in You; and the roads are barred save the road to You. O God, O Hearing, O Seeing, O Near, O Answering, forgive me and have mercy upon me, by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful; and make easy for me my provision, and make subservient to me the whole of Your creation; truly You are powerful over everything. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them peace. And know that these names and this cry for succour (istighātha) profit the distressed and the sorrowful, and whoever is worried, or grieved, or in fear of someone, or of a ruler, or of other than that. Let him recite them as we have mentioned, with their conditions, for he is answered on the spot, with the help of God, exalted is He.
I mention after it the invocation of the sura Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1), and its adjuration, its angels, and its servant-spirits

Know — may God grant you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — and that is that you recite the sura Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1) three times, after performing the ablution fully, and with complete purity, and abundant perfume, that is, /fol. 106r./ choice perfume; and the suffumigation is kept working, and it is everything possessed of a sweet scent. Then you recite the adjuration of the sura, for in it is a mighty secret; and it is this blessed adjuration. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O mountains, echo [the praise] with him, and you birds! And We softened iron for him (Q 34:10). Even so, O Master of masters, may the hearts of all created beings together, of jinn and of humankind, be made soft toward me, by the right of this noble sura and by the right of these blessed names: Malakī Kūndī Mīḥānast Bīkām Anwalsān Nabdīdā Anast Mārāmzakasar Markīntī Razah Anast Dunyānā. Everyone upon it is perishing (Q 55:26). I ask You, O God, that You make subservient to me the kingdom and the

Dominion (malakūt), until they look toward me submissive, with lowliness and awe and love; and by the right of they love them as [they should] love God; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165), had you spent all that is in the earth, you would not have united their hearts; but God united them; truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). I ask You, O God, that You make the decree and the determination and the revolving sphere run according to my desire, and that You make my awe and my love course in the hearts of the two weighty species, humankind and jinn. Ṣabūt — by the routing of the armies at [the charge of] the rider. God has written: I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers; truly God is Strong, Mighty (Q 58:21). And the king said: Bring him to me, that I may attach him to myself. And when he had spoken with him, he said: Today you are with us established in rank and trusted (Q 12:54), up to His word, exalted is He, and God prevails over His affair (Q 12:21). And We gave him means to everything (Q 18:84). Ṭasūm. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help (Q 1:5). This very hour! Quickly! Help from God and a near victory; and give good tidings to the believers (Q 61:13). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And this adjuration and the sura are of profit for weighty affairs, and for the routing of an army, and for the breaking of enemies, and for victory over the envious and the hateful. And the reciting of it profits and intercedes; and it is called al-Munjiya (the Deliverer). And it is thirty verses, so know its worth, for it is among the greatest of benefits. And we have brought forth and pointed to some of its occult properties. So understand. And God knows best.
I mention the invocation of Have We not expanded your breast for you?(Q 94:1)

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that the reciting of this sura has wondrous occult properties. So when you wish to operate with it, you fast for God three days, and you supplicate with the supplication seventy times, and the noble Fātiḥa likewise seventy times, and the noble sura seventy times. You say: Muḥammad, Muḥammad — seventy times. For the servant-spirit will come to you, bringing independence of created beings; and if you give him leave, he will convey you to Mecca in the swiftest time; and whatever you seek of him, he answers you and accomplishes it for you swiftly, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And the name of the servant-spirit is Daryāʾīl. And this is the adjuration. You say: I ask You, O Light of the divine lights, [who is] before the ages and the perishing times, the Active Substance without model, the All-Holy, the Pure, the High, the Overpowering, whom no place encompasses and to whom /fol. 106v./ no place is obscure, the Bringer-into-being of places and ages and times. Blessed are You, beyond the substance of the divine nature, the pre-eternal, everlasting lights. O Lord, clothe me from Yourself with the wellspring of the life of the spiritual spirits, qualified by the exalted power, the attribute that has no [peer]. O Creator, O Maker, and [I ask You] by what is not seen of the greatness of Your power, so that the cherubim (al-karūbiyyūn) have not the strength to raise their faces out of the veils of Your light. I ask You, O Lord, by [Your] perpetuity, by the greatness of the divine power, and by the might of Lordship, that You deliver me from the sea of this perishing creation, and that You cause me to look upon the true secrets hidden from created beings, which You bestow in grace upon Your well-pleasing servants, who seek the abode of subsistence, who forsake the abode of perishing, who are of one kind with the pure spirits. O God, turn away from me the perishing maladies, by the wondrousness of Your power and the greatness of Your majesty and the light of Your face within the holiness of Your lights. Single me out among the singular ones (afrād), and preserve me from consorting with rivals and from partnership with opposites, and cause me to look upon the hidden subtleties. O You who has robed Yourself in fidelity and in grandeur, O High, O Most High, O First of the first ones, truly You are powerful over everything. He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner (Q 59:24), to the end of the sura. Then after that you take a comb and suffumigate it, and comb your beard with it; and everyone who sees you will love you with an intense love and be submissive to you. And the suffumigation is benzoin (lubān jāwī). So fear God, and know the worth of what has reached you of the good of this world. And we have opened the door for you, so ponder it; and conceal your secret, and you will attain your object. And peace.
And likewise the invocation of Have We not expanded (Q 94:1), by another method

Know, O my brother — may God grant us and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that this noble invocation I have taken from the noble shaykhs, and that it has wondrous occult properties, the discussion of which will follow. And this is the description of the noble invocation. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You by "Have We not expanded your breast for you?" (Q 94:1). O God, that You expand for me my breast by the Name with which You expanded the heart of Your prophet Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace. Yā Salām (O Peace) — 3; Yā Muʾmin (O Granter of Security) — 3; Yā Allāh (O God) — 3. I ask You by the right of our master Muḥammad, whom You addressed with Your word and We removed from you your burden (Q 94:2). O God, O God, O God, I ask You by Your pre-eternal speech and by Your noble prophet, upon whom You sent down which weighed down your back (Q 94:3). I ask You, O God, O God, O God, O Manifest, O Hidden, from whom my state is not concealed, O You whom eyesight does not grasp (cf. Q 6:103), conceal me from the eyes of the wrongdoers, and suffice me against the evil of all Your creation. O God, O God, O God, I ask You by Your name with which You raised the rank of Your servant, the quintessence of Your creation and the lord /fol. 107r./ of Your messengers, so that You are not mentioned but that he is mentioned along with You, and by which You sent down the manifestation of the greatness of Your favour upon him: and We raised high for you your remembrance (Q 94:4). O Raiser, O Rememberer, remember me with the remembrance of those who remember, who remember God standing and sitting and upon their sides, and who reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You, so guard us from the punishment of the Fire (Q 3:191). O God, O God, O God, suffice me against the evil of the wrongdoers, and suffice me against the evil of enemies and of the envious, by the sanctity of the lord of all creation, our master Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace, the seal of the prophets, upon whom You sent down for truly with hardship comes ease; truly with hardship comes ease (Q 94:5–6). O You who has ordained hardship between two eases, appoint for me from every hardship an ease, and from every straitness a joy, and from every worry a way out, by the right of our master Muḥammad, the most excellent of created beings and the lord of the people of the earth and the heavens, upon whom You sent down, among these verses, so when you have finished, labour on; and to your Lord direct your longing (Q 94:7–8). I ask You, O God, by our master Muḥammad and his brethren the prophets and the messengers, and the angels brought near, and the family of our master Muḥammad and his companions and the followers, and all the rest of Your righteous servants, that You ward off from me

— the eyes of the wrongdoers, and that You suffice me against the evil of enemies and enviers; and that You subject to me the spiritual beings of this sura for the attracting of provisions and the inclining of hearts towards me; and that You grant me as provision the things that give joy, and repel from me the things that harm. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh! O Laṭīf (the Subtle), O Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), O Wadūd (the Loving), O Ḥayy (the Living), O Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O Mubdiʾ (the Originator), O Muʿīd (the Restorer)! O Possessor of the Glorious Throne, O Doer of what He wills, O Possessor of the mighty assault! I ask You, O God, by Your might that cannot be assailed, and by Your kingship that cannot be wronged. I ask You by Your light that has pervaded existence. I ask You by Your power, by which You have power over all Your creation. I ask You by Your mercy, which embraces all things. There is no god but You; by Your mercy I seek succour. O Succour of those who seek succour, succour us! And Dhū l-Nūn, when he went off in anger and thought that We would have no power over him; then he called out in the darknesses: There is no god but You; glory be to You! Truly I have been among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87) — up to His words We deliver the believers (Q 21:88). O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm: in You I seek succour! O Succour of those who seek succour: so set right for me my whole affair, and do not entrust me to myself for the blink of an eye, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. O God, truly I ask You by everything that is set apart as Yours, and by every special property that is Yours, and by Your munificence overflowing upon them, that You grant me as provision perfection, and soundness of state, and good fortune, and prosperity — myself, and my family, and my children, and my dependants; and grant us well-being from every ailment, and preserve us from every affliction, and guard us from every act of disobedience, and every calamity, and every misfortune. O Possessor of sublime gifts! O You who stretch out both hands with mercy and with giving! And may God bless our master Muḥammad, the best of creation, and his family and his companions, and grant them peace. Know, then, that this invocation, magnificent in worth /fol. 107v./ — we have abridged its occult properties. Know that whoever recites this noble sura, seeking some need among needs wherein there is God's good pleasure, let him recite it twenty-one times after praying two rakʿas; and you sit in the squatting posture (qurfuṣāʾ) and recite it the number stated. Then, when you have finished, you recite the supplication three times and ask God, exalted is He, for your need; for it shall be fulfilled, if God, exalted is He, wills, by His favour and His generosity. And God speaks the truth and guides to the way.
I mention the exposition of the five noble verses, in each verse of which there are ten qāfs

Know — may God grant me and you success in obeying Him — that there was a sultan among the sultans of former times who had a vizier, and that sultan wished to kill the vizier. Now the sultan had conveyed instruction to the executioner that, when the vizier came forward and he gave him the signal for the killing of the vizier, he should strike off his neck. Yet whenever the vizier came in to the sultan, that hatred would be changed, effaced by the leave of God, exalted is He, … from him inwardly; and he would then command the executioner to withdraw until the morrow. And the king continued in that condition for many days, being every day intent upon killing the vizier; but whenever the vizier came in to him and his eye fell upon his eye, God, exalted is He, would change that first condition, effacing it. [So it went on] until one day among the days the king rode out, and the vizier rode with him, and the two went forth travelling. And when they were upon a certain road, the king drew near to the vizier and then laid his hand upon the vizier's neck and said to him: O vizier, I wish to ask you about something, so fear nothing at all from me. The vizier said: O our master the sultan, ask about whatever occurs to you, for I shall speak truthfully to you concerning what you ask me about, if God, exalted is He, wills. The sultan said: Know, O vizier, that there is no day but that I harbour for you slaying and destruction, and I bring the executioner near to me and say to him: When the vizier comes forward and I give you the signal, strike off his neck. Yet when you come forward to me and I look upon you with my eye, that hatred is changed at that very time and moment, effaced. So inform me, and speak the truth, for I have pardoned you, and there remains in my inward being nothing of hatred for you. Do you have anything of litanies (awrād) and supplications by which you pray? Inform me of that. The vizier said: O our master the sultan, know that I had a jurist (faqīh) who used to teach me the Qurʾān, and one day the faqīh said to me: Memorize these five verses, for in each verse ten qāfs have been gathered. For everyone who persists in the recitation of these five verses before sunrise and before sunset, God, exalted is He, looks upon him. And if a king or a sultan recites these five verses, God, exalted is He, increases him in his kingship and grants him protection, [extending] to his retinue and his subjects. And if a poor man recites them, God, exalted is He, enriches him. And if one who has a need recites them and calls upon God, exalted is He, /fol. 108r./ after reciting them, then God, exalted is He, fulfils his need at its due time. And whoever persists in reciting them will be held in awe by all people, beloved among them, his word and his speech accepted, and everyone who sees him will stand in awe of him. And these five verses are as you see.

The first verse is in Sūrat al-Baqara, His words, exalted is He: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: Raise up for us a king, that we may fight in the way of God? He said: Might it be that, if fighting were prescribed for you, you would not fight? They said: And what is it to us that we should not fight in the way of God, when we have been driven from our dwellings and our sons? Yet when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, save a few of them; and God knows the wrongdoers (Q 2:246).

The second verse is in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, His words, exalted is He: God has indeed heard the speech of those who said: God is poor and we are rich. We shall write down what they said, and their slaying of the prophets without right; and We shall say: Taste the punishment of the burning (Q 3:181). That is for what your hands have sent forward, and because God is not unjust towards [His] servants (Q 3:182).

The third verse is in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, His words, exalted is He: Have you not considered those to whom it was said: Restrain your hands, and perform the prayer, and give the alms? Then, when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them feared men as they fear God, or with a still greater fear, and said: Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You would grant us respite for a near term! Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the hereafter is better for him who is godfearing; and you shall not be wronged by so much as the thread of a date-stone (Q 4:77).

The fourth verse is in Sūrat al-Māʾida, His words, exalted is He: And recite to them the tiding of the two sons of Adam, when they offered up a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other. He said: I shall surely kill you. He said: God accepts only from the godfearing (Q 5:27).

The fifth verse is in Sūrat al-Raʿd, His words, exalted is He: Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: God. Say: Have you then taken, apart from Him, protectors who possess for themselves neither benefit nor harm? Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darknesses and the light equal? Or have they assigned to God associates who have created as He created, so that the creating seemed alike to them? Say: God is the Creator of every thing, and He is the One, the Overpowering (Q 13:16).

Know — may God grant me and you success in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that when one of those in authority wishes to fight a people, and when the time of his entering into the war has come and his intent is victory over them by the help of God, exalted is He, let him perform the ablution and pray two rakʿas. Then let him pick up from the ground seven pebbles the size of chickpeas, picking up each pebble with one of the letters of Faqaj Makhmat. Then let him place them in the palm of his left hand. He takes one pebble from them with his right hand and recites over it the first noble verse ten times; then he raises his right hand with the pebble over which he has recited, and says Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not (Q 2:18), and he flings it in front of him. Then he takes another pebble with his right hand and recites over it the second verse ten times; then he raises his hand and says Did you then suppose that We created you in vain, and that to Us you would not (Q 23:115), and then he flings it behind him. /fol. 108v./ Then he takes another pebble with his right hand and recites over it the third verse ten times; then he raises his hand and says And We have set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them over, so they do not (Q 36:9), and he flings the pebble to his right. Then he takes with his right hand, from his left, a pebble, and recites over it the fourth verse ten times, and says O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the confines of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond! You shall not (Q 55:33), and then he flings it to his left. There remain behind in his hand three pebbles, which he places upon his head; and he enters the fray and comes out of it, and no evil whatever shall ever reach him, absolutely, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among its occult properties also: if you fear an enemy and are in a place of fear, then you take from the ground seven pebbles and say, as you take them, Faqaj Makhmat. Then he throws a pebble and says what he said before; and he throws them to his right and to his left, and behind him and in front, as we have mentioned. Then he sits upon the ground and says Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1) over the fingers of his right hand and closes his hand; and he says Ḥāʾ-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2) over the fingers of his left hand and closes his hand. Then he keeps silent and does not speak; and were the whole nation of the two weighty species (humankind and jinn) to come in upon him, they would not see him, and God, exalted is He, will hide him from them; and no one shall look upon him but that he stands in awe of him and magnifies him. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best. And that is the form of the blessed wafq, magnificent in worth.

A blessed fāʾida, if God, exalted is He, wills. Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in the understanding of His secrets — that whoever recites Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa after the afternoon prayer fourteen times, and the Most Beautiful Names of God the like of that; and that is that he recites this blessed supplication, then persists in reciting it for a week or two weeks — then God, exalted is He, opens for him the door of wealth and provides for him from whence he does not reckon. And it is this blessed supplication, magnificent in worth. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, truly I ask You by the magnificent, the eternal, the generous, the treasured store of Your names; and by the classes of the kinds of the genera of the ciphers of the engravings of Your lights; and by the mighty exaltation of Your might; and by the power of the largesse of the severity of Your strength; and by the measure of the mastery of Your power; and by the confirmation of the glorification of the beautification of Your magnificence; and by the sublimity of the increase of the elevation of Your exaltedness; and by the ever-subsisting perpetuity of Your everlastingness; and by the good pleasure of the security of the gracious bestowal of Your forgiveness; and by the lofty, the wondrous, the impregnable [might] of Your sovereignty; and by the blessing and the inclining of the outspread expanse of Your mercy; and by the gleamings of the lightning-flashes of the thunderbolts, the clamour and the raging, the resplendent, the dust-raising, of Your flashing forth; and by the dazzling and the overpowering of the auspicious [might] of Your oneness; and by the roaring and the spray of the waves of Your sea that encompasses Your Dominion; and by the breadth and the expansiveness of the field of the isthmuses (barāzikh) of Your Footstool; and by the celestial spiritual beings of the angels of Your Throne; and by the angels, the spiritual ones who govern

— to the stars of the celestial spheres; and by the yearning of the stilling of those who desire Your forgiveness; and by the burnings of the sighs of the steps of those who fear Your assaults; and by the bond of the bestowal granted to those who strive after Your good pleasure; and by the glorification of the exaltation of those who lead [others] to Your obedience. O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden, O Eternal, O Establisher: efface, by the talisman of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate", by the secret of Mahād Sūrīd, the hearts of our enemies and of Your enemies; and crush the heads of the oppressors with the keen blades of the swords of the arising of the subjugation of Your assaults; and veil us with Your impregnable veils from the glances of the flashings of their weak eyes, by Your might and Your power; and pour down upon us Your good pleasure from the pipes of the conduits of [Your] granting of success, in the watches of the night and at the ends of the day; and immerse us in the flowing channels of Your goodness and Your mercy; and fetter us with the fetters of safety from falling into disobedience of You. O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden, O Eternal, O Establisher, O Forbearing, O All-Knowing. O God: the intellects are dumbfounded, the understandings are hemmed in, the imaginings are lost, the conjectures are altered, the thoughts are bewildered, and the passing notions fall short of grasping the innermost reality of the modality of what has appeared of the first flashes of the lights of the marvels of Your power — let alone of attaining to the glittering of the flashings of Your countenance. O God, Mover of motions and Changer of stillnesses, Cleaver of the deaf, hard, firmly anchored rocks and Causer to gush forth from them of flowing water for the created things; Giver of life to all animals and plants; Knower of what stirs within their inmost secret, through the utterance of the hidden signs of the tongues of the roaming ants, and [Knower] of him who magnifies /fol. 109v./ and hallows and glorifies and declares [Your] oneness and proclaims [Your] greatness, by the majesty of the perfection of the Throne of the angels of Your seven heavens: make us, in this blessed hour, among those who called upon You and You answered him, and who asked You and You gave him, and who humbled himself before You and You had mercy upon him, and who sought of You release from his sins and You released him, by Your bounty and Your beneficence. O Munificent One, O Possessor of bounty and munificence and eternal beneficence. — You recite [this] 7 times. — O God, deal with us according to what You are worthy of, and do not deal with us according to what we are worthy of; truly You are the One worthy to be feared and worthy to forgive (cf. Q 74:56). O God, we cannot number the praise due to You; You are as You have praised Yourself. Majestic is Your Face, mighty is he who is under Your protection, and exalted is Your praise. God does what He wills by His power, and decrees what He desires by His might. O Living One, O Self-Subsisting, O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth, with You I seek succour, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Magnificent. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.
I mention this noble circle and the wondrous and mighty secrets that belong to it

Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that this noble circle is called the Circle of Lights (dāʾirat al-anwār), and it is a wondrous secret; so look upon it with the eye of inner discernment. And when you wish to summon whomever you will to your dwelling, then draw this circle, as I shall set it forth to you, upon paper, and write upon it the name of the one sought [and] the name of his mother, in the small circle. Then you place the sheet upon an eastern wall. Then you drive into the letter (alif) a fine iron nail, and you recite the conjuration 7 times while you fumigate with grains of male frankincense, saffron filaments, ḥabb raml, musk-sukk, and Javanese benzoin (lubān jāwī). And if the one sought is slow in coming to you, then shift the nail to the letter (bāʾ); and you keep shifting it from letter to letter, while you fumigate and conjure, until the one sought presents himself at one of those letters — the letter whose servant-spirit has brought him. Then you summon him by that letter and by that servant-spirit every time you wish to have him brought to you. And if the one sought is on a journey, then nail into every letter a fine nail, and recite the conjuration 7 times, and reckon the distance of the road; for he will present himself.

And know that this circle requires neither a [particular] time nor a [particular] hour, provided his heart be free of preoccupation. So draw it, and invoke your desire at the pole (quṭb), and say after the conjuration: Yā Malik (O King), Yā Qadīm (O Eternal) — 260 times; and your desire is obtained, if God, exalted is He, wills. And this conjuration is the conjuration of the letters. You say: In the name of God, the All-Holy, the Pure, the High — Mashlaḥaj — He is the Overpowering, the Lord — Shīshalakhakh Shalshalghalṭājūrab — the Lord of the ages everlasting and of the times, the Determiner of /fol. 110r./ the appointed moments, whose kingship does not shift and does not pass away, Possessor of towering might and of lofty majesty. And by His names I have called upon you, O you possessors of all the spiritual spirits, apportioned over the natures of the luminous letters, that you take charge of what I have commanded you — the drawing of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] to So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — by the right of these luminous names: Yaṭfar Ṭayhāṭaf Hayshafṭashahūh HalfīṭRīḥīf Ṭayhūb Hayz Lakhshaṭaf — every thing has shone forth at His name and every living being has answered His call — Ṭarfaqash Hashrāṭ, and the assault that overcomes every thing, Halnānīʿ Aslalīmūt Khūʿaṭashṭūhan Shahfīgh ShafūṣAsṭaʿṭanaj — You are the wellspring of the life of every spirit — Ḥajhashaʿṭalyālaf — no spirit has heard Your name and disobeyed it but that it was struck down and burned — TashaʿlāytaḥKhaṭahīṭah Arkhaṭīhayraṭahyah. Answer, O noble spirits, servant-spirits of these mighty letters, by the right of that by which I have adjured you! Take charge, O Ṭūniyāʾīl, and you, O ʿAshlahiyāʾīl, and you, O Ṭafiyāʾīl, and you, O ʿAmṣāʾīl, by subjugating the servant-spirits of these noble letters, that they may fulfil my needs and bring me the object I seek, of what I have named to you in this circle — the drawing of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together; indeed God is powerful over everything (Q 2:148). And He is powerful to gather them whenever He wills (Q 42:29). Come now, come now! Haste, haste! Speed, speed! This very hour, this very hour! By the right of what I have recited to you of the names and of the spiritual kings. May God, exalted is He, bless you and pour blessing upon you.

And know, O seeker — may God, glorified and exalted, grant me and you success in obedience to Him — that this gateway [of practice] is exceedingly mighty, so do not perform it save in what is lawful. And beware of following the ignorant, for this is the book of the friends of God and of the righteous. So fear God, glorified and exalted; and if you perform it in other than what is lawful, then you are held answerable for it before God, glorified and exalted. And here I have discharged it from my neck, and it has come to rest upon your neck, O you who attain to this mighty circle. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And this is the noble circle, as you see. Understand that, and you will be rightly guided. /fol. 110v./
[Circle diagram: the Circle of Lights (dāʾirat al-anwār), with its letters, as in the source — ] [Fig. 62]

Faṣl. Know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that the spiritual discipline of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣand its invocation is of majestic worth, and it is among the things to which certain of the elect among the men of excellence have drawn attention. It is related of the shaykh ʿAbd al-

Wāḥid al-Andalusī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he said: Truly I remained for a span of years asking the people of knowledge about the spiritual discipline of Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1). And a certain person said to me: In noble Mecca there is a shaykh named Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-ʿIrāqī, who has dwelt beside the noble Sanctuary for a span of years, and this spiritual discipline is from him. So I made ready /fol. 111r./ [and set out] from the lands of the Maghrib, until I reached Egypt; and I turned toward the noble land of the Ḥijāz, and I stayed there a year as a dweller beside [the Sanctuary]; and I gained access to that man, and I offered him a splendid gift, and I stayed a span of time keeping his company, and I did not broach with him anything of that. And when the companionship between me and him had grown long, and we sat one day discussing the matter of the spiritual discipline and what certain of the friends of God — may God be pleased with them — had mentioned to me concerning the wayfaring in it, and that the root of [all] matters is the pious fear of God, exalted is He, and purity of intention, and sincerity, and the seeking of the abode of the hereafter and of the highest degree with those upon whom God has bestowed favour — of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous; and how excellent are these as companions!(Q 4:69) — then the shaykh — may God have mercy upon him — said to me of his own accord: By God, O my brother ʿAbd al-Wāḥid, I am in no blessing and no good save from the spiritual discipline of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. So I smiled. And he said to me: What is this smiling of yours? Do you mock what I have said to you? I said: God, exalted is He, forbid! And how should I mock an attribute of the All-Merciful, mighty and majestic, exalted, the Lord of might and magnificence? And I said: the cause of my smiling is that, by God, I sought you out from the lands of the Maghrib and kept your company only on its account. He said: Do you say so, by the right of the Lord of this House? I said: Yes. So he said to me: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever seeks us out, his right becomes incumbent upon us.)) And I am a follower of his word and hold fast to his sacred law: since you have sought me out, your right has become incumbent upon me. And you are without doubt of the people of good and of the people of righteousness, and you are of the people of knowledge; for you sought me out from far lands, and you possess a beautiful patience — for you have been [here] a span of time and have not made known to me the cause of your keeping my company, which indicates the abundance of your intellect and the excellence of your discernment. Truly, by the Lord of this House, I shall not withhold it from you. So I kissed his hand, and he kissed my head. Then he said: Tomorrow morning, if God, exalted is He, wills, I shall set it forth to you and make known to you its method. So I supplicated for him for a goodly outcome; and I did not sleep that night, out of joy. And when morning came, I went early to the Kaʿba, and I prayed the dawn prayer and circumambulated the House; and there was the shaykh, sitting in his place of yesterday. So I came to him and kissed his hand, and he said: Do you know what I am saying to you and what I am indicating to you? I said: No, by God. He said: By God, my shaykh ʿAbd al-Ṣamad al-Khwārizmī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — imparted to me names which I recite at the time of sleep 10 times, and I invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — 10 times, and I ask God, exalted is He, for the unveiling of what I desire; and it is unveiled to me by the blessing of these noble names. And truly I did that this night, and I asked God, exalted is He, concerning your affair /fol. 111v./ — and whether your intent in this noble spiritual discipline is a worldly intent, and whether I should act or not act in my giving it to you. And I saw my shaykh ʿAbd al-Ṣamad al-Khwārizmī in sleep, and he said to me: O Abū ʿAbd Allāh, you have asked concerning the state of ʿAbd al-Wāḥid and what your intent is on his account regarding the noble spiritual discipline: do not turn him back from it, for he is of the people of good and is worthy of it. But take a covenant of him to guard it and to conceal it from those unworthy of it, and make known to him that whenever he alters his intention there will befall him from its servant-spirits grievous harm — and we ask God for well-being and safety. Then he said to me: Convey to him my greeting of peace. ʿAbd al-Wāḥid said: So I wept a great weeping, and I prostrated to God, exalted is He, in thanksgiving. Then he took a covenant of me at the Black Stone that I should not convey this mighty secret to any unworthy of it, and he enjoined upon me the pious fear of God, exalted is He. Then the shaykh handed me a leaf in which was written the description of this blessed spiritual discipline; and behold, written in it was: Whoever desires the spiritual discipline of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, let him take to deliverance, let him take to sincerity, and let him purify himself and perform the full ablution, and let him sit in a place empty of people, such that he speaks to no one of the creation of

God, exalted is He, during the aforementioned period. And let the one who serves him be a righteous man, sincere in the service. So guard carefully over purity and cleanliness; and let him fast, for the spiritual discipline, [beginning] the first Thursday of the month, in whatever month it may be; and let him carry [it] through in purity and cleanliness, and let him carry his fast through 15 days, a fast [broken] upon what is not possessed of a soul. And let his breaking of the fast be upon barley bread, salt, and oil. And you recite the noble sura every day 5000 times: after every obligatory prayer 1000 times, and at midnight 1000 times, for a period of 14 days, so that their number comes to 84,000 times. And the remainder of its times [is to be spent] with whatever is made easy of recitation, of the litany of remembrance, and of blessing upon the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace. And the suffumigation is kept working night and day; and the composition of the suffumigation is nadd aloeswood and grains of Javanese benzoin (ḥaṣā lubān jāwī). And when it is the eve of Friday — [that is] the sealing, and he has finished the reciting of it 16,000 times — then he supplicates with this blessed supplication. You say:

O God, truly I ask You, O Wāḥid (One), O Aḥad (Unique), O Fard (Single), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O You who have taken neither consort nor child, O You who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal (Q 112:3–4): I ask You that You subject to me the servant-spirits of this noble sura, that they may answer me unto what I desire; truly You are the Doer of what You will. Then you say: I adjure you, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, by the right of what you hold in belief — [I adjure you] only that you hasten the answer. Thereupon there enter in upon you three angels, their faces like the moon /fol. 112r./ on the night of the full moon at its completion; but their faces are large, like shields, and their light is as though it would snatch away the eyesight. And they say: Peace be upon you, O righteous servant, and the mercy of God and His blessings. We are the servant-spirits of this mighty sura; so what is it that you desire of us? So return the greeting of peace to them, and say: I desire — in honour, veneration, and magnification of Him whose description this sura is — that you serve me and obey me in what I command you, it being binding upon me that I desire of you nothing but a need that pleases the Lord. And they say to you: To hear is to obey. We have made good your oath and answered your invocation; but we have a condition upon you: that from this day of yours and this hour of yours you shall not fall into any act of disobedience nor into any lie; that you shall eat neither garlic, nor onion, nor fish; that you shall fast on Thursday always; that you shall recite, on that day and on the night — which is the eve of Friday — the sura 10,000 times, dedicating its reward to the dead among the Muslims; that you shall not break off the fast of Thursday unless it be the day of a feast; that you shall not omit the Friday washing; and that you shall visit the graves every Saturday before the rising of the sun, and recite it 11 times, and dedicate its reward to the dead among the Muslims. You say: Yes; and God is, over me, among those who bear witness to that. Thereupon they take you by the hand and say to you: You have become a brother to us, one of our brethren; so whatever need you request, we shall fulfil it for you, if God, exalted is He, wills. And you say to them: Give me — each one of you — a sign by which I may summon him. The first says to you: I — my name is ʿAbd al-Wāḥid. So recite the sura and say: O ʿAbd al-Wāḥid — and I shall answer you; and you have it binding upon me that I bear you to Mecca and return you to your dwelling in a single hour. And the second says to you: And I — my name is ʿAbd al-Ṣamad. So recite the sura and say: O ʿAbd al-Ṣamad — and I shall answer you, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and you have it binding upon me the bringing of whatever you desire of food and drink, and of silver and gold, from what is permitted of the earth and lawful. And the third says to you: And I — my name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. So recite the sura and say: O ʿAbd al-Raḥmān — and I shall answer you; and you have it binding upon me [in] three stipulations: the making to boil of the prepared waters, and that I hide you from the eyes of men, and that I bring you tidings from the [far] lands. Thereupon you prostrate yourself to God, exalted is He, in thanksgiving for this mighty blessing, and you say: May God give thanks for your endeavour, and may God, exalted is He, reward you with good. So guard it well and hide it from the ignorant, for this is a trust from me to you. And peace.
Faṣl, in which I mention the invocation of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣin another mode

Know [that as for] the operation with it: you betake yourself to a place empty of people, and purify your garments, your body, and your place, and you sit therein making remembrance of God, exalted is He. Then ask forgiveness /fol. 112v./ of God, exalted is He, the Magnificent, 100 times, and you bless the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace

— 100 times. Then you pray two rakʿas: you recite in the first the Fātiḥa once and al-Ikhlāṣ500 times, and in the second rakʿa Fātiḥat al-Kitāb once and al-Ikhlāṣ50 times. Then you make intimate colloquy and give the salutation. Then you set the suffumigation going, and it is male frankincense and benzoin (jāwī). Then you set your head upon your knees and recite Sūrat al-Humaza 100 times, with a righteous intention and presence of heart. And you aim at whomever you will, in whatever form you desire of the figures — such as a beast of prey, or one striking with a sword, or whatever you desire. And you repeat the operation until your need is fulfilled. And God, glorified is He, is the Granter of success.
Faṣl, in which I mention the noble Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣin another mode

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that when you desire the reciting of this noble sura, purify your garments, your body, and your place. Then you fast three days from everything possessed of a soul and from whatever issues from a soul. The beginning of your operation is to be on the day of Tuesday. And when it is the eve of Friday, you recite the noble sura 1000 times and you recite this blessed supplication. And when your reciting is complete, there enters in upon you three […] — so do not fear him. Then he greets you with peace; so return the greeting of peace to him, and magnify him, for he is an angel of majestic worth and station. And he says to you: What do you desire, O righteous servant? So request of him your need and what you desire, [and] he will fulfil it for you. And request of him a servant from among his servant-spirits, who shall be obedient to you in everything for which you deploy him; and take a sign from him. And when you desire a fulfilment, recite the sura and mention his name, and he will present himself before you; then deploy him in what you desire. And the suffumigation is benzoin (lubān jāwī). So fear God, exalted is He, and be sincere toward Him, and you will be rightly guided. And this is the form of the blessed invocation. You say:

O God, truly I ask You by the qāf of power (qudra) and encompassment (iḥāṭa), and by the lām of the Tablet (lawḥ) and of subtle kindness (luṭf), and by the hāʾ of awe (hayba) and of right guidance (hidāya), and by the wāw of sanctity (wilāya), that You make for me power and encompassment within the subtleties of the existents of the Tablet, rejoicing in the yāʾ of awe, rightly guided, guiding whomever You will to guide — You are the Guide of whoever seeks guidance of You. O You whose veiling embraces all directions, and [all] divestments, originated things, alterations, likeness, opposite, divisibility, and number: Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1). O One in the perpetuity of His eternal kingship, without alteration and without embodiment. O God, truly I ask You by the wāw of divine oneness (waḥdāniyya) and of unicity (wāḥidiyya), and by the bent alif (al-alif al-maʿṭūf), which is the root of the cyclical genesis, and by the ḥāʾ of pre-eternal Life, and by the dāl of everlasting Perpetuity — without limit, or time, or number, and without consort or child. You are /fol. 113r./ God, al-Wāḥid, al-Aḥad, al-Ṣamad. O God, make me one among the ones and a singular one among the singular ones, and supply me with a genesis from among the geneses of the spiritual being of the bent alif, that I may plunge, by the aid of that, into the seas of those brought near from among the singular ones; and give life to my soul by a wisdom-bearing breath from among Your breaths, and by a spiritual being replenished with the mighty sustaining supplies, that I may be one who hopes, of the people of felicity and of the granting of felicity, eminent among Your servants until the Day of the Return. O God, truly I ask You by the ṣād of truthfulness (ṣidq) and of patience (ṣabr), and the mīm of kingship (mulk) and of glory (majd), and by the yāʾ of wakefulness (yaqẓa) and of certainty (yaqīn), that You make me truthful, veracious, a man of truth (ṣiddīq), a possessor of kingship (mālik), glorious, glorifying, rising up in wakefulness, holding fast in certainty, replenished out of the greatness of Your generosity with a truthful friend from among Your angels, by whom I may seek help toward the wellbeing of my affair, worldly and otherworldly. And appoint for me a help toward that, without any hinderer bringing harm, for ever. He did not beget and was not begotten, and none is equal to Him (Q 112:3–4). O God, suffice me by the kāf of Your sufficiency (kifāya), that I may have recourse to none other than You among all Your creatures; and illumine me with the luminousness of that, that I may attain thereby the winning and the deliverance among Your servants brought near. Truly You are powerful over all things and worthy to answer, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. And this wafq is beneficial for what we have mentioned as belonging to this noble sura; and we have abridged the exposition of it, lest the discourse upon it grow long. And this is its form: [Wafq: cells as in the source — ]
I mention here a noble benefit

It has come in the noble hadith that a man came to the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — and said: ((O Messenger of God, this world has turned away from me and what my hand possesses has grown scant. And he — God bless him and grant him peace — said: Where are you with respect to the prayer of the angels and the glorification of created beings, whereby they are provided for? He said: And what is that, O Messenger of God? He said: Glory be to God the Magnificent. Glory be to Him unto whom one declares oneself quit of [all] power and strength. Glory be to Him the glorification of whom is a bounty upon whoever relies upon Him. Glory be to Him whom every thing glorifies with praise. Glory be to You; there is no god but You; and with Your praise. O You whom all glorify: take me in hand, for I am one who cannot endure. Then ask forgiveness of God, glorified and exalted, 100 times; and you do that between the dawn prayer and the Friday prayer.)) And it is related from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: ((Say: O God, veil me with well-being in this world and in the hereafter.)) And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Whoever says every day 100 times "There is no god but God, the King, the Real, the Manifest", he opens thereby the gates of provision, and it drives poverty away from him, and he knocks thereby upon the gates of the Garden, and he is guarded thereby against the trial of the grave, and this world comes to him submissive; and God, exalted is He, creates from every word an angel who glorifies God, exalted is He, and asks forgiveness for his sins.)) And this is the end of what is adduced here. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 410
The sixth name is Bazjalin; its letter is Wāw (%) and its lunar mansion is Hena. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names.
The sublime khawāṣṣ (occult properties) of this blessed name are:

For a wish or a need: Write this noble name on red paper before sunrise on a Thursday, without speaking. After you have presented your wish and purpose to God Almighty, if you cast the paper into the sea, God will grant your request within a week.

To undo sorcery: Put three pieces of salt, each the size of a hazelnut, into a bucket of water, recite the names Mazjalin and Bazjalin over it 66 times, and if the bewitched person performs a full ritual washing with this water, the spell is broken by God Almighty's leave.

For success in one's affairs: Whoever recites the noble names Mazjalin and Bazjalin before undertaking any task will succeed in it by God Almighty's leave. It was by the noble name Bazjalin that Venus (Zuhra) rose into the sky.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 410
The seventh name is Tarqabin; its letter is Ze (+) and its lunar mansion is Zira. Its Arabic meaning — [I 411] is its noble name. The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:
For abundant provision and income: On a Friday, write this noble

4×4 numerical wafq with the four archangels set around its frame — top: Gabriel [Jibrīl]; left: Michael [Mīkāʾīl]; right: ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl]; bottom: Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl]; a single Arabic letter marks each of the four corners. [I 411]
name once on a piece of paper, together with this noble verse:

name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Every time Zechariah entered the sanctuary where she was, he found provision with her.) along with the wafq of the noble name Rezzak (the Provider). After fumigating it with agarwood and benzoin incense, if this wafq is hung in a place of business, that business's trade will increase, its blessing will multiply, and many customers will come to it.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 411
The eighth name is Barhashin; its letter is Ha (*) and its lunar mansion is Nesre. Its Arabic equivalent:
,O God, this is Your servant — O Almighty) .(answer him
Line of talismanic cipher characters — comb-like and looped strokes written as one continuous formula; no labels. [I 412]
[I 412] These are its noble names. This blessed name was the litany of the Archangel Michael (peace be upon him). The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:

To make an oppressive enemy fall ill: Write this blessed name eleven times, and this talisman once, on yellow paper at the end of Ramadan. After fumigating what you have written with sandalwood, hang it, with the intention that the enemy should die, on a date palm bearing yellow fruit; the oppressor's illness will then worsen, and he will suffer from it until he dies. You! Fear God.

To draw a person to you (jalb): If, with the intention of drawing a person to you, you burn agarwood and frankincense incense at midnight, perform a tawkil (an invocation formula binding the servant spirits) once every hundred recitations, and for three or seven nights recite the names Tarqabin and Barhashin 1,209 times while thinking of the person you want to come, the maṭlūb (the object of the working) will present himself before you. The khadim (servant spirits) of these names are:
these are their names. You perform the tawkil once every hundred recitations using the names of these hadims.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 412
The ninth name is Ghalmashin; its letter is Ṭāʾ (0) and its lunar mansion is Tarfe. Its Arabic meaning — these are its names. The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:
For every kind of wish: If a person, while fasting and practicing ascetic discipline (riyada), recites this name 300 times at midnight for three nights, reciting once every hundred times this tawkil:
I 413] (Take heed, O servants of this name, in my]
description — I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so — and its command ,is upon so-and-so

4×4 letter wafq with the four archangels set around its frame — top: Gabriel [Jibrīl]; left: Michael [Mīkāʾīl]; right: ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl]; bottom: Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl]; a single Arabic letter marks each of the four corners. [I 413]

son of so-and-so, that my maṭlūb be fulfilled.) — if he recites this, then before three nights have passed, by God's grace he will attain his purpose regarding the thing and the person he wished for, and what he wanted will come to pass.

To draw someone to you: Write this noble name on white paper eleven times in disjointed letters (ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ — the letters written separately, unconnected), and beneath the names write this fourfold wafq of the noble name.

Around the wafq, also in disjointed letters, ring it with the letters of this name. Then, after fumigating the paper you have written on with a piece of clothing that has touched the maṭlūb's body, look at the letters of the maṭlūb's name and see which elemental letter predominates, and act according to its nature. If letters of fire predominate, throw the paper into a fire, or bury it beneath a fire. If letters of earth predominate, bury the paper you wrote at the maṭlūb's threshold or in a grave. If letters of air predominate, hang what you wrote up facing the wind, or carry it on your person. If letters of water predominate, bury what you wrote under water, or have the maṭlūb drink water that has touched it.
This working of attraction is extremely powerful, like a burning fire, and the maṭlūb will be present before you within three days.

If you want to drive jinn away from the place you are in: If you burn Bernuf incense and recite the name Ya Ghalmashin 1,370 times, the jinn will leave the place you are in. To bring them back to their places once your task is finished, sprinkle the place with water [I 414] in which agarwood has been boiled with rosewater, and recite the name Ghalmashin backwards — in the manner called Shemlagh — 1,370 times, reciting once every hundred times this tawkil:
By the truth of this name, O angels, give the jinn) .(permission to be among you and upon you
— then the jinn will return to their places. If, after having driven the jinn from a place, you fail to arrange for their return, they will inflict very great harm.
The tenth name is Hutirin; its letter is Ye (/) and its lunar mansion is Cebhe. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its names. The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:

For protection from jinn and the evil eye: After writing this noble name and Surah At-Tāriq in disjointed letters, if this ḥirz (protective amulet) is fastened onto a small child, the child is protected and kept safe from evil eyes, jinn, and the malice of devils.

To strengthen the memory: If a person recites this noble name 70 times every day, God Almighty causes him to retain everything he hears and never again forget it. It grants the one who recites it awe and dignity. Bursts of wisdom well up in that person's heart.

To gain strength in the eyes of others: Whoever engraves this noble name on a gold plate and carries the plate on his person will gain strength in the eyes of people and over those under his authority.
For love: If you recite this name over an apple seven times and then feed the apple to your maṭlūb, great love for you will arise in his heart, and he will strive to do everything you wish.

[I 415] To keep dogs from entering: If you write this noble name on tanned wolf hide and bury the hide at the threshold of a house's door, or at the entrance to a city, no dog will be able to enter that house or city — for as long as the inscribed hide remains buried there.

To gain superiority: If a person engraves these names — Mazjalin, Bazjalin, Tarqabin, Barhashin, Ghalmashin, Hutirin — on an iron ring made on that day and hour, and wears this ring on his finger, he will surpass all his companions in marksmanship, and no one will be able to overpower his arm. If a wounded person wears this ring, his pain will be eased by God Almighty's leave.
To make water disappear: In the hour of Saturn (Zuḥal), the first hour of Saturday, engrave these names and this noble verse — Mazjalin, Bazjalin, Tarqabin, Barhashin, Ghalmashin, Hutirin, Wa innā...
— on a black lead plate. After fumigating it with cloves, if it is lowered into a well on a black woolen thread, the well's water will recede and disappear.

For a wish: If a person writes these names on the palm of his hand, then approaches the person he wishes to bring under his command, pointing at him and reciting the names, that person will submit to him and do as he wishes.
[I 416] The eleventh name is Kalnehudin; its letter is Kāf (.) and its lunar mansion is Harasan. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The khawāṣṣof this name are:

For epilepsy caused by jinn possession: If, over a person made epileptic by a jinn, you burn amber shell, benzoin, frankincense, and liquid storax incense, and recite this noble name 20 times, the epileptic person will speak at once and answer whatever is asked. If the jinn does not depart, recite the whole set of the Barhatiyya (this family of noble names) over the patient seven times, and the jinn will leave the patient's body at once. Afterward, if you write out the Barhatiyya names for the patient and fasten them on as a hicap (protective amulet), the jinn will never return to the patient. The epileptic person will be healed by God Almighty's leave.
The twelfth name is Bershanin; its letter is Lam (-) and its lunar mansion is Sarfe. Its Arabic meaning — these are its noble names. The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:

For a wish to come true: If, after engraving this noble name on a tin ring in this Sulus Suleymani script, one wears the ring on his finger and turns his attention to the need he desires, what he wishes for will come to pass by God Almighty's leave.

To converse with spirits: If you wish to speak with spirits and receive news from them, recite the names Kalnehudin and Bershanin while fumigating with frankincense and mahlep incense, and then summon the spirits; they will gather there. You may then converse with them as you wish, and ask and learn whatever you want.

[I 417] The thirteenth name is Kazhirin; its letter is Mīm (4) and its lunar mansion is Avva. Its Arabic meaning — these are its noble names. This name was the litany of Jonah (peace be upon him). The

5×5 letter wafq with the four archangels set around its frame — top: Gabriel [Jibrīl]; left: Michael [Mīkāʾīl]; right: ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl]; bottom: Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl]; a single Arabic letter marks each of the four corners. [I 417]

Against thieves and fire: If, after engraving on a copper plate this noble name's five-by-five wafq with its letters, this wafq is hung in a corner of the house, no thief will be able to enter that house, and it will be protected from fire.
This is the form of the five-by-five wafq to be engraved:
To punish jinn and torment them: If this noble name is recited many times every day, it will punish them, and you will be protected from their harassment.
The fourteenth name is Nemushelhin; its letter is Nun (3) and its lunar mansion is Semak. Its Arabic equivalent — [I 418] these are its names. The khawāṣṣof this blessed name are:
For a cough: Write this noble name 17 times, before sunrise on a Saturday, on the leaf of a date palm that has never borne fruit, and, three times, in disjointed letters, this noble verse:
(...he has not surmounted the steep path. And what will make you know what the steep path is? It is the freeing of a slave...)
— then if this is fastened onto the person who has the cough, the cough will be cut short and he will be healed, by the leave of God Almighty.
To be freed from prison: A prisoner who continually recites this blessed noble name will be freed from prison in a short time, by God Almighty's leave.

For bleeding that will not stop: If, on a piece cut from the clothing of a patient whose bleeding will not stop, you write the names Kalnehudin, Bershanin, Kazhirin, and Nemushelhin, and the bleeding person then carries this writing on himself, the bleeding will halt at once by God Almighty's leave.
To make an enemy fall ill: On a piece of pitch shaped into a plate, write the enemy's name, with Nemeshelhin to the right of the name and Berheyula to the left, and in the middle:
(Let it depart from him and flee.)

— and also write the name of the illness you wish him to be afflicted with. Then nail the pitch to the ground at its four corners, or fix it to the wall on the east side of the house. After that, fumigate with coriander and myrrh incense and continue reciting the asmāʾ al-[I 419] Barhatiyya; if you continue this recitation, the oppressive enemy will, in the shortest time, be afflicted with the torment and illness you have written.

4×4 number wafq of the divine name Berheyūlā, written to recover lost or stolen property — the frame names the four archangels: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; talismanic cipher marks at the four corners. [I 419]
The fifteenth name is Berheyula; its letter is Sin (2) and its lunar mansion is Ghafir. Its Arabic equivalent: Subhanallah enallahu haifine Ya Kafi Ya Semiu Ya Allahu ruhi li ruhike muntesi betun.
(Glory be to God — surely God is the One who is to be feared. O Sufficient One, O All-Hearing One, O God, my spirit is affiliated to Your Spirit.)
These are its noble names. This noble name was the litany of Abraham (peace be upon him); with this noble name he glorified and remembered the Creator of the universe. The khawāṣṣof this name are:

To find something lost: If a person who has lost something writes this noble name's fourfold wafq — and around the wafq writes the noble name Berheyūlā seven times — and this wafq is then hung in the house where the item was lost, the lost or stolen property will be found by God's leave.

To see what you wish for in a dream: If you want to see something you desire in your dream, after performing a thorough ablution, for the sake of God's pleasure — [I 420] you perform a six-rak'ah prayer of need (ḥāja namazi), giving the greeting of peace at the end of every two rak'ahs.
After the prayer, write the name Barheyula seven times on your right palm and say the following:
Naming your wish in place of "such-and-such," whatever it may be, then lying down to sleep, you will see what you desire.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 420
The sixteenth name is Bashkaylahin; its letter is ayn (1) and its lunar mansion (manzil, one of the twenty-eight stations of the moon) is Zebane. Its Arabic equivalent is:
(O Believer! Might belongs to Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful.)
— these are its noble names. The exalted properties (khawāṣṣ) of this blessed name are:
For eye pain: On a Monday, write this name seven times on a piece of paper, and the following verses once:
By him I sought refuge when grief touched him — the shirt of) Yūsuf, when the bearer of good news brought it. By the right of (!Ya'kūb, O eye-pain, depart
[I 421] After writing it, if the person whose eyes ache carries it upon his head, he is freed from the eye pain.
For distress and stress: If a person in distress and under stress continues to recite this noble name seventy times every night, he will be freed from his troubles and distress in a short time.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 421
The seventeenth name is Qazmazin; its letter is fā (8) and its lunar mansion is Iklīl. Its Arabic equivalent is:
(O Guardian, through the might of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful.)

3×3 number wafq of the divine name al-Ghanī [Ghanī], written for abundance — the frame names the four archangels: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; cipher marks at the four corners. [I 421]
— these are its noble names. This noble name is the glorification recited by Jesus, peace be upon him. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

For abundance (baraka): On a new piece of blue silk, write this noble name together with the threefold wafq of the name Ghani, "the All-Sufficient." After writing it, place the inscribed silk inside a purse whose contents are of unknown amount, hang the purse from a blackberry-bramble rod, and, fuming it with raw amber and musk incense (bakhūr), recite the Barhatiyya names one hundred times on Friday night; you will see abundance descend upon it. If this purse is used like a wallet, you will find that your money never runs out.

[I 422] For protection from an enemy: Whoever wishes to be protected from an enemy's evil and to prevail over him should invoke the names Beshkaylehin and Qazmazin frequently; he will be protected from the enemy's evil and will prevail.
The eighteenth name is Enghalelitin; its letter is sād (7) and its lunar mansion is Kalb. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

To make someone depart: Write this noble name on a piece of unfired pottery together with Sūrat al-Fīl (the Chapter of the Elephant), then pound the piece thoroughly and grind it to powder. If this powder is scattered at the home of the enemy troubling you, he will leave that place at once.
To extinguish a fire: Whoever recites this noble name often, if he recites it facing a fire and wishes for the fire to go out, the fire will be extinguished before it can spread.

For an apparition: Write this noble name on a plate, wash off the writing with water, and if this water is sprinkled in a place where an apparition has been seen, no apparition will ever be seen there again.
The nineteenth name is Kabarātin; its letter is kāf (6) and its lunar mansion is Shūle. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
[I 423] To be safe from illnesses: Write this noble name on a piece of paper together with the following verse (Āyāt al-Karima):
.In the name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful (Today We shall deliver you in your body, that you may be a sign to" those who come after you." And indeed, many among mankind ..are.)
After writing it, whoever carries it upon himself will not be afflicted by plague or other contagious diseases, and his enemies will be unable to harm him either.

To never encounter what one dislikes: Whoever makes a habit (wird) of reciting this noble name sixty times every day will, by the permission of Allah Almighty, never encounter anything displeasing or unwelcome to him.
The twentieth name is Ghayaha; its letter is rā (5) and its lunar mansion is Nuaym. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To stop bleeding: Write this noble name ninety times — thirty at a time, over three sittings — on a red piece of paper, together with the following verse:

Compassionate, the Merciful. Indeed, He is truly able to bring it back.) written as detached letters (ḥurūf-u mukattaa, the disjointed Arabic letters), then, after washing off the writing with water, if this water is given to drink to a woman whose menstrual bleeding will not stop, her bleeding will cease by the permission of Allah Almighty.
[I 424] The twenty-first name is Keydehula; its letter is shīn (<) and its lunar mansion is Belde. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To nullify sorcery: On a piece of paper, draw the following seal (khātam, a talismanic seal):

3×3 seal [khātam] of the divine name Keydehūlā, written to undo sorcery, its cells filled with three repeating cipher glyphs — frame: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left. [I 424]
Around the seal, write the name Keydehūlā one hundred (100) times, and, written as detached letters, the following verses once (1).
In the name of Allah, the)

Compassionate, the Merciful. "And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. What they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician will not succeed ,wherever he goes. And Allah establishes the truth by His words (".even though the guilty detest it

[I 425] After writing it, whoever carries this amulet (ḥirz) upon himself will not be seized by sorcery; if sorcery has already been cast upon him, it will be nullified, and he will attain healing by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

Whoever continually recites the names Kabaratin and Ghayaha over someone afflicted by the evil eye (naẓar), or directs them toward the eyes of his enemies, blinds his enemies' eyes — his enemies lose the power of sight at that very moment and cannot see him.

To attain high ranks: Whoever wishes to reach the ranks attained by the blessed masters and achieve complete spiritual union (vuslat), let him enter spiritual retreat (khalwa), observing its conditions, and recite the names Ghayāhan and Keydehūlā frequently, reciting the Tījan names — the "crown" names — once at the end of every hundred repetitions; his wish will be granted by the permission of Allah the Exalted.
name is Shamhāhirin; its letter is tā (;) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd :al-Zābih. Its Arabic equivalent is
Tealeyte Ya Aliyyu Ya Alimu (You are exalted, O Most High, O All-Knowing.)
— these are its names. The exalted properties of this name are:

To drive away ants: Write this noble name seven (7) times on a clean plate, then wash off the writing with spring water; if this water is sprinkled where there are ants, the ants will leave that place and, by the permission of Allah Almighty, will never be seen there again.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 426
The twenty-third name is Shamhāhirin; its letter is se (:) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd al-Bula'. Its Arabic equivalent is:
Ya Kadi Ya Hu Ya Hu Ya Rabbahu Ya Rabbahu (O Judge, O He, O He, O my Lord, O my Lord.)
— these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
In a place where mosquitoes are plentiful, if this noble name is written fifteen (15) times on a piece of paper and then burned there, the mosquitoes will flee from that place.

[I 427] The twenty-fourth name is Shemhāhīrin; its letter is khāʾ (9) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd al-Water'ūd. Its Arabic meaning — these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To separate two people: Write this noble name one hundred (100) times on a piece of paper, and then once the following verse:
—enmity and hatred between them until the Day of Resurrection (.between so-and-so, son of so-and-so
