Faṣl 1: On the conditions binding upon everyone

Among them is cleaving to the community; then sound belief, conformable to explicit unveiling; and perseverance in purity, both sensible and spiritual; then the training of thought in meditating upon the meanings of these names, by way of reflection and by way of inductive survey, such that there is generated from that perfect certainty, the knowledge of their secrets, and complete conviction as to the efficacious influence of them all; then the assumption of their character, as has been set forth above.

Then know, [all of] you, that whoever desires a universal operative deployment must needs assume the character of all the names, so that each name may give him what lies within its power. That is attained by divesting oneself of every attribute and by emptying the locus of every thing. So whenever he desires operative deployment by a name, he turns toward the Presence of that name, made ready to receive what comes upon him from it, by means of emptying the locus of the surplus of every thing — of lights and rays — so that there is in it no room for anything other than it; and thus he becomes identical with it in act and in operative deployment. And a universal operative deployment may be obtained through the assumption of the character of a single name, by means of one of two things. Either that name is among the universal roots; or else this assumption of character comes about through the inner sight's taking hold of the matter of witnessing in relation to the Presence of this name, such that he witnesses it without its comprehending and gathering within itself all the remaining names. And [so it is] with what is related of the shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Sabtī, of the perfection of operative deployment [that came to him] through his assuming the character of His name, exalted is He, al-Jawād (the Munificent) — so much so that he, may God the Exalted be pleased with him, used to say: From al-Jawād existence is acted upon. And with what is related of Abū Mūsā al-Sadrānī, that he had, as his litany in a day and a night, 70,000 complete recitations, through his assuming the character of God's name, exalted is He, Bāsiṭ (the Expander). And I have mentioned, concerning the assumption of the character of the names, a company — such as Abū al-Qāsim al-Qushayrī, Abū al-Ḥākim al-Barjānī, Abū al-Barakāt ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī, Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ḥarrānī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Ibn al-ʿArabī, Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Aqlīshī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī, and a multitude whose number none reckons but God, exalted is He. So let whoever wishes to gain acquaintance with it ponder that in their words. So understand that, for it is a confirmation of what has preceded. And know that the human being is himself the Greatest /fol. 123v./ Name of God; and whoever knows himself has known his Lord. And the shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī — may God be pleased with him — said: I was present before my shaykh ʿAbd al-Salām b. Mashīsh, and he had a small son, and I set him in my lap. Then I was minded to ask the shaykh about the Greatest Name, whereupon the boy took hold of my chin and then said to me: O uncle, you are the Greatest Name of God — or he said: the Greatest Name of God is within you.
So the shaykh said: He has answered you — meaning the boy. So understand.
Faṣl 2: On the conditions binding upon some and not others

Among them is the taking of pure metal for the engraving; and the seeking out of the time appropriate to the request; and fumigating with the fitting suffumigation; and the wearing of the particular garment. For all these are only conditions in respect of the weak, who have not attained the attainments of [true] men. And know that whoever stands at the degree of adhering to these stipulations must take a chamber for the litany of remembrance, in which he does nothing other than that, and in which no one else does anything either. And let its measure be the measure of what he needs for his sitting and his standing, nothing at all of it being in excess beyond him. There is to be in it no aperture through which [anything] may enter at all, and it is to be far removed from all sounds. He sits in it in direct contact with the ground, without any barrier; and if he has need [of something], then [let it be] of what the earth causes to grow. And he does not sleep save from being overcome [by sleep]; and he keeps up the fragrant suffumigations at most of his times.

*A subtle point (laṭīfa). One of them was asked about the meaning of withdrawal (ʿuzla), and he said: its very description announces its meaning, and its form gives tidings of what lies in its purport — that is, whoever chooses withdrawal, al-ʿuzla, then al-ʿizz lahu*, "might is his". And it is said: the [solitary] sitting is the loftiest of them. And know that the precious spiritual retreat is the bond of the people of election, and that withdrawal is among the signs of union. So understand that. And how excellent is the saying of him who said:
The house of sainthood (wilāya) — its pillars have been apportioned; our masters within it are of the Substitutes (abdāl):
between silence and unceasing withdrawal, and hunger, and wakefulness — pure and exalted.

And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Silence bequeaths the knowledge of God, exalted is He; withdrawal bequeaths the knowledge of this world; hunger bequeaths the knowledge of Satan; and wakefulness bequeaths the knowledge of the soul.))

I say: Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that the forebears (al-salaf), may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them, are agreed that the limit of the Lordly opening (al-fatḥal-rabbānī) and of the ṣamadānī unveiling is not attained save by one in whose stomach there is not the least trace of a mote of food; and that is the limit of corporeal self-sufficiency (al-ṣamadāniyya al-jismāniyya). And there has been disagreement about that: it is said that it comes about within two weeks; but the more widely held view among them is that it does not come about save with the completion of the 40 [days]. And that is what God, exalted is He, stipulated in the case of /fol. 124r./ His interlocutor Moses son of ʿImrān — peace be upon him — in the 40, so that his stomach might be purified of the grossnesses of foods, and thereby the spiritual being of his spirit grow strong, and his heart become clear, and his intellect grow strong, and his soul become wholesome. This, then, is the self-sufficiency of the spirits; and the forebears have set its limit at the end of the 60th day. And in it one apprehends the marvels of the dominion (malakūt), the subtleties of the omnipotence (jabarūt), and the secrets of the kingdom (mulk). As for the self-sufficiency of the intellects, by the totality of the human essence, it is 70 days; and that is the end of the period for those who undertake the spiritual discipline. And from it [comes] another genesis — that is, his interior grows up with lights of special election such as he had not known before, neither from the masters of the [mystical] states nor from the ranks of the deeds; and the secrets are unveiled to him, and the veils are lifted from his inmost secrets. And he it is who died through annihilation (fanāʾ) and was then brought to life through subsistence (baqāʾ). And this is the last rank of self-sufficiency within humanity, by the totality of the essence, in respect of its worlds and the kinds of its self-disclosures (tajalliyāt).

Know that the substance of the natural appetites is not cut off save after a complete hunger — thus has the ancient custom run in the secrets of the spiritual disciplines. As for the self-sufficiency of the natures, its limit is 28 days; and there is nothing less, for one who traverses the beginnings of the secrets of self-sufficiency, than a discipline of 14 days. As for the one upon whom the traces of habit stir within a week, they bind him to [the ordinary] means and bring him out of the retreats, because of their knowledge of the ruin of his interior in respect of the Lordly incomings and the gifts of faith. And some of them used to diminish his food each day by [the weight of] a date-stone; and among them is he who does not work at the lessening of the sustenance, but rather works at deferring it by degrees, until his gradation ends at 7 days, and 10 days, up to 40. And among them is he who alters his eating by a moist stick, diminishing his food every night by the measure of the drying of the stick. And Sahl said: whoever goes without food (ṭayy) for 40 days, power in the dominion (malakūt) is made manifest to him. And we have already disclosed the secrets of wayfaring (sulūk); so understand, and you will hit the mark. And let us seal this noble conclusion and subtle introduction with a rare litany of remembrance and a wondrous litany (wird), whose suns of meaning and subtleties of expression shine forth. This fragrant blossom and gleaming secret: God holds intimate colloquy by means of it with no servant but He sets him free; nor with any captive but He releases him; nor is there any prisoner but he is delivered, nor any man in fear but he is made secure, nor any poor man but he is made rich, nor any abased man but he is made mighty. And in it is a marvellous meaning for the crushing of tyrants and the cutting off of the last remnant of the wrongdoing folk. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself, every obstinate tyrant and rebellious satan is abased before him; and no one sees him but loves him. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God gives life to his interior with the light of the gnoses and to his exterior with the spirit of the subtleties, and guards him in his family and in his own self, and suffices him against the evil of what you fear. /fol. 124v./ And no king makes remembrance of it but his kingdom is enlarged and his word takes effect. And in it is the Greatest Name of God. And whoever recites it before a tyrant at the time of his anger, his anger is stilled; and he does not ask God, exalted is He, for a need but He gives him what he asked. And whoever knows how to turn [to God] (tawajjuh) by this hidden secret and treasured pearl is dispensed thereby from many of the operative litanies of remembrance of this kind. And it has a spiritual retreat [devoted] to it, which the masters of inner sight know; and the litany of remembrance for it is the All-Comprehending Name, for the greatest of those enraptured [in love], and Ḥayy Qayyūm (Living, Self-Subsisting) for the masters of the beginnings. And were a man to wish to give clear expression to the secrets of this radiant ruby and dazzling emerald from the side of its numerical secrets, its letter-borne effects, its luminous names, and its dispositions in awfāq, he would be wholly taken up with the arduousness of it. And it behooves kings, princes, viziers, the righteous, the most excellent of the scholars, and the most skilled of the sages to turn [to God] by it in the first [hour] of the day of Friday, or the day of Sunday, or the day of Monday, or the day of ʿArafa, or the day of the two feasts, or the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ, or the eve of mid-

Shaʿbān, or the eve of the 27th of the month of Ramadan, or at the new moon of every month, or on the nights of all time; and that is after a prayer of 6 salutations. And when he sits at the end of it, let him say: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest, and there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. O God, bless the Prophet Muḥammad, and his family, and his wives — the mothers of the believers — and his progeny and the people of his house, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham; truly You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. Then let him pronounce the takbīr and prostrate himself; and let him say, while prostrate, Fātiḥat al-Kitāb 7 times, and the Throne Verse 7 times, and "There is no god but God alone, who has no partner; His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is powerful over every thing" 10 times. Then let him say: O God, truly I ask You by the bonds of might from Your Throne, and by the utmost reach of mercy in Your Book, and by the right of Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, and Your highest majesty, and by Your perfect words. And after that let him ask for his need. Then let him raise his head and give the salutation to the right and to the left. Then, if it be possible, let him slaughter a fat ram, free of defects, in an empty place, with a lawful slaughtering, turned toward the qibla; and let him say at the slaughtering: O God, this is from You and unto You. O God, truly it is my ransom, so accept it from me. And let him dig a pit for it and fill it in with earth; and let him cut it into 60 portions — the hide a portion, the head a portion, the right side a portion — and distribute it among the poor and the destitute, and feed 60 destitute persons with the most excellent of food; or let him give in alms 7 dirhams to 7 destitute persons. So understand; for the gates have been opened for whoever wishes to enter. And God bestows His bounty upon whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of magnificent bounty. And He is the Granter of success. /fol. 125r./

And this is the litany, magnificent in measure. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. And you say: O God, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham among the worlds; truly You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And you say There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87) 126 times. And you say God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129) 7 times. And you say: I ask forgiveness of God, beside whom there is no god, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance — 3 times. And you say: In the name of God, with whose name nothing in the earth nor in the heaven can do harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing — 3 times. And you say "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58) 16 times. And you say: There is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty — 10 times. And you say: O Wadūd (the Loving), O Wadūd, O Possessor of the Glorious Throne, O Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O Muʿīd (the Restorer), O Doer of what He wills. I ask You by the light of Your face, which has filled the corners of Your Throne; and I ask You by Your power, by which You have power over the whole of

Your creation, and by Your mercy, which embraces every thing: there is no god but You. O Mughīth (the Succourer), succour me — 4 times. And you say: O ʿAlī (the Exalted), O ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O Walī (the Protecting Friend), O ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O Ḥannān (the Tender), O Mannān (the Bounteous), O Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O Jamīl (the Beautiful), O ʿAṭūf (the Ever-Kindly), O Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle): I ask You by Your name that is hidden in the knowledge of Your treasured Unseen, that You pour out upon me, from the outpouring of Your most holy beauty and Your most precious perfection, a luminous secret and a lordly name, that I may deploy it operatively upon souls and bodily forms, life-bloods and spirits, with the stirrers of love and the stirrers of affection. O You by whom is the relief of the sorrowful, and the intimate companion of the desolate: I ask You by the secret of the bent alif (al-alif al-maʿṭūf), which is the origin of the letters. O Wahhāb (the Bestower), O Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), O Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), O Rāfiʿ (the Raiser): [grant me] a longing that will bring me to You, and a light that will guide me to You; and receive me with repose and fragrance, and gladden me with security from You and with [Your] good pleasure. I ask You, O Bāsiṭ (the Expander), O Wāḥid (the One), O Mājid (the Glorious), O Wājid (the Finder): God, God is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him. O God, whoever intends against me evil, or harm, or ill toward me — subdue his might, tie up his tongue, bridle his mouth, restrain his guile, and come between me and him. O Dāʾim (the Everlasting), O Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O Mujīb (the Answerer), O
Majīd (the All-Glorious): by the sanctity of Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad, Muḥammad.

O God, truly I ask You by the all-comprehending secret and the shining light, that You bestow upon me a criterion (furqān) from You, whereby my breast may be expanded and my worth raised. You are my direction and my standing, and unto You is the return and the ultimate end. You mend the broken and break the tyrants. There is no god but God, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but God, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but God, Lord of the seven heavens and of the earth and of what is between the two, and Lord of the noble Throne. O God, God of Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl, and of Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac: grant me well-being, and set none of Your creation over me with anything for which I have no strength. O Hearer of the invocation, /fol. 125v./ O Answerer of supplication! So He will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing (Q 2:137). I have put my trust in the Living who does not die. Praise belongs to God, who has taken no child, and who has no partner in sovereignty, and who has no protector out of abasement; and magnify Him greatly (Q 17:111). God is greatest, God is greatest, God is greatest — mightier than the whole of His creation. God is greater than whatever I fear and whatever I guard against. And I take refuge in God, other than whom there is no god, who holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth save by His leave (Q 22:65), from the evil of every obstinate tyrant and every rebellious satan. O God, truly I ask You for security from rejection, and security from being driven away, and security from poverty, and security from blame, and security from anxiety, and security from grief, and security from abasement, and security from ignorance, and security from the [evil] eye, and security from being swallowed up by the earth, and security from the quaking of the earth. O God, make good our final outcome in all matters, and grant us protection from the disgrace of this world and from the punishment of the hereafter. O God, truly I ask You by Muḥammad, the perfect lord, the opener, the seal, the light of the lights of the gnoses and the secret of the secrets of the bestowed graces (ʿawārif), the choicest of Your creation, the secret of Your knowledge, the mirror of Your Essence, and the witnessing-place of Your attributes; and I ask You by the light of Your Face, and by the carpet of Your mercy, and by the seven and the eight and their secrets that are joined [in unbroken succession] from You. O God, O God, O Aḥad (Unique), O Ṣamad (Eternal Refuge), O Ḥayy (Living), O Qayyūm (Self-Subsisting): bestow upon me, from Your knowledge, knowledge and action and intellect; and from Your life, a spirit; and from Your will, a decree; and from Your power, an act; and from Your words, a tongue; and from Your hearing, understanding; and from Your sight, unveiling; and from Your encompassment, a standing firm. And grant me, from You and through You, a secret before which the necks of the arrogant shall bow low and to which the souls of tyrants shall be led in submission. For to You belongs praise, O Barr (the Benign), upon every beginning; and to You belongs thanks, O Bāqī (the Everlasting), upon every ending. Truly You are al-Mughnī (the

Enricher), al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), and al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy). My God, lay me down upon the bed of Your mercy by Your favour, and keep watch over me with the watchman of Your safekeeping and Your preservation; and wrap me in the mantle of awe (hayba), and seat me upon the couch of magnificence, crowned with the crown of resplendence; and pitch over me the pavilion (surādiq) of safekeeping, and unfurl over me the banner of might; and fill my inward with reverent fear and mercy, and my outward with magnificence and awe; and give me mastery over the forelock of every obstinate tyrant and every rebellious satan; and preserve me from error and from slipping, and strengthen me in word and in deed. O God, truly I ask You by You, and by what Your Essence comprises of that which none knows but You — of You I ask that You bless the Muḥammadan Essence and the subtle unitary reality (al-laṭīfa al-aḥadiyya), the sun of the heaven of secrets and the place of manifestation of the lights, the pole of the sphere of Beauty and the centre of the orbit of Majesty. O God, by his secret with You and Your secret with him: give security to my fear, and pardon my stumbling, and take away my covetousness and my sorrow, and make complete what is deficient in me, and take me to Yourself away from myself, and provide me with annihilation (fanāʾ) in You away from myself; and do not make me one infatuated with my own soul, veiled by my sense-perception; and unveil for me every concealed secret, O Ḥayy, O Qayyūm; and suffice me in that with a subtle kindness (luṭf) in which the spirits of the friends of God (awliyāʾ) find rest and for which the souls of the felicitous are made eager. For to You belongs the most ample glory /fol. 126r./ and the most all-embracing kingship.

O God, truly I ask You by every name that has gone before in Your knowledge — truly You refuse no petitioner who asks by it, and You turn away disappointed none who asks You by it — I ask You to fulfil my need in that wherein I am Your poor one, and to accompany me in that with goodly well-being. Truly You know what I desire; with You are the keys of all affairs, and You are powerful over all things. O God, truly I ask You by the secret of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate" that You pour out upon me, of the raiment of Your lights, that which shall send back the eyes of the enemies abased and their hands in loss; and that You clothe me, in everything I undertake, with a splendour from You in which the spirits of those who perceive find rest, upon which the eyes of the beholders are fixed in wonder, and by which the innermost secrets of the gnostics are gladdened. Truly You are the All-Knower of hidden things and their Teacher, the Unveiler of secrets and the One who gives understanding of them. To You belongs praise and laudation, and in Your hand are the triumph and the opening. O God, bless Your prophets and the messengers, and Your angels brought near, and Your righteous friends, and all the people of Your obedience; and convey to them our peace and our greeting, and bring us their intercession, together with our request and our wish. O God, truly I have turned my hope toward Your noble Face, and I have thought well of Your mighty pardon; so have mercy upon me, and have mercy upon my parents and upon those who turn [in repentance] to me, and make well pleased with me those who turn [others] away from me and who set themselves against me; and do not turn my hope away from Your Face disappointed, and do not make my good opinion of Your pardon a lie. My God, how should I depart from Your door in disappointment, when I have loved it in confidence in You? And how should You leave me bereft of Your bestowal, when You have commanded me to call upon You? O most merciful of the merciful! O Lord — when my appointed term has run out, and my work is cut off, and I have put on my shroud and parted from my dwelling: O Lord of lords, O Causer of causes, O Setter-free of necks, O Remover of torment: the harm of my own soul has touched me, so have mercy upon me, for You are the most merciful of the merciful. In the name of God, al-Shāfī (the Healer). In the name of God, al-Kāfī (the Sufficient). In the name of God, al-Muʿāfī (the Restorer to Health). Alif-Lām-Mīm-Rāʾ. Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād. Ṭāʾ-Sīn. Ḥāʾ-Mīm. Qāf. Nūn. God is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful (Q 12:64).

Then you say "There is no god but God" 100 times, and you say Yā Laṭīf 129 times, and you say Yā Kāfī 111 times, and you say Yā Ḥalīm (O Forbearing) 88 times. [Those secrets] which none may attain save the single ones among the masters of secrets and the singular ones among the masters of lights — and none is granted it save those who have been patient, and none is granted it save one possessed of great fortune (Q 41:35). So ponder this red sulphur and this greatest theriac, and there will gleam for you a flash from the science of the names and the letters, and the secrets of the numbers, and the meanings of the receptacles (ẓurūf). And you say Yā Mujīb 55 times, and you say Yā Salām (O Peace) 131 times, and you say Yā Ḥafīẓ (O Preserver) 998
times. The blessed litany (wird) is completed, with the praise of God and His help.
Chapter 16 (al-bāb al-sādis ʿashar): On the Most Beautiful Names of God and on their beneficial, tried-and- tested awfāq [190]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success — that this is the first […], well-guarded, a hidden [pearl], issuing forth from the valley of purity to the intimate friends of fidelity and to the elect of purity: those who ride upon the necks of the winds of longing, who fly upon the wings of the draughts of [spiritual] tasting toward the understanding of these sciences of divine bestowal /fol. 126v./ and of the understandings that come by effusion, and the musk-scented seals, and the inscriptions of [divine] opening, and the Indian ciphers, and the subtleties of the letters, and the gnoses of number, and the luminous names, and the realities of the Furqān, and the spiritual concordances. May God bring me and you into the garden of secrets and the orchard of lights. I say — and from God comes success, and from Him unveiling and verification: Know — may God bring me and you into the Frequented House, and grant me and you accord with the companions of the Unrolled Parchment — that the names of God, exalted is He, considered with respect to what of them has come in the Book and in the Sunna, whether in the form of a noun or in the form of a verb from which, however, a noun is derived; and with respect to what the people of unveiling apply to Him by way of the realities of the names, of whatever is an attribute of perfection — are exceedingly many. For if we count such [pairs] as al-Qāhir (the Subduer) and al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), and al-Shākir (the Thankful) and al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), as two names, they come near to reaching three hundred; and it is said that they reach six thousand. The purpose in this indication is only brevity, and a hinting toward this hidden science and this treasured secret, so as to alert him who seeks it. And whoever has been allotted anything of a share in it, let him hasten to cut through the obstacles of wayfaring, and to divest himself of the blameworthy traits of character and the basest of them, and to adorn himself with the praiseworthy and fairest of them, which are the character of the Real, glorified and exalted. Then you will attain to the like of these matters here set down; for the taking of this science is [otherwise] a dead thing received from a dead thing. God, exalted is He, said: No soul knows what comfort of the eyes has been hidden away for them, as a recompense for what they used to do (Q 32:17).

For that reason I have set myself to speak upon the ninety-nine names; and I have thought fit to adduce them first, under a condition, as has come in the hadith; and then [to set out] the discourse upon each name according to its rank, after alerting [you] to the secret of the enumeration (iḥṣāʾ). So I say — and in God is help sought: al-Tirmidhī related from Abū Hurayra — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Truly God has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters the Garden. And they are these names: He is God, there is no god but He; al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), al-Malik (the King), al-Quddūs (the All-Holy), al-Salām (the Peace), al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), al-Jabbār (the Compeller), al-Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great), al-Khāliq (the Creator), al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), al-Muṣawwir (the Shaper), al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), al-Qahhār (the All-Subduing), al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Razzāq (the Provider), al-Fattāḥ (the Opener), al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Qābiḍ (the Constrictor), al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), al-Khāfiḍ (the Abaser), al-Rāfiʿ (the Raiser), al-Muʿizz (the Giver of might), al-Mudhill (the Giver of abasement), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Ḥakam (the Judge), al-ʿAdl (the Just), al-Laṭīf (the Subtle), al-Khabīr (the All-Aware), al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), al-Shakūr (the Most Thankful), al-ʿAlī (the Exalted), al-Kabīr (the Great), al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), al-Muqīt (the Nourisher), al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account), al-Jalīl (the Majestic), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Raqīb (the Watcher), al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life), al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death), al-Ḥayy (the Living), al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), al-Wājid (the Finder), al-Mājid (the Glorious), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Aḥad (the

Unique), al-Fard (the Sole), al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), al-Qādir (the Powerful), al-Mutaqaddir (the Determiner of measures), al-Muqaddim (the Advancer), al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer), al-Awwal (the First), /fol. 127r./ al-Mujīb (the Answerer), al-Wāsiʿ (the All-Embracing), al-Ḥakīm (the Wise), al-Wadūd (the Loving), al-Majīd (the All-Glorious), al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead), al-Shahīd (the Witness), al-Ḥaqq (the Real), al-Wakīl (the Trustee), al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Matīn (the Firm), al-Walī (the Protecting Friend), al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner), al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), al-Ākhir (the Last), al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest), al-Bāṭin (the Hidden), al-Wālī (the Governor), al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted), al-Barr (the Benign), al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting), al-Muntaqim (the Avenger), al-ʿAfū (the Pardoner), al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion), Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), al-Muqsiṭ (the Equitable), al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer), al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), al-Mughnī (the Enricher), al-Māniʿ (the Withholder), al-Ḍārr (the Bringer of Harm), al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), al-Nūr (the Light), al-Hādī (the Guide), al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), al-Bāqī (the Abiding), al-Wārith (the Inheritor), al-Rashīd (the Rightly Guiding), al-Ṣabūr (the Patient).)) And these are ninety-nine names, which the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — enumerated out of the whole of the names of God, exalted is He. And you have already learned that the names of God, exalted is He, are many, and that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — singled these out for mention only because they are comprehensive, containing within them the meanings that are the degrees of the Gardens. For that reason he said: ((Whoever enumerates them enters the Garden.)) And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — did not mention the name that completes the hundred only because it is proper to him — God bless him and grant him peace — since its meaning is al-wasīla (the Means of Access), which is a degree in the Garden that is not fitting for any one of the servants of God, exalted is He, but belongs to the most perfect of His servants, our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace.
And know that whoever enters the treasure-house and comes forth with the abasement of disappointment dies in the fires of regret; and if he seeks to return to it, his face is blotted out.
Let him weep over himself whose lifetime has been squandered, and who has of it neither portion nor share.

So O the regret of one who has been heedless in the daylight of his negligence, and held back from the company of those possessed of the lordly gnoses! His loss has become plain beside the gains of the worlds, and his name has been erased from the tablet of those brought near. May God grant us and you refuge from the abandonment of being driven away, and preserve us and you from the ignominy of estrangement. Truly He is bountiful, generous, self-disclosing, comely, compassionate, munificent, magnificent.
Faṣl 1: On His name, exalted is He, Huwa Allāh alladhī lā ilāha illā Huwa (He is God, there is no god but He)

And if you say: Why have you not counted the name al-Ilāh (the God)? I say: The Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — did not count it among these ninety-nine names; rather he brought it in within what he predicated of the name of God, exalted is He, by way of the affirmation of oneness. And for that reason he did not make the whole of His name Huwa an independent name within this number; rather he counted, in place of it, His words He is God, there is no god but He (Q 59:22) as a single name — and that for a secret which those possessed of inner sight know.

As for His name, exalted is He, Huwa (He): it is a pronoun of absence, and it is among the most proper of His names, exalted is He, since true absence belongs to Him alone, for the intellects do not conceive Him and the imaginations do not delimit Him. And it is the name of the Essence, considered in respect of the all-encompassing reach of its absence and of its absoluteness from all the restrictions and descriptions that entail determinations (taʿayyunāt). And it is the opening of the names and the mother of their Book; and it may occupy among them the rank that the alif occupies among the letters. And it is a name of majestic worth, and it is said that it is the Greatest Name. And whoever makes it his litany of remembrance, being a brother of divestment (tajrīd), 11 times — so that nothing other than it occurs to his heart —

God opens for him, at the last time, a door of unveiling according to the measure of his preparedness. And it is among the names of majestic worth /fol. 127v./ proper to the greatest of those devoted to God (al-mutaʾallihūn). And it has, of number, 11; and it is the fourth prime number, and this number is from what the hāʾ requires. For that reason it was the fifth odd number; and it is an essential number, since it is a sealed whole in which there is no cleaving apart. And as for the names of its letters, they point to His name Hādī (Guide) from one aspect, and to His name Wāḥid (One) from another. And as for its square, it is according to this form:
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 372]

[The corresponding square of names: 3×3, cells as in the source — (Munjī, the Deliverer), (Khafī, the Hidden), (Ṣāḥib, the Companion),(Mubīn, the Manifest),(ʿAdl, the Just), (Wafī, the Faithful),(Wāf, the Fulfiller), (Munjadh), (Kahf, the Refuge)]

And as for His name al-Ilāh (the God): it is of majestic worth. It has a three-by-three square, complete in respect of its even number; and it has a four-by-four square in respect of its odd number. And the starting-point of its threefold square (muthallath) is from the letter hāʾ. Whoever engraves this threefold square upon a ring of silver, with Saturn in its exaltation, all the spiritual beings obey him; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one who is obeyed in the world. I say: and if one of the gnostics utters it, the spiritual beings answer him after seven [days], following a fast and a litany of remembrance, and they ask what he desires. And it has, of number, 37 in utterance (lafẓan) and 36 in figure (raqman); and it is among the names that gather [the secret of] the even and the odd. And it has 43 in meaning; and that is by reason of the wāw's being latent within the hāʾ. And as for its square, it is according to this form which follows, and opposite it the threefold square. So ponder that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

[The four-by-four square (murabbaʿ) of al-Ilāh: 4 columns, cells as in the source. The first row gives the names of the letters —(hāʾ), (alif),(lām),(hamza); the two middle rows give the numbers; the last row gives the names (Mubīn, the Manifest),(Huwa Awwal, He is First),(Hād, Guide),(Mubīn)]

[The threefold square (muthallath) of al-Ilāh: 3×3, cells as in the source, the values written in abjad letter-numerals — =, 16 =, 11 = 9,, 8 = ,15 =, 14 =, 10 == 13, the centre cell being written as the numeral 12; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 36, the number of Ilāh. This is the threefold square to be engraved upon the ring of silver.]

And as for His name, exalted is He, Allāh: it is a name of majestic worth, and it is a name in which the Maker (al-Bāriʾ) stands alone; and its meaning is "the Lord" (al-sayyid); and it is the comprehensive Name. For that reason all the names are a description of it, while it is not a description of any of them. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it — no one can bear to look upon his face, out of reverence for the awe he inspires. And whoever writes it, with the Sun in its exaltation, upon a noble body, burns thereby every rebellious satan. And if he keeps it with him on a day of severe cold and multiplies the remembrance of it, he feels no pain of cold at all. And if one afflicted with the phlegmatic fever wears it as a signet, it departs at once. /fol. 128r./ And whoever engraves its square upon a thin parchment, with the Sun in Leo, and carries it after making remembrance of it 317 times — he does not lay his hand upon water but that that water sinks away, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And that is on condition that he be a man of [spiritual] state with God, exalted is He. And whoever knows its worth is made independent by it of every thing, for it is the Greatest Name of God, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. And hence its manifest powers point to that: Huwa Mujīb (He is Answerer). And it is the first of the manifesting names, the gatherer of their realities, and that which comprises their fine points and their subtle threads. And it has a square according to this form; and its elevation (rafʿa) is sixty-six. Understand that, and you will be rightly guided.
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 66, the number of Allāh]
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 66, the number of Allāh]

And whoever draws it in a fivefold wafq and carries it, nothing of [his] affairs shall be hard for him, and by it hardships are made easy. And this is its form. And it is the litany of remembrance of the great ones, distraught with love, among the masters of the spiritual retreats. And it is suitable for one whose name is Muḥammad, that he multiply the remembrance of it. You say: Allāh Allāh; then he passes over the measure of a word; then he returns and says likewise again — in accordance with his words, God bless him and grant him peace: ((God, God is my Lord; I associate nothing with Him.)) And likewise for one whose name is ʿAbd Allāh. And it has, of number, 67 in utterance and 66 in figure. And as for the names of its letters, they are 260, pointing to two majestic names, namely ʿAlī (Exalted) and ʿAlīm (All-Knowing). So ponder it.
Faṣl 2: On His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful)

This noble name has a square of five by five, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul), with Saturn in its exaltation. Its possessor does not cease to move about within the good pleasure of God, exalted is He; no one sees him but that he grows tender toward him, and the religious communities come to him one after another. Whoever places it in water and gives one afflicted with burning fever to drink of it — it departs from him on the instant. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the servants [of God] look upon him with the eye of mercy. Its remembrance is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. It is related from al-Khaḍir — peace be upon him — that he said: Whoever prays the afternoon prayer on the day of Friday, and faces the qibla, and says "O God, O All-

Merciful" (Yā Allāh, Yā Raḥmān) until the sun sets, shall ask God for nothing but that He gives him what he has asked. And it has, of number, 298; and it is an even-odd, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 153, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mubqī (the Perpetuator). This is with respect to its figure (raqm); but with respect to its utterance (lafẓ) it has, of number, 299, /fol. 128v./ and it is an odd, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 37, which point to His name al-Ilāh (the God). As for the names of its letters, they are 406, which point to two majestic names, namely Mubdiʿ (the Originator from nothing) and Fāṭir (the Originator). And as for its square, it is in this form:

[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 299 — the number of Raḥmān written with its alif. The top row holds the five letters of the name, which read from right to left
Faṣl 3: On His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate)

This name, majestic in worth, is set in a square of four by four by the secret of interpenetration; and whoever carries it is treated with gentle kindness in all his states. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes one whose invocation is answered, and it is a security against the assaults of time. The time befitting it is when the Moon is in its exaltation. It is also beneficial for all burning fevers. And there is written together with its wafq And We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82). Its remembrance is suitable for one whose name is Ibrāhīm, and it is proper that there be adjoined to it his purified name. And it has, of number, 258; and it is an even-odd, oblong, composite number: it is al-Laṭīf (the Subtle) doubled, al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator) tripled, and al-Awwal (the First) sextupled. And it is an abundant number: its aliquot parts are 270, which point to His name al-Karīm (the Generous). And this name has a wafq swift in effect. And this is its form, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 258 — the number of Raḥīm. The top row holds the four letters of the name, which read from right to left (raḥīm).]
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is likewise 258.]

As for the names of its letters, [they are] 313, which point to His name, exalted is He, Yā Baṣīr (O All-Seeing), with the yāʾ of address. So ponder it. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best. Know, [all of] you — may God grant me and you success unto obedience to Him — that as for al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm, these are noble litanies of remembrance for those in dire straits and a security for those who fear. And no one engraves them upon a signet-ring on the day of Friday, at the end of the day, but that he is treated with gentle kindness in all his affairs. So ponder it.
Faṣl 4: On His name, exalted is He, al-Malik (the King)

This name is suitable for kings, and for others in their presence. It has a square of three /fol. 129r./ by three, which is set down upon a sheet of gold; and there is placed together with it Say: O God, Master of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will (Q 3:26), to the end of the verse. It is among the majestic secrets: he who carries it does not cease to be held in awe and magnified in the souls of kings. The remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Malik, and its square is among the greatest of squares in benefit. And this is its form:
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 90, the number of Malik]

The author of Taysīr al-maṭālib ("The Facilitating of the Objects of Request") said: And if its numerical threefold square (muthallath) is engraved upon a leaf of gold, with the Sun in its exaltation, and a bezel-stone of red ruby is set upon it, and it is placed in a ring, and a king carries it with him — then he will not stand before any tyrant but that God, exalted is He, grants him success; and none will be able to endure looking upon him, even were he among the most courageous of created beings. So know it and ponder it, for it was in the hand of Dhū l-Qarnayn, and Plato the Sage devised its arrangement for him; and the lions would flee from him, by the occult property of the arrangement and of the name. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see. And perhaps some of them have arranged it in this form, and it is as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.

[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the three letters standing upon the main diagonal are (mīm, 40),(lām, 30), and (kāf, 20) — the letters of Malik — and the constant is again 90]
[Fig. 75 — the second arrangement of the square, as in the source; not reproduced in the text stream — ]

And it is a noble arrangement, so guard it well, for it is of the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar). And it has, of number, 90; and this is among the realities of the letters of worship. And it is among the names arrayed in accordance with the ranks of number, in descending order. And it is an even-odd, oblong, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 144, which point to His name al-Bāqī (the Abiding), reckoned with its article. As for the names of its letters, they are 262, which point to His name Mujīb al-daʿwa (the Answerer of the invocation). So ponder it.
And God opens the pure hearts of the righteous to the understanding of the radiant secrets.
Faṣl 5: On His name, exalted is He, al-Quddūs (the All-Holy)

This name is of mighty worth. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a state from it comes to prevail over him — God takes away from him every blameworthy appetite. It is set within a numerical threefold square (muthallath) encompassed by a letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī), when Jupiter is in its exaltation; and as for its bearer, God exchanges for him, in place of every blameworthy trait of character, a praiseworthy trait. He becomes beloved to created beings and honoured among them, and God looses tongues in praise of him. And the remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Quddūs, and likewise for one whose name is Isḥāq. /fol. 129v./ And it has, of number, 174 in utterance (lafẓan) and 170 in figure (raqman). So it is among the treasured secrets, and among the mighty names that are even-numbered from every aspect. And this, in respect of the uttered number, is an even-odd, oblong, composite, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 176, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mūsiʿ (the Enlarger). As for its number in figure, it too is abundant: its aliquot parts are 191, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mannān (the Bounteous). And as for the names of its letters, they are 341, which point to two noble names, namely Ilāh (God) and Raqīb (the Watcher). And as for its square, it is according to this figure — so ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets — and it is as you see.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of Quddūs —(qāf, 100),(the doubled dāl, 8), (wāw, 6),(sīn, 60) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 174]

Faṣl 6: On His name, exalted is He, al-Salām (the Peace)

This name is of mighty station. No one has carried it with him and then had God, exalted is He, show him what he detests; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is kept safe from all afflictions. And in the remembrance of it there are secrets for the people of beginnings and secrets for the people of endings. No fearful one has multiplied the remembrance of it but that he was granted security, nor any deficient one but that he was made complete. And it has a square of four by four, and it is a square of mighty worth; and this is the form of its arrangement.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of Salām —(sīn, 60),(lām, 30), (alif, 1),(mīm, 40) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 131]

And it has, of number, 131, and it is a prime number, which points to His name, exalted is He, Kāfil (the Guarantor). And as for the names of its letters, they are 392, which point to two noble names, namely Raḥmān (the All-Merciful) and ʿAzīz (the Mighty). And the remembrance of it is suitable for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Salām, and likewise for one whose name is Muḥammad. And know that if you pair the odd number of al-Salām with one, that name is the name of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. /fol. 130r./ And he is the heart of the world, just as the heart of the Qurʾān is none but Yā-Sīn, and the heart of Yā-Sīn is "Peace!" — a word from a Merciful Lord (Q 36:58). And it is a verse of mighty worth, and in it is the Greatest Name of God. And it has a figure of mighty worth, to which I have alluded in the book Kashf al-asrār al-rabbāniyya ("The Unveiling of the Lordly Secrets"); so let whoever desires to put it to operative deployment come to a knowledge of it, for it is among the treasured secrets. So ponder it. And God, exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Faṣl 7: On His name, exalted is He, al-Muʾmin (the Granter of Security)

This noble name: its occult property is the granting of security. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God preserves his tongue from lying. And it has a square of four by four, which is set down when Jupiter is in its exaltation; and its possessor does not cease to be accepted among all created beings, and God makes easy for him the affair of his religion and of his worldly life. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Muʾmin. And it has, of number, 136; and it is an even-even-and-odd number, [its number being] the number of al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) twice. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 134, which point to Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge). And as for the names of its letters, they are 299, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful). And this is the form of its arrangement:

Faṣl 8: On His name, exalted is He, al- Muhaymin (the Overseer), glorified is He

This name is among the majestic, all-comprehending names. Therefore, whoever perseveres in its remembrance until a state from it comes to prevail over him, his knowledge encompasses its essence, and the hidden part of its secrets, and what God has brought forth concerning Him in the atoms of his existence, of faith and of acknowledgement. And whoever engraves it in a square upon a signet ring, with the Moon in its exaltation, or Saturn, after remembering the name by its number — God makes him secure from the evil of the accursed Satan. And if he perseveres in its remembrance and is the possessor of a truthful state, God, exalted is He, discloses to him the hidden part of his [Satan's] guile and his whispering. And it is among the names of encompassment, and it is the king of the all-comprehending [names]; none can gauge its true measure save one to whom the realities of the names have been unveiled. And it has, of number, 145; and it is an odd, oblong number, since it arises from the multiplication of the inward of all the letters gathered together, while it is in the outward of all of them, even in the outward of itself — and hence encompassment holds true of it. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 35, which points to the return of the whole affair to Him, by reason of His encompassing of it. And thence [arises] the query-term hal ("whether"), by which one asks about the aspects, for the realization of witnessing. And as for the names of its letters, they are 303, which point to two majestic names, namely Aḥad (the Unique) and Fāṭir (the Originator).

It is related of one of the rightly-guided caliphs — and he was ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, and God knows best — that he was asked about its meaning, and he paused over the answer. /fol. 130v./ And behold, a Bedouin woman possessed of a portion of eloquence brought before him the case of her husband, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, truly my husband is a bondsman where my right is concerned, and there he is at the threshold (al-waṣīd), and I have over him a muhaymin (an overseer) — so have you any mind for a musayṭir (a controller)? And thereupon ʿUmar, and those who were with him, glossed it as al-shāhid (the witness).

And this name has a square of five by five, and it is among the hidden secrets; and the beginning in it is from five, by the secret of His words, exalted is He: Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād (Q 19:1), Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2). And it is a natural odd number, because of what the odd numbers require of production, which is the fruit sought and the end intended. And for this reason the odd numbers are the more receptive to the world of contraction (qabḍ) and of majesty (jalāl), and the even numbers to the world of expansion (basṭ) and of beauty (jamāl). And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see:

The master said: And in it is the secret of al-Jalīl (the Majestic), al-Jamīl (the Beautiful), al-Mujmil (the Beautifier), al-Malik (the King), al-Malīk (the Sovereign), al-Mālik (the Possessor), al-Mannān (the Bounteous), al-Muhaymin (the Overseer), al-Kāmil (the Complete), al-Mukammil (the Perfecter), al-Kālī (the Guardian), al-Mukallim (the One who speaks), al-Munzil (the Sender-down), al-Muzayyin (the Adorner), and lā ilāha illā Llāh ("there is no god but God"), and Mālik al-mulk (Possessor of the Kingdom), and Alif-Lām-Mīm, and Ṭā-Hā, and Amānī, and Malī, and Zakī (the Pure), and Muzakkī (the Purifier), and Munīl (the Bestower), and Munjī (the Deliverer), and Munjiz (the Fulfiller), and Ilāh (God) — and whatever else accords with these names. And the total of its letters is ten, namely

their number is 175, which is the number of the wafq of the sevenfold figure (al-musabbaʿ). So ponder these numerical secrets and these letter-correspondences, for in them are wondrous secrets for one who has a tasting (dhawq) of the wisdom of divine inspiration, which none attain save the singular few among those devoted to God. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Faṣl 9: On His name, exalted is He, al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), glorified is He

This name is magnificent in worth. It has a square of four by four, save that it cannot be set down by the secret of interpenetration (tadākhul), because of the repetition of the zāy in it. Whoever engraves it while Mars is in its exaltation shall have might over the enemies of God, exalted is He; and likewise whoever multiplies the remembrance of it. And whoever dreads having recourse to one of the princes, and humbling himself before him in the seeking of a need, let him multiply the remembrance of it; for whenever he multiplies the remembrance of it, /fol. 131r./ God, exalted is He, makes that easy for him without his humbling himself before anyone. I say: whoever multiplies the remembrance of al-ʿAzīz attains might in his religion and in his worldly life; and whoever perseveres in its remembrance, God, exalted is He, makes him mighty after his lowliness and secure after his fear. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz; and whoever understands its secret, God adorns his inward with the secrets of might. Do you not see that it points to His name, exalted is He, Yā Jamīl (O Beautiful), with the yāʾ of address? It has, of number, 94; and it is an even-odd, oblong, deficient number: its aliquot parts are 50, which point to the letter (nūn), which is the pivot of every thing — of inward knowledge and of outward provision — such that every thing humbles itself and seeks that of which it has need. And because of the mastery of al-ʿAzīz over the outward and the inward, [its number] is the number of al-Wālī (the Governor) twice: so the first governance is for the inward, and the second for the outward. As for the names of its letters, they are 178, which point to two majestic names, namely Malik (the King) and Ḥakīm (the Wise). So ponder that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And this is the form of its square:

Faṣl 10: On His name, exalted is He, al-Jabbār (the Compeller), glorified is He

This dazzling name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it looks upon no one but that an awe of him overcomes that man, and he cannot endure to look upon him. It has a square of four by four, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration, with Mars in its exaltation. He who carries it is held in awe by all people, and no one meets with him but that he is abased before him and forsakes his own will for his. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Jabbār, and likewise for one whose name is Mūsā. It has, of number, 208 in utterance (lafẓan) and 206 in figure (raqman). The first is an even-even-and-odd number; it is from the multiplying of a deaf number (ʿadad aṣamm), namely 13, by the square of the square, namely 16. And it is among the abundant numbers: its aliquot parts are 226, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Ṣādiq (the Truthful), reckoned with its article — by reason of what the good contains of correspondence, by way of that which is fairest, between the two things; a wisdom.

One of the kings said to his vizier — and he was a wise man: Why did God create the fly? He said: For the abasing of the tyrants (jabābira): it descends upon their high stations, and then it climbs upon their beards. And for that reason the fly never alighted upon him whose freedom from this claim was complete — and that is our master Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, God bless him and grant him peace.

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obeying Him — know that whoever perseveres in its remembrance until a state from it comes to prevail over him, and then engraves it /fol. 131v./ upon a plate of red copper and casts it into the house of a wrongdoer, [that house] is laid waste. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided. And it is suitable for kings in particular, because when they persevere in the remembrance of it, all besides them fear them. And whoever writes His name al-Jabbār and the name Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour) upon a slip of paper, at whatever time he wishes, in a state of purity, and places it upon his head at the time of his sitting among the people — God, exalted is He, will make him fair in their eyes. As for its square, it is according to this operative deployment:

Faṣl 11: On His name, exalted is He, al- Mutakabbir (the Supremely Great)

This name is mighty in station. Whoever writes it upon the wall of a city, or the wall of a house, or of anything else, running around it in ninety-four places, while the preacher is upon the pulpit on Friday — God, exalted is He, guards that city or that house from every night-comer that comes upon it with evil. And whoever engraves it in an interpenetrating five-by-five [square], by the secret of the numbers and the letters, with Mars in its exaltation, abases thereby every arrogant man; and likewise whoever multiplies the remembrance of it. And some of the masters of inner sight have mentioned that the tyrants are led in submission to him who makes remembrance of it, and that his word takes effect among them. And it has, of numbers, 664, and it is an even number, of the even-even-and-odd [class]. And it is among the deficient numbers: its aliquot parts are 596, which point to two majestic names, namely Qāhir (the Subduer) and Fāṭir (the Originator). And this number is measured by al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting) four times over, and by al-Jalīl (the Majestic) eight times over. As for the names of its letters, they are 799, which point to two majestic names, namely Ḥakam (the Judge) and Khāliq (the Creator). And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.

Faṣl 13: On His name, exalted is He, al-Bāriʾ (the Maker), glorified is He

This dazzling name — its occult property is assistance in those operations which require shaping by stages (taṭwīr) and tempering, and the preparing of materials for the reception of forms. So it is suitable for the blacksmith, the carpenter, the goldsmith, and their like. And whoever perseveres in it, there is unveiled to him something of the World of Images (ʿālam al-mithāl). Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — that whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and is one who treats bodies, the cure will prosper at his hands. And it has, of number, 213; and it is an odd, oblong, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 75, which point to His name, exalted is He, Dayyān (the Requiter). And it arises from the multiplication of (jīm, 3) by (Alif-Lām-Mīm, 71): for the jīm stands for gathering, and the alif for beginning, and the mīm for completion, and the lām for the linkage between them. And because in al-barʾ (the bringing forth) there lies the carrying of the shaping of matter through to its utmost limit, its utterance is sealed with the hamza. And it is sometimes set within a numerical threefold square (muthallath) encompassed by a letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī). And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

Faṣl 14: On His name, exalted is He, al- Muṣawwir (the Fashioner)

/fol. 132v./ This name, of majestic worth — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, there is made easy for him whatever he wishes to make of those crafts in which there is compounding and shaping. And if its square is engraved upon a ring of glass or of earthenware, no work of his will ever be spoiled. And if one possessed of a truthful spiritual state and of a footing firmly planted multiplies the remembrance of it, the intelligible meanings will descend upon him within sensible forms. And none will understand what we have alluded to save one possessed of complete unveiling (kashf) and penetrating insight. This is according to the method of the masters of secrets. As for the names of its letters, they are 399, which point to two majestic names, and they are Māniḥ (the Bestower) and Mukrim (the Honourer). And as for its square, this is its form:

Faṣl 15: On His name, exalted is He, al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), glorified is He

This generous name — whoever sets it in a square on the last night of the month, upon a sheet of lead, after reciting the name according to its number, and carries it: God, exalted is He, blinds to him the sight of every wrongdoer. Faṣl 17: On His name, exalted is He, al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), glorified is He

This name, of majestic worth — if a wayfarer perseveres in the remembrance of it, he sees how the provisions are apportioned. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes his provision abundant for him. And likewise whoever engraves it and carries it with him, Saturn being in its exaltation: he asks God, exalted is He, for nothing but that He gives it to him. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Sulaymān, and likewise for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Wahhāb. And it is among the all-comprehending secrets and names, and among the secrets of oddness (witriyya) and the secrets of evenness (shafʿiyya). And the second is a prime number, which points to divine oneness (tawḥīd) under this description; and for that reason it corresponds to al-Wāḥid (the One). And since its letters are according to this form, and its wafq is 142, it points to His name, exalted is He, Yā Salām (O Peace), with the yāʾ of address. Understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills. And God — glorified and exalted is He — speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. /fol. 133v./
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 142, the number of Yā Salām.]
Faṣl 18: On His name, exalted is He, al-Razzāq (the Provider), glorified is He

This mighty name, dazzling in its proof, is a litany of remembrance from among the litanies of remembrance of Mīkāʾīl — peace be upon him. No one makes remembrance of it but that God, exalted is He, makes easy for him his food and his drink. And likewise whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring and multiplies the remembrance of it on the night of mid-Shaʿbān. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Razzāq, and likewise for one whose name is Yūsuf. And it has a square of majestic worth, and this is the form of its arrangement:

And this name has, of number, 315 in utterance (lafẓan) and 308 in figure (raqman). So it is among the names that comprehend the secret of oddness and evenness. As for its number in utterance, it arises from the multiplication of the first odd number by the first fikrī dhikrī number, then the multiplication of the first odd number by the first perfect number, then from the multiplication of the total of the one by the total of the other. So its construction is from (alif),(jīm),(hāʾ), (zāy),(yāʾ),(kāf): for in it there is the self-subsistence of the alif, and the gathering of the jīm, and the inwardness of the hāʾ and its hiddenness, and the might of the zāy, and the descent of the yāʾ, and the bringing-into-being of the kāf. And because of the repetition of the zāy within it, in utterance and in numeration, every seeker of provision must inevitably be overtaken by hardship. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 311, which point to His name, exalted is He, Qahhār (the All-Subduing); for everyone who seeks provision from another is abased before him and subdued, and enters beneath his subduing power. We seek refuge in God from abasement before any other than Him.
Ḥikma (a wise saying). Cleave to a single door, and the doors will be opened to you; and submit to a single lord, and necks will submit to you.

As for its number in figure, it is an even-even-and-odd number: al-Qadīm (the Eternal) measures it twice over, and al-Mawlā (the Patron) four times. And it is a deficient number: its aliquot parts are 356, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mūṣil (the One who brings to arrival), and to His name Nūr (the Light). So it is at one with the heart in its aliquot parts; and for that reason what destroys people is the headlong rush after provision. A man said to Ḥātim al-Aṣamm: "From where do you eat?" He said: And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand (Q 63:7). As for the names of its letters, they are 512, which point to two majestic names, and they are Munʿim (the Bestower of favours) and Qarīb (the Near). Sometimes some of the masters of secrets have set it in a fivefold [square] according to this form, as you see. /fol. 134r./
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 315, the number of al-Razzāq in utterance.]

And likewise, whoever sets His name, exalted is He, Kāfī (the Sufficient), with the aforementioned ascendant, within a square, then looks upon it much while he is making remembrance of the name — and let the engraving be in the material befitting the object desired, after the square has also been written upon the instrument of engraving — and let him not cease making remembrance of the name until he becomes aware of an efficacious influence (taʾthīr), each according to his state: then it will be a help to him toward what we have mentioned and toward what he desires, if God, exalted is He, wills. And it is proper that the Moon be increasing in light and fortunate, in a fortunate sign; and if it be in the ascendant, that is stronger. So whoever gives the operations their full due is close to attaining what he seeks, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And whoever recites over his operation And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little (Q 17:74), God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter (Q 14:27) — be firm, if you are a believer in God and the Last Day — Man says on that day: Where is the place of escape? No indeed! There is no refuge. To your Lord, on that day, is the place of rest (Q 75:10–12), That is the abode of the hereafter: We appoint it for those who desire neither exaltation in the earth nor corruption; and the [good] outcome belongs to the God-fearing (Q 28:83). The more the conjurations are recited from a truthful heart and with a gathered resolve, the more fit is he for attaining what he seeks. So seek refuge in God from the ignorant: And do not take God's signs in mockery (Q 2:231), if you are people who understand. God wrote in the first Psalter that the denier of the manifest truth shall surely be cursed. And this is the form of its square, as you see.
