Faṣl 48: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wadūd (the Loving)

This attracting magnet and procuring ruby: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes beloved in the sight of everyone; and God makes the hearts of created beings firm upon love of him, and makes his own heart firm. And it is among the beautiful litanies of remembrance. And whoever sets down His name Wadūd and His name, exalted is He, Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account) in a threefold square (muthallath) whose centre /fol. 146r./ is with Jupiter in a conjunction of love, and carries it with him, is granted the love of hearts. And whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it and in the remembrance of the name al-Dāʾim (the Everlasting), his blessing endures. And it is fitting, in that the figure is, in [the matter of] love, of majestic worth. And know that whoever writes this name upon a white silk cloth thirty-five times, with the moon in its house and in conjunction, let him set it down in the first [hour] of Friday, with Venus in its exaltation; then let him persist in the remembrance of these names, and he will see marvels. And the operations of this are munificent (jawād). And [as for] the setting of the threefold square within the interior of a square of 96 — no one's gaze falls upon him but he loves him. And whoever wishes to set down this figure of magnificent worth, let his carrying of it be in a state of purity and fasting. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And some have set it down in this following form, and it is a litany of remembrance noble in its setting-down, so guard it well. And some of the masters have mentioned that whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him — then whoever sees him inclines to him by his very nature and loves him in his inmost being; and God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and his inward by the spirit of love, and adorns his outward with the secrets of affection. So ponder that and you will be rightly guided. And this is the form of what is promised by its remembrance, as you see.

And whoever sets it down in a four-by-four square by the names of its letters, in the first [hour] of Friday, and persists in the remembrance of it until the setting of the sun — no one's gaze falls [upon him] but he loves him. And in it is a strange secret and a wondrous meaning, for the attracting of the inward parts and the spirits and the procuring of the outward parts and the bodily forms. And it is a litany of remembrance for the masters of beauty, and for him who has tasted of the drinking-place of love and has sat upon the carpet of affection.

Do you not see that its letters correspond to Badūḥ, and that the names of its letters point to His name Sūl (the Object of Request), and the aliquot parts of its number to His name Ḥabīb (the Beloved)? So understand. And as for its majestic wafq, of lofty renown, this is its form, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided. So ponder that and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And this noble name has, of number, 20; and it is an even-even-and-odd number. There corresponds to it among the names Hādī (the Guide); and it is among the noble numbers. ((Show affection to one another and you will love one another.)) And as for the names of its letters, they are

96, which point to His name, exalted is He, Sūl (the Object of Request); for the Beloved, the Loving, is Himself the object of request. And when it produces its effect, there is affection — for it comes from the multiplication of the first cube number by the first number behind it. And it is an abundant number, its aliquot parts being 22, which point to His name Ḥabīb (the Beloved); for love is the fruit of affection. Love — from it is made the pursuit, which is among the traces of His name, exalted is He, Ṭālib (the Pursuer). So reflect upon that; and God bestows His bounty upon whom He wills, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing. And if you say: What is love? we say: the purity of affection. And it has been said: the perpetual inclination, with a heart distraught with longing. Waṣl: in a section belonging to this station there are four appellations:— al-ḥubb (love);— al-wudd (affection);— al-ʿishq (passionate love), which is the excess of love;— al-shaghafa (heart-smitten passion), which is the emptying out of the will into the beloved and attachment to him.
Faṣl 49: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Majīd (the All-Glorious)

This name, mighty in station and majestic in proof, is suitable as a litany of remembrance for kings — so understand. When they persevere in it, their kingdom becomes ample. And likewise it is suitable for the Poles (aqṭāb) and for those appointed as vicegerents. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him — his word is not turned back. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Majīd. And the master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: If a possessor of a truthful state perseveres in the remembrance of this noble name, God makes easy for him what is right (al-ṣāʾib), and gives life to his spirit by the light of the gnoses, and strengthens his inward by the subtleties of the secrets; and God, exalted is He, provides for him from whence he does not perceive. And it has a threefold square (muthallath) of majestic worth; and this is the form of its arrangement:
[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 57, the number of the name]

And in it is an object of desire: the bringing to light of the hidden stores of the earth, of treasures, and the lighting upon the secrets of the concealed things of the symbols. And it has, of number, 57. So the seven points to the fact that He is the One who is free of the liabilities of kingship — none is free of that save one who is a Doer of whatsoever He wills /fol. 147r./ — and that belongs to none but Him. And the fifty points to the fact that He is the One in whose hand is the pivot of everything; and that too is among the things that belong exclusively to Him, glorified and exalted is He. And it is an odd, oblong, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 21, which point to the alif of establishment (iqāma) and the kāf of the Word. And as for the names of its letters, they are 190 by one reckoning and 188 by another reckoning. So by the first reckoning they point to His name, exalted is He, Huwa Allāh al-Wāḥid (He is God, the One), the Necessary of Existence; and by the second reckoning they point to His name, exalted is He, Mawlā l-kull (the Patron of all). And its letter wafq (wafq ḥarfī) and its numerical threefold square are at times gathered together in a single square; and this is its form, as you see. So understand that.
Faṣl 50: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāʿith (the Raiser of the dead)

This most great name and most luminous secret is suitable for one whose resolve has grown weak in some matter; and whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is roused up to every good. Some of them said: it serves for the prevailing of life and health over the bodies, and for the preservation of the powers. If you desire that, then take clean garments, and fumigate with aloeswood and clove, and recite the name in a spiritual retreat (khalwa) made ready, and in purity of heart, until a [spiritual] state from it accrues to you; for God supplies you with strength and rouses your aspiration to the acts of obedience. The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God, exalted is He, sanctify his inmost secret — said: Whoever engraves this majestic name and beautiful secret upon a plate of lead in the first [hour] of Saturday, then makes remembrance of the name 4011 times while he gazes upon its drawn figure with a gaze of majesty, and then says: "O Zuḥal (Saturn), I have set you in power, by such-and-such, over So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]" — that comes to pass swiftly, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And this is the form of its square, and it is as you see:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 573, the number of the name]

And it has, of number, 573. The ʿayn and the thāʾ in it remain as they are, while the bāʾ of causation was taken together with the upright alif — which is the Causer of causes — so that there appeared the jīm, which indicates conjunction and the union of the cause with the Causer. And this number is odd and deficient. Its aliquot parts are 195, which point to His name, exalted is He, Ṣādiq (the Truthful), and to Mawlā l-mawālī (the Master of masters). And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.
Faṣl 51: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Shahīd (the Witness)

This lofty name and sublime secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, it yields him watchful vigilance (murāqaba) in his spiritual retreat (khalwa) and in his coming forth into company (jalwa). And if he is a possessor of a state of assimilation of character (takhalluq), that yields him the dyeing of his soul with the dye of unity and justice, so that he is secure from excess and from defect in the whole of /fol. 147v./ his soul's traits of character. And it is among the majestic litanies of remembrance. Some of them said: it is suitable for one who seeks the rank of martyrdom (shahāda). And I did indeed command one of the jurists to make remembrance of it, and he attained that at once. And the author of ʿIlm al-hudā mentioned that whoever inscribes it in the first [hour] of Friday upon a sheet of paper, to the number of its outward powers, before the Possessor of Lights (Dhū l-Anwār), and hangs it upon his heart without any barrier, the bodily forms bear witness to his generosity and his excellence, and mouths [base text: al-aqwāh] speak for him of his right guidance and his intellect; and God provides him with gravity, awe, might, and splendour. And it is among the treasured secrets. And it has a square of majestic worth, mighty in station. And this is the form of its arrangement:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries Qurʾānic disconnected letters —(mīm, 40), (Yā-Sīn, 70),(Ṭā-Hā, 14),(Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, 195) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 319, the number of the name]

And this name has, of number, 319; and it is a prime number, because its meaning, by reason of the threat it comprises, is a closure with no rift in it: Say: God suffices as a witness between me and you (Q 17:96). And as for the names of its letters — 412 — they point to His name, exalted is He, Mujrī l-fulk (the Setter of the ship in motion), because the ship courses before the eye of God, exalted is He, so He is its witness, even as there has come concerning that His word, exalted is He: coursing before Our eyes (Q 54:14). So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.
Faṣl 52: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥaqq (the Real)

This name, mighty in station and lofty in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes him firm in the acts of obedience, and makes manifest through it the realities of things, and gives him to look upon the hidden things of the secrets, and makes falsehood hateful to him, and makes his word subduing and exalted. And it is among the names of magnificent worth; and by it God makes firm those who believe. And whoever engraves its square under the ascendant of one of the fixed signs (al-burūj al-thawābit), upon an instrument in which he wishes to make firm something that has no firmness — God makes it firm for him. And that comes about only after the remembrance of the name, until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over the one who makes remembrance. And there is written upon the surface of the square, on its four sides: But as for what brings benefit to people, it abides in the earth (Q 13:17). And this is its form:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; four of the sixteen cells carry words instead of figures —(Awwal), (Ilāh),(Muḥīṭ) and (Kāfī) — and the wholly numerical rows and columns sum to 208, the number of the name in utterance]

And it has, of number, 208 in utterance (lafẓan) and 108 in figure (raqman). As for the first, it is an even, even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 432, which point to two majestic names, namely Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge) and Ṣabūr (the Patient), by reason of what the ṣād contains of the secret of correspondence with the body.

And as for the second number, it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 172, which point /fol. 148r./ to His name Muqbil (the One who turns toward). So understand that. And this is the form of its square:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells exactly as printed in the source, each row read from right to left; in the table below every row, column and both diagonals sum to 108, the number of the name in figure, except rows 2 and 3 and the first column, which as printed do not — reproduced unemended]
Faṣl 53: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wakīl (the Trustee)

This radiant ruby and dazzling secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, suffices him, and makes him independent of secondary causes, and provides for him whence he does not reckon. And if he be a possessor of a truthful state, he eats from the world of being (al-kawn). And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad. And it has a square of majestic worth; and this is its form:

[Wafq: 3×3, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; six of the nine cells carry words standing for their abjad values — (Ṭayyib, 21),(Wāḥid, 19),(Hādī, 20),(Ḥabīb, 22), (Ḥayy, 18),(Ṭabīb, 23) — and the constant of every row, column and diagonal is 66, the number of the name]
And whoever gathers its numerical wafq and its letter wafq in a single square — [it is] upon this form, as you see.

And it has, of number, 66; and it is an even-odd, oblong number. And this name is among the names that belong exclusively to Muḥammad and to the family of Muḥammad; and for that reason God, exalted is He, named him in the earlier scriptures al-Mutawakkil (the one who puts his trust [in God]). And by reason of the comprehensiveness of this name it has a special relation to the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace. It corresponds in number to the all-comprehending Name: for Allāh is 66, and Wakīl is 66, and the sum of that is 132, and that is his name — God bless him and grant him peace. And this number is an abundant number, according to what has preceded; its aliquot parts are 78, which point to His name Ḥakīm (the Wise), for if the trustee (wakīl) is not wise, he does not set things in their [proper] places. And concerning that, verse has been spoken:
When you send a man upon an errand, send one who is wise, and give him no instructions.

And the aliquot parts of each of the two names exceed its own base by 12; and that is His name, exalted is He, Aḥabb (Most Beloved), and it is among the names most proper to him — God bless him and grant him peace. And when the excess of the one is joined to the other, that comes to /fol. 148v./ 24, which is his name — God bless him and grant him peace — and His beloved. So the sum of the names is Muḥammad and His beloved, just as the sum of each of the two was Allāh [and] ḥubb (love), or Wakīl [and] ḥubb. And as for the names of its letters, they are 197, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), with the article — by reason of what trusteeship (wakāla) contains of standing over [affairs] (qiyām).
Faṣl 54: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Qawī (the Strong)

This name, magnificent in worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is strengthened by it for the carrying of heavy burdens, outward and inward; and his spirit is strengthened, and by it he gains command over everything. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of ʿAzrāʾīl. And it is fitting that one who labours at the carrying of heavy burdens should engrave it and carry it. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Mūsā (Moses); and it is proper that His name al-Mubdiʿ (the Originator from nothing) be added to it. And likewise for one whose name is Yūnus (Jonah). And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it does not grow weary in his journey, so long as he persists in its remembrance and in the carrying of it. And as for its square, it is according to this form:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 126, the number of the name in utterance (lafẓan)]

And it has, of number, 126; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 186, which point to a majestic litany of remembrance — whoever cleaves to it, nothing shall render him powerless — and it is Allāh maʿī (God is with me). This is what its numbers give you to understand, in utterance (lafẓan). But if you consider it in figure (raqman), it is 116; and it is an even, even-odd, deficient number; [its aliquot parts are] 94, which point to His name, exalted is He, ʿAzīz (the Mighty). And for that reason might (ʿizza) is the companion of strength (quwwa). And the first number points to Mūsā, and the second points to Yūnus. And as for the names of its letters, they are 206, which point to His name, exalted is He, Jabbār (the Compeller); and it is the place of manifestation of Mūsā. By [another] reckoning, 218, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muṣfiḥ (the One who overlooks [faults]); and it is the place of manifestation of Yūnus — peace be upon him. And know that whoever is nearer to the Presence of His name al-Qawī, and whose witnessing of it is the more complete, is the more bound to weakness, by reason of the turning to the Real (al-Ḥaqq) from the standpoint of that name. For that reason Mūsā — peace be upon him — said: And my brother Hārūn is more eloquent than I in tongue, so send him with me as a support; truly I fear that they will deny me (Q 28:34); Truly I have killed a soul among them, and I fear that they will kill me (Q 28:33); So Mūsā conceived within himself a fear (Q 20:67); They both said: Our Lord, truly we fear that he may act rashly against us, or that he may transgress (Q 20:45). The Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said ((concerning Yūnus b. Mattā, peace be upon him: He was a weak man)). And look at how the two of them share in being cast into the sea /fol. 149r./ — this one in the darkness of the chest (al-tābūt), and that one in the darkness of the belly of the whale. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.
Faṣl 55: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Matīn (the Firm)

This name of majestic worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not grow weak before a matter he has strength for, even were it doubled. And it is fitting that whoever fears the cutting off of his strength in some matter or other should multiply the remembrance of it. And when it is adjoined to al-Qawī (the Strong), it is of the utmost swiftness of efficacious influence in respect of one who labours at the carrying of heavy burdens. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him becomes awe-inspiring, possessed of strength, valour, leadership, and might. And in it is a wondrous meaning for the subjugation of kings. And it has, of number, 500; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 592, which exceed the original by that to which His name Amān (Security) points. For in firmness (matāna) there is security from the derangement of strength; and for that reason its end is the nūn, which is the existence of that through which manifestation and the making-manifest come to be. God the Magnificent said: Truly the best of those you might hire is the strong, the trustworthy (Q 28:26). And God, mighty and majestic is He, said: Truly We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and were afraid of it; and man bore it (Q 33:72). And they refused to bear it and were afraid of it only because they, though they have strength, have no firmness; and firmness is the trust (al-amāna) — that is, the security against the cutting off of strength. Then He said: and man bore it; truly he was a great wrongdoer— to himself, by laying upon it what it has no strength to bear — exceedingly ignorantof the cutting off of his strength, for want of his trustworthiness. And as for the names of its letters, they are 608, which point to two majestic names, namely Mukrim (the Honourer) and Rāziq (the Provider). And this is the form of its arrangement:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the four letters of Matīn —(mīm, 40),(tāʾ, 400),(yāʾ, 10), (nūn, 50) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 500, the number of the name]
Faṣl 56: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Walī (the Protecting Friend)

This sublime, dazzling name and radiant secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God takes him under His protection and takes him as His friend. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of the angels of the exalted Presence, those who are called the cherubim (al-karūbiyyūn). Whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it, realizing its meaning — which is the removal of the intermediaries — is established in the station of sainthood (wilāya). And know that the one who makes remembrance of it: nothing of the states of created beings calls upon him but that he is given an unveiling of it. And it has, of number, 56 in utterance (lafẓan) and 46 in figure (raqman). As for the first number, it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 60, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mubīḥ (the One who makes lawful) — because whoever has removed the intermediaries between himself and God, exalted is He, has had made lawful to him, from Himself, what is forbidden to others. And as for the second number, it is an even-odd, deficient number; its aliquot parts are 26, which point to a

/fol. 149v./ majestic name that is among the litanies of remembrance of the greatest of those who profess [His] oneness, namely your saying Aḥad Aḥad (Unique, Unique). For the walī (the saint) is he whose parts and particulars speak forth this litany of remembrance. And as for the names of its letters, they are 96, which point to His name, exalted is He, al-Dayyān (the Requiter), with the al- — so understand. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad. And this is the form of its arrangement:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 56, the number of the name in utterance]
Faṣl 57: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy)

This lofty litany of remembrance and manifest secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it becomes praiseworthy in his qualities, thanked for his deeds, and magnified in the eyes of all people. And whoever writes it by its number in a cup (jām) and gives it to drink to one who has an illness, God, exalted is He, heals him of it. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Maḥmūd. And know that whoever realizes this name is praiseworthy in character; and whoever unveils it with a complete unveiling is the most praiseworthy of you. And as for Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — he is the locus of manifestation of praise, His manifest creation; and he is the opening of the Book of Existence, as he said — God bless him and grant him peace: ((The first thing God, exalted is He, created was my light.)) For he — God bless him and grant him peace — is entirely praise. With him the Real, exalted is He, opened the Book of Existence, for it is a matter of consequence; and had He not begun it with the praise of God — who is Muḥammad and the most praiseworthy of them — it would have been maimed. And for that reason the last call of the prophets was his call, by force of And the last of their call is: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds (Q 10:10). So he — God bless him and grant him peace — is the Opener and the Seal, just as he is the Praise. And just as the Real — glorified, exalted and hallowed is He — opened with him the Book of the Beginning, so likewise God, exalted is He, will open with him the Book of the Return, as he said — God bless him: ((I am the first over whom the earth will split open.)) And for that reason he — God bless him and grant him peace — was singled out with Sūrat al-Ḥamd, which is the Fātiḥa of the Book, His mighty Book, from a treasure beneath the Throne that was not opened save by his name —

God bless him and grant him peace — Aḥmad. So understand these luminous tastings and ṣamadānī secrets, and you will win an ample portion of the knowledge of the bestowals of faith and the gnoses of the heart. And God — glorified and exalted is He — speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And this name has, of number, 62; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 34, and they point to your saying Huwa Ṭabīb (He is a Physician). And as for the names of its letters, they are 147, which point to your saying Huwa Muʾmin (He is a Granter of Security); and by another reckoning it is Muhaymin (the Overseer), or al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer). And as for its square, it is according to this form. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills. And praise be to God alone, and God bless … … … /fol. 150r./ And this is the form of its square, as you see.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 62, the number of the name]
Faṣl 58: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muḥṣī (the Reckoner)

This name, majestic in station and magnificent in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him to inherit watchful vigilance (murāqaba). And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one for whom al-Ḥasīb (the Bringer to Account) is suitable — except that, this [name] being free of the bāʾ, it is less in threat and in affliction. And it has, of number, 148. So the eight is for perfection, and the forty for completeness, and the hundred for encompassment; and al-Muḥṣī is He who possesses a perfection that is complete and all-encompassing. And this number is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 118, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muḥṣī (the Reckoner) among the people of the secrets, and to Ḥayy Malīk (Living Sovereign) [readingfor the edition's ] among the people of the lights; and that is by reason of what life requires of perfection, and kingship of encompassment.

Tanbīh. Know, all of you — may God, exalted is He, grant you success — that the generality of what has preceded, from His name al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate) to His name al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy): the notice they give (iʿlāmuhā) is only in respect of what pertains to the meaning of the secondary causes (asbāb) — such as al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), al-Karīm (the Generous), al-Razzāq (the Provider) and their like — and to knowledge — such as al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) and their like — and their conclusion has come to be al-Ḥamd (praise). But as for what is ranged in order along with them, from the name al-Muḥṣī to His name al-Ṣabūr (the Patient), the generality of them lie in a rank that brings into being the servant's incapacity, as has appeared in al-Muḥṣī, and as will appear in al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator) and al-Muʿīd (the

Restorer) and the rest, if God, exalted is He, wills, up to al-Ṣabūr; and in [a rank] that brings gnosis into being as a disposition, as has appeared to you in His name al-Hādī (the Guide). And it is as though He, glorified and exalted is He, began with that in which creatures have the semblance of a share — even if only by [their own] claim — and then sealed with that in which they have no share at all; rather all of them confess their incapacity before it, such as the initiating [of creation], and the restoring, and the giving of life, and the giving of death. So ponder that. And God knows best. And as for the names of its letters, they are 205, which point to two majestic names, and they are ʿAzīz (the Mighty) and Kāfī (the Sufficient). And this is the form of its square, as you see.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the four letters of Muḥṣī —(mīm, 40), (ḥāʾ, 8), (ṣād, 90),(yāʾ, 10) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 148, the number of the name]
Faṣl 59: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator)

This luminous name and lordly secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, the hidden aspects of affairs are disclosed to him, and God, exalted is He, causes him to speak with wisdom; and nothing of him becomes apparent to anyone save what he wishes. And it is among the majestic names, for whoever desires the accomplishment of his affair in the world of generation. And whoever /fol. 150v./ perseveres in it, his works become good and endure. And it is suitable for whoever wishes to make a beginning in some affair among affairs. And know — may God grant me and you success — that whoever is assiduous in the remembrance of it grows intimate with the sublime sciences, and speaks of the matters of wisdom, and speaks in verse. And it has, of number, 56. So it stands to al-Walī (the Protecting Friend) as al-Wakīl (the Trustee) stands to His name, exalted is He, Allāh. And therefore, when the two are joined together, His name, exalted is He, Mubīn (the Evident), appears; and by patronage (walāya) and initiation — which is the bringing to manifestation — everything is made evident. And as for the names of its letters, they are 141, which point to His name, glorified and exalted is He, ʿĀlim (the Knower). And as for its noble square, this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; purely numerical, and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 56, the number of the name]
Faṣl 60: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muʿīd (the Restorer)

This noble, spiritual name and verdant, all-merciful name: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it sets right by it everything corrupt, and recovers everything that has gone. And when it is set down with one of the movable signs (al-burūj al-munqaliba) in the ascendant [reading

for the edition's ,]and is hung up in the path of the wind, and the person keeps on reciting the Name the whole night long over a runaway slave or a traveller, he returns to his place from which he went out, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. Some have said: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it recovers everything he has forgotten. And it has, of number, 124; and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 100, which point to His name, exalted is He, Malīk (the Sovereign) — for none restores things after they have gone save one who owns them with a complete ownership.

And for that reason the Real, glorified and exalted is He, manifests Himself by the name al-Malik (the King), since it is the day of restoration. And this number also indicates the letter (qāf), by reason of what lies in the encompassment of the utmost limit of the descent of the beginning (al-badʾ). And as for the names of its letters, they are 266, which point to two majestic names, namely Malīk (the Sovereign) and Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). And as for its square, it is according to this form:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the four letters of Muʿīd —(mīm, 40),(ʿayn, 70),(yāʾ, 10),(dāl, 4) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 124, the number of the name]
Faṣl 61: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muḥyī (the Giver of Life)

This dazzling name of self-sufficiency (ṣamadānī) and radiant lordly secret — whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, gives him life by the spirit of divine oneness (tawḥīd), and gives life through it to every thing. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of Isrāfīl. And know that whoever perseveres in this name, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and makes manifest the power of his inward in his outward; and in it there is a relation (nisba) to /fol. 151r./ His name al-Ḥayy (the Living). And whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring of steel at the time of the Friday prayer and wears it, God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and to his renown, and magnifies his worth, and he sees of the subtlety of God, exalted is He, toward him what descriptions are powerless to encompass. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of the secrets know. And it has, of number, 68; and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 58, which point to His name, exalted is He, Azalī (the Pre-eternal). And as for the names of its letters, they are 144, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muʿizz (the Giver of might), by reason of what there is in giving life of the granting of might, and in bringing death of abasement. And this is the form of its square.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 68, the number of the name]
Faṣl 62: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mumīt (the Bringer of Death)

This name, mighty in station and evident in proof, is for whoever intends by it the destruction of the wrongdoers and the cutting off of the last remnant of the transgressors. And no one multiplies the remembrance of it and then invokes against a wrongdoer but that he perishes on the spot. And it has a mighty efficacious influence (taʾthīr) in quieting what is stirred up of appetite. And no one perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him, and then makes mention of the name of the one whose destruction he intends, but that God, exalted is He, destroys him on the spot. And it has, of number, 490; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 536; and it is a number which niʿma l-mawlā (excellent Patron) measures by twos. And as for the names of its letters, [they are] 592, which point to two majestic names, namely Amān (Security) and Matīn (the Firm). And it has a square of majestic worth; and this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

Faṣl 63: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ḥayy (the Living)

This name of exalted worth and secret of manifest effect: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until the spirits come into accord with him, it increases his continuance in this world, and God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart with the spirit of divine oneness. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of Jibrāʾīl — peace be upon him. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is

Idrīs. And this name has, of number, 28; and it is an even-even-and-odd number, and it is the second of the numbers [that is] a perfect number; and the perfect numbers are nobler than the abundant and the deficient. And it is very rare, for there is not found of them save a single number in each rank, by which that rank has life. So in the rank of units, 6; and in the rank of tens, 28; and in the rank of hundreds, 296 — and that is /fol. 151v./ his name, God bless him and grant him peace, Rasūl (Messenger); and in the rank of thousands, 912. So the matter returns to the manifestation of the twenty-eight. And since perfection — which is life — is the ultimate end, there could be upon it no increase and in it no deficiency; for if it admitted increase it would not be perfection, and so would not be life; and if anything were diminished from it, there would be in it death to the measure of the deficiency in it. And for that reason the twenty-eight arises from the multiplication of the first complete number by the first square number. And this number is the number of the letters, which are the perfection of existence, and the number of the mansions determined in the greatest sphere, which are [the locus of] the descent of the divine command, standing to it as the points of articulation (makhārij) stand to the letters. And the secrets of this number are many, and are not suited to this epitome. And in sum: nothing comes into being from the Living save what is living. This is in respect of its utterance. And as for it in respect of its figure: it is composed of two letters, and,and that is 18; and it is an even-odd, abundant number, its aliquot parts being 21; and that is a composite number, [arising] from the multiplication of the first odd number by the first complete [number]. So what was multiplied by the encompassment of the dāl came to be multiplied by the comprehensiveness of the jīm, and the number is diminished by seven; and these are the realities of the letters, which here are danā al-danā [reading and sense uncertain: perhaps "the nearest of the near"; the printed form is not the elative " , the lowest of the low", which the context would as readily support], by which is the life of longevity — which is a turning-back in creation, as God, exalted is He, has said: And whomever We give length of days, We turn him back in creation (Q 36:68). And for that reason the Fātiḥa was kept safe from these letters, so that it came to be twenty-one letters. So ponder that. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And as for the names of its letters, they are 20, which point to His name Hādī (the Guide). And as for its square, it is by the names of its letters, according to this form:

Faṣl 64: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting)

This greatest, radiant name and generous, dazzling secret: whoever makes remembrance of it, God establishes his affair, outwardly and inwardly; and if he be the possessor of a truthful state, God, exalted is He, establishes through him every thing. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of operative deployment (taṣrīf) know. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Yūsuf (Joseph) — a verification that is not hidden from any possessed of understanding. And know that self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya) belongs exclusively to Him, exalted is He: Is He, then, who stands over every soul with what it has earned…(Q 13:33); And God encompasses them from behind (Q 85:20); And He is with you wherever you are (Q 57:4); To God belong the East and the West; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God (Q 2:115); Truly those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to God; the hand of God is above their hands (Q 48:10); Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the alms (Q 9:104); And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw (Q 8:17). ((Truly the alms falls into the hand of the All-Merciful.)) ((I fell sick, and you did not visit Me.)) ((It is not I who carry you; God has carried you.)) ((I am his hearing and his sight.)) /fol. 152r./ So His name, exalted is He, al-Qayyūm is explicit as to the encompassment of His oneness (tawḥīd) over every one of His names, in every outward thing of creation and inward thing of the Command, and in the barzakh between the two: Alif-Lām-Mīm. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 3:1–2); And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them save in truth (Q 15:85). For just as the name of God, exalted is He, is such that nothing other than He is established alongside it — by reason of what creation sees of His oneness — so likewise is the name al-Qayyūm; and it is among those [names] from which God has withheld the tongues, so that none other than He has been named by it. And there has come, concerning the Greatest Name, His saying, exalted is He: And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 2:163); God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255). And the Greatest Name of God is that which, when any appearer other than He appears, the appearing things dissolve away through its self-subsistence. Indeed, every thing apart from God is vain. And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them save in truth (Q 15:85). And the living die through the perfection of His life: Everyone upon it is perishing, and there abides the Face of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour (Q 55:26–27); Truly you are to die, and truly they are to die (Q 39:30). And all perishes save God, by reason of His divinity: And there is no god but God (Q 3:62); God bears witness that there is no god but He (Q 3:18); Truly those upon whom you call apart from God will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it; and if the fly should snatch something from them, they could not rescue it from him (Q 22:73). And every mercy is cut off by the all-mercifulness (raḥmāniyya) of the All-Merciful: Do you know any namesake for Him?(Q 19:65). And every multiplicity is brought to nought by His unicity (waḥdāniyya): And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qurʾān, they turn away upon their backs, recoiling (Q 17:46).

And it has, of number, 166; and it is an even-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 86, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mawʾil (the Place of Recourse) — for the recourse of every thing is unto its sustainer (qayyim) — and to His name, exalted is He, Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator); for the sustainer of every thing, its reality, is only a wondrous origination, as He said, exalted is He: the Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth (Q 2:117). And this number also points to the highest of the names in establishment (iqāma) and to the lowest of them in descent, and that is His name Malīk (the Sovereign). This is if you consider its letters in utterance (lafẓan); but if you consider [them] in figure (raqman), it has, of number, 156; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 236. And this number is the coming-to-be (kāna) of every sustainer and every station, which is "Be", and it is (Q 2:117). And as for the names of its letters, they are 308, which point to His name, exalted is He, Rāziq (the Provider); for the subsistence of every thing is by His sustaining supply (madad), by that from which comes the root of its existence — and that is provision. So ponder that. And as for its wafq, it is according to this form:

And al-Qayyūm is the inward of al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent). And at times the letter [square] and the numerical [square] are gathered together in a single square, in this form, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 152v./
And this is the noble square.

And know that al-Ḥayy (the Living) and al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting) are two majestic names, and they are a litany of remembrance for the people of the Presence. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — and of all the angels of the Trumpet. And whoever engraves the two names at the rising of the sun on Friday, facing the qibla, and keeps it by him — God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart and to his renown, even if he were obscure, and gives life to his provision, even if it were scant; and measure [the rest] by it. And whoever composes its wafq — and it is one hundred and seventy-four — and carries it, witnesses wonders. And this is the best of the ways. And this is the form of its arrangement:

Al-Kattānī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy on him — said: I saw the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — in a dream, and I said to him: O Messenger of God, call upon God, exalted is He, for me, that He not cause my heart to die. And the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: Say every day forty times: O Living, O Self-Subsisting, there is no god but You. And know that whoever sets down His name, exalted is He, Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver) in a square, and deposits it within the interior of the figure whose mention has preceded, with the Sun in its exaltation, and carries it with him — God, exalted is He, gives life to his heart, and enlarges his provision, and preserves him in his family, his person, and his property. And whoever writes it upon anything, it is preserved, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And whoever knows its secret is made independent by it of all besides; for it is of a perfection of an utmost degree that expression cannot attain. And within it is the Greatest Name of God, which, when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see. /fol. 153r./
Faṣl 65: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wājid (the Finder)

This name, majestic in worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it loses nothing of what he wills to find; and by it the wayfarers come to know their own souls with a gnosis of ecstatic finding (wajd). And whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him finds within his inmost being what had not been within his prior acquaintance of the sciences and the landmarks [of knowledge], and his foot becomes firmly rooted in the judgements that come of [immediate] tasting (dhawq). And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Wājid. And it has, of number, 14; and it is an even-odd, oblong number — save that there is in it a nobility, inasmuch as it is composite, from the multiplication of the first even number by the first complete number, so that it is measured by the seven twice over. And it is the number of the luminous letters, and of the nights of the increase of the light; for they are nights of finding (wajd), and the nights of the decrease are nights of losing (faqd). And it is a deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 10, which point to the letter (yāʾ), which is a name for the lofty descent, in His saying, exalted is He: ((By Me he hears, and by Me he sees)). And for that reason the names of its letters point to your saying [huwa fāṣil, "He is one who separates"]; so by the names of its letters is separation (faṣl) effected. And as for its square, it is according to this form:

13),(alif, 111), (jīm, 53),(dāl, 35) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 212, the number of the names of its letters]
Faṣl 66: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mājid (the Glorious)

This dazzling name and radiant litany of remembrance: when a king multiplies the remembrance of it, his kingdom becomes wide, his word takes effect, and the hearts of his subjects are gathered upon love of him. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is ʿAbd al-Mājid. And it has, of number, 48; and it is a noble number, because it is from the multiplication of the first perfect number by the first number, then from the multiplication of the aggregate by the first number as well. And it is a number that indicates the perfection that is made easy and complete, of which the exemplar in respect of hearing is Ḥā-Mīm, which he — God bless him and grant him peace — took as his watchword, and which he commanded on the day of Uḥud, seeking glory (majd) for his community — [glory] which is the all-gathering of the kingdom, and its widening, and its permanence. And it is an abundant number, which none of the odd numbers measures except the three. Its aliquot parts are 86, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mawʾil (the Place of Recourse); for whoever's kingdom becomes wide is the place of recourse of every seeker, and he is the patron of whoever makes request of him. And it points to His name — glorified, blessed, and exalted is He — Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator). And it has a noble square in which the names of its letters are set down; and this is its arrangement. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified is He, speaks [the truth], and He guides to the way.

Faṣl 67: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Aḥad (the Unique)

This ṣamadānī name (of self-sufficiency) and all-merciful secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it grows estranged from multiplicity. And in it is a subtle secret for whoever desires to render a man or a woman barren of childbearing. And it is among the litanies of remembrance of the great ones. The author of Taysīr al-maṭālib — may God, glorified and exalted is He, sanctify his spirit — said: it is among the nearest of the names to the name of the holy Essence, and hence it comes immediately after it in Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. And when it is annexed to the all-comprehending Name, it is among the mightiest of the litanies of remembrance and the most majestic of them; and it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Aḥmad. And as for al-Aḥad and al-Wāḥid (the One), they are a litany of remembrance majestic in station, for the wayfarers who cleave to the secrets of divine oneness (tawḥīd). Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī — may God sanctify his inmost secret — said: As for al-Aḥad, it is a name that is suitable for the people of annihilation (fanāʾ), those immersed in the very source of union (ʿayn al-jamʿ), those consumed away in the seas of singling out (tafrīd). And as for al-Wāḥid, it is a name that is suitable for the people of annihilation in the Presence of union, for they witness none but One. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, glorified and exalted is He, opens up to him divine oneness. And whoever engraves the two names at sunrise on Sunday (yawm al-aḥad) upon a sheet of paper, facing the qibla, in a state of purity and making remembrance, and places it in his turban — God, exalted is He, provides him with might, awe, gravity, and magnificence. And this is the form of its arrangement.
[Wafq: 7×7, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; every row is a cyclic rotation of (Aḥad Wāḥid), the two names named in the text, and all seven rotations occur once each]

And this name has, of number, 13; and it is a prime number, because the meaning of oneness (aḥadiyya) is a closing-up (ratq) in which there is no rending open (fatq). And as for the names of its letters, they are, by one reckoning, 102, and by another reckoning, 156. So the first number points to His name, exalted is He, Mubīn (the Evident), on account of what there is in oneness of meaning for the name Allāh; and for that reason it comes immediately after it in Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. And it points also to His name, exalted is He, Aʿlā (the Most High), on account of what it contains /fol. 154r./ of exaltation above the apprehensions of creation, since it is a clear declaration of the all-comprehending Name. And the second number points to His name, exalted is He, Muʾnis (the Bestower of Intimacy), for by the oneness of creation every estranged one is made intimate: and He is with you wherever you may be (Q

57:4), there is no secret counsel of three but He is the fourth of them (Q 58:7). And therefore whoever has found intimacy [with Him] has grown estranged from all that is other than Him. And as for its square, it is by the names of its letters; and this is its form, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

The master Abū ʿAbd Allāh Zayn al-Dīn — may God sanctify his inmost secret — said in his book Kanz al-asrār wa-dhakhāʾir al-abrār ("The Treasure of Secrets and the Stores of the Righteous"): And whoever sets down these names, magnificent in worth and majestic in worth — and they are Allāh, Aḥad (the Unique), Wāḥid (the One), Wājid (the Finder), Jawād (the Munificent), Wahhāb (the Bestower), Ḥayy (the

Living), Mūjid (the Bringer into Existence), Dāʾim (the Everlasting), Walī (the Protecting Friend), Mujīb (the Answerer), Awwal (the First), Wadūd (the Loving), Hādī (the Guide) — in a square (murabbaʿ), and deposits it in the interior of the square of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, beholds of the making of God, exalted is He, what expressions are powerless to compass. And know that every name among these names gives to the one who bears it what lies within its power of life of the heart through the light of the gnoses and the subtleties of divine oneness. And if one possessed of a truthful [spiritual] state persists in the remembrance of it, God, glorified and exalted is He, enlarges for him his provision, the inward and the outward; and he asks God for nothing but that He gives him what he asked. And it is among the mightiest of figures in benefit and the most complete of them in profit. It is set down for kings and sultans, for their triumph over their peers, in the exaltation of the Sun; and for commanders and soldiery, in the exaltation of Mars; and for judges and scholars, in the exaltation of Jupiter; and for scribes and viziers, in the exaltation of Mercury; and for the masters and the [spiritual] poor (fuqarāʾ), in the exaltation of Saturn. So ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets and the guarded gems. And its pole points to the noble stone, and it is a letter from among the letters of the Greatest Name of God. And whoever writes it a hundred times and intends the destruction of a tyrant or a wrongdoer, God, exalted is He, destroys him on the spot. And it cannot be expounded in explicit expression, but only by veiled allusion (talwīḥ), which is understood by one whose custom it is to understand from God, glorified and exalted is

He. So blessed be God, the best of creators, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified and exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 154v./
Faṣl 68: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge)

This magnificent name and generous secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, his need of the engendered beings grows small. And it is fitting that the practitioners of the spiritual disciplines (riyāḍāt) take it as a litany of remembrance — they who forsake what created beings stand in need of, of food and sleep and the rest. And when a possessor of a truthful state perseveres in the remembrance of it, the needs of created beings revert to him. And know: as for al-Ṣamad, it is a litany of remembrance that is suited to those who undertake the spiritual discipline by hunger especially. The one who remembers it feels no pang of hunger at all, so long as he does not admit upon it any other litany of remembrance. So understand that. And it has, of number, 134; and it is an even-odd, oblong, deficient number. And as for the names of its letters, they are 220, which point to His name Malīk (the Sovereign) and His name Makīn (the Firmly Established). So understand. And it has a majestic square, and this is its form:

Faṣl 69: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Qādir (the Powerful)

Faṣl 70: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent)

This noble, lofty name and subtle, manifest secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes easy for him all operations. And it is suitable for master-craftsmen and for those who employ in service the artisans who are under their hands, and for everyone who wishes to bring operations to manifestation at the hand of one below him. And it has a noble square, five by five, /fol. 155v./ which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul); and it is of majestic worth for whoever esteems it with the esteem that is its due. And as for al-Shadīd (the Severe), al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Qāhir (the Subduer), and al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent) [the edition prints, al-Mutaqaddir] — they are names of subduing and of overcoming and of their mastery. No one invokes by it against a wrongdoer at the combustion of the month, in the seventh [hour] of the night, in a darkened house, bare-headed, upon the ground with no barrier between him and it, saying at the end of every hundred, "O al-Shadīd, take for me my right from So-and-so", and fixing his gaze upon nothing, [but that … — lacuna in the edition]. And God knows best what he does. And no one engraves them upon a signet-ring and wears it but that it clothes him with an awe which he perceives in his own self and which others perceive in him; and every obstinate tyrant is terrified of him at the sight of him, so that it is as though majesty were upon his shoulders for as long as he looks at the one who is with him. So understand, and you will be rightly guided; and reason by analogy upon it. And this is the form of its arrangement.
