Faṣl 71: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muqaddim (the Advancer)

This manifest, dazzling name and beautiful, radiant design: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has an operative deployment (taṣrīf) in the world of [divine] power. And whoever engraves it within its square, and makes remembrance of it thereafter, and asks by it for the advancement of a person, is answered on the spot. And it is among the treasured secrets, so ponder it. And it has, of number, 188 in utterance (lafẓan); and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 148, which point to His name, exalted is He, Muḥṣī (the Reckoner). And 184 in figure (raqman); and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 176, which point to His name, glorified and exalted is He, Mūsiʿ (the Enlarger). /fol. 156r./ And as for its square, it is according to this form.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the letters of Muqaddim —(mīm, 40),(qāf, 100),(the doubled dāl, 4 + 4 = 8),(mīm, 40) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 188, the number of the name in utterance]
Faṣl 72: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muʾakhkhir (the Deferrer)

This luminous, majestic name and beautiful, all-merciful secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it has a subduing operative deployment (taṣrīf) in the world. And whoever operates by it as has preceded in the foregoing [name], it gives him what lies within its power. And it ought not to be made a remembrance except together with al-Muqaddim. And know that whoever wishes to advance someone to his [proper] rank, let him depict a form upon a tablet after the most beautiful of forms, and let him set the tablet before him, gazing at it with gathered aspiration, purity of the inward, and presence of heart, while he makes remembrance saying Yā Mutaqaddim (O Foremost), until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him. And he may behold the form performing the remembrance along with him; let him not flee, but keep to that state for a temporal hour, for his need will be fulfilled by the leave of God, exalted is He — especially for the masters of [spiritual] states. So understand that, for it is not possible to declare more openly than this saying in this place. And God knows best. And this is appended to the secret of His name, exalted is He, Muqaddim (the Advancer). So understand, and measure what is absent by what is present, and the circle of understanding will widen for you. And be a believer in it, even if there is not opened to you a door from the Dominion (malakūt) through which the secrets are witnessed. So glory be to Him who has granted the gnostics the enjoyment of the unveiling of the secrets of self-sufficiency (ṣamadāniyya), and has barred the doubters from the well-spring of the substance of the lordly lights.

And this name has, of number, 1446 in utterance (lafẓan) and 846 in figure (raqman). As for its number in utterance, it is an even-odd, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 1458, which point to two majestic names, namely Mulqī al-Rūḥ (the Caster of the Spirit) and Ghālib (the Prevailer); and it exceeds its base by the name Wājib (the Necessary). And as for its numbering in figure, it is an even-odd, abundant number: its aliquot parts are 1026, exceeding its base by what points to His name, exalted is He, Mulqī (the Caster), and Muqīl (the Remitter), and Mufnī (the Annihilator), and Samīʿ (the All-Hearing). And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of inner sight (baṣāʾir) know. So ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets.

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the four letters of Muʾakhkhir —(mīm, 40), (wāw with hamza, 6),(khāʾ, 600), (rāʾ, 200) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 846, the number of the name in figure]
Faṣl 73: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Awwal (the First)

This healing, noble name and lofty, subtle secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it becomes one who presses onward to the virtues, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until some of its worlds come into accord with him — the one who makes remembrance of it remains tranquil throughout the whole of his life. And it has, of number, 43 in utterance (lafẓan) and 37 in figure (raqman). As for /fol. 156v./ the forty-three, it is a prime number, because the meaning of al-Awwal is a closure with no rift in it. And as for the thirty-seven, it has already been dealt with under the name Ilāh (God). And as for the names of its letters, by the first consideration they point to His name, exalted is He, Qadīm (the

Eternal), because of what firstness contains of the meaning of pre-eternity (qidam). And as for the second consideration, it points to His name, exalted is He, ʿĀlim (the Knower), or Qāʾil (the Speaker). And from this it has become clear to you which of the two considerations is the more transparent. And it has a noble square, which the masters of operative deployment (taṣrīf) know. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 37, the number of the name in figure]
Faṣl 74: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ākhir (the Last)

This noble name and subtle secret: whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it will be the one who remains after his enemies, and God, exalted is He, will give him the earth to inherit after them; and none will show him enmity but that God, exalted is He, destroys him. And know that whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it — God gives him of strength against the enemies, and of victory over them, what tongues are powerless to describe; and he has awe-inspiring presence and acceptance. And whoever writes it upon a tablet of red copper in the first [hour] of the day of Saturday, with the moon in the dark of the month (muḥāq) — or [where the writing] proceeds from perfect faith and a collected inmost being — while he recites the Name until he perceives its efficacious influence (taʾthīr) according to his state, and then casts it into the fire: that wrongdoer, against whom the operation has been performed in his name, perishes after a few days, according to what certain of the scholars — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them — have expressly stated concerning that. And this name has, of number, 802; and it is an even-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 404, which point to two majestic names, and they are Rabb (the Lord) and Munʿim (the Bestower of favours). And it has a noble square, of majestic worth, known to whoever has inner discernment (iṭṭilāʿ) of the occult properties (khawāṣṣ) of the names and the secrets of the numbers. And this is its form.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 802, the number of the name]
Faṣl 75: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest)

This name of exalted worth and secret of manifest affair: whoever persists in the remembrance of it, the Real, exalted is He, makes manifest to him the hidden aspects of affairs, and by it treasures are brought forth. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the people of the lights know by its congruity [reading for the edition's .] Some of them have said: whoever engraves it upon a sword and fights with it will be the one who triumphs and prevails over his enemy — especially if he be a possessor of a truthful state. And it has, of number, 1106; and it is /fol. 157r./ an even-odd, deficient number, its aliquot parts being 814, which point to two majestic names, namely Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer) and Khafī (the Concealed). And as for the names of its letters, 1222, they point to two majestic names, namely Mughnī (the Enricher) and Maʿbūd (the Worshipped). And it has a noble square, which the masters of inner discernment (arbāb al-iṭṭilāʿ) know; and this is the form of its arrangement:
[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 1106, the number of the name]

Know that as for His name, exalted is He, al-Nūr (the Light), and al-Bāsiṭ (the Expander), and al-Ẓāhir (the Manifest) — it is the litany of remembrance of the masters of the unveilings. And whoever wishes to behold something in his sleep, let him make remembrance of these names in a state of purity while he is in his bed, until he falls asleep upon this litany of remembrance, and let him set his aspiration (himma) to work upon what he desires; for the unveiling of that will be represented to him in his sleep. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.
Faṣl 76: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāṭin (the Hidden)

This mighty, lordly name and generous, self-sufficient secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is made safe from what he fears, and his soul is set at rest, and his heart is enlarged, and his inward is illumined. And some of them have said: whoever persists in the remembrance of it until its worlds accompany him and make remembrance along with him — he comes to no land but that its people turn to him with kindness and obedience, and with him are all the worlds; and everyone who sees him loves him, and everyone whom he calls answers his invocation with kindness. And in it are secrets for the people of divine oneness (tawḥīd) which none know but they. And whoever gathers together within a square its numerical and its letter secrets — of the letters and of their names — is given to look upon the inward aspects of the secrets and their realities. And it is among the noble litanies of remembrance for one who has a spiritual discipline (riyāḍa). So take to the remembrance of it with its conditions. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Muḥammad.

The master Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God sanctify his inmost secret — said: Whoever writes it by its number, with the moon increasing in light, in a bowl of glass, and multiplies the remembrance of it until a state from it comes to prevail over him, and effaces it with rainwater and drinks it for a number of days equal to its number, while he is seeking the lordly unveilings and the luminous gnoses — he attains them; and nothing of the affairs of the world remains hidden from him but that God, exalted is He, gives him to look upon it in his sleep, or in his waking [reading for the edition's

,] according to his state. And if he be a possessor of a truthful state and of complete orientation, the veil of the husk is lifted from his inward, so that he needs no explanation along with it; rather that is a plain, verified unveiling and a sound, well-guided description. So understand the symbol, and conceal the treasure, and make your belief sound — you will prosper. And God has, within every one of the names, wisdoms and secrets and subtleties and effects such as are not grasped by the way of rational speculation, but rather by something beyond that, which he grasps who has been dislodged from halting with the intelligibles to what lies beyond that, of noble secrets and wondrous effects. And above every possessor of knowledge there is one all-knowing (Q 12:76).

And know — may God bring you forth from the abysses of the dense things to the degrees of the subtle things — that just as He alone is the One characterized by manifestation, so He alone is the One characterized by hiddenness; and His is the hiddenness to whose ending there is no limit. So it comes about that every hidden thing is a manifest thing in relation to what is /fol. 157v./ more hidden than it. So the Command is the hidden aspect of creation, and He to whom belong the Command and creation is hidden from them both; and so the hiddenness of the Command is a matter of relative consideration, not a real one, and the Hidden in reality is none but He such that, when a coursing [ray] from His light courses forth, it makes manifest every hidden thing.

And this name has, of number, 62; and it is an even-odd, deficient number, its aliquot parts being 34, which point to this noble phrase, namely your saying huwa Ṭabīb (He is a Physician). And as for the names of its letters, they point to the inward of the human being, which is his heart, since their number is 132. So they are written as heart after heart: [the heart] of the Qurʾān, which is expressed by Yā-Sīn, and [they point] to the heart of the world, which is expressed by Muḥammad — in the tasting (dhawq) of some, and to both matters in the tasting of certain others. And His name al-Bāṭin is the origin of unity and of justice, and the heart is the locus of the manifestation of them both. And Muḥammad the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — is the most hidden of what has become manifest to creation, and the most manifest of what has been hidden of the Command. And in another respect they point to His name al-Munīl (the Bestower) and al-Sanī (the Sublime). And as for its wafq, it is mighty; and this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 62, the number of the name]
Faṣl 77: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Wālī (the Governor)

This mighty, dazzling name and ancient, radiant figure is suitable for governors, and for the Poles (aqṭāb), and for those appointed as vicegerents, and for the masters and the spiritual guides, and for everyone who has a flock whose affairs he governs. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is held in awe by created beings all together. And whoever breaks it within its square, with the moon in the increase of light, and makes remembrance of it by its number while he is seeking a governorship — he attains it. And it has, of number, 47, and it is a prime number. As for the seven, it is on account of what governorship contains of deliverance by severity; and as for the forty, it is on account of what it contains of the completion of kingship. And as for the names of its letters, they have, of number, 207, which is a number between al-Jābir (the Restorer) and al-Jabbār (the Compeller); it points to two majestic names, namely Sulṭān (the Sovereign) and Majīd (the All-Glorious). And in another respect it points to His name, exalted is He, Jābir (the Restorer). And as for its square, it is according to this form, as you see.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 47, the number of the name]
Faṣl 78: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mutaʿāl (the Most Exalted)

This name, lofty in station, and this secret, sublime in proof: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not vie in loftiness with anyone in any matter whatsoever but that he /fol. 158r./ rises above him. And it is suitable for whoever is exposed to a dispute or to a legal proceeding. And whoever sets its square in a plate of lead, with Saturn in its exaltation or in its house and in sound condition, and makes remembrance of the name according to its number, subdues by it every obstinate foe. And it is among the names of majestic worth. Some of them have said: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, hardships are made light for him, and by it every difficult matter is humbled. And it has a square of majestic worth, which the people of inner sight know. Whoever inscribes it upon a yellow silk cloth with saffron, the moon being in its exaltation, and makes remembrance of the name three hundred times, and carries it with him — he sees, of the kindness of God, exalted is He, toward him, such luminous awe and sovereign might as the vessels of the letters are too narrow to hold. And this name has, of number, 551; and it is an odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 49, which point to two lofty letters, namely (ṭāʾ) and (mīm); and these are two letters that indicate the complete deliverance from the fetters of the ranks, which is the utmost of exaltation. And it is a square number, from the multiplication of the first complete number by itself. And as for the names of its letters, they are 814, which point to two majestic names, namely Mukrim (the Honourer) and Rashīd (the Rightly Guiding). And as for its square, it is according to this form:

[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the five letters of Mutaʿāl — read from right to left, (mīm, 40),(tāʾ, 400),(ʿayn, 70),(alif, 1),(lām, 30) — and the constant of every row and of every column, and of one diagonal, is 541]
Faṣl 79: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Barr (the Benign)

This majestic name and beautiful design: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it is treated with gracious kindness (luṭf) in all his states; blessings follow one upon another for him, together with abundance of increase. And whoever sets it upon a plate of silver, together with such of the names as derive from it, asks God, exalted is He, for nothing by it but that He gives it to him. And in it is safety for the traveller by land and by sea. And when the traveller multiplies the remembrance of it, God makes his objects of request easy for him, and God smooths his road for him, and he is preserved among his family. And if the wind grows distressful, or turns against the people of a ship, and they multiply the remembrance of it, the fair wind comes to them. And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you — that whoever drinks much wine and commits much fornication, and makes remembrance of the name seven hundred times every day, comes to loathe all of that. And it has, of number, 402 in utterance (lafẓan) and 202 in figure (raqman). As for the first number, it is an even-odd number, which al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit), al-ʿĀṣim (the Protector), and al-Munjī (the Deliverer) — with the article — and al-Mufīd (the Bestower of benefit) without it, measure by threes; and it is among the abundant numbers. Its aliquot parts are 414, which point to His name Mujrī l-fulk (the Setter of the ship in motion). As for the second number, it too is an even-odd number, which al-Ṣāḥib (the Companion) measures by twos; and it is a deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 104, which point to His name, exalted is He, Mudnī (the Bringer-Near), and to /fol. 158v./ His name Jāʿil (the One who makes and appoints). And as for its square, it is according to this form:
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 202, the number of the name in figure (raqman)]
Faṣl 80: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Tawwāb (the Ever-Relenting)

This name, mighty in worth, the lofty; magnificent in proof, the manifest: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, makes easy for him the return to his origin. And it is fitting for every wayfarer that he not be without the remembrance of it every day and night, even if only for some little while. And in it is a majestic secret for driving flies away from the body. And it has, of number, 415; and it is an odd, oblong, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 89, which point to our saying huwa ḥakīm (He is Wise), because of the wisdom there is in repentance, inasmuch as it is a turning back to the place of return. And likewise it also points to our saying huwa subbūḥ (He is All-Glorified), since the return to the origin is a return to the locus of transcendence (tanzīh), where the lights of the glories (subuḥāt) have shone forth. So the penitent swims in the sea of the light of the glories; by it and in it his purification comes about: Truly God loves those who turn [to Him] in repentance, and He loves those who purify themselves (Q 2:222). And the names of its letters, they are 530, which point to two majestic names, namely Rafīʿ (the Sublime) and Quddūs (the All-Holy). And it has a square of majestic worth, which the masters of the wisdom of illumination (al-ḥikma al-ishrāqiyya) know.
[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 415, the number of the name]
Faṣl 81: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Muntaqim (the Avenger)

This lofty, radiant name and impregnable, dazzling secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it and then invokes against a wrongdoer, that wrongdoer is seized on the spot. And it is among the names of subduing, which are the litanies of remembrance of ʿAzrāʾīl — peace be upon him. And it has, of number, 630; and it is an even-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 1252 [so the edition; read 1242 — the aliquot parts of 630 sum to 1242, which is also the value of huwa qawī ẓahīr], which point to your saying huwa qawī ẓahīr (He is Strong, a Supporter). And as for the names of its letters, they are 868, which point to two majestic names, namely Dhū l-Ṭawl (Possessor of Bounty) and Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator). And it has a square magnificent in worth and dazzling in proof, which the masters of awe and majesty know. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God — glorified and exalted is He — wills.

[Wafq: 5×5, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the five letters of Muntaqim — read from right to left,(mīm, 40), (nūn, 50),(tāʾ, 400),(qāf, 100),(mīm, 40) — and the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 630, the number of the name]
Faṣl 82: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-ʿAfuww (the Pardoner)

This shining name and gleaming secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, there are made beloved to him the noble traits of character and the refraining from taking [others] to task for sin. And whoever commits a sin and fears punishment for it from a king or from another, and then makes remembrance of this name to the number of its letters — God, exalted is He, secures him from what he fears, by the blessing of this name. And it is suitable as a litany of remembrance for one whose name is Yūsuf.

Know: as for His names al-Ghafūr (the Forgiving), al-Ghāfir (the Forgiver), and al-ʿAfuww — they are a closely allied arrangement, suitable for the repelling of what causes pain, especially of the pains of religion and of this world together. So glory be to Him who deposited His secrets within His names. The author of al-Muntakhab ("The Choice Selection") — may God, exalted is He, have mercy on him — said: he who makes remembrance of this name is smitten by no anxiety, no terror, and no dread, nor does he taste the calamities of time.

And it has, of number, 162 in utterance (lafẓan) and 156 in figure (raqman). As for the number in utterance, it is an even-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 201, which point to His name, exalted is He, ʿĀṣim (the Protector), and to Fāṣil (the Separator) — because of what ʿafw (pardon) contains of preservation (ʿiṣma) from the appearance of the trace of sin. So al-ʿĀṣim comes from what the ʿayn of ʿafw requires, and al-Fāṣil from what its fāʾ requires. And as for its number in figure, it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number; its aliquot parts are 236, which point to His words, exalted is He: "Be", and it is (Q 2:117). And as for the names of its letters, they are 225, which point to two majestic names, and they are Wāḥid (the One) and

Jabbār (the Compeller). And it has a square of majestic worth and benefit, based upon the secret, which the masters of the Yūsufī tastings and the masters of the operative deployments of beauty know. And this is its form:
[Wafq: 4×4, the sixteen cells exactly as they stand in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column and diagonal is 156, the number of the name in figure]
Faṣl 83: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle)

This subtle name and figure majestic in worth: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, his heart is made tender, his spirit is made subtle, and he is granted compassion for the creatures of God, exalted is He. And as for its bearer: when he meets a tyrant, that man's heart grows tender toward him. One of them said: and whoever perseveres in the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him — then whoever sees him, his good cheer goes out to him in yearning, and he inclines toward him with his heart.

And it has, of number, 281 by one aspect, 286 by another, 287, and also 292. And the truth is that a form such as this is not reckoned with a one, because of the concealment of the ruling of the alif that is within it, through its being turned toward the elevation of the wāw. So let us restrict ourselves, out of the four numbers, to two numbers. The first number is 286, a number in which the letters of the name are firmly established, and they were manifest in their numerical ranks just as they were in their /fol. 159v./ configurations in figure. And whatever of knowledge is of this standing has a rank above what is other than it. And this number is even-odd, deficient; its aliquot parts are 218, which point to two majestic names, and they are Ḥayy (the Living) and Muṣallī (the One who blesses) — because of what life contains of the spirit of perfection, and what blessing (ṣalāt) contains of the tenderness that necessitates gentleness (raʾfa). And as for the second number, it is 292; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. Its aliquot parts are 358, which point to two majestic names, and they are Mawjūd (the Existent) and Raḥmān (the All-Merciful). And as for the names of its letters, they are 297, which point to two majestic names, and they are Ṣādiq (the Truthful) and Mubīn (the Evident). And it has a square noble in proportion, which the people of the inward things know. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see:

[Wafq: 5×5, the twenty-five cells exactly as they stand in the source, each row read from right to left; the constant of every row, column and diagonal is 286, the first of the two numbers of the name that the text selects]
Faṣl 84: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, Mālik al-Mulk (Master of all Dominion)

This all-comprehending name and shining secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it while seeking a kingdom, God, exalted is He, grants him that. And it has a square of majestic worth, its letters being placed in this form —| |

[four-cell letter figure; the cells are the letters as they stand in the source, spelling Mālik al-Mulk; their abjad values total 212, the number of the name — ] — and it is set down in the exaltation of the Sun. And if the king multiplies the remembrance of this name, his kingdom endures. And it has, of number, 212; and it is an even-even-and-odd, deficient number. Its aliquot parts are 166, which point to His name — blessed and exalted is He — Qayyūm (the

Self-Subsisting). And it is a number which the name nūn measures by two, and the name jīm by four; so its half is Wafī (the Fulfiller), and its quarter is Mūjid (the Bringer into Existence). And it has a square of majestic worth, and this is its form:

Faṣl 85: On His name, exalted is He, Dhū l- Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour)

This majestic, magnificent, luminous name, and wise, lordly litany of remembrance, is among the majestic names. And it has come [in tradition] that it is the Greatest Name of God; and for that reason, whoever multiplies the remembrance of it does not ask God, exalted is He, for anything without His granting it to him. And in the hadith: ((Cleave persistently to "O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām")). And whoever writes it upon a chest in the first [hour] of the day of Thursday — it is preserved from thieves and robbers, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And whoever looks upon its drawn figure and its inscribed secret every day, by the number of its letters, while he recites the name — God makes easy for him the affairs of this world and the next, according to what some of the masters — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — have laid down. And this name has, of number, 1100; and it is an even-even-and-odd, abundant number. There corresponds to it, among the names, Mughnī (the Enricher). /fol. 160r./ Its aliquot parts are 1504, which exceed that which is rich by 404; and that is His names Rabb (the Lord) and Munʿim (the Bestower of favours). Faṣl 87: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Jāmiʿ (the Gatherer)

And know that the letter awfāq stand in the likeness of the body, and the numerical ones in the likeness of the spirit. So understand, and you will be rightly guided. And this is the form of the gathering together of its numerical threefold square (muthallath) and its letter-square (murabbaʿ ḥarfī). So ponder it, for it is among the noble secrets. Faṣl 88: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient)

This lofty name and splendid secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it until some of his worlds come into accord with him in the remembrance — God, exalted is He, enriches him by it so that he has no need of anything other than Him. For al-Ghanī is among the names of assimilation of character (takhalluq), while al-Mughnī is among the names of attachment (taʿalluq); and where al-Mughnī is among the names of assimilation of character, al-Ghanī is among the names of realization (taḥaqquq). Faṣl 89: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Mughnī (the Enricher)

This majestic, luminous name and beautiful, lordly secret: whoever multiplies the remembrance of it, God, exalted is He, enriches him so that he has no need of created beings; and whoever is assiduous in the remembrance of it until some of his worlds come into accord with him finds what he wishes to find. And it has a square of majestic worth, and it is set with Saturn in its exaltation. And whoever carries it with him, and makes remembrance of the name to the number of its letters, then recites Sūrat wa-l-Ḍuḥā (Q 93) after it, and says immediately following that: "O God, make [things] easy for me with the ease that You have made easy for many of Your servants, and enrich me by Your bounty, so that I have no need of any besides You" — and is assiduous in that for forty days: God sends to him one who will teach him that, whether in his sleep or in his waking. And likewise also, if he sets it with the Sun in its exaltation.

And I once mentioned that name to a friend and directed him to the remembrance of it, and he sat in spiritual retreat (khalwa) for forty nights, making remembrance of the name; and at their completion the roof was cleft open above him, and there came down upon him forty Iraqi qinṭārs of gold, and it was said to him: "If you wish, We will increase you; and if you deem it sufficient, We will suffice you." And the Proof of Islam, Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī — may God be pleased with him — mentioned in Iḥyāʾ ʿulūm al-dīn ("The Revival of the Religious Sciences") that whoever makes remembrance and says after the Friday prayer: "O God, O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Ḥamīd (the Praiseworthy), O al-Mubdiʾ (the Initiator), O al-Muʿīd (the Restorer), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Wadūd (the Loving): enrich me by what You have made lawful, so that I have no need of what You have forbidden; and by obedience to You, so that I have no need of disobedience to You; and by Your bounty, so that I have no need of any besides You" — whoever perseveres in this holy litany of remembrance, God, exalted is He, enriches him so that he has no need of His creation, and provides for him from whence he does not reckon. And whoever keeps up the remembrance of it, the means of this world become many for him, and its provisions become wide for him. And likewise, whoever writes it and hangs it upon himself, his trade turns a profit /fol. 161r./

Know, my brother — may God bring you to the most great enrichment and to the red sulphur (al-kibrīt al-aḥmar) — that by the secrets of the names and their lights God folds up the earth, and lays bare the waters, and inclines the winds, for whom He wills among the elect of His friends; and by them he pierces through the engendered beings; and by them God opens the river of wisdom from the heart. And God, exalted is He, has said: And to God belong the Most Beautiful Names, so call upon Him by them (Q 7:180). And He, exalted is He, has said: Call upon Me, and I will answer you (Q 40:60). And he — peace be upon him — said: ((Nothing turns back the decree save supplication, and nothing increases the life-span save righteousness)). And he said: ((Supplication is of benefit against what has come down and against what has not come down)). And he said: ((Supplication is the weapon of the believer)). And he said: ((Supplication is the marrow of worship)). And he said: ((Whoever has a door opened to him in supplication, the gates of the Garden are opened to him)). And he said: ((Whoever does not call upon God, He is angry with him)). And he said: ((Truly God loves those who are insistent in supplication)). And in another hadith: ((Truly God does not weary until you weary)).

And this name has, of number, 1100; and it corresponds to His name Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), because He, glorified and exalted is He, is beautiful in His attribute, and in His enriching most generous — so there is no need to repeat the discourse upon it. And as for the names of its letters, they are 1267, which point to two majestic names, namely Ḍārr (the Bringer of Harm) and Mukawwir (the One who wraps the night over the day). Faṣl 90: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Māniʿ (the Withholder)

So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant you success in the understanding of the meanings of the vessels and in the unveiling of the secrets of the letters — that harm is according to the measure of knowledge and encompassment. So whoever's knowledge is the greater and whose encompassment is the more complete, his harm is the more far-reaching. And when the Real — exalted and hallowed is He — willed to stand alone in this name, He made the harm of every harmer a benefit for the one harmed, by what He appointed upon it of reward and recompense and of welfare immediate and deferred. For if a person had an enemy in whose humoural temperament the blood had come to predominate, until it was near to destroying his spirit, such that, were he to remain in his condition, he would die that very night — and [the other] hastened to harm him and struck him a blow that diminished his blood — then his harming him would be the utmost benefit for that harmed man, because of his ignorance of the seat of the harm. So none brings harm in reality save God, exalted is He. I say: many a harm is repelled by a harm more complete than it, so that the repelling harm becomes a benefit for the one from whom it is repelled. So understand that.

And Abū ʿAbd Allāh Zayn al-Dīn al-Khāfī [base text: al-Kāfī] — may God, exalted is He, sanctify his inmost secret, and adorn his name with subtleties …, and beautify his inward with the lights of the secrets — said: Whoever sets this luminous name and marvellous, ṣamadānī secret upon a plate of lead in the first hour of the day of Saturday, with the moon in its combustion, and remembers this name according to the number of its letters, seven times, while he gazes upon the drawn figure with a gaze of majesty, and then asks for the harming of a person — he is answered on the spot. And in it is a marvellous secret for the masters of [spiritual] states. And had I known that this would not be disclosed to anyone, I would have disclosed of it the strange secrets and the wondrous effects. And whoever has had a provision from it decreed for him, I have disclosed of it what is after the manner of the attracting magnet, from breast to breast. And God casts the Spirit, from His command, upon whom He wills among His servants (Q 40:15). So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. /fol. 162r./
Faṣl 92: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Nāfiʿ (the Bringer of Benefit)

This majestic, all-comprehending name and mighty, beneficial secret: in it is a healing for every sick man and a restoration to health for every one afflicted. Whoever multiplies the remembrance of it in a state of harm, God, exalted is He, restores him to health from it. And if he be one possessed of a truthful [spiritual] state, and he persists in its remembrance until some of its worlds come into accord with him, he does not pass his hand over one who has been harmed but that God, exalted is He, wipes away his harm. And it is proper that there be written upon the surface of the square, on its four sides, We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82). And it is a noble name, suitable for the people of unveilings. And it has a square of majestic worth, known to the people of pure hearts. And this is its form.

And whoever adds to it His name al-Badīʿ (the Wondrous Originator), and recites that until a state from it comes to prevail over him, on an empty stomach and with purity of the inward — he will have no need of the light of a lamp. And it is set apart for the people of inner sight (baṣāʾir) among the people of God, exalted is He. And God knows best.
Faṣl 94: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Hādī (the Guide)

This manifest, lofty name and dazzling, sublime secret is suitable for every wayfarer in his wayfaring (sulūk), so long as he remains sincere toward the light. And whoever hangs it upon the neck of an infant boy who is not guided to the suckling — he is guided. And it is among the majestic names for one who wanders lost from the path. And whoever enters into a darkness and says Yā Hādī (O Guide), guide me — he is rightly guided to the object sought. And in it are strange secrets for the people of the [spiritual] states. And it is proper to the masters of the states that are truthful with God, exalted is He. And in it is a beautiful matter and a majestic secret for kings and the great ones. And no king multiplies the remembrance of it until a [spiritual] state from it comes to prevail over him but that the lands obey him and affairs on the part of the servants are led in submission to him. And in it is a wondrous meaning for whoever among the wayfarers desires to ascend with his spirit to the world of subsistence (baqāʾ). So understand this luminous secret and lordly name. And God bestows His kingship upon whom He wills, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing (Q 2:247). And this name has, of number,

Faṣl 96: On His name, glorified and exalted is He, al-Bāqī (the Abiding)

The Explanation and Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ) of the Junnetu'l-asmāʾ
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 324
Hujjetu'l-Islām Imam Ghazālī (may God be pleased with him) relates the following.

I was residing at the Nizamiye Madrasa in Baghdad, the city where the ascetics (ābidīn) and the Kutb and Ewtād — [saints of the highest spiritual ranks] — lie buried. I taught knowledge to students (tālib) as best I could, and at times gave sermons. One day, while I was sitting alone, there was a knock at the door; I opened it. A man entered, gave the greeting of peace, and said: "I come from the Commander of the Faithful, His Excellency the Caliph. The Caliph wishes to see you at once." I said, "Could we not go an hour from now?" He replied: "By no means! His Excellency the Caliph requests that you come immediately." "Very well, let us go. Bismillah!" — saying this, I rose from my place and mounted a donkey.

When we arrived at the palace, I saw that they were waiting for me. They took me to a private room; the Caliph entered and greeted me with honor. In response I stood up. The Caliph said to me: "O Imam, my purpose in summoning you so urgently is this: in the palace treasury I found several documents written on leather, left behind by my ancestor Hārūn er-Reshīd. These were written by the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (may God ennoble his countenance); they are extremely difficult to read, and no one has been able to read them or discover what is written in them. While I was still a child, the Caliph before me would, at the start of every year, place it upon his head with reverence and honor, open it, hold it in the smoke of fragrant incense (bakhūr) while praying, and pass it over his face and eyes. Then he would return it to its chest. He would take it with him into battles, and always won. I follow the same custom, but I am curious as to what is written in the documents. O Imam! In this age there is no scholar of religion greater than you. Be gracious and generous, and resolve this difficulty of mine." I said: "O Sultan! May God the Exalted gladden you in this world with every kind of favor and grace, and may your rank be exalted in the hereafter as well, for you honor the scholars. God willing, the Merciful, I shall fulfill this wish of yours." The Caliph gave an order to a young man; they opened the treasury and brought a chest adorned with every kind of jewel. The chest was opened, and inside it another chest, made of steel, was found. Its key hung on a chain attached to it. That steel chest, too, was opened, and inside were several documents wrapped in silk. The Caliph took the documents, passed them over his face and eyes, and then [I 325] handed them to me. I took the documents with reverence and respect, and opened them. I saw that, just as had been said, they were written in the blessed hand of Hazreti Ali (may God ennoble his countenance), in Kufic script. I examined them a little and began to read. It opened with the noble Basmala, praise and thanks to God Almighty, and then it spoke these couplets:
(Whoever rejects our words, we too shall reject him wholeheartedly.)

After this couplet, two odes (qaṣīda) were written. In them were counsels concerning this world and the next, and certain divine names (asmāʾ). Through symbols (rumuz) he sought to convey the Greatest Name (Ism al-Aʿẓam) to those worthy of it, while concealing it from those who were not. Alongside these, also in Kufic script, he explained his purpose in writing these two odes and the manner in which he had composed them.

In them he says: a great plague broke out in Kufa and Basra. Many people died. Indeed, in some places the losses were so great that the dead could not be buried, and birds of prey began to devour the corpses. (I had read in the history books that a plague occurred in Kufa and Basra during the caliphate of Omer el-Fārūk, may God be pleased with him. Was this that same outbreak, or did it happen later? In any case—)

At a time when this disease had spread everywhere, Abdullah ibn Ebu'l-Munzir (may God be pleased with him), one of the notables of Kufa, rose and came to me. He spoke to me of the suffering and afflictions the Muslims were enduring, and asked how they might be delivered from it. I said: "O Ebu'l-Munzir! There are many prayers which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited when such conditions occurred. Why do you not recite them and ask the Almighty to remove this disease?" Ebu'l-Munzir said: "By God, O Imam! After the five daily prayers we recite, as best we can, whatever prayers we know, and we implore. But we obtain no result." Hazreti Ali (may God ennoble his countenance) said:
("Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we shall return.")

[I 326] "Is it, perhaps, that your prayer is not accepted, or that your intention is not sincere? Or is there mockery (istihza) in your prayers?" "God forbid, my lord, we do not mock in prayer. But, as you say, our intention is not sincere. Be gracious, and teach us that Greatest Name which you learned from our exalted Prophet, so that we may write it and carry it upon our heads." "O Ebu'l-Munzir! To say plainly what you ask would be to disclose (ifshā) the Greatest Name. But I will tell you a few things. This will be a means of delivering you from affliction and plague. If someone, out of ignorance, does not accept our words, then let this verse of God, glorious and exalted, [be recited against him]:
(Indeed, they devised their plots and schemes, and their schemes are known to God; even if their scheming were enough to move mountains, they shall be requited for it.)
Because of this, let ruin come upon that disbelieving denier. [Recite also] the 122nd noble verse of Sūrat el-En'ām:
He said that this noble verse

consists of 19 letters, that these letters are written on the foreheads of the guardians of Hell (zebānī), and that it is because of these letters that they are able to withstand the fire of Hell; and he named six (6) divine names whose letters likewise total nineteen (19). He explained that these names are sharper than a sword and repel the fire of the plague.

Hazreti Ali, may God ennoble his countenance, also gave Ebu'l-Munzir this counsel: "This method I have shown is a remedy for every spiritual illness and affliction. When you write this Junnetu'l-Asmāʾ (Shield of the Names), write it in a solitary place, and show what you have written to no one! Let your heart also hold good intention. You must be clean and in a state of ritual purity (abdest), and anoint yourself with pleasant fragrances. When you write it for someone and give it to him, tell him not to open and look at it, for it will have a greater effect that way. You must teach this only to people who are clean of face, virtuous, and righteous — [I 327] I grant permission (icazet), by the grace and leave of God, glorious and exalted, to whoever knows and carries these documents," he says.

Imam Ghazālī, may God be pleased with him, relates: after I read these writings and explained them to the Caliph, he was very pleased, and asked me to write down exactly what I had told him and give it to him. I agreed. The Caliph gave me a period of three days. I took the documents and went to my house. I studied them with a tranquil heart, wrote one copy for the Caliph and one for myself, and reported to His Excellency the Caliph. He gave me leave, and bestowed upon me every kind of favor and generosity.

Through these names I attained many divine favors. Even my bearing and appearance improved. One day someone said to me: "O Imam! We always used to see you as weak and sickly, but these days we see a different state in you. Your face is full of light and your body is healthy. What, I wonder, is the cause of this sudden change? Be so gracious as to tell us, so that we too may improve thanks to you." I answered that person's question appropriately, and cautioned him to conceal this secret from those unworthy of it. I myself occupied myself with these names on certain occasions.

I had gone somewhere as a guest. On my way back, we were attacked by bandits on the road. There were about a hundred (100) horsemen. They had charged at full gallop into our caravan. The people of the caravan with me were frightened; they had given up all hope for their goods and their lives, and stood trembling with their arms bound. I, this poor servant, uttered the Takbīr ten (10) times in the manner Hazreti Ali, may God ennoble his countenance, had taught, and recited the Asmāʾ al-Aʿẓam (the Greatest Names) toward them nineteen times. Suddenly the horses were startled and stopped where they stood; they could not take even a single step. One of the bandits called out to us: "O people of the caravan! For the sake of the Sacred Kaaba, tell us — is there someone among you who practices sorcery? Or is there someone present who knows the Greatest Name? For you have rendered us powerless in an instant — our horses cannot move. It has made us unable to plunder you." One of us called back: "There is no sorcerer among us, but there is someone present who knows the Greatest Name!.." "Yes, what you say is true. This cannot be sorcery, but it could be through the Greatest Name, for sorcery could not instill such fear as this. Go now, be on your way!"
We gave thanks to God Almighty, the All-Glorious, and continued on our way.

O you who wander about filled with divine love! These writings of mine have come into your hands. Guard them as dear as your own life, for this is a gift from the Almighty to His servants. If you recognize their worth, act in accordance with their due, conceal them from the eyes of people, and place your trust in my words, you will be able to exercise many powers within this created world (ālem-i kevn u fesād), and among the people of the world [I 328] ...you will become the beloved of hearts. Strive to do this without error! I will now explain to you, one by one, the Quranic verses (Āyāt al-Karima) connected with this purpose — those with nineteen letters. Have no doubt that the Greatest Name (ism Aʿẓam) is contained within them. Believe this. Whoever carries this circle upon himself must be in a state of complete ritual purity.

I have not related this copy in any of the books I have written, for I sought to heed the admonition of Hazreti Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him). I did not wish its fame to spread abroad. When it comes into your hands, do not broadcast it carelessly either! Whenever you give this circle to someone, do not let him open it and look at its design — hand it over sealed. If the person you give it to is able, let him offer a sacrifice and distribute its meat to the poor.

I had this circle engraved upon a silver plate, and had the Āyāt al-Kursī (the Throne Verse) engraved above the circle, and I carried it upon my person. I persisted in reciting the Asmāʾ (the Divine Names) and the verse after each of the five daily prayers, and by the permission of Allah Most High, I found healing.

O seeker! Into whosever hands these pages come, let him make a vow to the spirit of Hazreti Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him), in reverence for his power, and fulfill it once his wish is granted — and let him remember this humble servant with a good prayer.

The reason the sacrifice is required is out of reverence for the Divine Names (Asmāʾ al-ilāhiye), and in emulation of the Prophet Hazreti Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The meat of the sacrifice must likewise be distributed to the poor who are in need.

This work of Imam Ghazali (may God be pleased with him) was obtained in the city of Damascus by the dervish Mustafa es-Surizi from a perfect saint; that saint had seen it in the treasury of a sultan named Shahruz Mirza, and copied it in the year 847 of the Hijra.

According to the description given by the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali (may God be pleased with him and honor him), after every obligatory (farz) prayer one first recites the Takbīr ("Allahu ekber" — God is greater) ten (10) times, and then this:
(The One, the Living, the Judge, the Just, the Holy.)
After the Names (Asmāʾ), one adds the Quranic verse suited to one's purpose, and it must be recited nineteen (19) times.
For example: if you wish to ease a difficult and burdensome matter, after every obligatory prayer first say the Takbīr (Allahu ekber) ten (10) times, then recite this verse:

Add it to the Names and recite it 19 times. The practice must be carried out neither less nor more than prescribed. These Names and this verse are to be recited after every obligatory prayer, nineteen (19) times each, for a period of 19 days.

It must be recited according to the order set forth by Imam Ghazali (may God be pleased with him). For nineteen (19) days, after each of the five daily obligatory prayers, first say the Takbīr (Allahu ekber) ten (10) times, then nineteen (19) times:

The rule for making the fourfold wafq: you take the jumal al-kabir value of the Aya to be placed in the wafq and subtract 30 from the total. The remainder is divided by 4. The whole quotient is written into the first cell, and, adding one at each step, you proceed to the last cell to complete the wafq. If the division leaves a remainder of 3, add one extra to the 5th cell; if the remainder is 2, add one extra to the 9th cell; if the remainder is 1, add one extra to the 13th cell — completing the wafq in this manner.
The fourfold wafq belongs to the planet Jupiter, and its day is Thursday. Its celestial angel is Sarfeyail and its earthly angel is Shemhuresh.

[I 361] The Secret of the Seven Letters These seven letters, which do not occur in the Surat al-Fātiḥa, are of exalted worth and lofty standing. Some of these seven letters point to good, and some to evil.

The letter Fe (8): this letter is dry and hot, its nature being fire. Its lunar mansion (manzil) is Eklil. The spirit (rūḥāniyya) of this letter is generally employed in works of good, though its exact nature is not clearly determined. If you use this letter for righteous works in this world, you will attain success, by the leave of Allah, Glorious and Exalted is He.

The letter Jīm ((): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Sureyya. The spirit of the letter Jīm is used for gaining a place among prominent men — for entry among the great, the men of worldly standing, and the men of the pen.
The letter Shīn (<): this letter is dry and hot, its nature being fire. Its lunar mansion is Belde. The spirit of the letter Shīn is of a confused nature and serves none of the affairs of this world.

The letter Se (:): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Sa'dil beli'. The nature of the spirit of the letter Se is temperate (moderate), and it is fitting for every good work.

The letter Ẓāʾ (>): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Feraul muahhir. The nature of this letter's spirit is composite, and it hinders undertakings and endeavours.

The letter Khāʾ (9): this letter is moist and cold, its nature being water. Its lunar mansion is Sa'dil suud. The nature of this letter's spirit is temperate (moderate). It is auspicious and lends aid in every good work.

The letter Ze (+): this letter is moist and hot, its nature being air. Its lunar mansion is Zera'. The spirit of the letter Ze is used for driving away sickness, for the opening of the melekūt (the realm of spirits), and in every work, whether good or evil.

[I 368] The Forty Names It is related from the peerless scholar of his age, the unrivalled savant of his time, he who brought others to perfection, the pole (kutub) of the people of truth, Shihabuddin Suhrewerdi, may his secret be sanctified, that Allah, Exalted is He, gave him forty of His Beautiful Names. There is no son of man who does not stand in need of these Names, which possess many properties. Some of these properties are as follows:

Angels, jinn, men, the heavens, the earths, and everything in the realm of existence are made subservient to these Names. Throughout his entire life the Sheyh never let these Names leave his side. He performed all his wondrous works through the blessing of these Names.

He also enjoined the following: whoever wishes to occupy himself with the prayer of these Names must have a pure heart. He must persevere in reciting it with heart and soul, that he may witness many strange and wondrous things among the works of Allah, and that the secrets of the unseen world (gayb) may be opened to him.
These Names contain such astonishing secrets that, were the seas to become ink, the trees pens, and every created thing a scribe, they could not write out the full commentary on these Names.
When Allah, Exalted is He, wills good for one of His servants, He grants him success in attaining these Names and in reciting them. In the end, astonishing properties are seen in that person.

Shihabuddin Suhrewerdi, may his secret be sanctified, enjoined the following: it is forbidden for those brethren who know these Names to give or entrust them to persons they do not trust or who are unworthy. It is not permitted to put them to trial in unlawful matters. Whoever tests them in what is unlawful, Allah will afflict him with such trouble that he can never be rid of it; on the Day of Judgment, Allah, the Truth, will be his adversary.

Whoever recites these Names must possess piety (takva) and sound belief. He must have no evil habits. He must not be dissolute or a liar. His conduct must be upright and his word true. He should believe in these Names and put them to trial when he has need, and then, God willing, his needs will be met.

After reciting each Name, he fasts for seven days. In the middle of the seven days he recites these Names. Then he will witness astonishing things, as we shall briefly relate under the properties of each Name. It is Allah, Exalted is He, who grants success in what one loves and is content with.
