And this is the Seal of Obedience, and in it are the swift Name and the lofty ascendant. It is written in one thousand one hundred and eighty names, and that is what you write the ascendant in. And this number is gathered in three letters, and in it there is preposing and postposing — so understand; for walls have ears, and that a mindful ear might keep it in mind (Q 69:12). And this is the form of the seal.

You write these names in the pillow of two spouses who hate one another — and they are the names of the mother of Moses, peace be upon him — on a Friday, when the imam sits upon the pulpit and the first call to prayer is begun, with saffron, with good rose-water, with good cloves, and with yellow male frankincense.

— [male frankincense] that is good, powdered, and with cloves rubbed fine, in sweet-scented Naṣībī rose-water. Then fold up the writing and anoint it with fine, choice ghāliya-perfume; and you put the writing inside the pillow upon which the two of them sleep, for they will love one another, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is what you write: Ṭasūm Ṭasūm ʿAyshūm ʿAyshūm ʿAlūm ʿAlūm Kalūm Kalūm Ṣayūm Ṣayūm Qayyūm Qayyūm Dayūm Dayūm. Glory be to Him by whose remembrance hearts are set at rest! Be at rest, O heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], for the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. O God, set right [what is] between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], as You set right [what was] between Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and his helpers (anṣār). O God, O You who caused the love of Joseph to enter into the heart of Zulaykhā; O You who caused the love of Moses to enter into the heart of Āsiya bint Muzāḥim; and O You who caused the love of Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — to enter into the heart of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid and of ʿĀʾisha bint Abī Bakr: cause the love of such-and-such to enter into the heart of such-and-such, as You caused the night to enter into the day and the day into the night, and the male into the female. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And if you wish, you write it after the rising of the sun on a Friday.

And among them also: Dhū l-Nūn ibn Ibrāhīm al-Miṣrī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — was asked /fol. 176r./ about the names of the mother of Moses, peace be upon him. And he said: The transmissions we have are many, but that whose trial has been verified with us is this: that when you wish to employ them, you fast seven days and speak to no one; and you give alms each day to three poor men; and each day you suffumigate your place of prayer, morning and evening, with male frankincense and aloeswood; and you recite the names by number, after each prayer, seven times. And when that has been completed for you, you recite it within yourself; and you shall not invoke over a lock, nor over a chain, nor over a bolt, but that it opens for you swifter than the blink of an eye, by the leave of God, exalted and hallowed is He. And it is this. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Lord of Hulbā bint Raghbā, the believing woman, the truthful, the mother of Moses — peace be upon him — by God, the Mighty, the Wise, Haliyā, the Supremely Great, the Great, the Overseer, the Magnificent, by whom the layers [of heaven] are opened, and by whom the horizons were made to shine, and by whom the hardest things were opened: open this lock, or this fetter! And if you wish, you say: So-and-so son of So-and-so, with the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so, by God, the Mighty, the Supremely Great, the Great, the Overseer, the Magnificent. And it is said in another transmission that the names of the mother of Moses — peace be upon him — which loose locks and fetters and other things than that, are these: Ṭasūm Ṭasūm Ayūm Ayūm Ḥayūm Ḥayūm Qayyūm Qayyūm Dayūm Dayūm. O God, O You who opened the sky with abundant rain: open such-and-such — and you make mention of whatever you intend of locks and fetters, or of hearts — truly You are powerful over everything.

O God, Ashbīh Ashbīh wa-Shabīh wa-Zaydūḥwa-Badīḥwa-Ṭāḥūl wa-Muḥīl lah wa-Takāmad wa-Salām wa-Māyūḥā wa-Muḥallalūt wa-Umm Aḥrāh Junūduhā Ḥābūrah Būrah Badīḥā wa-Ḥānīt Ḥanūnah Mardūdah Qāl Maj Maʿaj Ṭafaf Lafaf Kafaf Sahaf Faʿīl Yālīṭā wa-Ṭāyā Dabā Lakarīrah — [I adjure you] that you assuredly take charge, and answer, and obey God and His Messenger and His power and His authority. Open this lock! And if it be of iron, make it fly away; and if it be of brass or of copper or of wood, then break it, by the right of these names that are upon you. And if you wish: open the heart of such-and-such with love and affection toward such-and-such. Completed with the help of God, exalted is He.
Faṣl: In which I mention the seal of Solomon — peace be upon him

Know that whoever seals with it, God, exalted is He, preserves him — inasmuch as he preserves himself from disobedience, and is pure, clean of garment, silent of tongue, God-fearing before God, mighty and majestic is He — with swiftness of response. And it is the Seal of Obedience: none touches it save one who is mighty. Wahb b. Munabbih — may God be pleased with him — said: The seal of Solomon — peace be upon him — was upon four corners; above each corner there was written: on the right side, "I am God, I have never ceased to be"; and on the left side, "I am God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting"; and on the third side, "I am God, the Mighty; there is no mighty one but Me, and mighty is he whom I have clothed with My seal"; and on the fourth there was written /fol. 176v./ the Throne Verse, encircled by "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace."

And it is said that these names, which were upon the seal of Solomon — peace be upon him — are these: There is no god but God, alone, having no partner. I am God: I am alone in the kingship and the authority. Īl Īl Īl. I am God: I have made Myself mighty with might and with power. Yāh Yāh Yāh. I am God, Living, Self-Subsisting; I do not sleep. Ayh Ayh Ayh. I am God, All-Aware, Powerful; everything has obeyed Me. Anūkh Anūkh Anūkh. I am God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Dāʿūj Fayʿūj Māʿūj. There is no god but God: [it is] My fortress — whoever enters it is secure from My torment. I have fortified myself with the names of this seal, and with the Possessor of might and of omnipotence; and I have taken refuge from my enemies with the Possessor of power and of strength and of the Dominion; and I have committed my affair to the Living who does not die; and I have thrust back whoever intended harm against me — with no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. God is our sufficiency, and excellent is the Guardian (Q 3:173). Say: O God, Master of all Dominion — to His words — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27).

And it is mentioned that these names were upon the collar of the robe (julla) of Solomon — peace be upon him — and that they are of mighty blessing, proper to kingship and authority. And they are: Īl Īl Īl. I am God: I am alone in the might and the strength and the power. Yāh Yāh Yāh. I am God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, a Self-Subsisting one who does not sleep. Ah Ah Ah. I am God, the One, the All-Subduing, Living, Powerful; nothing of mine is lost. Anūkh Anūkh Anūkh. I am God, the Mighty; there is no mighty one but Me; I have made Myself mighty above the like and the equal. Dāʿūj Fayʿūj Dāʿūj. There is no god but God: a fortress — whoever enters it is secure from My torment. I have fortified myself with the Possessor of might and of the Dominion, and I have taken refuge with the Possessor of strength and of omnipotence, and I have relied upon the Living who does not die; and I have thrust back whoever cast at me and intended for me evil, or guile, or deception, or a false invocation — with no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And I have taken refuge with God, and I have relied upon God, and upon His names, the treasured, the concealed, the generous, the majestic. Ah Ah Ah Lūʿālīh Dāyūm Ṭasūm Qayyūm

Dayūm; and by the right of Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, and by the right of Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, and by the right of the Ḥawāmīm and the generous verses that are in them: I have veiled myself with them, and with the might of God by which He created Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace.

And it is related concerning these names — and they are among the names of the shining light whose light overcame every light — that Solomon son of David, upon him be blessing and peace, when he sat in his session, the jinn would tremble before him in awe and in fear of these names. And they are: There is no god but God; the command is wholly God's; and there is no victor that overcomes God. Light, light, light! Glory be to Him whose light has overcome every light! And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād. Jahlās Wāḥiṣlī Waraḥsamā Kasṭasṭī /fol. 177r./ MaṭaṭhaṭaṭHaṭāhaṭHayf. Answer! There is no god but God. It has shone and blazed forth. Ṭūb Ṭūb, All-Glorified, All-Glorified, Hayṭūb Hayṭūb, All-Holy, All-Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit! Upon the Throne He is established, and over the kingship He has taken hold, and to Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. There is none to repel what He has decreed, and none to withhold what He has given. He does in His kingdom what He wills, and He judges among His creatures as He wishes; and He is powerful over everything. You write [them] upon gazelle parchment, or upon the parchment of a lamb (ʿabūr), with musk and saffron; and you suffumigate them with the sweetest incense.

And this chapter is operatively deployed in seventy-one matters: for going in before sultans; for standing before rulers, and prisoners, and the bewitched; and for empty roads; and for hard labour in childbirth, and fever, and the divorced woman, and a blow (laṭma); and for love between a man and his wife, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers; and for selling and buying. And its operative deployment is manifold. So know its worth, and guard it with all your effort, and beware of disobedience — for in it is the name of God, the Magnificent, the Greatest. And they are the names whose mention has gone before, and the seals that were upon the collar of Solomon — peace be upon him.

And it is related from al-Ḥajarī, from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār — may God be pleased with him — that he said: Upon the carpet of Solomon — peace be upon him — were names that struck the jinn senseless, and by which they were torn apart, and by which he was obeyed by them, and by which he tormented them. And in the middle of the carpet were four Hebrew names, locked; on account of which the jinn and the satans were obedient, not disobeying him for the blink of an eye. And they were the helpers of the carpet, charged with the raising of it: four ʿifrīts, who were among the greatest of the viziers of Solomon — peace be upon him — from among the jinn. And the viziers of Solomon from among mankind were three hundred, the greatest of them being Āṣaf b. Barakhyā, and three hundred from among the jinn, the greatest of them these four: Ẓamriyāṭ, Ṣanʿīq, Hadliyāj, and Shūghāl. And these names have a mighty obedience over the jinn and the satans. So know their worth and their excellence, and do not squander them, and do not disclose them to anyone of God's creatures, exalted is He. And beware of commanding the helpers to be made subservient; rather say to them: O company of the four helpers and the honoured viziers, [I adjure you] that you assuredly command one who will fulfil my need and act freely in what pleases me, by the right of the prophet of God, Solomon, and by the right of Him who said: An ʿifrīt of the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place; and truly I am strong and trustworthy for it (Q 27:39); It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves above me, but come to me in submission (Q 27:30–31) — hastening, with tranquillity and with gravity.

And you write each name upon its day, while you are pure of body, of garment and of place, and in the hour of its brilliant star (durrī); and you suffumigate them with the sweetest and finest incense; and you take its star-reading by night beneath the stars, with Sūrat Yā-Sīn and Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion (Q 67:1). And to these /fol. 177v./ four names belong four days. The first, and it is for the day of Sunday, and its first hour, at the rising of the sun; and its helper is Ḍamriyāṭthe ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is al-Mudhhab al-Kibrīt; and this is its name: Hashṭashlahakūsh — nine letters. And the second is for the day of Tuesday, and its first hour; and its helper is Shūghāl the ʿifrīt, and the lord of…

— the hour is al-Aḥmar Abū l-Tawābiʿ, and this is its name: Kashkashlīʿūsh — nine letters. The third is for the day of Wednesday, and its first hour; and its servant is Dībāj the ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is Barqān, and its brilliant star (durrī) is ʿUṭārid (Mercury); and this is its name: Baḥshahshalṭūsh — nine letters. And the fourth is for the day of Saturday, and its first hour; and its helper is Ṣanʿīq the ʿifrīt, and the lord of the hour is Maymūn Abū Nūkh; and this is its name: Shaṭlaṭaṭlakūsh — nine letters. And these nine letters belong to each name only because the nine is the utmost of number and the strongest of it, and to it the numbers come to their end. So understand that. And this is the form of the seal.

And it is related that this is its conjuration (ʿazīma) and the utterance upon which it stands; and it is: O God, O al-Qawī (the Strong) — there is no strong one but You. O God, O God, O God. O Creator of the night and the day, O Sender of the clouds and the winds, O Lord of lords, O Emancipator of necks, Powerful over whatsoever He wills and desires, from whom nothing among things is hidden, who fears no punishment and hopes for no reward, the Subduer by His power, the Compassionate by His mercy: I have asked you by the signs of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate, the Lord of the trustworthy Spirit, Gabriel; and of the mighty, sublime angel, Mīkāʾīl; and of the angel charged with the blast [of the Trumpet], Isrāfīl; and of the dread angel from whom hearts tremble, ʿAzrāʾīl; and of the bearers of the Throne, all of them — that you assuredly command one who will fulfil my need and act freely in what pleases me, by the right of the prophet of God, Solomon — peace be upon him — by the right of Him who said: Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? An ʿifrīt of the jinn said — to His saying — trustworthy (Q 27:38–39); It is from Solomon — to His saying — in submission (Q 27:30–31). O God, I ask You by these spiritual spirits, honoured in Your sight, that You make subservient to me the four ʿifrīts, by Your power /fol. 178r./ and Your majesty: Bahshahash Mahshahash Faṭūsh Layhūsh Kashkash Layūsh ShakhshalūṭShaḥshaṭKhajaj Khajaj. Answer, and take charge, and do what you are commanded.

And it is said that the seal of Solomon — peace be upon him — which was upon his hand, and in which lay his kingship, and in which was the Greatest Name of God, exalted is He, that was written upon the heart of Adam — peace be upon him — was in this form:

I say: and among the occult properties of the majestic benefits is His word, exalted is He: And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41). This verse is for whoever has a ship, and it is at sea, and he desires its safety from the deeps of the sea: let him engrave that upon a plank of teak wood and nail it at the prow of the ship — and in [another] copy: at the stern of the ship — for that will be for it a protective charm and a safeguard, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((A security for my community against drowning, when they ride in the ship, is that [they say]: In the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41); And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse.)) Thus it stands in some of the copies: "when they ride"; and it does not say "" ,"…in the ship, that they say: And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate". You say: /fol. 178v./ And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse. And he stands in the rear parts and faces the prow and gestures to the right and to the left; then he says: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar — and he gestures toward the stern; then he says: ʿUthmān > and ʿAlī < — and he gestures toward the prow; then he says: ʿAlī; then he says: In the name of God. In the name of God we have named; by Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād we have been sufficed, and by Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf we have been protected. And God is encompassing them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22). Ibn ʿAbbās said to his companions: Whoever says, when he mounts his riding-beast or his conveyance: In the name of God, the King. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due, and the whole earth shall be His handful on the Day of Resurrection — to His saying — above what they associate (Q 39:67); And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41) — then he turned to his companions and said: If it comes to harm or sinks, then his intention is upon me. Ibn Shabak said: I came to the shore of Baḥr Barsh, and I found upon the shore twenty-two ships laden with grain. So I went aboard one of them, and said the words and recited the verses, and the ships ran on with a fair wind until a third of the night; then the wind blew violently and the waves rose high, and none reached a shore — for there was none other than the ship I was in — and of the rest of them no trace was seen.

And from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, that he said: A security against drowning and shipwreck for whoever rides the sea is that he say: In the name of God, the King, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due (Q 39:67), the verse. And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41). And when you and those with you are settled upon the ship, say: Praise be to God, who has delivered us from the wrongdoing people (Q 23:28). Truly God upholds the heavens and the earth, that they should not pass away (Q 35:41) — the verse, to its end. And God is encompassing them from behind (Q 85:20), the verse. And in a report from Ibn ʿAbbās — may God be pleased with them both — that he said: Whoever says, when he rides the sea: In the name of God, the King. Kingship belongs to God. O You for whom the seven heavens are in fear, and the seven earths in trembling, and the lofty mountains in humility, and the surging seas in submission: guard me — You are the best guardian, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. And they have not esteemed God with the esteem that is His due — to His saying, glorified and exalted is He — above what they associate (Q 39:67). And may God bless our master Muḥammad, and his family and his companions, and grant them peace, and all the prophets and the messengers and the

angels brought near. And he said: Embark in it; in the name of God is its sailing /fol. 179r./ and its anchoring. Truly my Lord is Forgiving, Compassionate (Q 11:41) — then Ibn ʿAbbās turned to his companions and said: If it sinks, his debt is upon me.
Chapter 18 (al-bāb al-thāmin ʿashar): On the occult properties of the Throne Verse (Q 2:255) and the God-given (ladunnī) blessings that belong to it [284]

Know — may God grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of His secrets — that the names have significative meanings, and that among the greatest and most majestic of the names is that which some of the eminent righteous ones, from among the masters of [spiritual] states, of inner discernment (iṭṭilāʿ), and of the names, have pointed out: that the greatest verse in the Book of God is the magnified, honoured Throne Verse, on account of His words, exalted is He, His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255); and that in His words, exalted is He, Alif-Lām-Mīm (Q 2:1) there is a majestic meaning, for the alif is from Allāh, and the lām from To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255), and the mīm from Master of all Dominion (Q 3:26). And know that when this noble verse was sent down upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — forty thousand angels descended with it, in reverence and in magnification of its worth. So know the worth of what has come to you, for it is the delivering verse and the preventing verse, the repelling verse and the protecting verse; and it is the mistress of the Qurʾān, and it is a third of the Qurʾān. That has come down in sound hadiths. And it has come down that whoever recites it at the beginning of the night, no devil comes near him; and likewise whoever recites it at the beginning of the day, and there comes to him the Obeyed Master (al-sayyid al-muṭāʿ) for the understanding of the unveiling of the Throne Verse. And the Throne Verse is reckoned at one hundred and seventy letters, fifty words, and seven sections. And whoever recites it according to the number of its letters — one hundred and seventy times — and desires intercession with one possessed of authority, whoever he may be, his intercession is accepted. And whoever recites it while he is in hardship — the aforementioned number, one hundred and seventy times — in the depth of the night, in a state of ablution and facing the qibla, God, exalted is He, grants him relief soon. And whoever recites it the number of its words over some small quantity [of a thing], blessing is put into it, and it is guarded from the promptings of Satan. And whoever recites it the number of its sections on a Friday, after the afternoon prayer, in a place free of voices, in a state of ablution and facing the qibla, will find within [himself], and his heart will be in a state such as he has never known before, and in humility; so let him supplicate God, exalted is He, and he will be answered with the good of this world and of the hereafter. And whoever recites it in the middle of the night two hundred and twenty-five times is made secure from his enemy, and God, exalted is He, destroys him and takes him away from him. And whoever recites it three hundred and thirteen times to seek provision and to draw it in, it comes to him, and love for him goes forth to the whole of creation. And whoever is troubled by some matter and recites it three hundred and thirteen times, God suffices him against what troubles him in the affair of his religion and of his world, and opens for him the door of good things for as long as he keeps reciting it.

Let him recite this noble verse and write it in separated letters in a glass bowl with saffron, rose-water, and musk, and let it be drunk according to the number of its letters, over [that many] days; and let him be fasting, /fol. 179v./ and let him break his fast with nothing but it: God, exalted is He, will make him speak with the varieties of wisdom. And let the beginning of the operation be in the month of Nīsān; and if he adds to it some of its water, that is better. And when he wishes to break the fast upon the verse as we have mentioned, let him recite the Throne Verse seven times and say: "O God, I ask You by the right of this noble verse that You inspire me with Your God-given (ladunnī) knowledge. I ask You for a knowledge from among the sciences" — and let him name it; for God, exalted is He, grants success to your request. And I counselled one of the brethren to that, and he put it to use, and he had not completed the aforementioned number before God opened to him with diverse sciences, and he attained what he had been seeking, and beyond what could be added. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path (Q 2:213). And among its occult properties: when you put on a new garment, you recite it at the sewing of the garment and at the putting on of it, saying: "O God, as You have clothed me anew, [grant] that You make me live in felicity and appoint for me a lifespan increased." For the angels who are the servant-spirits (khuddām) of this verse ask forgiveness for the wearer of that garment until it wears out. And if he adds to it the sura Truly We sent it down on the Night of Power (Q 97:1), that is better.

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: when you visit a sick man, ask him about the condition of his illness. If his illness is from a headache in his head, or a pain, you write it out for him in separated letters and hang it upon him on the side of the pain and the ache. And if the sick man tells you that his ache is from his interior, or from his whole body, then draw its renowned wafq in a glass bowl, the writing being with musk, saffron, and rose-water; then write the noble verse also in separated letters, and write with it the verses of healing, which are His words, exalted is He: and He will heal the breasts of a believing people (Q 9:14); and a healing for what is in the breasts, and a guidance and a mercy for the believers (Q 10:57); in it is a healing for mankind (Q 16:69); And We send down of the Qurʾān that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (Q 17:82); And when I fall sick, it is He who heals me (Q 26:80); Say: for those who believe it is a guidance and a healing (Q 41:44). Then the writing is effaced with bees' honey, and the noble verse is recited over it seven times, and the sick man drinks it: he will be restored to health by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among the occult properties of this generous verse: whoever is afflicted by phlegm — let him take seven pieces of small white salt and recite over each one of them the noble verse seven times, and let him use them on an empty stomach for seven successive days, for God takes away from him what he suffers. And it is related of one of them that he used to see in his sleep frightening matters and things that terrified him, so he came to one of the masters, of /fol. 180r./ those possessed of operative deployment (taṣrīf), and complained to him of what he was finding in his sleep. The master said to him: When you betake yourself to your bed, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan three times; then recite the Throne Verse three times, and when you reach His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), repeat it three times and go to sleep, and you will be safe from what you find. So the man did that, and after it he found nothing that he disliked.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: when you wish to go in upon a king or a tyrant and you fear his mischief, you say, as you go in upon him, "Shāhat al-wujūh" ("may the faces be disfigured") three times; you recite the Throne Verse three times; then you say: "O God, cast [upon me] of Your adornment, and Your love, and Your honour, and the attributes of Your lordship, that whereby hearts are dazzled, and souls are abased, and eyes flash, and thoughts are made dull, and every arrogant tyrant is made to submit. O al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), O al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), O Allāh, O al-Wāḥid (the One), O al-Aḥad (the Unique). O God, guard me in what You have given me to possess, by that whereby You are more its possessor than I am; and supply me with a subtle strand from the subtle strands of Your name al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), and snatch away thereby the sights of all existing things; and clothe me in a coat of mail of Your sufficing and Your safekeeping; and gird me with the sword of Your aid, and Your honour, and Your protection; and crown me with the crown of Your might and Your honour; and wrap me in the mantle of Your favour and Your well-being; and mount me upon the vessel of deliverance unto death; and supply me with a subtle strand from the subtle strands of Your names of subduing, and repel from me thereby whoever intends evil against me from among the whole of Your creation, as You made the sea subservient to Moses son of ʿImrān; and soften their hearts for me as You softened iron for David — peace be upon him — for they do not speak save by Your leave; their forelocks are in Your grasp, which You turn about as You will. O Turner of hearts, O Knower of all unseen things: I have quenched the wrath of So-and-so son of So-and-so" — and if you wish, you may say, "I have quenched the wrath of the people" — "by 'there is no god but God'; and I have drawn their hearts by Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace.

And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the Exalted, the Mighty. And a guarding against every rebellious devil (Q 37:7); and a guarding — that is the ordaining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing (Q 41:12); and We have guarded it from every accursed devil (Q 15:17); Truly it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and truly We are its guardians (Q 15:9); He has attendant angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God (Q 13:11); and God encompasses them round about; nay, it is a glorious Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22); and truly we are his guardians (Q 12:12); and We delivered him from the distress, and thus do We deliver the believers (Q 21:88); and I am not a guardian over you (Q 6:104); there is no soul but has a guardian over it (Q 86:4); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord /fol. 180v./ of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129); God is Guardian over them, and you are not a trustee over them (Q 42:6)." He says: "Ḥafīẓ, Ḥafīẓ, Ḥafīẓ. O al-Ḥāfiẓ (the Guardian), O al-Ḥafīẓ (the Preserver), guard us! O God, watch over us with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter us within Your shelter that cannot be assailed. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Lord of the worlds." Then you fall silent, you and whoever is with you, and you do not speak; for even if the whole nation of Rabīʿa and Muḍar were to come in upon you, they would not harm you nor injure you, and God would hide you from them. And I have tried it many times over. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided.

And know, my brother — may God, exalted is He, grant success to us and to you in the understanding of His secrets — that this noble verse and these lofty names were sent down from beneath the leg of the Throne; and when it was sent down upon the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — seventy thousand angels descended with it, in honour and in magnification of it. And it is the deliverer from fear and terror, and from the evil of humankind and of jinn. And whoever recites it in places of fear is made secure and guarded and sufficed, for it is the verse of guarding. And it has seventy-two operative deployments (taṣrīf); but I have turned away from mentioning them for fear of the ignorant, lest it fall into the hand of one who does not know its worth, so that he violates by it what is sacrosanct and does with it what does not befit it. And we have [nonetheless] opened the door for whoever wishes to enter into this treasure, mighty in station. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path (Q 2:213).

And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: when a person sets out on a journey and is about to leave his house, let him say: "A thousand, a thousand, a thousand Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad (Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ) and the Throne Verse — by them I fortify property and family and child. A thousand, a thousand Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad and the

Throne Verse are at my right and at my left — by them I guard myself against every one. I have put on the veil of God, the All-Encompassing, the Exalted; and I have fortified myself in the fortress of God, the Pre-eternal; and I have girded myself with the sword of the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī; and I have wrapped myself in the mantle of ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers; and I have entered into the treasuries of 'In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate', whose locks are 'Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds'." Then he recites the Throne Verse and Qul huwa Llāhu aḥad three times, and blows to his right and to his left. And if he wishes to abridge it, let him recite what we have mentioned, then blow into his palms and wipe with them his head and his face and the rest of his body; for God, exalted is He, makes him secure from all that he fears and is wary of, until he returns to his dwelling.

And among its occult properties: whoever recites it in the morning, God, exalted is He, keeps him secure until he comes to the evening; or in the evening, God keeps him secure until he comes to the morning. And among its occult properties: if you recite it over the head of an epileptic (maṣrūʿ) eleven times, he comes to his senses on the spot; and if the afflicting [spirit] (al-ʿāriḍ) persists and does not come out of the body, it is burnt. And among its occult properties: if it is recited immediately after the prayers, it effaces the faults and the slips that lie upon the one who prays. And among its occult properties: if it is recited when going in /fol. 181r./ upon a tyrant or an unjust ruler — and one says in the course of it: "O God, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), I ask You by the right of this generous verse and by what is in it of the secrets of understanding, that You bridle his mouth against me and strike his tongue dumb against me, so that he speak nothing but good, or else keep silent. Your good, O you, is before you, and your evil is beneath your feet" — and he goes in upon him: God bridles his mouth, and there accrues to him other than harm, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among its occult properties: if you fear the evil of someone and harm has come to you from him, then you pray two rakʿas after the evening prayer, with the Fātiḥa and the Throne Verse. And when it is the last prostration, the Throne Verse is recited three times while you are prostrate; and when you reach His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), you repeat it three times, or seven. You say in the course of your recitation: "O God, come between me and So-and-so son of So-and-so, as You have come between the heaven and the earth; and bridle his mouth against me, as You bridled the beasts of prey away from Daniel — peace be upon him — by the right of these noble names." For you will be secure from his evil, and you will bridle his mouth against you, so that he will not speak of you save with good.

And among its occult properties: if you are in a company of people and you desire to be sufficed against their evil and their harm, recite the generous verse three times and blow into your palms three times, and wipe with your hand over your face and your whole body, while you say:

"O God, suffice me against the evil of these people, O Sufficer; and grant me well-being from their harm, O Granter of well-being." For God will make you secure from them, and no evil from them will befall you, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And among the occult properties of this magnificent verse: if you recite it by night, you are secure until the morning; and if you recite it by day, you are secure until the evening.

And it is related that a man lodged in an abandoned house; and when night fell upon him, lo, there was a foulness and a clangour. The man looked, and there was a black figure, with fire issuing from his nostrils, crawling upon the ground and making toward him. He said: When I saw him I feared him with a great fear, and I was inspired to recite the Throne Verse; and every time I said a word, he said it with me — until I reached His words, exalted is He, The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255), and he did not say it. So I repeated it upon him many times over, and he vanished from me, and I did not see him for the remainder of my night. And when it was morning I looked, and lo, one of the corners of the house was ashes; and I marvelled at that. Then I told my story to a brother of mine among my brethren, and he was a righteous man, and he said to me: This was an ʿifrīt who wished to harm you, and this generous verse burnt him, because you were inspired to recite it. And when I heard that, I took it as a litany (wird) and a remembrance by night and by day; and I saw of its blessing something mighty. /fol. 181v./

And among its occult properties: it is written for the companion-spirits (quranāʾ) and the attendant spirits (tawābiʿ); for whoever has it hung upon him is made secure from that. And if there be joined to it His words, exalted is He, and God encompasses them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22); God is the best guardian, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful (Q 12:64); He has attendant angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of God (Q 13:11); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129); and a guarding against every rebellious devil (Q 37:7); and We have guarded it from every accursed devil (Q 15:17); and a guarding — that is the ordaining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing (Q 41:12) — and there is written with it al-Ikhlāṣand the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān), then it is a mighty veil against the companion-spirits and others, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among the occult properties of this verse: when it is placed among goods, they are preserved, and their owner is made secure over them against thieves and others. And when the generous verse is drawn in the wafq of the Sun — be it numerical or literal — in the hour of the Sun, and then placed among the loads of merchandise, they increase and yield profit. And if the aforementioned square is placed in the money chest, it is preserved, and the money is not emptied out of the chest so long as the noble square is in it. And among the occult properties of this verse, which is His words, exalted is He, Alif-Lām-Mīm. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 3:1–2): this noble verse contains the Greatest Name of God, and it has, of number, 483. Whoever sets it down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul) in the first [hour] of the day of Friday upon a noble body, and carries it with him, sees of the wonders of God's making, exalted is He, what descriptions fall short of, in the way of high standing, might, and awe in the eyes of people. And in it is a marvellous secret for going in upon rulers, kings, grandees and viziers, and for the seeking of needs. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see:

[Wafq: 4×4, cells as in the source, each row read from right to left; the topmost row carries the four segments of the verse in place of figures — read from right to left,(Alif-Lām-Mīm Allāh, 137),(lā ilāha illā huwa, 110),(al-Ḥayy, 49),(al-Qayyūm, 187) — and the last cell of the bottom row likewise carries a word, (Kāfī, the Sufficer, 111); the constant of every row, column, and diagonal is 483, the number of the verse]

And it is related from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī — may God ennoble his face — that he said: I am surety for whoever recites this verse, up to twenty verses of it, that God, exalted is He, will preserve him from every rebellious devil, and from every wrongdoer, and from every treacherous thief, and from every ravening beast of prey — the Throne Verse, and three verses from al-Aʿrāf, Indeed your Lord is God (Q 7:54), and ten verses from the beginning of al-Ṣāffāt, and three verses from al-Raḥmān, O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the confines of the heavens and the earth (Q 55:33), and the closing verses of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the end of Sūrat Tabbat. And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: when some matter troubles one of you, let him perform the ablution in the depth of the night and pray two rakʿas, each rakʿa with the Fātiḥa and the Throne Verse three times; /fol. 182r./ and when he has given the salutation, you recite the noble verse seven times, and after it he says this blessed supplication: "O God, truly You hear my speech, and see my place, and know my secret and my open state, and nothing of my affair is hidden from You. I supplicate You with the supplication of the destitute, the poor, who cries for help, who seeks refuge, who confesses his sin and his shortcoming; and I ask You with the asking of the needy; and I entreat You with the entreaty of the lowly sinner — the entreaty of one whose neck is bowed before You, and whose tear has overflowed toward You, and who has abased his cheek before You and rubbed his nose in the dust for You: that You quicken our hearts, and expand our breasts, and make our endeavours pure for Your generous Face and a cause of attaining to bliss. And grant us success, our Lord, in that which is Your pure good pleasure; and seal for us from Yourself with good; and make us tomorrow with those upon whom You have bestowed favour — of the prophets, and the truthful, and the martyrs, and the righteous; and how excellent are those as companions! And suffice us, O God, in what troubles us of the affair of religion, and of this world, and of the hereafter; and do not let the enemies gloat over us, nor the envious folk; and do not make our affliction to be in our religion; and do not make this world our greatest care, nor the sum of our knowledge; and do not, because of our sins, give power over us to one who does not fear You and does not have mercy upon us; and let us enjoy our hearing and our sight; and give us life; and open for us the doors of good; and provide for us, for You are the best of providers (Q 5:114); Our Lord, forgive us, and our brethren who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts any rancour toward those who have believed (Q 59:10); and forgive us — our Lord, truly You are Ever-Gentle, Compassionate (Q 59:10); Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affair, and make firm our feet, and give us victory over the unbelieving people (Q 3:147); Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and guard us from the torment of the Fire (Q 2:201) — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful."

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: if it is written upon the shroud of a dead man in three places — it is written at his head, and at his middle, and at his shins — then that dead man is not tormented in his grave, and the two angels deal gently with him at the time of the questioning; for it is the greatest verse in the Qurʾān, and He began it with His generous name, and He said — mighty and majestic is He who speaks — God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255). So know, O you, its worth, and supplicate with it in weighty affairs and at the fulfilling of needs. And it is related also of one of the righteous that he said: I was in a ship, and the black wind rose against them, so that scarcely would anyone be saved from it. So he drew the Throne Verse upon a sheet of paper (qirṭās) and hung it facing the blowing of the wind, and spread out his palms to God, exalted is He, in supplication; and he says in his supplication: "O God, I ask You by Your magnificent name, /fol. 182v./ God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255) — to the end of it — I ask You, O God, by its blessing, that You deliver us from what has come down upon us; and You are the Knower of all unseen things and the Dispeller of distresses. I ask You, O God, by the deliverance of Your most generous beloved, Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace." And he had not completed his supplication before God, exalted is He, gave them relief, and the fair wind came to them, and they journeyed on in security, in safety, and in soundness.

And among the occult properties of this noble verse: whoever desires that God, exalted is He, heal him of every disease in his body and of all the pains and the sicknesses — and there is written with it His words, exalted is He, Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God (Q 59:21) — to the end of the sura — and His words, exalted is He, And if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were set moving, or by which the earth were cleft asunder, or by which the dead were spoken to — nay, but to God belongs the whole affair (Q 13:31). And when he has finished writing it, the Throne Verse is recited over it seven times, and you suffumigate it with whatever there may be of sweet perfumes, and he drinks it over three days, morning and evening: God, exalted is He, heals him and grants him well-being from everything he dislikes. And if he also writes it and hangs it upon him, that is more effective and better. And God is the Healer, and the Sufficer, and the Granter of well-being.
And among the occult properties of this noble verse: it is written for ophthalmia and for pain of the eye; it is written and hung upon him. The Throne Verse is written three times, and His words

…exalted is He: God is the light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light…— to His words, exalted is He — and God is Knower of all things (Q 24:35); and you write Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1). In the eye is ophthalmia, a redness within a whiteness. God the Eternal Refuge is my sufficiency. O my Succour in hardships, by

Your being too mighty [to have] a child! There was no doubt concerning God, and none is equal to Him, not one. I adjure you, O ophthalmia, O inflamed one that clings to the veins and to the skins; for I adjure you by Joseph son of Jacob and his rent shirt, and by the Torah of Moses and the Gospel of Jesus and the Psalms of David, and by the Mighty Qurʾān, and by Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — the lamp of existence and Messenger of the Lord who is worshipped: depart, O ophthalmia, from the bearer of this writing of mine, by the truth of "there is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God", and by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant peace.

Among the occult properties of this noble verse: it is written for the weeping of children and hung upon them. You write the noble Fātiḥa in separated letters, and likewise the Throne Verse — you write it in separated letters, three times. And you write And God prevails over His affair (Q 12:21); But if they turn away, say: God suffices me; there is no god but He. Upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne (Q 9:129). Ṣar ṣar ṣar ṣar, ṣah ṣah ṣah ṣah! Be still, O newborn, and be silent, by the sanctity of the Lord who is worshipped. And voices are humbled before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a hushed whisper (Q 20:108). And faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; and he who bears wrongdoing has failed (Q 20:111). Faces that day /fol. 183r./ shall be bright, laughing, rejoicing at good tidings (Q 80:38–39). Do you then marvel at this discourse, and laugh and not weep, while you divert yourselves heedlessly?(Q 53:59–61) — and you are silent! Be silent, O newborn, by the truth of the King who is worshipped and the Loving Lord! Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf. And God encompasses them from behind. Nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22) — preserved, preserved! I place under the protection of God, exalted is He, whoever has this writing of mine hung upon him, from the evil of what He has created; and I have fortified him by God, the Living who does not die. And lift, O God, evil and harm from the bearer of this writing of mine. I have fortified him with "there is no god but God, Muḥammad is the Messenger of God", and by the truth of "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate": Say: I take refuge with the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, and from the evil of the night-darkness when it closes in, and from the evil of those who blow upon the knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies (Q 113:1–5) — by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty".

Among the occult properties of this noble verse, for the binding of tongues: the noble verse is written on Indian paper in separated letters, and there is written with it these names — nūw, then fūw, then nūwā: so they do not speak. Every king is a possession owned by God; and every rich man is, with God, a destitute pauper; and every tyrant is, with God, abased, and he has no refuge from God. I seek help against you, O

So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by God the Magnificent. And voices are humbled before the All-Merciful, so that you hear nothing but a hushed whisper (Q 20:108). And a bar is placed between them and that which they crave (Q 34:54). This is a day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). Kāf-Hāʾ-Yāʾ-ʿAyn-Ṣād, Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf, Qāf, Nūn. Dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb; blind, blind, blind, blind, blind, blind, blind. So they do not see. So they do not speak. So they do not talk. And We have set before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them over, so they do not see (Q 36:9). I have bound your tongue, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by that wherewith God bound the heavens from falling upon the earth save by His leave; and by that wherewith God bound the beasts of prey away from Daniel — peace be upon him; and by that wherewith God bound […] from giving birth; and by that wherewith God bound the barren wind, which leaves nothing that it comes upon but makes it like decayed bones (Q 51:42). And I have bound all the tongues of creation and of humankind, of every female and male among the children of Adam and the daughters of Eve, away from the bearer of this writing of mine: they shall not speak concerning him save with good, or else they shall be silent. Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not speak. And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they attained no good.
And God sufficed the believers in the fighting; and God is Strong, Mighty (Q 33:25).

[Among the occult properties of] the noble Throne Verse: if you have an enemy, or an obstinate adversary, or you fear the evil of a tyrannical ruler or an oppressive wrongdoer, and you wish to quench his evil away from you, or to destroy him if he deserves that — then, when it is the eve of Friday, rise at midnight, or in the last third [of the night], in a state of ablution, and pray two rakʿas with the intention of what you want of what we have mentioned. And you recite in the first the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse nine /fol. 183v./ times, and you do in the second rakʿa the like of the first; and when you have given the salām ⟨you recite the Throne Verse nine times and you do in the second rakʿa the like of the first; and when you have given the salām⟩he says the Throne Verse nine times also. Then you say: O God, You are severe in seizing-grip, painful in seizing, magnificent, Possessor of the subduing power that is exalted above opposites and peers, transcendent above consort and children. I ask You for the subduing of enemies and the crushing of tyrants. You devise against whom You will, and You are the best of devisers. I ask You by Your name before which forelocks are bowed low, by which You brought down [those who were] in the fortresses, and cast terror into the hearts of the enemies, and made wretched the people of wretchedness — I ask You to supply me with a subtle strand from among the subtle strands of this name, coursing through my enemies with the universal and the particular substances, until I am enabled to do what I will to him who has wronged me. I desire that no wrongdoer reach me with harm, and that no arrogant tyrant assault me; and make my anger for You and in You, conjoined with Your anger for Your own sake; and blot out the sight of my enemies, and harden their hearts, and strike between me and them a wall having a gate: its inner side, therein is mercy, and its outer side, facing it, is the torment. Truly You are severe in seizing-grip, painful in retribution. And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns in their wrongdoing; truly His seizing is painful, severe (Q 11:102). And there is suited to it, of the verses of the Mighty Qurʾān: So God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against God (Q 40:21); Truly the seizing-grip of your Lord is severe (Q 85:12); So He seized them with a mounting seizure (Q 69:10); So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off; and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds (Q 6:45). And you say: O God, I ask You, by the blessing and the secret of that wherewith I have called upon You, to subdue my enemies and whoever intends evil for me. And He is the Subduer above His servants (Q 6:18) — subdue So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]! For I thrust You against his throat: so suffice me against his evil, and turn away from me his treachery and his guile, O Lord of the worlds. For God will preserve you and guard you from him, and you will be safe from his evil; and if he transgresses against you, he perishes forthwith. And if the invoker is the possessor of a truthful state, he does not rise from his place but that his need has succeeded. So understand. So whoever pardons and sets things right, his reward rests with God (Q 42:40); and God supports with His help whom He wills (Q 3:13). No servant has ever communed with God, exalted is He, by this litany of remembrance in the first [hour] of the day of Saturday and invoked against one who wronged him, but that he was seized on the spot.

Among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if he has a need among pressing needs, then you enter one of the mosques and pray two rakʿas. You recite in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse seven times, and in the second rakʿa you do likewise. And when /fol. 184r./ you have given the salām, rise up by your own strength and stand in the prayer-niche (miḥrāb), and take hold of its sides with your hand and shake it; and say Yā Rabb (O Lord) seven times, and say Yā ʿAẓīm (O Magnificent) seven times, and say Yā Ḥalīm Yā Ḥalīm Yā Karīm Yā Raḥīm (O Forbearing, O Forbearing, O Generous, O Compassionate) seven times, and say Yā Qāḍī l-ḥājāt (O Fulfiller of needs) seven times. Then you say this blessed supplication: O Lord, enrich me by You, apart from all besides You, with a richness that makes me independent of every portion that summons to any outward creation or inward affair; and cause my innermost secret to reach [its term]; raise me to the Lote-tree of my own uttermost bound; and make me witness existence with vision and with joy, upon the secret of the sending-down to the endings and of munificence to the beginnings, until speech is cut off, and the movement of mankind grows still, and the dot of the ghayn is effaced, and the one stands in place of the two. O God, make easy for me [something] of the secret which You have made easy for many of Your servants; and support me in that with a resplendent light whereby the sight of every envier among jinn and humankind is snatched away; and grant me a lofty degree in every station; and enrich me, apart from all besides You, with a richness that establishes my poverty toward You. Truly You are the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. O God, I ask You to enrich my poverty, and to ease my affair, and to mend my brokenness, and to gather up my dishevelment and my abasement, and that You accomplish my need, which is such-and-such — and you ask for what you want: of the enriching of poverty, and the easing of an affair, and the removal of care and grief, and all that you want. For God, exalted is He, will grant you what you seek and what you want; and He is the most generous of those who are asked and the best of those who give. So make your opinion and your intention good, and you will attain your wish. And there is suited to it, of the verses of the Mighty Qurʾān, His words, exalted is He: Did He not find you an orphan and give shelter? And He found you erring and guided; and He found you in want and enriched (Q 93:6–8). So understand these strange indications. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
Among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if you have a need with one of the great ones and you wish it to be fulfilled, then you fast that day from…

…greasy foods (al-zafar); and if you wish, your fasting that whole day would be better. And when the time of your breaking of the fast comes, break your fast upon something that is sweet. Then you pray the sunset prayer, and after the prayer you sit in your place of prayer and begin with the recitation of the Throne Verse; and you never speak any word of this world. And you continue thus until you pray the night prayer (ʿishāʾ). Then you sit [and recite] the Throne Verse seventeen times; and every time you have recited the verse once, you say in the course of your recitation: O God, make subservient to me the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — or So-and-so son of So-and-so. And you do not cease from that until you complete the number mentioned. And you say: O God, I ask You, O Living, O Abiding, O Everlasting, O Loving: I ask You to cast affection and love into the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and to fulfil my need; and to seize hold of his heart with affection and love for me — and you name yourself — so that he be pliant to my hand and not oppose me in what I command him, by the right of Your name al-Wadūd (the Loving), and by the right of the secrets of this /fol. 184v./ noble verse. Take charge, O servant-spirits of the Throne Verse, of the drawing of the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] to the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and stir up the spiritual force of love and affection between me and him. They love them as God should be loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And I cast upon you a love from Me, that you might be fashioned under My eye (Q 20:39).

Then you write upon clean paper (kāghad) what will be set out below, and the writing is to be with musk, saffron and rose-water. You write: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And you write: Ṭamūsh Ṭamūsh Yāṭūsh Yashṭūsh Yasṭūsh Saʿāb Saʿyāb Hīliyūthā Shaliyūthā Ahyāwush ʿAlshāqash Mahrāqash Shāʿūb Shīghūb Yaḥūm Saḥūm Marḥūm Daymūm Dayūm Ahyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt Āl Shadāy. I have taken the meanings of the letters. And beneath them three verses, and the square of the felicities (wafq al-suʿūd), from the Sovereign who is worshipped and the good that is found. O servant-spirits of these names and these letters, stir up the spiritual force of love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of what I have recited over you of the mighty names of God; and take hold of the gathering-points of his heart and his mind, so that he can utter nothing but my name, and look upon nothing but my person, and hear nothing but my word and my speech. Come forward, and do not fear; truly you are among those who are secure (Q 28:31). And I cast upon you a love from Me (Q 20:39). Wa-Daḥab Wa-Daḥab Wud Wud Wud. Love is obtained, drawn, drawn, like sugar in hearts. Draw, and attract, and endear, and make loving, and cast the robe of love, and the crown of awe, and the light of gnosis, by the majestic names and the mighty adjurations. Hayhayūh Ahyāhayūh! Abased is every tyrant before the awe of God's majesty, and submissive is every arrogant one to the command of God. Fear not, you two; truly I am with you both — I hear and I see (Q 20:46). You shall not fear being overtaken, nor shall you be afraid (Q 20:77). And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31). Take charge, O servant-spirits of these names, of the fulfilment of the need of So-and-so from So-and-so. They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded (Q 66:6). Do, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], what I have commanded you of the fulfilment of my need, and it is such-and-such — by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11). Even so let So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] obey So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] in what he asks of him, and not oppose him in anything of the fulfilment of his needs. Take charge, O lord of this day and this hour — you and your helpers — and be all of you helpers to So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] for the fulfilment of his need from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of these mighty verses and these generous adjurations, and by the right of God, the King, the All-Knowing. Hear and obey, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and fulfil the need of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Let no one speak concerning So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] save with good, or /fol. 185r./ let him keep silent. This is a day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). Make your excuse, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and fulfil for him all that he asks and all that he desires, by the right of God, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious, and by the right of Ṭahṭahūb Ṭahṭahūb

Lahūb Lahūb, the life of everything. No servant has disobeyed You but that he was burned, and no tyrant but that he was abased and perished. Hayd Hayd Wahā Hā Hū Hū Hū Ah Ah Yah Bīh Wah Wah. And He is the Subduer above His servants (Q 6:18). To Him belongs the lofty kingship and the towering might. You are He, He; and You are powerful over everything. I ask You, O God, that You make subservient to me Your generous angels who serve these names and who obey these adjurations, that they take charge and comply with what he has commanded them of assistance to So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] against So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; and fulfil for him all that he asks, and make him pliant to his hand, not opposing him in any matter whatsoever. Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour! May God bless you and pour blessing upon you.

And you write this noble wafq whose mention comes next. Then you suffumigate the paper with fine Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), mastic, pepper, saffron in filaments (zaʿfarān shaʿr), nadd-aloeswood, marshmallow seed, seven grains of mountain-apple, seven grains of black cumin, and seven grains of church incense. And when you have suffumigated the paper, you fold it over the name of whomever you wish, and you say: I have folded up your tongue, O So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], away from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], as I have folded up this paper. Then you circle the paper about the head of the one you desire three times; and if that is not possible for you, then circle the sheet at a distance, in whatever way is contrived. Then the seeker puts it beneath his turban, between his eyes, and goes in upon whatever he desires.

This is when it is upon the name of a particular person. But if he wants it for the whole of humankind, of every female and male, then let him suffumigate it with the aforementioned incense and put it in his turban: he will see wonder upon wonder in the submission of creatures to love of him. And the condition in that is that he keep constantly to the recitation of the Throne Verse seventeen times every day; he will see wonder upon wonder. And this is its form.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse for love and intimacy between two who bear hatred toward one another — and among the occult properties of that: you begin your operation in a fortunate, good hour, for what we have mentioned. Then you write the names of the two who hate one another upon a sheet and set it before you. Then you take forty grains of male frankincense, of the size /fol. 185v./ of peppercorns, and forty grains of jinn-apple. Then you divide the incense into two halves, twenty from each, and you suffumigate with two grains until the incense is completed — forty times — while you recite the Throne Verse. And every time you have recited it five times, you say: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble verse, of the casting of love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of this sura upon you and of its blessing with you, and by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11). And when you have finished your recitation, you draw the wafq whose mention comes next upon a sheet from among those sheets; and you write together with the square these noble verses and these lofty names. You say: O God, I ask You, O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O You whom eyes do not see and conjectures do not mingle with, whom describers do not describe and characterizers do not characterize; O You whose command is between the kāf and the nūn — His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say "Be", and it is (Q 36:82): I ask You, O God, to cast love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right of these noble verses. They love them as God should be loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts in affection; but God joined them in affection. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63). And truly, in the love of good he is intense (Q 100:8). And I cast upon you a love from Me, that you might be fashioned under My eye (Q 20:39). O God, O You who created in the fourth heaven an angel half of whom is of snow and half of fire, so that the fire does not melt the snow nor the snow quench the fire, and the angel calls out with the tongue of omnipotence: All-Glorified, All-Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit! O God, O You who joined together snow and fire, join together the heart of Your servant So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; truly You are powerful over whatever You will. [And this is] the form of the aforementioned square.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant me success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse is [its use] for love, and for acceptance, and for standing among the great ones. So when you desire that, draw this square, which I shall set out for you, upon gazelle parchment; and the writing is with musk, saffron and rose-water; and you write around the square the Throne Verse; and you suffumigate, at the time of writing and at the time of carrying it, with Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), and ʿūd al-ṣalīb (cyclamen). So understand that. /fol. 186r./

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that I shall mention for the Throne Verse also an occult property bound up with matters of love and intimacy among the great ones, and with the casting of awe into their hearts; and it profits for meeting kings and viziers, when one carries it and recites it. And they are these verses and names. You say this blessed supplication, and it is this: O God, I ask You, O God of the first and the last, O Answerer of the invocation of those who ask — I ask You, O God, by the right of God: there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255), that You deliver me from So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], and that You make him smitten with love for So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him (Q 2:255) — even so let neither slumber nor sleep overtake So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]; even so let him rave the whole length of his night with love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth (Q

2:255) — even so let the heavens and the earth be straitened upon So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], so that he sees, in his sleep and his night, nothing but his phantom with him and the mention of him upon his tongue, from the intensity of the abiding love between them. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) — even so let there intercede for So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] these…

…this generous and noble verse with So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], without the intercession of created beings, but rather by the intercession of the word of the Real. He knows what is before them and what is behind them (Q 2:255) — likewise So-and-so son of So-and-so knows that So-and-so son of So-and-so is before him and not behind his back /fol. 186v./: obedient to his command, answering his call, responding to his word, fulfilling his need, love firmly rooted in his heart. And they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills. His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255) — likewise let the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so embrace love for So-and-so son of So-and-so, as His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth. I have widened your heart and set it beating, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, toward So-and-so son of So-and-so, as His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth; he has no strength to be patient away from him. I have set you beating, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, toward So-and-so son of So-and-so, until you accomplish for him all his interests, and whatever he seeks and whatever he desires, without turning back and without opposition. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). O God, I ask You — O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh — that You settle love for So-and-so son of So-and-so in the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so, so that he obeys him and disobeys no command of his, by the right of this noble verse. Take charge, O servant-spirits (khuddām) of this noble verse, of So-and-so son of So-and-so: incline his heart, and soften all his limbs with love for So-and-so son of So-and-so, by the right of this generous verse — They love them as God is loved; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165); Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but God brought them together. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63); And I cast upon you love from Me (Q 20:39) — O So-and-so son of So-and-so, by the right of these noble verses.

And it is related of one of the righteous that when night fell upon him he would rise to his prayer-niche (miḥrāb) and pray as much as God willed; and when his prayer was completed he would say — this supplication is for this noble verse: "[O God,] You are You! Hope is cut off save from You, and expectations come to nothing save in You, and the ways draw their supply from none but You, O Trust of him who has no trust in any but You. I ask You, O God, by Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest — God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255): You are the Living, the Abiding for ever. Neither slumber seizes Him nor sleep (Q 2:255) — for slumber and sleep belong to created beings, not to the Creator. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255): You are the God of the heavens and the earth, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth, there is no god but You. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) Who is there that has power over that over which You have power? You — all created things are [subject to] the subduing might of Your magnificence. O You who knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills. His Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255): You are He who has embraced all things in mercy and knowledge, and You are Knower of all things. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). Our Lord, our Lord! Our Master, our Master! Our Patron, our Patron! You are He who gives and withholds, and You are He who raises and lowers; and You are He who sees and hears, and nothing in the earth or in the heaven is hidden from You. I ask You by the hiddenness of Your gentleness and by the majesty of Your might that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad, the greatest beloved, the honoured Prophet, the magnified Messenger, our master and our prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace; and I ask You by the standing of the people of his House, the good and the pure, by the standing of his companions all together, and by the standing of the Successors and of those who follow the Successors in excellence until the Day of Judgement: I ask You to gather me in their throng and beneath their banners, and to supply me with their supply. Amen, O Lord of the worlds!" Whoever communes with God with this /fol. 187r./ blessed supplication in the depth of the night and asks God, exalted is He, He gives him all that he has sought; and God is the possessor of magnificent bounty. So understand and ponder.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if one of you has a need among the needs of this world and of the world to come, let him rise in the depth of the night and pray four rakʿas, reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse ten times; and let him raise his head and his hands to heaven and invoke with this supplication: "O God, I ask You — O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh, O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O You whom neither slumber seizes nor sleep — I ask You, O God, by the sanctity of the Throne Verse with You, that You do for me such-and-such, and that You grant me all my desires and my purposes and what I seek from You" — and you ask for your need and name it; for it is a right upon God, exalted is He, that He accomplish it. Then pray for the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — at the beginning of your undertaking and at the end of it, and your operation will prosper, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God is the Granter of success.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever recites it by day, God — exalted is He — guards him on that day; and if he recites it by night, God — exalted is He — guards him during his night. And whoever recites the Throne Verse after every prayer, all his sins are forgiven him. And among the occult properties of the Throne

Verse: whoever recites it after every prayer, God forgives him his sins and effaces from him his evil deeds until the next prayer. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: whoever recites it at his sleeping, it is a protective charm for him against the accursed Satan. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: [whoever recites it] when he is angry, and spits to his left, the Satan slinks back — his own satan — and there departs from him his anger, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Let us now set down this blessed supplication for the noble Throne Verse. I have abridged the exposition of it and the discourse upon it, lest it fall into the hands of one who does not know it, and he invoke with it and be answered. It is a mighty supplication, majestic in worth, magnificent in proof, magnificent in worth. You say: God — there is no god but He (Q 2:255) — He is alone in abiding and in permanence. The essence of created beings: their reality does not subsist alongside His essence, nor their attributes alongside His attributes, nor their names alongside His names, nor their acts alongside His acts; and there is none other than Him, not one. There is no beauty save His beauty in reality, and no majesty save His majesty, and no perfection save His perfection; and He is everlasting, ever returning in His perfection, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, abiding upon His Throne by the perpetuity of His kingship. And all creatures are led to the knowledge of Him, and they know that He is One in His kingship, Unique in His everlastingness, mighty in His eternity. Despite the diversity of their intellects and of their religions, they all /fol. 187v./ return to the reality of knowledge, and they know that He is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of life and the Bringer of death, and that the whole affair returns to Him. As for the gnostics and the verifiers (muḥaqqiqūn): they have wandered lost in the reality of the knowledge of that which has illumined their hearts and their sights through the disclosure of the realities of the knowledge of His handiworks. They have wandered lost in the seas of His love and of what He has bestowed upon them, and they have plunged into the waves of the fathomless deeps of the seas — and there is no buffeting against His power. They confessed their incapacity to attain the knowledge of Him, and they drowned in the seas of His dominion; and they knew and verified that there is no god but He; and it pointed to His being Living and Self-Subsisting. So He gave life to their hearts and illumined their inner sights and their inmost hearts, so that they beheld in existence none but Him, and no Lord but Him alone, and they confessed their incapacity before Him. [Neither] slumber seizes Him nor sleep (Q 2:255) — that is: no lassitude seizes Him away from the creating of things made, and no sleep away from the apprehending of things known. Truly His command, when He wills a thing — and He says: Be! and it is (Q 36:82). So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and unto Him you shall be returned (Q 36:83). All existent things hallow Him above indwelling and above likeness, above union, above beginning and end, above conjunction and separation: the like of whom there is nothing (Q 42:11). He is before things; and the return of creatures and their submission is unto Him. The First and the Term, One, Unique, alone in Himself in the hidden things, beyond eyes and understandings. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth (Q 2:255). And all beings bear witness to Him and are knowers of His handiworks, [testifying] that He is the God of the earths and the heavens.
