Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255) There glorify Him the people of the heavens and of the earths: and there is nothing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification (Q 17:44). Every speaker, then, [speaks] by His leave, and every utterer, then, by His knowledge. He is knower of all things and independent of all things; and everything is in need of Him, submissive to Him, abased before Him. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge (Q 2:255). Glory be to You! We have no knowledge save what You have taught us; truly You are the All-Knowing, the Wise (Q 2:32). He knows what is in the land and the sea; not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Book (Q 6:59). And they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills (Q 2:255). He has encompassed all things in knowledge (Q 65:12). And God is encompassing them from behind; nay, it is a majestic Qurʾān, upon a preserved Tablet (Q 85:20–22). And His power has encompassed the dominion of His might, so that all things journey unto Him. Our Lord, You have embraced all things in mercy and knowledge (Q 40:7). The spirits departed, and the faces were disfigured and wandered lost within the temples of their phantoms, and disposed themselves among the fashioned works of their traces, and took shape within the moulds of the spiritual beings, for the witnessing of the diversity of the forms within the moulds of composition, in the circuit of the barzakhs, for the manifestation of the decree upon the indication and the manifestation of knowledge. Their outward is the outward of power, and their inward is the inward of the Command and the secret of the [divine] confirming, for the reception of the courses of the decree and of free disposal by it. His Footstool embraces /fol. 188r./ the heavens and the earth, and the guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). Widen for us, out of Your self-subsistence, a knowledge and an understanding whereby we may dispose within the beings — there is no power and no strength save in You. I have raised up my need to You and my destitution before You: so do not disappoint my hope of You, for You are the All-Embracing, the Generous, the Magnificent Lord. I ask You by the wellspring of the life of the spiritual souls, and by the lights of the secrets of Your name, the Magnificent, the Greatest, by whose self-disclosure was cleft open the thirst of the innermost hearts of the people of a love whose proof is manifest — so that they wandered lost in the valleys of the purity of their inmost secrets and the lights of their essences, and cried out: O You whose Footstool embraces the heavens and the earth, and the guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255)! I ask You, O al-Wāsiʿ (the All-

Embracing), O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing), O al-ʿAlī (the High), O al-ʿAẓīm (the Magnificent), O al-Karīm (the Generous), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Raʾūf (the Ever-Gentle), O al-Ḥalīm (the Forbearing), O You who are God — there is no god but He, the Living…

…the Self-Subsisting. Neither slumber seizes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. The guarding of them does not weary Him, and He is the Exalted, the Magnificent (Q 2:255). I ask You, O God, by the right of these mighty verses and generous names, that You illumine our hearts, and widen our provision, and refine our characters. O Comforter of hearts, O Veiler of faults, O Dispeller of distresses, O Forgiver of sins, O Knower of all unseen things! You have known what has been of my asking and of my excusing myself in my retreat (khalwa), and of my seeking pardon for my slip and my disavowal of my sin. And You, O God, are best acquainted with my aspiration, and aware of my intention, and knowing of my inner disposition; the Master of all Dominion, my Lord, who holds my forelock, my goal in my request, my hope in my hardship, my comforter in my solitude, the merciful toward my tears, He who grants me release from my stumbling, the Answerer of my invocation. And if I have fallen short of what You commanded me and have committed what You forbade me, yet by Your standing You have protected me and by Your veiling You have veiled me. So, O most generous of the generous, O goal of the seekers, O Master of the Day of Judgement: You know what is hidden in the conscience, and You are the Disposer of the affairs of small and great. If You have accomplished my need, it is by Your bounty. I ask You to make me an intercessor for my own soul, and to have mercy upon me by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful. I ask You, O God, by the right of this generous verse and of the names of understanding (al-asmāʾ al-fahmiyya), that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad and to the family of Muḥammad, and that You give me my request and what I have sought from You. O Allāh, O Allāh, O Allāh, O Lord of the worlds!

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: if the servant is much given to sins and offences, and desires repentance for what he has perpetrated and separation from what he has done, let him rise in the White Nights of whatever month it may be — that is, the thirteenth /fol. 188v./, the fourteenth and the fifteenth. Let him purify his garments and his place, and let him rise in the depth of the night, and perform the ablution, and pray four rakʿas, reciting in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse seven times; and he does in every rakʿa the like of that first one. And when he has given the salām, let him sit and ask forgiveness of God, exalted is He, the Magnificent, seventy times, and pray for the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — seventy times. And the form of the prayer upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — is that you say: "O God, bless our master Muḥammad with a blessing whereby You deliver us from all terrors and afflictions, and whereby You accomplish for us all needs, and whereby You purify us of all ambiguities, and whereby You raise us to the highest degrees, and whereby You bring us to the furthest ends of good things in life and in death — a blessing that You store up for the Day of the

Greatest Terror and its dread; and upon his family, and his kin, and his companions, and grant peace." Then you begin by reciting this blessed supplication. You say: "O God, You are the Ever-Relenting toward whoever repents, and He who draws near whoever turns [to Him], and the Remover of the darkness of the veil. You know the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; and You have power over all things; and unto You the affairs return; and by You are evils repelled. O God, I ask You by the secret of Your name for a secret from Your secret, and a light from Your light, and a spirit from Your Command, that shall bequeath to me stillness before what You have decreed; and grant me a success from You that shall awaken what is heedless in me, and teach what is ignorant in me, and make plain my road to You, and be my companion in the going out and the returning. For in You is my striving, and upon You is my reliance, and unto You is my return, and before You is my falling. You know the reality of my affair and of my asking; with You are my secret and my open state. You are exalted above the marks of originated things, and transcendent above defects and afflictions, and Your knowledge is [too high] to be contested by ambiguities. I ask You, O God, for a repentance whereby You efface my slips, and whereby You make my work weigh heavy, and whereby You set right my outward, and whereby You purify my inward, and whereby You gather my scattered state, and whereby You hallow my innermost secret, and whereby You make my sanctification easy, and whereby You purify my soul, and whereby You cleanse me of my defilement. And grant me a light from You whereby I may walk among men; truly You are the Bestower, the Giver of lights, the Discloser of secrets, and everything with You is by measure. O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour)!" And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever fears the outcome of some affair and wishes to know it and to come out of it — let him purify himself and put on pure, clean garments, and purify the place in which he sits in seclusion. Then, when he has prayed the last night prayer (ʿishāʾ) /fol. 189r./, let him pray two rakʿas before the witr prayer, reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and the Throne Verse eleven times. And when he has given the salām, let him recite the Throne Verse twenty-one times, and recite the sura Truly We sent it down on the Night of Power (Q 97:1) once, and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣthree times, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-muʿawwidhatān) once. And let him say: "O God, I have sought an omen by Your ancient speech, so show me that which is hidden away. O God, show me in this night of mine all that I have asked about and what I have not asked about, and make plain to me the way out of this affair which I fear and am wary of. O God, if it be good for me, show me whiteness and greenness; and if it be evil for me and against me, show me blackness and redness. And [I ask] that You send me a servant-spirit (khādim) from among the servant-spirits of this noble verse, the Throne Verse, who shall tell me in my sleep what is kept hidden from me. My God, You are the Real: make plain to me the truth, O Real — the Real! Truly You have power over all things." Then you name what you want and what you seek. Then you pray the witr prayer, and you lie down upon your right side, and you pray for our master Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — to the measure of your capacity, and you sleep, and you set your mind upon your need. For God, blessed and exalted is He, sends you a servant-spirit from among the servant-spirits of this verse, and he informs you of all that you want and all that you seek, and makes clear to you your need, and what is good for you and what is evil against you. And if you do not see in your night what you seek and what you have asked about, then repeat the operation and the prayer on the second night and on the third, and you will see what you seek. So make your intention sincere, for the intention precedes the act; and God guides whom He wills to a straight path. And know the worth of what has reached you, for it makes you independent of much learning.

And among the occult properties of the noble Throne Verse: whoever is harmed by passionate love and infatuation and distracted longing toward some person, and fears scandal from people or from his own household — he recites the Throne Verse five times over a glass cup with musk and saffron and rose-water; then he sets it out beneath the open sky, after he has written the name of the person whose love he wishes to be rid of. Then, when morning comes, he dissolves the writing with rose-water and drinks it on an empty stomach. He does that […] times over three days; and God, exalted is He, will make him forget that person and will pluck the love of him out of his heart. And the intention precedes the act: whoever makes his intention sincere attains his wish.

And know — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of His secrets — that the Throne Verse has many occult properties and majestic, abundant benefits. It benefits one who is afraid, when trembling comes upon him: that departs from him by the leave of God, exalted is He. And among its occult properties: it is written for pain of the heart, and palpitation, and pain of the liver, and griping of the bowels. It is written as we have mentioned /fol. 189v./ in a pure vessel three times, and the one afflicted drinks it, saying as he drinks it: "I have intended healing from such-and-such an ailment" — and he names the ailment. For God, exalted is He, by the blessing of the noble verse, heals him and restores him — by the blessing of the noble verse, by the leave of God, exalted is He; and God is the Healer and the Restorer. And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse: it is of benefit for the dispelling of [the disease of] the spleen and of its pain. Let the noble verse be written and hung above the spleen, and God will heal him and restore him, by the blessing of the noble names.

And among the occult properties of the Throne Verse, for headache and migraine: let the Throne Verse be written upon gazelle parchment, if that be possible, or upon clean paper (kāghid); and there is written with it His words, exalted is He: Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God. And these similitudes We strike for men, that they may reflect (Q 59:21) — to the end of the sura; and His words, exalted is He: And to Him belongs whatsoever dwells in the night and the day; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 6:13). Be still, O pain, and headache, and migraine, and throbbing, away from the bearer of this writing of mine, as the Throne of the All-Merciful is still! And by the secret of these noble, blessed, lofty letters —

— still the distress of him over whom I have pronounced these names, by the right of these names! God is the Healer, God is the Sufficer, God is the Restorer. So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. This is among what has been tried and proved sound.
Know, O my brother — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him and in the unveiling of the secrets of His names — that this noble verse, I mean the Throne Verse, has occult properties…

…beyond counting and beyond number, for it is the greatest verse in the Book of God, exalted is He. And among the greatest of its occult properties is what I now mention to you, namely this: I was sitting before my master Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Andalusī, and we were conferring together upon some of the sciences, when there came in upon us a man trembling like a palm-frond in a raging wind. Then he gave the greeting, and fell upon the shaykh's hand, kissing it and weeping. So the shaykh said to him: What ails you, O man, and what has made you weep? The man said: My lord, I am in fear of certain enemies, that one of them should treacherously assail me with harm; and I have no power against him. And I have come to you, my lord, in the hope that you may relieve me of my care and remove from me my distress. And when the shaykh heard this speech from the man, he said to him: Rejoice, O man, and fear not — if God, exalted is He, wills — after this day, from anyone. Then the shaykh took a slip of paper (ruqʿa) and wrote upon it: "I take refuge with God from the accursed Satan. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. And God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant abundant peace." Then he wrote the Fātiḥa of the Book, and His words, exalted is He, /fol. 190r./ the Throne Verse; then you write Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣand the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān); then you write His words, exalted is He: And fear not; truly you are among the secure (Q 28:31); You shall fear neither being overtaken, nor shall you dread (Q 20:77); And fear not, you two; truly I am with you both, hearing and seeing (Q 20:46); Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing folk (Q 28:25); Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favour, said: Enter upon them by the gate; for when you have entered it, you shall be the victors. And upon God rely, if you are believers (Q 5:23); Fear not; truly you, you are the higher (Q 20:68). O God, guard me with Your eye that does not sleep, and shelter me within Your shelter that cannot be assailed, and forgive me by Your power over me, that I may not perish; for You are my hope. My Lord, how many a favour have You bestowed upon me for which my thanksgiving to You was little, and yet You did not deprive me! And O You who have seen me amid trials and did not disgrace me! O Possessor of kindness that is never cut off, and O Possessor of blessings that are never numbered: I ask You, O God, that You bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You preserve me and guard me from my enemies and from whoever intends me evil or harm. And turn back, O God, his violence upon him, and set his good between his eyes and his evil beneath his feet. And whoever desires for me evil, or treachery, or guile — let it return upon him, and make it cleave fast to him. And God turned back those who disbelieved in their rage; they attained no good. And God sufficed the believers in the fighting; and God is Strong, Mighty (Q 33:25). Deaf, dumb, blind — so they do not see; so they do not speak; so they do not talk. A day on which they shall not speak, nor shall they be given leave to make excuses (Q 77:35–36). Ṣād (Q 38:1). Qāf (Q 50:1). Nūn (Q 68:1). So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). And there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Then the shaykh folded the slip and handed it to the man, and said to him: Put it in your turban, for you will be safe from every harm. And the man never saw any evil come upon him thereafter.

And know, my brother, that these names of mighty worth — none has carried them but that God, exalted is He, delivered him from what he fears and guards against. And if he goes in with them upon a tyrannical ruler, he is safe from his evil; and none disputes with their bearer but that he overcomes him and subdues him, by their blessing. And their excellences are renowned among the learned and among those who know their worth. And God supports with His help whom He wills (Q 3:13). And God is the Possessor of mighty bounty (Q 3:74).

A blessed benefit, for guarding against enemies and against the fear of highwaymen and others. One of the righteous — may God, blessed and exalted, have mercy upon him — said: We halted, on one of our journeys, by a flowing river; and a people came to us and said: no one has halted in this place but that his baggage has been plundered. So my companions departed out of fear, and I stayed behind, on account of a noble hadith I had heard from Ibn ʿUmar — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((Whoever recites thirty-three /fol. 190v./ verses from the Book of God, exalted is He, no ravening beast of prey and no marauding thief shall harm him that night, and he shall be granted well-being in himself, his family, and his property, until morning.)) So when evening came, I did not sleep until I saw a company who had come brandishing their swords to draw near to me; but they could not reach me. And when I rose in the morning I departed, and there met me a shaykh upon a horse who said to me: O you, are you a human or a jinnī? I said: A human, of the children of Adam. He said to me: What is your case? We came upon you this night more than seventy times, and every time there was interposed between us and you a wall of iron. I said to him: Ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — related to me, from the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ((Whoever recites thirty-three verses from the Book of God, exalted is He, in a night, no ravening beast of prey and no marauding thief shall harm him, and he shall be in the safekeeping of God, exalted is He, until morning.)) And when the shaykh heard that, he dismounted from his horse and kissed my head, and gave God, exalted is He, a covenant that he would never return to what he had been doing. And these verses that have been mentioned are recited [as follows]: four verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara, up to His words, exalted is He, the successful (Q 2:5); and the noble Throne Verse and the two verses after it, up to His words abiding therein (Q 2:257); and the three last verses of al-Baqara, To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; and whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it (Q 2:284), to the end of the sura; and three verses from al-Aʿrāf, His words, exalted is He, Indeed your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days (Q 7:54), up to His words, exalted is He, of those who do good (Q 7:56); and ten verses from the beginning of al-Ṣāffāt, up to His words, exalted is He, clinging (Q 37:11); and the end of al-Isrāʾ, Say: Call upon God, or call upon the All-Merciful; whichever you call upon (Q 17:110), to the end of the sura; and two verses from Sūrat al-Raḥmān, O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the confines of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond! You shall not pass beyond save by an authority (Q 55:33), up to His words, exalted is He, you will not be helped (Q 55:35); and the closing verses of al-Ḥashr, His words, exalted is He, Had We sent down this Qurʾān upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of the fear of God; and these similitudes We strike for mankind, that they may reflect (Q 59:21), to the end of the sura; and two verses from Sūrat Say: it has been revealed to me (Q 72:1), up to His words, exalted is He, And the places of worship belong to God (Q 72:18); And He — exalted be the majesty of our Lord — has taken neither consort nor child (Q 72:3), up to His words, exalted is He, outrageous falsehood (Q 72:4).

And know that these verses are called the Verses of Guarding (āyāt al-ḥaras); and it is said that in them is a healing for a hundred maladies, such as leprosy (judhām), vitiligo (baraṣ), and the like. And it is related from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with them both — [who said]: I recited them over a shaykh who had been struck with hemiplegia (al-fālij), and God, exalted is He, took that away from him, by the leave of God, exalted is He, and by the blessing of His eternal speech. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided. And whoever engraves this noble wafq /fol. 191r./ upon a signet-ring of silver, or upon a plate of the same, in the first hour of the day of Friday — which is from sunrise until the shadow measures twenty-eight feet — then whoever does that sees marvels in himself. And it is for love, for acceptance, for awe, and for the widening of provision. And this is its form:
[Wafq: 9×9, cells exactly as they stand in the source table — ]
Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together; indeed God is powerful over everything (Q 2:148)

A majestic benefit, for the meeting of kings, rulers, viziers, judges, and governors, and of the masters of the pen and the holders of office. It is set down in the exaltation of the Sun, or in the exaltation of Jupiter, upon a plate of gold, or of silver, or of red copper; and let the engraver be fasting. And it is suffumigated, at the time of its engraving and at the time of its being carried and of the need for it, with Indian aloeswood, benzoin (jāwī), mastic, nadd aloeswood, and saffron. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. /fol. 191v./

And it is related of one of the righteous that he said: I had a need [to lay] before God, exalted is He, and I remained thirty years asking God, exalted is He, for it; and with all that I did not despair of it. Then one night I took to my bed and slept, and behold, one was saying: Take these adjurations that are beneath your head, and adjure [God] by them in your need, and it shall be granted. So I awoke, and I found these adjurations written upon a scroll in separated letters. So I gathered them together, and behold, they were as you see. And I have never adjured [God] by them in any need but that it was granted, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And they are these verses:

By the humility of hearts at the prostration, to You, O my Master, without any denial; and by You, O God, O Friend — for nothing draws near to You in the solemnity of covenants; and by Your Footstool, crowned with light, [rising] to Your mighty, glorious Throne; and by what was beneath Your Throne in truth, before the creation of heaven and the sound of the thunders —
that was when You had never at any time ceased to be a God known by divine oneness (tawḥīd).

And you say, when you have finished these noble verses: I ask You, O God, that You bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad and to the family of our master Muḥammad, and that You accomplish my need, which is such-and-such. For God, exalted is He, will accomplish it, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And there follows it this blessed supplication, which is the supplication of the noble Throne Verse. /fol. 192r./ You say: O Living, O Self-Subsisting! You are God, other than whom there is no god; truly I was among the wrongdoers. I ask You by Your self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya) that You establish me through You unto You; and I ask You by Your life for a life for my heart, and for well-being in that, in religion and in this world and in the hereafter and in what lies between the two. And preserve all of that for me, O You whom the guarding of nothing wearies! O High, O Magnificent — until I meet You while You are pleased with me: O God, in the best of states from You, and in the most easeful of minds, without trial and without punishment, neither in religion, nor in this world, nor in the hereafter — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.
And know, my brother — may God grant you and me success in obedience to Him, and illumine our hearts with the light of gnosis of Him — I used often to persevere in the recitation of the Throne Verse…

…and the closing verses of Sūrat al-Baqara, from His words, exalted is He, The Messenger has believed (Q 2:285), to the end of the sura; then the opening [verses] of Āl ʿImrān, up to His words, exalted is He, the Mighty, the Wise (Q 3:6), together with the two verses, His words, exalted is He, Say: O God, Master of the kingdom— up to His words, exalted is He — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27). Then you say: O God, I ask You for soundness of fear, and the overmastering of yearning, and the coming of knowledge, and the perpetuity of reflection. I ask You, O

God, for the secret of secrets that wards off harms, so that we may have no abiding-place along with sin and blemish. And give us life, and guide us to act by these words which You spread out for us upon the tongue of Your Messenger, and with which You tried Abraham Your friend: and he fulfilled them. He said: I am making you a leader for mankind. He said: And of my progeny? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers (Q 2:124). So make us of those who do good, of his progeny and of the progeny of Adam and Noah; and lead us along the paths of the imams of the God-fearing. O God, I have wronged myself with much wronging, and none forgives sins but You; so forgive me and have mercy upon me. There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). O God, O High, O Magnificent, O Forbearing, O All-Knowing, O All-Hearing, O All-Seeing, O Willing, O Powerful, O Self-Subsisting, O All-Merciful, O Compassionate, O You who are Yāh Yāh, O First, O Last, O Manifest, O Hidden! Blessed is Your name, Possessor of Majesty and Honour. And relent toward me. And enter my names beneath Your names, and my attributes beneath Your attributes, and my acts beneath Your acts, unto the degree of safety and the casting off of regret. And send down a secret with which sins do no harm at all, and make for me from it a face whereby needs are accomplished — for the heart, and the intellect, and the spirit, and the yearning, and the soul, and the body. O God, join me to Your mighty name, together with whose name nothing in the earth nor in the heaven can do harm — and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And grant me from Yourself nobility (karāma) and the manifestation of leadership (imāma); and be for me, in that wherewith I have been tried, [as You are] for the imams of guidance among Your learned ones. And enrich me, that You may enrich by me whomever You will; and give me life, that You may give life by me to whomever You will and to whatever You will of Your servants; and make me /fol. 192v./ a treasury of the Forty, and one of the elect of the God-fearing; and forgive me, for ⟨none but⟩ the wrongdoers attain it. Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm (Q 26:1). Ḥā-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf (Q 42:1–2). He has let forth the two seas that meet together; between them is a barrier (barzakh) they do not overpass (Q 55:19–20). Then the noble Fātiḥa to its end, and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1) three times. So whoever recites these verses and adjurations and seeks a need among the needs of this world and of the hereafter attains it, by the leave of God, exalted is He. Behold, we have opened the door for whoever desires to enter into the treasure of regrets; and God gives His bounty to whom He wills. And after it you say: O God, O Real, O Light, O Evident! Open my heart by Your light, and teach me of Your knowledge, and preserve me by Your preservation, and make me hear, and make me understand, and give me sight through You; and appoint for me a means from Your bounty whereby You enrich me out of poverty, and give me might out of abasement, and set right for me this world and the hereafter, and bring me thereby to the beholding of Your generous Face in the Garden of Bliss. Truly You are powerful over everything; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. And whoever recites these verses and adjurations as we have set out the mention of them attains what he has sought from
God, exalted is He, by His grace and His generosity.

And among the occult properties of the supplication of the noble Throne Verse, [transmitted] from certain of the righteous — may God be pleased with them: whoever supplicates with it in all his affairs and his weighty concerns is answered. And it is this blessed supplication. You say: Praise be to God, who has set up for the worlds the standards of the sciences, and made the bearers of the Mighty Qurʾān His elect ones and His companions, [chosen] out of the whole and the generality; and who has given rest to the spirits of the [spiritual] poor (fuqarāʾ) from weariness, toil, and cares; and who has made the world like a lapis-blue robe whose embroidered border is the righteous. So he who obeys Him is praised, and he who disobeys Him is blamed. And whither shall the wrongdoer flee when the wronged calls down upon him and complains of him before a King mighty in awe, before whom kings stand? For His wrath there grow wrathful the water and the air, and the night and the day, and the sun and the moon and the stars, and the heat and the cold, and the clouds, and the trees, and the clods, and the mists. And death and life stand at His door as the servant stands before the one served. God — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting (Q 2:255). He has governed existence day after day, and made the bygone generations to pass away, people after people; and He has stilled the movements of those who are in the earth and those who are in the heaven, so that they have neither gesture nor striving. He has sated the people of extravagance and left hungry the people of fasting; and He has annihilated all those bodily forms — and He is the Everlasting, the

Abiding, in perpetuity and unto eternity. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him (Q 2:255). Master of what is above the above and of what is below the below, and of the length and the breadth; and He has decreed deliverance, and presence, and the recommended and the obligatory, upon His servants, and has required of them that obligation. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (Q 2:255). All created beings take refuge in the might of His pillar; and the believer is in His fortress and the hypocrite in His prison. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, every one of them is too preoccupied [to attend] to his father and his son. /fol. 193r./ None intercedes with Him save whom He has approved, by His grace. Who is there that shall intercede with Him save by His leave?(Q 2:255). Creator of the water, and the fire, and the earth, and the air, and He made them for the elements four essences. For the water, and the fire, and the earth, and the air are but as a grain in the water; and the water, and the fire, and the earth, and the air, and the Footstool are but as a star in the heaven; and the water, and the fire, and the earth, and the air, and the Footstool, and the Throne are but as fourteen dirhams; and the whole of it is in His grasp like a mote — by the knowledge of the beginning and of the end. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He wills (Q 2:255). He created the bearers of the Throne, four [in number]; they have risen on high, setting their heads above the rocks of old, resembling in their faces a lion, or an eagle, or a cock, or cattle. The Five Noble Verses with Ten Qāfs Each

The Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Recite these Five Noble Verses at all times." Shaykh Abdulwahid (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Each of these five verses contains ten (10) letters qāf. In the science of letters, the numerical value (abjad — the system that assigns a number to every letter of the alphabet) of the letter qāf is one hundred (100), so the total comes to five thousand (5000). Allah Almighty gave these five verses to the community of Muḥammad and to the Kutub (the Pole, the axis-saint of the age). Judgement in the warding-off of calamities is passed by means of these five verses. Whoever recites these five verses with sincerity (Ikhlāṣ) will not be deprived of the special graces granted to the Kutub. I myself attained the rank of Kutub through these five verses. During the pilgrimage season I met with Khidr (peace be upon him), who advised me to recite these five verses. Because I recited these five verses, I found my [spiritual] stations through the secret power of these verses.

[II 125] Shaykh Yahya Shirwani (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Through these five verses I reached the rank of Kutbu'l-aktāb (the Pole of Poles, the highest of the axis-saints). Those I met would both recite them and carry them written upon their persons. I saw this and asked, "Why do you recite this? What is its property?" They said: "If a person recites these five verses, his enemies and indeed all people become subjugated (musahhar) to him. His enemies can do him no harm." Shaykh Ma'ruf al-Karkhi (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: I met with the Kutub. They would recite these five noble verses every day and carry them upon their persons, and thereby prevailed over their enemies. Whoever harboured evil intent toward them would have all manner of calamities fall upon his own head.
Ibrahim ibn Adham (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: Whoever recites these five verses and carries them written upon himself will find his enemies' tongues bound.
Shaykh Bayezid-i Bistami (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: I recited these five noble verses for seven days and attained the rank of Kutbu'l-aktāb. The Kutub revealed his secret to me.

Shaykh Kirmani (may Allah sanctify his secret) said: In this world there are four thousand (4000) persons empowered to exercise spiritual authority (taṣarruf) — drawn from the Rijalu'l-gayb (the Hidden Men, the unseen order of saints), the Budelā (the Substitutes), the Ewtād (the Pegs), and the Kutub (the Pole). All of them exercise their authority by means of these five verses. Whoever continues to recite them, and writes them out and carries them properly upon himself, becomes a master of spiritual authority both outwardly and inwardly. He exercises his authority in both the higher and the lower worlds, and moreover comes to meet both the Kutub and the Rijalu'l-gayb.

According to a report transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite these five verses both at home and while travelling, and in battle, and thereby gained the upper hand over the unbelievers and the hypocrites. Allah Almighty would aid him and grant him the means to achieve his conquests.

According to a report transmitted from Aisha al-Siddiqa (may Allah be pleased with her), the Pride of Creation (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever writes out these five verses — in which there are fifty qāfs — on a Friday, washes off what he has written with water, and drinks that water, will have placed within himself a thousand cures, established a thousand states of health, set down a thousand mercies, a thousand measures of compassion, a thousand certainties, a thousand strengths, and sent down a hundred thousand lights. Every kind of illness will be drawn out and taken from him, and his sorrow and grief will be lifted.

Shaykh Muhyiddin Ibn al-'Arabi (may Allah sanctify his secret) says: The Noble Qur'an has 6,666 verses. I saw a commentary (tefsir) on the Word of Allah in Egypt; it ran to 660 volumes. In that commentary it was recorded thus: within the Noble Qur'an there are five verses. If a person recites these five verses once a day, or once a week, or even once a month, Allah Almighty grants that person rank both in this world and in the hereafter, and in Paradise He raises him degree upon degree.

[II 126] To overwhelm one's enemies and to repel the envious, if these five noble verses are recited three times, or even just once, in the morning and in the evening, these verses themselves become the very elixir that brings about the effect.
The properties of these noble verses have been explained in the Qur'anic commentaries and in the noble hadiths. It is beneficial to recite them once every morning.

that year. Ibn Qutayba said: A man of the people of Mecca related to me, saying: Hardship befell me, and I complained of that to a man among the righteous. He said to me: Write upon a slip of paper Truly We have granted you a manifest victory (Q 48:1); If you seek a decision, the decision has come to you (Q 8:19); and it may be that God will bring the victory, or a command from Him (Q 5:52); And with Him are the keys of the Unseen; none knows them but He (Q 6:59); Our Lord, decide between us and our people with the truth, for You are the best of deciders (Q 7:89); And had the people of the towns believed and been godfearing, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth (Q 7:96); And when they opened their baggage, they found their goods returned to them (Q 12:65); And they sought a decision, and every obstinate tyrant was brought to nothing (Q 14:15); And even if We opened upon them a gate of the heaven, so that they kept ascending through it (Q 15:14); Truly my people have denied me. So decide between me and them with a [clear] decision, and deliver me and those of the believers who are with me (Q 26:117–118); Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can send it forth after Him; and He is the Mighty, the Wise (Q 35:2); until, when they come to it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: Peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it to abide (Q 39:73); and He rewarded them with a near victory, and abundant spoils that they will take (Q 48:18–19); So We opened the gates of the heaven with water pouring down (Q 54:11); help from God, and a near victory (Q 61:13); and the heaven is opened and becomes gates (Q 78:19); When the help of God comes, and the victory, and you see people entering into the religion of God in throngs — then glorify the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness; truly He is Ever-Relenting (Q 110:1–3). Write them and hang them upon your right upper arm. So I did that, and God opened [the way] for me, and made things easy for me whence I did not reckon.

His words, exalted is He: So you will remember what I say to you; and I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44). This noble verse: whoever engraves it upon a signet-ring and seals with it is dealt with in subtlety in all his states; and if he enters in upon a wrongdoer while he is reciting it, He strikes him deaf and suffices him in his affair, by the might of God, glorified and exalted, and His power. And this is the form of its arrangement.

Some of the scholars — may God be pleased with them — said: whoever desires to attain the most great enrichment (al-ghinā al-akbar) and the most magnificent measure (al-kiffa), let him set His words, exalted is He, Say: O God, Master of all Dominion, You give kingship to whom You will— to His words — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27) upon a plate of gold or of silver, or upon pure parchment, in the first [hour] of the day of Thursday.

And let whoever desires to attain the most great secret /fol. 196r./ and the talismanic treasure fast forty days, in which he eats no animal and nothing that comes out of an animal; and let him break his fast upon what is lawful — and if he can manage the permitted food to which the aspirations of people have not attached themselves, that is better. And let him recite every day, at the rising of the sun, Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā a thousand times; and let him say at the end of that: "O God, make easy for me the secret which You have made easy for many of Your servants; and enrich me by Your bounty, so that I need none besides You." And likewise let him recite the sura after sunset the aforementioned number of times. And let him place the drawn figure in a pure purse on the first day, and with it 40 dirhams; and if he wishes to spend anything, let him recite the sura the number of what he spends from it — [and it does not fail] but that it stands fixed for the length of the days, abiding in its state, unchanged. And it is proper to the masters of [spiritual] states. So understand that, for I have opened the door of the most great enrichment to whoever desires to enter. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And know — may God grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that kingship and sovereignty: Say: O God, Master of all Dominion, You give kingship to whom You will— to His words — without reckoning (Q 3:26–27). And the vizierate and the emirate: And appoint for me a vizier from my family: Hārūn my brother; strengthen by him my back (Q 20:29–31); And We appointed with him his brother Hārūn as a vizier (Q 25:35). Love and obedience: And I cast upon you a love from Me, and that you might be fashioned before My eye (Q 20:39); Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together; but God brought them together. Truly He is Mighty, Wise (Q 8:63); and truly, in the love of wealth, he is vehement (Q 100:8); they love them as they should love God; but those who believe are stronger in love for God (Q 2:165). And as for victory and overcoming: And victory is only from God (Q 3:126); and that God may help you with a mighty help (Q 48:3); Enter upon them by the gate; for when you have entered it, you will be the victors. And upon God rely, if you are believers (Q 5:23). So understand that, for it is not possible to speak more plainly than this. And measure, by what has been understood of the verses, what has not been understood.

And know that whoever perseveres in the recitation of al-Ḍuḥā for forty days, saying every day at the conclusion of his litany of remembrance and his recitation: "O God, O al-Ghanī (the Self-Sufficient), O al-Mughnī (the Enricher), enrich me with a richness after which I shall not fear poverty; and guide me, for I am astray; and teach me, for I am ignorant" — God sends to him one who teaches him wisdom in his sleep or in his waking.

His words, exalted is He: And Muḥammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If then he dies or is slain, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels will not harm God in anything; and God will reward the thankful (Q 3:144). If it is drawn in this form, and upon its sides the name Muḥammad, [and] Isrāfīl and Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl and ʿAzrāʾīl — peace be upon them — and a person carries it, there is with him safety from the evil of jinn and of humankind, and from the evil of the visitants of the night and of the day; and he is preserved and guarded, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And God is the one who grants success to what is right. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see; so understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified and exalted, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 196v./

So understand and ponder. And know that whoever writes Sūrat Muḥammad in a bowl of glass, and effaces the writing with Zamzam water and drinks it, is of high standing among people, his speech given a hearing; and he hears nothing from anyone but that he retains it by heart, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted.

His words, exalted is He: So when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast, and the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with a single crushing — on that day the Event befalls, and the heaven is split apart, for on that day it is frail (Q 69:13–16). This noble verse is written for the making of blood to flow in whatever place you wish. So whoever desires that, let him draw the names upon a plate of lead with the moon in Scorpio, and let him draw in it the name of the one whose bleeding he desires and the name of his mother; and let the writing be with Byzantine cinnabar. Then you bury the operation in a water-channel that flows toward the east; and you are to have placed what you wrote inside a reed, and you wind a red thread about it and tie it to the side of the channel. And beware lest the reed be carried away, for then the one against whom the operation has been performed perishes, and it is you who will be held answerable for it before God, exalted is He. And do not leave him more than seven days, or else the one against whom the operation has been performed perishes. And if you wish to undo it, take out what you wrote, then efface it with water; then write for the one against whom the operation has been performed the Throne Verse, and al-Ikhlāṣ, and the two suras of refuge-seeking, and the Fātiḥa, in a pure vessel, and give them to him to drink: he will be healed, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see; understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, glorified and exalted, wills; and He is the granter of success. /fol. 197r./

His words, exalted is He: It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you: Muslim women, believing, devout, penitent, worshipping, given to fasting — previously married and virgins (Q 66:5). This verse is for the divorcing of women. It is written in a blue bowl with ink and tar, and you draw their names and efface them with fleeing water, and you sprinkle it in the house in which they dwell: they will separate and will not remain in it. And this is the form of what is written.

His words, exalted is He: That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, and so they do not understand. And when you see them, their bodies please you; and if they speak, you listen to their speech — as though they were propped-up timbers. They reckon every cry to be /fol. 197v./ against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. God assail them! How are they turned away!(Q 63:3–4). This verse is for the binding of tongues, and the silencing of an enemy, and the cutting of him off from contention and disputation. It is written upon a plate of iron with Libra in the ascendant and Mars in it, and Scorpio in the first face. And let him who intends contention carry it with him and set himself facing whomever he wishes; for it silences the tongue of his enemy, and he is granted victory. And this is its form.

His words, exalted is He: Our Lord, upon You we rely, and to You we turn, and to You is the homecoming. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us. Our Lord, truly You are the Mighty, the Wise (Q 60:4–5). This verse: when it is drawn upon a signet-ring of iron and someone puts it upon his hand, then God, exalted is He, grants him victory and supports him and makes him mighty, even were he abased; and He teaches him the knowledge of what he did not know; and his provision comes to him in plenty from God; and He is for him a helper and an aider — because in it is the name of reliance, and of might, and of judgement. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path. And this is the form of what is written, and it is as you see.

His words, exalted is He: So I said: Ask forgiveness of your Lord; truly He is All-Forgiving. He will send the heaven upon you in abundant rain, and will supply you with wealth and sons, and will make for you gardens, and will make for you rivers (Q 71:10–12). This verse is for increase in provision and growth in trade and abundance of profit. It is written upon a signet-ring of white silver, and he puts it upon his finger; and he will not know how God, exalted is He, makes things easy for him. And it is among the wondrous matters, for it is a matter that no one is able to describe, on account of the blessings and the abundant good things that are in it, by the help of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of what is written, and it is as you see; understand, and you will be rightly guided.

His words, exalted is He: Truly your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, and its half, and its third — and a party of those who are with you. And God determines the night

— and the day. He knows that you will not be able to keep count of it, so He has relented toward you (Q 73:20). This noble verse is for whoever desires increase in worship and turning back in repentance to God, exalted is He. Whoever desires that, let him take a basin of red copper and draw in it the noble verse on Friday, while the people are at the prayer, and say: God has relented toward So-and-so. And wash it off with pure water, and recite over it a hundred times, and drink it for three nights when you wish to sleep. For God, exalted is He, guides the possessor of that name to righteous work, and draws him near to the acts of worship and of obedience, by the might of God, glorified and exalted is He, and by His power. And this is the form of the awfāq, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is
He, wills. And God, glorified and exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 198v./

His words, exalted is He: When the help of God comes, and the victory, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in throngs — then glorify with the praise of your Lord, and seek His forgiveness; truly He is Ever-Relenting (Q 110:1–3). Whoever writes this sura upon a blue rag on Saturday, in the hour of ʿUṭārid (Mercury), the Moon being auspicious, and casts it upon his head — everyone who disputes with him, he overcomes him, by the help of God, exalted is He. And if it is engraved at the exaltation of the Sun with Mars in opposition, he is granted victory over his enemy, by the help of God, glorified and exalted is He. And whoever carries it is guarded from wounds, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And this is the form of its arrangement, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.

His words, exalted is He: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy (Q 57:27) — to His words, exalted is He — and they became the uppermost (Q 61:14). These verses are for disputation, for litigation, for contention, for the subduing of enemies and adversaries, for triumph over them and for victory over them. So whoever desires that, let him draw these verses upon gazelle parchment with myrtle-water, on Friday, when the people disperse from the prayer; and suffumigate it with aloeswood and ambergris; and place it in a tube of silver; and cast it upon your head. Then litigate with whomever you wish of the enemies, and confront whomever you wish of the governors — you will overcome him, by the help of God, glorified and exalted is He. And this is what you write.

And know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that whoever wishes to confront a ruler, or a vizier, or a judge, or one of the governors, and desires the binding of his tongue and the withholding of his harm from him, even were the matter one of killing: let him write the names whose mention now follows upon gazelle parchment, with musk, saffron, and rose-water; and let him suffumigate them with the sweetest of suffumigations, such as aloeswood, nadd, ambergris, and musk; then let him carry them in the front of his turban. And let the writing be in the hour of the Sun on the day of Sunday; and if it be at the exaltation of the Sun, that is better. And if you are in doubt of that and wish to put it to the test, then hang it upon a ewe brought forward for slaughter, and it will not be slaughtered so long as it has it hung upon it. And if you enter the bath-house with the writing upon you, the bath-house grows cold, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of the talisman and of the noble verses.

Come forward and do not fear; truly you are among those who are secure (Q 28:31). Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people (Q 28:25). Do not fear; truly you are the higher (Q 20:68). Truly, in My presence the messengers do not fear (Q 27:10). Two men of those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favour, said: Enter upon them by the gate; for when you have entered it, you will be the victors. And upon God put your trust, if you are believers (Q 5:23). Come forward, O So-and-so, O son of So-and-so, as the preacher comes forward /fol. 199v./ to the pulpit, and the sultan to the army! I have bound the tongue of whoever disputes with him, and the tongue of every speaker: they shall not speak concerning the bearer of this writing of mine save with good, or else they shall be silent. Deaf, deaf, deaf; dumb, dumb, dumb; blind, blind, blind — so they do not see (Q 36:9). I have made the bearer of this writing of mine victorious and supported over everyone, as God, exalted is He, gave victory to His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — on the day of Badr, and supported him with the names of God; as God supported His prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — with the angels: Gabriel on his right, and Mīkāʾīl on his left, and Isrāfīl behind his back, and the names of God, exalted is He, encompassing him about. Shāhat al-wujūh ("may the faces be disfigured")! And faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting; and he who bears wrongdoing has failed (Q 20:111) — by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". So God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing (Q 2:137). Shāhat al-wujūh, shāhat al-wujūh, shāhat al-wujūh, and faces are humbled before the Living, the Self-Subsisting! Māhat, bāhat, tāhat, ḥat, maḥat, inṭilāḥā, maḥallā, ahlā! Come forward, delivered, victorious, supported, by the One, the Unique, the Singular, the Eternal Refuge, who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal (Q 112:3–4).

And know, O my brother, that this is a wondrous talisman and a strange secret, which the learned have stored up and concealed out of fear, lest it fall into the hand of an ignorant man and he violate chaste women by means of it. So by God, O you who come upon this book: do not perform it save in what is lawful, for you are the one who will be held to account for it on the Day of Resurrection. So when you wish to operate with it, write upon your right palm with sukk, musk, saffron, and rose-water; and let it be suffumigated with a fragrant perfume; and let the writing be on Wednesday, in the first hour; and recite over it the Great Adjuration whose beginning is "In the name of God, the All-Holy, the Undefiled". Then hide your hand inside your sleeve, and open your hand in the face of whomever you wish, until he looks upon the writing. Then go on your way, and do not turn back behind you; for the one sought will follow you wherever you wish. And this is the form of the talisman.

If you see someone complaining of pain of the spleen, write for him this blessed talisman upon a sheet of paper, and place the paper over the spleen, over the shirt. Then take a new spoon and put in it a little ash, and set upon the ash a live coal of fire; then place the spoon over the talisman. For the sufferer in his spleen will feel the fire, as though it had entered his belly. So leave it as long as the sick man can bear, even if it be but half /fol. 200r./ a degree; then lift it away. For the spleen will not remain long before it is cut up and passes out with the stool, and the sufferer recovers, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of the talisman.

If you wish to retain everything you hear and never forget it, then write these letters in a bowl of glass and drink them with pure water for three days; for you will see wonders, from the intensity of understanding. And you recite, when you drink it, His words, exalted is He: And We gave Solomon understanding of it (Q 21:79) — the verse. And this is the form of the talisman, as you see.

If you have an enemy, or he has an evil neighbour, and you wish to remove him from your side, then write this talisman upon an unbaked potsherd or upon a tablet of lead, and let it be buried beneath the threshold of the door of whomever you wish; for he will depart from that place. And by God [I charge] you: do not perform it save for one who deserves it.
If you wish to bind the tongue of someone against you, or the tongues of all people, you write this talisman and place it in the front of the turban — you will see a wonder

And whoever has satanic whispering (waswās) in his soul, or in his ablution, or in his prayer, and desires the removal of that, let him write upon a slip of paper these names and carry them; for he will be in safety from the whisperings. And this is what you write, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And whoever fears for his wealth or his merchandise from a thief or a robber or anything else, let him draw these noble names upon a slip of paper and place it in the money chest, or in the merchandise, or wherever he wishes; for God, glorified and exalted is He, guards it from everything he fears, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And this is its form, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified and exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 201r./

If you are in fear of an enemy, or of one who intends you evil, and you wish to be secure from his evil, then pray two rakʿas after the evening prayer. You recite in the first rakʿa the Fātiḥa and Say: O you unbelievers (Q 109:1), and in the second rakʿa the Fātiḥa and the sura Say: I take refuge with the Lord of the daybreak (Q 113:1). And you say: O Kāfī (Sufficer), suffice me against the evil of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] — and you mention what you wish. Then you write these names and place them in your turban; for God will suffice you against the evil of what you fear and are wary of. And this is the form of what you write, and it is as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided.

His words, exalted is He: Truly We have given you al-Kawthar. So pray to your Lord, and sacrifice. Truly it is he who hates you that is the one cut off (Q 108:1–3). Whoever wishes to bind the urine of someone, let him draw the noble sura in an unlucky hour upon an eggshell, after the name of the person and the name of his mother have been written upon a red or a blue sheet of paper; and let it be buried beside the fire. For the one against whom the operation has been performed will have his urine bound, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. So fear God, and do not leave it more than seven days, or the one against whom the operation has been performed will perish — and you are the one who will be held to account for it on the Day of Resurrection. And this is what you write, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, glorified and exalted is He, wills. And God, glorified and exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. /fol. 201v./
And the suffumigation for that is sal ammoniac (nushādir), cypress-nuts, and pepper.

Fāʾida, for the reconciling of those who hate one another. This talisman is hung upon whomever one wishes, or it is placed beneath the pillow upon which the two of them sleep; for they will be reconciled, even were the sword fallen between them. You write it on Friday, while the preacher is upon the pulpit; and it is suffumigated with aloeswood, mastic, blue bdellium (muql azraq), and calamus (qaṣab al-dharīra). And this is what you write, as you see. So understand that, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Take charge, O servant-spirits (khuddām) of these names, of the casting of love and affection between So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so daughter of So-and-so [f.], by the right of these names that lies upon you!

I ask You, O Reconciler of hearts: bring into concord the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] and So-and-so daughter of So-and-so [f.], by the right of Him who said to the heavens and the earth Come, willingly or unwillingly! They said: We come willingly (Q 41:11); And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you might be fashioned before My eye (Q 20:39). Take charge, O ʿUnqūd, of the casting of love and affection between the hearts of those who hate one another, [turning them] to the love of these names, by the right of Ayūsh Ayūsh Badūḥ Ḥab Wad Wadḥab! O Badūḥ, cast love after enmity, and concord in place of separation, by the right of Ahyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt Āl Shaddāy — and truly it is a mighty oath, if you but knew (Q 56:76). Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour!

I say: and whoever places this talisman in the wall of a wrongdoer and invokes against him with what will be set out below — the wall collapses, and the master of the house perishes, and his household is scattered. So fear God, exalted is He, and do not perform it save against a wrongdoer who harms people with his hand and his tongue; and beware of performing it for one who does not deserve it, for you are the one who will be held to account for it on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever pardons and sets things right, his reward rests with God (Q 42:40). And this is what you write, and it is as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

Take charge, O Sarīʿ, and O Barīq, and O Khandas, and O Lāzib al-Aḥmar, of the removal of So-and-so from this place, by the right of these names! And do what you are commanded, by the might of Karyārūsh ʿAbkuwālkayārūsh Mahlalkayūsh Halkayūhalīs Ṣārash Ṣalṣārash — before whose dread the angels tremble, and to whose magnificence the creatures render obedience. Ṭūr hayā hayā hafṭiyā haliyā shaliyā ʿaliyā hūrash aṭūr kayākarūr hayā kūrāthā! The fugitive was shaken, the earth was made to quake, the hearts reeled, and [all] was turned about unto obedience to Him. Answer, O Aḥmar; and you, O Wafālak, and your partisans, and the people of your obedience — by the light of Shaghyūr Fayār Qayār Samūhal Damār ʿAyṭūr BahārhārakaṭSalīhūr Hashkūr Hārlūr Hafṭūr Hayṭūr Hūr! Speed! Haste! This very hour! So fear God, exalted is He. And you sprinkle it — for it lays waste villages and lands and cities, and it serves for the parting of those who are not in the obedience of God, exalted is He. You write it upon an unbaked potsherd on the day of Mars and in its hour; and you suffumigate the potsherd with peach leaves, vine leaves, and male frankincense; and you dissolve the potsherd in wine vinegar with a little tar and hot oil — inside the threshold of whomever you wish. And the conjuration (ʿazīma) is what we have mentioned. So whoever pardons /fol. 202v./ and sets things right, his reward rests with God (Q 42:40).

If you wish to shoot with the bow and not to miss in your shooting, then write these names upon gazelle parchment with ink, saffron, hair, and the gall of a hoopoe; and let the pen be from the feather of a vulture or an eagle; and draw them in an auspicious hour, the Moon being in an airy sign; and the suffumigation is male frankincense. And this is what you write. And know, O my brother — may God grant us and you success — that this is a wondrous talisman.

And know, O my brother — may God grant us and you success in obedience to Him — that this noble letter, namely the letter shīn, is Arabic and Syriac and Fīṭūshī; and it is a fiery letter, and its natures are hot and dry in the third degree; and its occult properties are for the halting of ships from journeying upon the sea, and the halting of the traveller upon the land, and the halting of others than these. So write upon a tablet of lead in an unlucky hour, and let it be buried in the road — you will see a wonder. And the suffumigation is a sparrow's tongue and a bat's head. And this is what you write, as you see.
If you wish that a human being love you, and that your love be established in his heart until death, and that the two of you never part, then [write] these names upon seven white sheets of paper

For the bringing back of a runaway slave, even were he in chains and fetters. This wafq, whose exposition follows, is written; then you take a beetle — if it be for a male, then a male, and if it be for a female, then a female — and you tie it in the middle of the circle with a fine thread, and you drive a nail into the pole of the circle and tie the beetle to it. Then, every time the beetle turns about seeking release, just so does the runaway turn about, and he returns to the place in which this talisman is, even were he in chains: God, exalted is He, brings about for him the means of return, through the blessing of this. And when I looked at them at that hour, I remembered the words of the shaykh, and I invoked God's mercy upon him, and I said within myself: These are the breaths of the men who are truthful with God, exalted is He. And he had been saying, in that state: After my death you will come to them without asking and without weariness. So I contemplated them with a satisfying contemplation, and behold, there was written in it, saying: Let him know into whose hand these names have fallen that he must guard them /fol. 206v./ from those unworthy of them; for they came down with Adam — peace be upon him — and he set himself to look upon them every day and to say: "Glory be to You! [I 118] The Secret of the Awfāq The numbers and letters placed inside a figure formed, within a murabba (square), by straight lines that intersect lengthwise and crosswise are called a WAFQ.

Every wafq consists of width, length, and diagonals. The sections formed by straight lines running from top to bottom are called DIL (edge, or column); the sections formed by straight lines running from right to left are called SATIR (row). The cells running from the upper right corner to the lower left corner, and from the upper left corner to the lower right corner, are called KUTUR (diagonal).

Numbers are written into the wafq's cells as numbers, and letters as letters. A number or letter written into one cell of the wafq is never used again in another cell. The sum of a row must equal the sum of an edge.

The first cell of every wafq is the miftah (the key, or starting cell), and its final cell is the mughlak (the closing, or last cell). Every wafq has eight (8) distinct stations. The eight rules governing awfāq are as follows:
1. Miftah: The "key," or starting point; it is the wafq's first cell.
2. Mughlak: The wafq's very last cell.
3. Adil: The sum of the miftah and mughlak cells.
4. Wafq: The total of one edge or row of the wafq.
5. Mesahe: The sum of all the dil (edge cells).
6. Zabit: The sum of the wafq-total and the mesahe.

8. Asil: The product of the ghaye and the mughlak. In every wafq, the asil governs the ghaye, and the ghaye of every wafq in turn governs all of its other cells. Every wafq belongs to one of the seven planets.
The threefold wafq belongs to the planet Saturn (Zuḥal).
The fourfold wafq belongs to Jupiter (Mushtarī).
The fivefold wafq belongs to Mars (Mirrīkh).
The sixfold wafq belongs to the Sun (Shams).
The sevenfold wafq belongs to Venus (Zuhra).
The eightfold wafq belongs to Mercury (ʿUṭārid).
The ninefold wafq belongs to the Moon (Qamar).
The tenfold wafq belongs to the sphere of the Zodiac (the celestial sphere that revolves upon itself).

[I 119] The Threefold Wafq Every wafq consists of width, length, and diagonals. This is the origin and foundation of the threefold wafq, the threefold wafq that belongs to Earth:
In the threefold wafq, half of ten — the sum of the miftah (starting) and mughlak (final) cells, that is, 1 + 9 = 10 — is the vasat (middle) cell.
Since the vasat of the threefold wafq is five (5) and its mughlak is nine (9), multiplying five by nine gives 45, which is the mesahe (the sum of the edge cells) of the threefold wafq.
As with every wafq, the threefold wafq also has eight distinct stations; these eight rules are as follows.
1. Miftah: The key or starting point, being the threefold wafq's first cell.
2. Mughlak: The final cell, the threefold wafq's ninth cell.
3. Adil: The sum of the miftah and mughlak cells: 9 + 1 = 10.
4. Wafq: The total of one edge or row. In the threefold wafq the sum of an edge or row is fifteen (15).
5. Mesahe: The sum of all the edges or rows found in a wafq. The mesahe of the threefold wafq is 15 × 3 = 45.

6. Zabit: The sum of one edge and the whole wafq-total. In the threefold wafq the zabit is 7. Ghaye: Twice the zabit. In the threefold wafq, 60 + 60 = 8. Asil: The number obtained by multiplying the ghaye by the mughlak, or pole, number: 120 × 9 = 180. In every wafq the asil governs the ghaye, and the ghaye of every wafq in turn governs all its other cells. The threefold wafq has forms arranged according to the four elements (ʿanāṣir-i arbaʿa). If the working (amal) you are to perform pertains to fire, you arrange the fire-element form of the threefold wafq; if it pertains to earth, the earth-element form; if to air, the air-element form; and if the working you are to perform pertains to water, the water-element

In the threefold wafq, the first cell is one (1). This is called the miftah (the key, or starting point).
In the threefold wafq, the last cell is nine (9). This is called the mughlak (the pole, or final cell).

Let us now explain how the celestial (Ulwi) and terrestrial (Arḍi) spirits of the threefold wafq are derived. 5. Hujjetul Islam ("the Proof of Islam") Imam Ghazālī, may Allah be pleased with him, has given the following account of obtaining khuddām (spirit-servants) by means of the threefold wafq.

If a person wishes to obtain khuddām by performing riyada (ascetic spiritual discipline) with the threefold wafq, he must first obtain permission (icazet) from his shaykh. If he proceeds without it, not only will he see no benefit, but great harm will come to him.

Beginning on a Wednesday, keep an ascetic fast for 17 days. On the night of the seventeenth day, which is a Friday, after the night prayer, enter into khalwa (spiritual retreat) and fumigate the place where you are with lubān (frankincense). While in retreat for seven nights and days, recite the following noble awrād (litany) one thousand and one times, each night and day:
O Thou whose deeds are praiseworthy, I have wronged myself in ( respect of all that is due to Him; by His grace I have resolved.)

Continue this practice for seven nights and days in this manner. On Friday night two spirits (rūḥānī) will come to you in a dream. Ask these spirits their names. They will tell you their names. You then write the name of the first spirit to speak in the final cell of the threefold wafq, and the name of the second spirit beneath it, in the middle cell.

This triple wafq has letters, natures, angels, verses, and conditions that must be observed. The letters of the triple wafq are nine (9)

in number. Four of the letters — Dal, Wāw, Ha — are for good; these four letters are called "el-Muzdewijāt" (the Paired Ones). Five of the letters — Alif, Jīm, He, Ze, Ṭāʾ — are for evil; these letters are called "el-Mufredāt" (the Singular Ones).

The triple wafq has different forms according to the four elements (ʿanāṣir-i arbaʿa). When numbers or letters are placed into the cells of the wafq, they must be placed according to the relevant element. Here are the forms of the triple wafq according to the four elements:
Element of Fire Element of Earth Element of Air Element of Water Each letter of the triple wafq has an angel. The angels of the letters of the triple wafq are as follows:
The angel of the letter Alif is Āyehin.
The angel of the letter Be is Bikitriyālin.
The angel of the letter Jīm is Jelīshin.
The angel of the letter Dal is Demyālin.
The angel of the letter He is Hetatūshin.
The angel of the letter Wāw is Wehīmin.
The angel of the letter Ze is Zenkatā.
The angel of the letter Ha is Hadāyehin.
[I 155] The angel of the letter Ṭāʾ is Tifyālin.
The triple wafq has nine (9) Qur'anic verses (Āyāt al-Karima).

Without these nine verses, a working (amal) performed with it is not valid. Whenever you wish to carry out any working, after fulfilling its elemental conditions and requirements, at the moment you begin placing the letters or numbers into the cells of the wafq, you recite the name and verse belonging to that letter of the wafq.
Each of the letters of the wafq is bound to a verse and a name. You recite these names and verses as you place the letters or numbers into the wafq. The nine verses of the triple wafq are these.
When placing the letter Alif into the wafq, recite its name and verse once (1):
This is the Throne Verse (Āyāt al-Kursī): "Allah — there is no deity .except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence

Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except what He wills. His seat extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.") Be harfini wafq ikinci hanesine koyarken Ism wa Āya Kerimeyi iki (2) defa oku:
When placing the letter Be into the second cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse twice (2):
Bikitriyālin. Bedī'us samāwāti wa-l- arḍi wa izā kadā emran fe innemā yekūle lahu kun fe yekūn.
(Bikitriyālin. "The Originator of the heavens and the earth; and when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.")
[I 156] When placing the letter Jīm into the third cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse three (3) times:
(Jelishin. "Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished — falsehood is ever bound to vanish.")
When placing the letter Dal into the fourth cell of the wafq, you recite its name and verse four (4) times:
fragments of the verse: "...and their) greeting therein is peace, and the last of their call is: praise be to (".Allah, Lord of the worlds
When writing the letter He into the fifth cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse five (5) times:
(Hetatūshin. "He is Allah, besides whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.")
When writing the letter Wāw into the sixth cell, you recite its name and verse six (6) times:
(Wehīmin. "And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice of their own. Glory be to Allah, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.")
When writing the letter Ze into the seventh cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse seven (7) times:
[ I 157] wa-l- kanātīril mukantarati minez zehebi wa-l-
