When writing the letter Ha into the eighth cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse eight (8) times:
the verse: "...to those before you — Allah, the Almighty, the (".Wise
When writing the letter Ṭāʾ into the ninth cell of the wafq, recite its name and verse nine (9) times:
a reminder for those who fear...") Him; a revelation from Him who created the earth and the high (".heavens; the Most Merciful, who rose over the Throne
The letters of the triple wafq are also associated with certain days and planets. The days and nights to which the letters of the triple wafq belong are as follows.
[I 158] The day of the letters Alif and Ha is Sunday, whose planet is Shams (the Sun).
The day of the letters Be and Ṭāʾ is Monday, whose planet is Qamar (the Moon).
The day of the letter Jīm is Tuesday, whose planet is Mirrīkh (Mars).
The day of the letter Dal is Wednesday, whose planet is ʿUṭārid (Mercury).
The day of the letter He is Thursday, whose planet is Mushtarī (Jupiter).
The day of the letter Wāw is Friday, whose planet is Zuhra (Venus).
The day of the letter Ze is Saturday, whose planet is Zuḥal (Saturn).
The letter Ha is the head, and the letter Ṭāʾ is the feet.
3x3 wafq [wafq] written in abjad letters — nine cells, no headings or labels. [I 158]
The same 3x3 wafq written in numerals, each abjad letter replaced by its numeric value — no headings or labels. [I 158]

Some scholars have written the triple wafq either with letters or with numerals. The two forms of the triple wafq of earthly nature — one written with letters, the other of fiery nature written with numerals — are these:
The earth-element form written with letters; the fire-element form written with numerals.
3x3 wafq in abjad letters, the mirror arrangement of the preceding square — no headings or labels. [I 158]
The mirrored 3x3 wafq written in numerals — no headings or labels. [I 158]
The two forms of the triple wafq of watery nature — one written with letters, the other of airy nature written with numerals — are these:
The water-element form written with letters; the air-element form written with numerals.
Other scholars, however, wrote out the triple wafq and also entered the governing angel of each letter into the hane (cells) of the wafq's grid. This is the strongest, best, and most fitting method.
3x3 letter wafq with servant spirits — each of the nine cells carries an abjad letter above and the name of that letter's governing spirit [muwakkil] below; no headings. [I 159]
[I 159] Here is its form: (the fire-element wafq).

Sheyhulislam, the Proof of Islam, Imam al-Ghazali, may God be pleased with him, said: this exalted wafq and noble khātam (seal) must be arranged in full together with its verses. Four great angels must be appointed to the four sides of the wafq. In the service of these four great angels stand four assisting angels, namely: Semkeyāīl, Newāīl, Sharnetyāīl, and Meytatarūn.

When writing the wafq: write the word Kawluhu ("His word"), stretching it from right to left so that it closes off the edge of the wafq, and above it write the name Jebrāīl (Gabriel). Write the word Elhak ("the Truth"), stretching it downward along the left side of the wafq, and above it write the name Mīkāīl (Michael). Write the word Welehu ("and His is..."), stretching it along the bottom of the wafq from right to left, and above it write the name Isrāfīl (Isrāfīl). Write the word Elmulku ("the Dominion"), stretching it upward from the bottom along the right side of the wafq, and above it write the name Azrāīl (ʿAzrāʾīl). (Together, read around the wafq, these four words form the phrase: "Wa kawluhu'l-hakku wa lahu'l-mulku" — "And His word is the truth, and His is the dominion.")
Write the name Sharnetyāīl between Jebrāīl and Mīkāīl, and the name Meytatarūn between Isrāfīl and Azrāīl. In this manner you arrange the wafq.
After this, write on the right and left of the wafq the verses that form the dawa (summoning invocation) of this blessed seal — the disjointed letters Kāf-He-Ye-ʿAyn-Sat and Ha-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sin-Qāf.
This, then, is the complete triple wafq, fully arranged with its letters, its numerals, its four great angels, its avan melekleri (auxiliary angels), and the angels of its letters.

3x3 letter wafq with its spirit-names, set within a bordered frame naming the four archangels — Gabriel [Jibrīl] along the top; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] at the left; Isrāfīl at the right; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] at the lower left; the remaining marginal words are illegible. [I 160]

[I 160] This exalted seal, in its entirety, is like a cutting sword, a deadly poison, a healing remedy, a rising sun, a shining light, a falling star, and a piercing arrow. Allah Most High has said in the Noble Qur'an:
Fear Allah Most High, and do not use this seal for evil deeds, for you will bear the sin of it.
Abu Ali ad-Daqqaq said: within this seal there are many hidden secrets. This is the secret about which Allah Most High has said in His noble verse:

(A sign for you will be that the Ark will come to you, in which there is a calm reassurance from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind, the angels carrying it.)

[I 161] The Ark, the tranquility, and the knowledge mentioned in this noble verse all point to this seal. They relate to the secrets contained within the phrase "Tahmiluhul melāiketu" ("the angels carrying it") that continues the verse, for these secrets are sometimes called angels, sometimes spirits (rūḥāniyya), and sometimes powers and natures. These same meanings lie hidden within the secrets Allah Most High taught to King Talut (Saul), for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has said:
And We increased him) [.(abundantly in knowledge and in body [strength
The meaning of "knowledge" here is the knowledge of the secrets of the seal.

Imam al-Ghazali, may God be pleased with him, said: I gathered the letters of this triple wafq from the following noble verses. These verses contain ten (10) letters. Since the letter ʿAyn occurs twice, I removed one of them, leaving nine (9) letters. Some of these letters remained unchanged in their own form, while others were transformed and used according to the cells of the wafq.

The letter Ye has the numerical value of ten (10). After subtracting nine (9) once, one (1) remains, corresponding to the letter Alif. That is, the letter Alif derives from the letter Ye. In the triple wafq, the letter Alif is placed in the first cell.

The letter Kāf has the numerical value of twenty (20). After subtracting nine (9) twice, two (2) remains, corresponding to the letter Be. That is, the letter Be derives from the letter Kāf. In the triple wafq, the letter Be is placed in the second cell.

The letter Qāf has the numerical value of one hundred (100). According to the ordering of abjad (the numerical alphabet), it is third in the sequence of the hundreds. Accordingly, the letter Jīm derives from the letter Qāf. Its place in the triple wafq is the third cell.

[I 162] The letter Mīm has the numerical value of forty (40). After subtracting nine (9) four times, four (4) remains, corresponding to the letter Dal. That is, the letter Dal derives from the letter Mīm. In the triple wafq, the letter Dal is placed in the fourth cell.
The letter He remains as it is; its original form is not altered, and in the triple wafq the letter He is placed in the fifth cell.

The letter Sin has the numerical value of sixty (60). After subtracting nine (9) six times, six (6) remains, corresponding to the letter Wāw. That is, the letter Wāw derives from the letter Sin. Its place in the triple wafq is the sixth cell.

The letter ʿAyn has the numerical value of seventy (70). After subtracting nine (9) seven times, seven remains, corresponding to the letter Ze. That is, the letter Ze derives from the letter ʿAyn. In the triple wafq, the letter Ze is placed in the seventh cell.
The letter Ha remains unchanged. Its numerical value is eight (8), and its place in the triple wafq is the eighth cell.

The letter Sat has the numerical value of ninety (90). After subtracting nine (9) nine times, nine (9) remains, corresponding to the letter Ṭāʾ. That is, the letter Ṭāʾ derives from the letter Sat. In the triple wafq, the letter Ṭāʾ is placed in the ninth cell.

Imam al-Ghazali, may God be pleased with him, said: within the seal there are five noble verses that hold its secret; its tasrifat (transformations) and its amal (ritual workings) all lie within this framework. These five verses begin with the initial letters Kāf-He-Ye-ʿAyn-Sat and end with the initial letters Ha-Mīm-ʿAyn-Sin-Qāf. They are as follows — the Āyāti Hamse, the Five Verses:
(These noble verses are: Surah al-Kahf, verse 45; Surah al-Hashr, verse 21; and Surah Sad, verses 1 and 2.)

(Sense: these fragments touch on the fleeting nature of worldly life — like plants scattered to stubble by the wind — God's knowledge of the unseen and the seen, the terror of the Day when hearts leap to the throat, the soul knowing what it has sent forth, an oath by the receding stars and the breaking dawn, and the Qur'an itself as a reminder against the arrogance of those who disbelieve.)

These five noble verses, the Āyāti Hamse, are the dawa (summoning formula), the working framework, and the secret of the seal, for everything that follows draws on all their properties. A working performed over the wafq — whether Kamālī (Complete), Mufradāt (Single), or Muzdawijāt (Paired) — is not complete unless these five verses are recited 45, 25, or 20 times respectively. Over the Kamālī wafq you recite the five verses forty-five (45) times; over the Mufradāt wafq, twenty-five (25) times; and over the Muzdawijāt wafq, twenty (20) times.

Whenever you wish to perform a working, after writing this triple wafq together with its conditions, its angels, and its verses, you write around the wafq the verse relevant to the working you intend to perform. After you have written the wafq out in full and prepared it, [I 164] for beneficial workings you take a long branch from a sweet date palm, pomegranate, or other sweet fruit-bearing tree, and for harmful workings a long branch from a sour pomegranate or other sour fruit-bearing tree, and hang the wafq from the branch with silk thread (ibrishim). Beneath the branch, place a bowl holding a burning ember, and cast onto the fire an incense that is pleasant-smelling — such as agarwood, frankincense, or ambergris — for beneficial workings, or foul-smelling bakhūr (incense) — such as onion and garlic skins and asafoetida — for harmful workings. While the incense is smoking, recite the Five Verses, the summoning formula of this wafq, forty-five (45) times. After reciting, the wafq is used according to its element (one of the four elements), or else simply carried on the person.

3x3 letter wafq in reversed order, framed by directional arrows and archangel names — Gabriel [Jibrīl] along the top; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] at the left; Isrāfīl at the right; the further corner inscriptions are illegible. [I 164]

You must perform the triple wafq on a suitable day and hour. If the working is for love, you perform it on the first Friday of the Arabic lunar month, at sunrise, in the first hour — the hour of Zuhra (Venus) — or in the eighth hour, likewise the hour of Zuhra. If the working you intend is for healing, to stop a child's crying, for a headache, or some other such simple matter, it is enough to recite the Āyāti Hamse three (3) or nine (9) times; in that case you need not write out the wafq's full tevkilat (assignment of governing spirits), its verses, its avan angels, and its cell-angels in their entirety.
It suffices to write the wafq in the following form:
After writing the wafq in this manner, you write around it verses of healing, verses of alleviation, or similar verses, and recite the Five Noble Verses over the wafq three or nine times.
The conditions of this working are as follows:

1. Whenever you are about to perform a working, withdraw into a secluded room and shut its door. Let no one enter the place where you are, disturb you, or see what you are doing. Perform it with full conviction, resolve, and secrecy.
[I 165] 2. Be in a state of complete ritual purity, having performed the ablution, with your body, your clothing, and the place you are in clean, and face the direction of the qibla.

3. Before beginning the working, burn incense. For beneficial workings burn sweet-smelling incenses such as agarwood, frankincense, and ambergris; for harmful workings burn foul-smelling incenses such as onion and garlic skins, asafoetida, and sulfur.
4. For beneficial workings, write with an ink mixed from musk, saffron, and rosewater; for harmful workings, write with a mixture of myrrh, aloes, indigo, and black ink.

5. Before beginning the working, you perform the sarfi imar (the rite of dismissing the jinn dwelling in the place). If you do not perform this dismissal, they will spoil your working. To send away the jinn present in the place, recite the following sarf (dismissal formula) three or seven times:

When the earth is shaken with its (,earthquake, and the earth throws out its burdens, and man says What is wrong with it?" — that Day it will report its news, because" your Lord has inspired it. That Day mankind will proceed in scattered groups. I have parted you and scattered you, O rulers of this place and this house — depart and withdraw from me, and do !not hinder my working, by the right of Allah, the One, the Subduer And indeed it is a mighty oath, if only you knew. Elwāhan — at ,once, twice; el-acele — in haste, twice; es-sā'ate — this very hour twice.)

[I 166] After this, having recited the Qasam (oath/conjuration) proper to that day the number of times assigned to it, you write the letter, the tilsam (talisman), and the celestial (ulwi) and terrestrial (sufli) angel of that day, together with its verse. The incense must be smoking throughout. Beneath these, after writing out the triple wafq in full with its verses, its four great angels, its avan angels, and its cell-angels, you recite the Āyāti Hamse three or nine times — or, if the working is important, forty-five times. Once you have completed the working, you use the wafq according to its nature, or carry it on your person, and what you desire will come to pass.

The cetvel (table) below shows, for each day, its celestial and terrestrial angels, its arshi meleghi (throne angel), the letter of the day, its divine names, its talisman, and its verse. Whenever you wish to perform a working, these must without fail be recited and written in every working. Here is the form of the table:

Table of the seven days and their correspondences, columns running right to left: Sunday [Sunday]; Monday [Monday]; Tuesday [Tuesday]; Wednesday [Wednesday]; Thursday [Thursday]; Friday [Friday]; Saturday [Saturday]. Rows are unlabelled: sigil of the day; abjad letter; divine name; presiding angel; king of the jinn; further spirit names; the day's verse of Surat al-Fātiḥa; and its operative name. [I 166]

When we wish to perform a working, after reciting the Qasam proper to that day, we write the letters, angels, verses, and divine names on a sheet of paper: on Sunday one (1) time, Monday two (2), Tuesday three (3), Wednesday four (4), Thursday six (5), Friday six (6), and on Saturday seven (7) times. Beneath these you write out in full the triple wafq with its verses, its four great angels, its avan angels, its cell-angels, the letters or numerals of the wafq, and its element and conditions — [I 167] and while doing so, your incense must be smoking. Afterward, you use the wafq according to its nature, or carry it upon yourself. If you fully observe these conditions, your working will come to pass by the permission of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

To make this better understood, let us give a clear example. Suppose our purpose is mahabba (love), and the element of our maṭlūb (the object of the working) is fire. On Friday, in the first hour — the hour of Zuhra — sit facing the qibla, and after reciting the sarfi imar three (3) or seven (7) times, recite the Qasam proper to Friday six (6) times. Then, on a sheet of paper, write the letter of Friday, Khāʾ, six (6) times; its divine name, the noble name Habir, six (6) times; its talisman six (6) times; its celestial angel, Anyail, six (6) times; its terrestrial angel, Ebyad, six (6) times; its throne angel, Shetsah, six (6) times; the verse of Friday, Siratellezine en'amte aleyhim ("the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor"), six (6) times; and the name belonging to the Tehatil group, Cehhattil, six (6) times, in the following order:

Ha Ha Ha Ha Ha Ha Habir Habir Habir Habir Habir Habir (Friday [I 168] ...day's talisman) Anyaīl Anyaīl Anyaīl Anyaīl Anyaīl Anyaīl Shetsah Shetsah Shetsah Shetsah Shetsah Shetsah Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim Sirātellezīne enamte aleyhim. Cehhattil Cehhattil Cehhattil Cehhattil Cehhattil Cehhattil.

After drawing the threefold wafq beneath what you have written, fill in its cells with the letters or numbers according to their element, and as you write, recite each letter's governing angel and its associated verse (Āyāt al-Karima) as many times as that letter's numerical value.

Then write the four great angels on the four sides of the wafq, and the auxiliary spirits (a'wān) at its four corners. On the right side of the wafq write the verse Kāf Hā Yā 'Ayn Sād, and on the left the verse Hā Mīm 'Ayn Sīn Kāf — these being among the mysterious disjointed letters that open certain surahs of the Qur'an. After that, write around the wafq the following verse concerning love:
Merciful, the Compassionate. And I cast upon you love from Me.) Write the angels belonging to the wafq's cells, and those set around it, in the following order:

3×3 wafq — each cell pairs an abjad letter with its numeral and the name of its servant spirit; the four archangels ring the square: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above, Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left, ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right, Isrāfīl below, each under a Quranic word or letter-group; further spirit names run diagonally at the corners. [I 168]

Once you have prepared the wafq in this way, hang it with silk thread from a branch of sweet pomegranate wood, burn incense (bakhūr) beneath it, and recite the Five Verses (Āyāt-i Hamse) forty-five times.

[I 169] Then bury the wafq beneath, or near, a burning fire. Or, if instead you carry the wafq on your person, the person who is your maṭlūb (the object of the working) will come to love you deeply and be unable to bear being apart from you. The oaths (Qasam) for the days of the week are as follows — each follows the same pattern, invoking the day's fortunate celestial body (kevkeb), its ascendant sign (tāli'), the governing angel-king (melikul muwekkel) enthroned under a given name, and the angel who commands him, together with the corresponding verse of the Fātiḥa, the day's letter, and its talismanic word:
:Oath (Qasam) for any given day, recite the following verse once

Imam Ghazali (r.a.) took his commentary on this threefold wafq from the work called Ilm-i Jafr (the science of jafr, a system of letter-based divination) by Hazrat Ali (k.r.v.), and wrote a book titled Essirril Masun wa-l- Cevherul Meknun (The Protected Secret and the Concealed Jewel), in which he set out the commentary on the wafq and explained its occult properties (khawāṣṣ).

This threefold wafq is used for workings such as: overpowering an enemy, afflicting tyrants with illness, removing oppressive rulers from their posts, freeing someone from prison, taslīt (unleashing an affliction upon another), binding the tongue, kadā-i hājet (having a need fulfilled), healing the sick, undoing sorcery, releasing one who has been bound by magic, stirring excitement, jalb (drawing someone or something toward oneself), inducing love, and having one's request granted in the presence of the great. For the fulfillment of anything you desire, it shines like a light. Allah the Exalted has said in the Noble Qur'an:
We have not left anything) .(out of the Book

[I 175] Only sincere servants who fear Allah (c.c.) possess these secrets. For this reason one must fear Allah as He truly deserves to be feared, and must hold to riyāzat (ascetic self-discipline). One should not even entertain the thought of wronging another person unjustly.

The kamālī wafq (the complete square) is used for workings both beneficial and harmful. The mufradāt wafq (the square of single letters) is generally used for harmful and injurious workings. The muzdawijāt wafq (the square of paired letters) is used for all workings of happiness and good.
Plain 3×3 wafq, its nine cells filled with abjad letters alone (the standard budūh square); no headings or labels. [I 175]

This threefold wafq has a distinct property of its own: the actual numbers or letters are placed into its cells according to their element. Unlike the other threefold square, the abjad (numerical) value of the Names and verses is not calculated and placed into it.
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 175
The kamālī wafq (the whole of the wafq) is the complete form of the threefold square, comprising the cells (Alif, Be, Jīm, Dal, He, Wāw, Ze, Ha, Ṭāʾ).
This is the form of the kamālī wafq's natural and earth element:
The Glorious Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ) of the Kamālī Wafq
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 175
14. To draw customers: Write the Kemal wafq's earth element on a Monday, in the hour of the Moon, and around the wafq these noble verses. The verses to be written are these:
And proclaim the Pilgrimage among the (,people: they will come to you on foot and on every lean mount from every distant mountain road, that they may witness benefits for themselves.)

After writing it, fumigate it with a sweet-smelling incense and recite the Five Āya forty-five times, and, forty-five times, the verses you have written around the wafq. Then, if you hang what you have written in a place of business, customers will be drawn to that place of business. More customers than expected will come to the shop.
15. For abundance: Write the Kemal wafq's earth element on a Monday, in the first hour, which is the hour of the Moon, and around the wafq this noble verse:
The likeness of (those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain that sprouts seven ears, a hundred grains in every ear; and God multiplies it further for whom He wills.)

[I 190] After writing it, fumigate it with fresh oud and benzoin (cavi), and recite the Five Āya forty-five times and the Sura al-Ikhlāṣforty-seven times. Then take seven (7) grains of any kind of grain (hububat), and recite the Throne Verse (Āyāt al-Kursī) together with the verse you wrote around the wafq seven (7) times over all of them. Put the grains you have recited over inside the wafq you have written, wrap them together in a cloth, and if you place this among your provisions — in a pantry or storeroom, for instance — you will see, by God's leave, glory be to Him, and by the secret power of the wafq, abundance come down upon that place.

16. For a wish: Write the Kemal wafq's natural and earth element on a piece of paper on a Monday, in the first hour, which is the hour of the Moon, and recite the Five Āya forty-five times over the wafq while burning incense. After reciting, set it facing the spot where you make your prostration. Having kept to ascetic discipline (riyada), fast for three days, and on the morning of the third day, after the dawn prayer, write the letters of the names as disjointed letters (ḥurūf-u muqaṭṭaʿ'a — the isolated letters that open certain Quranic suras) with musk, saffron, rosewater, and rainwater — with your right hand onto your left palm, and with your left hand onto your right palm. 1. Miftah (the Key): the key, or starting point — the wafq's first cell.
2. Mughlak (the Closure): the last cell — the sixteenth cell of the fourfold wafq.
3. Adil (the Balance): the sum of the Miftah and Mughlak cells. 1+16=17.
4. Wafq: this term denotes the total of a single diagonal or row. In the fourfold wafq, the sum of one diagonal or row is 34.
5. Mesahe (the Measure): the combined total of all the diagonals or rows in a wafq. The mesahe of the fourfold wafq is 34x34=136.
6. Zabit (the Sum): the total of the Wafq and the Mesahe — that is, one row plus the whole wafq. In the fourfold wafq, the Zabit is 34+34=170.
7. Ghaye (the Limit): twice the Zabit. In the fourfold wafq, the Ghaye is 170+170=340.

8. Asil (the Root): the number obtained by multiplying the Ghaye by the Mughlak, or by the number of cells. In the fourfold wafq this is 340x16=5440. In every wafq, the Asil governs the Ghaye, and the Ghaye of each wafq in turn governs its other cells. The fourfold wafq has forms arranged according to the four elements (anāsir). If the working (amal) you are to perform pertains to fire, you arrange the fourfold wafq's fire-element form; if it pertains to earth, the earth-element form; if to air, the air-element form; and if to water, the water-element form.

Fire-element form of the four-by-four wafq [atesh unsuru shekli] — an unlabelled 4×4 wafq of the numbers 1–16, cells counted from the top right; the natural and basic arrangement from which the other three elemental forms are derived. [I 244]
Earth-element form of the four-by-four wafq [earth unsuru shekli] — unlabelled 4×4 wafq of 1–16, the fire form turned through 180°. [I 244]
Air-element form of the four-by-four wafq [air unsuru shekli] — unlabelled 4×4 wafq of 1–16, the fire form mirrored left to right. [I 244]
Water-element form of the four-by-four wafq [water unsuru shekli] — unlabelled 4×4 wafq of 1–16, the fire form mirrored top to bottom. [I 244]
[I 244] The most commonly used form of the fourfold wafq is the fire-element form, for fire is the origin and foundation of the fourfold wafq.

The First Rule of the Fourfold Wafq
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 244

Subtract thirty (30) from the number to be worked into the wafq, and divide the remainder by four (4). Write the quotient in the first cell, then proceed to the last cell, adding one (1) each time, to complete the fourfold wafq.

If the division leaves a remainder of three (3), add one (1) extra to the fifth cell; if the remainder is two (2), add one (1) extra to the ninth cell; if the remainder is one (1), add one (1) extra to the thirteenth cell — and in this way the fourfold wafq is completed. The fourfold wafq allows for remainders.
The fourfold wafq belongs to the planet Jupiter (Mushtarī), and its day is Thursday. Its celestial angel is Sarfeyāīl, and its terrestrial angel is Shemhūresh.

The Fifth Rule for the Fourfold Wafq
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 248

We write in order from the wafq's first cell to its eighth cell. Then we divide by two (2) the numerical value of the Verse or Divine Name to be worked into the wafq, and subtract 8 from the half. We write the remainder in the 9th cell and complete the wafq by ascending one at each step. If the division leaves a remainder of 1, we add one extra to the 13th cell; if it leaves a remainder of 2, we add one extra to the 9th cell, and so complete the fourfold wafq.

For example, let us construct the fourfold wafq of the name Celil according to this rule. We write the base numbers from the first cell to the eighth cell. The name Celil's numerical value is 73; we divided this by 2. The quotient is 36, with a remainder of 1. We subtracted 8 from 36, leaving 28. We write this number in the 9th cell and ascend by one at each step up to the 13th cell. We add the leftover remainder to the 13th cell and, again ascending by one at each step, complete the wafq.

In the fourfold wafq, the first cell is one (1). This is called the miftah (meaning "key" or "starting point").
In the fourfold wafq, the last cell is 16. This is called the mughlak (meaning "pole" or "final cell").
In the fourfold wafq, the sum of the miftah and the mughlak is 17. This is called the adil.
In the fourfold wafq, the sum of one dil (side, i.e., a row or column of the square) or one row is 34. This is called the wafq sum.
In the fourfold wafq, the sum of all four dils, or four rows, is 136.
[I 250] In the fourfold wafq, the sum of one dil and the mesahe is 170. This is called the zabit.
In the fourfold wafq, twice the zabit, which is 340, is called the ghaye.

In the fourfold wafq, the number that results from multiplying the ghaye by the mughlak (pole) number is 5440. This is called the asil, or mughlak mea'l-ghaye wa-l- wasil (the pole joined to the goal and the means).

[I 273] The Five-celled Wafq and its First Rule Sixty (60) is subtracted from the number to be worked into a wafq, and the remainder is divided by five (5). The quotient is written into the first cell, and the wafq is completed by proceeding upward, adding one at a time, up to the last cell. If the division leaves a remainder of four (4), one (1) extra is added to the sixth (6) cell; if the remainder is three (3), one (1) extra is added to the eleventh (11) cell; if the remainder is two (2), one (1) extra is added to the sixteenth (16) cell; if the remainder is one (1), one (1) extra is added to the twenty-first (21) cell — and in this way the five-celled wafq is completed. The five-celled wafq has forms that admit a remainder and forms that do not.

Chapter 20 (al-bāb al-ʿishrūn): On the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn and the answered invocations that belong to it [303]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant success to me and to you in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that among the occult properties of this noble sura is what is related from Anas b. Mālik — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((For everything there is a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is Yā-Sīn. Whoever recites it, God writes for him, for his reciting of it, the reciting of the Qurʾān ten times.)) And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Sūrat Yā-Sīn is called al-Muʿammima (the Enveloping).)) It was said: O Messenger of God, and what is al-Muʿammima? He said: ((It envelops its possessor with good in this world and in the hereafter. And it is called al-Dāfiʿa al-Qāḍiya (the Repelling, the Fulfilling): it repels from its possessor every evil, and fulfils for him every need, and bears on his behalf every trial in this world, and repels from him the terrors of the hereafter.)) And it is related with a sound chain of transmission from Abū Bakr and Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ((Whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn as far as His words And strike for them a similitude: the people of the town (Q 36:13), and then supplicates for something immediately upon it, is answered without fail.)) And it is tried-and-tested (mujarrab): it has been put to the test and proved sound in many places.

And whoever writes Sūrat Yā-Sīn and drinks it — there enter into his belly a thousand remedies, and a thousand lights, and a thousand blessings, and a thousand wisdoms, and a thousand mercies; and every disease and ailment is stripped away from him. So let him write it upon gazelle parchment on a Thursday, in the hour of Jupiter, with the moon increasing in light, and hang it upon the left upper arm: he is made secure from the pain of the spleen.

And it is said that whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn in the graveyard, God lightens [the punishment] for them on that day, and he has good deeds according to the number of those buried in it. And whoever recites it in the evening does not cease to be in joy until the morning; or in the morning, does not cease to be in /fol. 208r./ joy until the evening. And whoever recites it beside a Muslim upon whom death has come down — God sends down, for the number of every letter of it, angels who stand before him in ranks, and pray for him, and ask forgiveness for him, and accompany his funeral bier, and witness his burial. And whatever Muslim recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn before his need, it is fulfilled for him. And whoever recites it while he is fearful is made secure; or hungry, is filled; or thirsty, is given to drink. And whatever Muslim recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn while he is in the throes of death — the angel of death does not seize his spirit until he sees the good pleasure (riḍwān) of the Garden and it is made beloved to him.

And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Truly there is in the Qurʾān a sura that is called "the Mighty" in God's sight, and its possessor is called "the Noble" in God's sight. It will intercede for its reciter on the Day of Resurrection for more than [the tribes of] Rabīʿa and Muḍar; and it is Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān).)) And he — upon him be blessing and peace — said: ((Truly there is in the Qurʾān a sura that intercedes for its reciter, and its listener is forgiven — behold, it is Yā-Sīn. And whoever recites it on the day of Friday rises in the morning forgiven.)) And it is related from al-Ḥasan that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Whoever recites Yā-Sīn and Ḥā-Mīm al-Dukhān on the eve of Friday, in faith and in the seeking of reward, is forgiven what has gone before of his sin.))

For battle and for other [purposes]: one recites the istirjāʿ three times — Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we are returning (Q 2:156) — and recites Yā-Sīn. And whoever is a captive, or fearful, or gone astray, or absent, or in debt — let him recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn three times: he is set loose, and made secure, and guided, and brought back, and his debt is discharged. And likewise in all pressing affairs. Or [if he is] fearful or gone astray, he recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn seventy times, and you recite this supplication seven times after the first time; then you recite [it] at every time. And the supplication is this: "O company [of spirits] made subject and obedient to this blessed sura, by the right of the prophets of God and His friends, and by the right of your Creator: make my word to run current, and my speech heard and accepted; and suffice me in my pressing affairs, near and not far off; and supply me and help me in all matters, universal and particular, by the right of It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate (Q 27:30). Haste! Speed! This very hour! Truly He is powerful over whatsoever He wills, and worthy to answer."

For an unjust enemy: whoever has an enemy who has wronged him and wishes to destroy him — let him take a mud-brick and set it before him upon the bank of a running river or of a cistern, and let him be facing [the qibla]; and let him recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn forty-one times, and with each time let him draw a line upon that brick. Then, when he has finished the reciting, let him pray over the brick the funeral prayer, and let him make the brick the image of his enemy; then let him cast it into the river or the cistern — for he perishes swiftly. And this is a trust, not to be employed save after grave compulsion and great wronging. So fear God, glorified and exalted is He, and have mercy upon His servant, and dread lest God take vengeance upon you. /fol. 208v./

For the departing of care and of […]: a certain one of the gnostics mentioned that when a man is laden with care he recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and when he has completed it he supplicates with this blessed supplication. He says: "[Glory be to] the Reliever of every care-laden one; glory be to the Bringer of relief to every debtor; glory be to the Deliverer of every prisoner; who has set His treasuries, by His power, between the kāf and the nūn: His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He say to it 'Be', and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned (Q 36:82–83). O Reliever of care, relieve my care!" He says it three times.

And among the occult properties of this noble sura, for retention: whoever writes the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn with rose-water and saffron, and writes it seven consecutive days, once each day — he retains what he hears, and overcomes whoever disputes with him, and is magnified in the eyes [of men]. And among the occult properties of the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn: it is drunk for the promoting of urine. And whoever gives it as a drink to a nursing woman, there is in it for the suckling child a good nourishment and a complete healing, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted is He. And whoever writes it and hangs it upon his neck is made secure from evil eyes, and from the jinn, and from vermin, and from pains.

And among the occult properties of this sura, for the destroying of a wrongdoer: al-Kalbī mentioned that there was a man who had killed by mistake, and the next of kin of the slain man charged him with having killed him deliberately, and so kept seeking him out in order to kill him. A certain righteous man said to him: If you are truthful in your account, then recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn before you go out of your house, and go out to meet him; for by God he will not see you, since he is your wronger. And that man used to recite it before going out of his house, and his pursuer would not catch sight of him on his road. I say: and it is soundly established that our master the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — recited the beginning of it when he went out to Quraysh, when they had plotted by night to kill him; and he went out upon them and they did not see him, and he put dust upon their heads.

And a certain one of the righteous — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said in his discourse: And among the things that have been made clear, and whose blessing has been ascertained, is that whoever is in fear of a tyrannical ruler, or of one who seeks him out unjustly, or [upon whom] a need has come knocking, or whose riding-beast has strayed from the road — [it is] that he should recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn and then say: "In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. In the name of God, other than whom there is no god, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. In the name of God, other than whom there is no god, the Possessor of Majesty and Honour. In the name of

God, with whose name nothing can do harm, neither in the earth nor in the heaven, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. O God, truly I take refuge with You from the evil of So-and-so son of So-and-so." That suffices.

And know that even were the heavens to close down upon the earth, and the world to blaze up in fire with civil strife, and then the servant were to obey his Lord within himself with a truthful taking of refuge — God, exalted is He, would deliver him according to the measure of his sincerity.

And as for His word "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58): it is recited for the fulfilment of needs and the sufficing of pressing affairs, one thousand four hundred and ninety-nine times, and the object sought is obtained, by the leave of God, exalted is He. /fol. 209r./ And for the sufficing against the evil of the night-visitant and of the epidemic: whoever writes "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58) 5 times and hangs it upon himself is kept safe from the visitants of the night and the day. And whoever makes remembrance of it in the days of the epidemic, twenty-eight times every day, is kept safe from the plagues of the epidemic. And from ʿAṭāʾ b. Abī Rabāḥ, who said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — [said]: ((Whoever recites Sūrat Yā-Sīn, his needs are fulfilled.)) Al-Dārimī related it as a mursal report. And from the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Whoever recites Yā-Sīn by night or by day, no sin overtakes him that day.)) And from him — God bless him and grant him peace — that he said: ((Praise be to God, who has honoured me and honoured my community with Sūrat Yā-Sīn, and the Throne Verse, and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1).))

And Sahl [b.] ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī said: A man came to Ibrāhīm b. Adham and said: What do you say concerning Yā-Sīn? He said: Truly, in it there is a name — whoever knows it and calls upon God by it is answered, be he righteous or dissolute, when he calls upon it in the thing that is proper to it. He said: What do you say — may God set you aright — if I invoke with the whole sura? He said: No, not until you invoke with the very name itself, in the name that is proper to it. Do you not see that if you came to the shop of the apothecary while you had a disease, and you knew that your remedy was in the shop but did not know it specifically, and you took of everything that was in the shop and drank it for that [disease] — would it profit you, until you know that remedy itself and then use it as it ought to be used? And just as God created the disease and created for it the remedy and made it efficacious in it, so likewise to each name of the names of God there belongs something proper to it, with which one invokes in that matter, and he is answered on account of it.

The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((For everything there is a heart, and the heart of the Qurʾān is Yā-Sīn.)) And that suffices it for nobility, and [so too] the names that are in it…

…in greatness, since God, exalted is He, made it the heart of the Qurʾān. And the noblest of the members of the animal's body is the heart, and the power mingled with the heart is the noblest of powers. And it is, in the body of man, as the sun is to the world, by which life subsists; and that is because it gives life to the body, and is the wellspring of life and of breath and of heat ⟨and of breath and of the innate heat, and it is, of the body of man, as the sun⟩. And when its light is dispersed, the horizon grows dark, and everything of the animal grows still and sleeps. And these two powers are the two that resemble the two blasts which Isrāfīl — peace be upon him — blows into the Trumpet. And in the sun there is life for every plant in the earth and in the air, and the light of the moon and the splendour of the heaven. And no one has recited Sūrat Yā-Sīn and invoked with it while he was care-laden but that God relieved him of his care; nor any drowning man but that God, exalted is He, delivered him from drowning; nor any prisoner but that he was set free; nor any hungry man but that he was fed; nor any thirsty man but that his thirst was quenched; nor any fearful man but that he was made secure; nor any dead man but that God lightened the torment for him. And all this is from the nobility of the Name that is in it.

And it is related concerning Yā-Sīn that in it there is a name from among the names of God, glorified and exalted is He. /fol. 209v./ Whoever lights upon it by the secret of the letters, and writes it, and effaces it with pure water, facing the qibla, and drinks it for as many days as the number of the names — God causes him to speak with wisdom, and makes plain to him something of the secret of the worlds. And it is in the middle of the sura; and it is five words which sixteen letters make up, among them four dotted letters: two of them dotted from below and two from above. And that is by the secret of the natural, compositive, fourfold world. And likewise, if you multiply the four by itself, sixteen issues from it — and that is the sum of the names, I mean its letters. And by this secret the names appeared in it, in the heaven and the earth and the Footstool and Paradise; and by it the soul can be firmly established in the sensory world; and by it the secret ran through the world of the highest Dominion; and by it was ennobled the form of the heart that is in the secret. And that secret is not in Ṭā-Sīn; and that is because Ṭā-Sīn is joined in its meaning to the meaning of the sīn, whereas Yā-Sīn is not so, because the yāʾ falls in the inward. And this is what I have summarized from the gnostic.

For the repelling of the guile of enemies: His words, exalted is He, Truly We have set shackles upon their necks— down to His words, exalted is He — so they do not see (Q 36:8–9). These verses are for repelling the guile of enemies, and for turning back their harm and their destruction, and for turning away their faces, and for the blinding of their eyes, and for [the repelling of] their opposition. Whoever engraves them upon a shield, or engraves them upon a plate of copper or gold and nails it into the grip of the shield, and meets with it the enemies and those who oppose the religion — they are forsaken, and their guile is turned back upon them. And whoever recites them when he goes into his bed is safe that night from thieves and mischief-makers. And whoever recites them in a dispute between two men — the wrongdoer of the two is forsaken.

For security from fear: His words, exalted is He, "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). This is a verse of majestic worth, and in it is the Greatest Name of God. So if that is set down in a letter-square — and it is four by four — it is a security for every fearful person. And this is the form of its arrangement.

This noble verse — namely His words, exalted is He, "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord— this noble, majestic verse: in it is the Greatest Name of God, and it has, of number, 820. So if that is set down in a square, it is a security for every fearful person. And I have tried it many times, and I have not seen anything more successful than it in operation. And it is related also — he said: A man came to Ibrāhīm b. Adham and said: What do you say concerning Sūrat Yā-Sīn? He said: Truly, in it there are names — whoever knows them and calls upon God, exalted is He, by them does not ask God, exalted is He, for anything but that He gives it to him. /fol. 210r./
And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

And it is said that they are fourteen letters. Whoever draws them in a sixfold [figure] upon a signet of red gold, at the exaltation of the Sun and the Moon, increasing in light — its bearer sees of the traces of the subtlety of God, exalted is He, toward him what increases him in certainty, and he seeks no need but that he attains it. And if it is drawn with its eight appendages and carried, God, exalted is He, gives him kingship and leadership and high standing, and God, exalted is He, enriches him after destitution; and its benefits are many. And if one in pain, or one who has been stung, seals with it, he is healed forthwith, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And its benefits are for everything you seek: for the relieving of care, and the seeking of a livelihood, and acceptance, and high standing, and everything you desire — by the leave of God, exalted is He. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And one of the masters of free disposal (taṣarruf) said: no one writes this noble verse in a bowl of glass in the first [hour] of the day of Monday, at the beginning of the month, sixty times, and washes it off with rainwater and drinks it — for whatever matter he wishes to put out of mind — but that God uproots that matter from his heart, and makes him forget it, and turns it away from his thought, and expands his breast, and gives him his wish, and realizes his hope in what he purposed and hoped for.

And know that this lofty name and manifest secret has a square, mighty in station, dazzling in proof, which is set down by the secret of interpenetration (al-tadākhul), with Venus in her exaltation or in her house, in the first [hour] of the day of Friday, or the eighth. Its bearer sees of God's doing toward him, exalted is He, what descriptions are powerless to convey. So ponder it, for it is among the treasured secrets.

And if you wish, you may write in the place of 136 His name, exalted is He, Muʾmin (the Granter of Security) — for it is among the most special of the attributes of the Prophet, our master Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace. And if you want, then write in the place of 135 His name, exalted is He, Musahhil (the Facilitator); and in the place of 129 His name, exalted is He, Laṭīf (the Subtle); and in the place of 130 His name, exalted is He, Munīl (the Bestower) — and it is among the most special of the attributes of Abraham, peace be upon him. And this is the form of its arrangement, as you see.

And know, O my brother — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that Sūrat Yā-Sīn is a magnificent sura, and that it has weighty occult properties that are not to be counted or numbered, because it is the heart of the Mighty Qurʾān, and the heart of this sura is "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:58). And we have already mentioned something of its occult properties; and I shall mention here something of its benefits and of what pertains to this noble sura. May God profit me and you by it. Amen.
Faṣl: On the subjugation of hearts and on concord between those who hate one another

He writes them, as I shall explain to you, upon paper (kāghad), written with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water. Let the writing be in a felicitous hour; and let whoever wishes carry it, upon the name of whom he wishes and the name of his mother. And he recites the noble sura seven times and says: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura! — seven times; and you say: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, with the procuring and the attracting of the heart of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.] to the love of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.]. Then let him carry the sheet with him, and he will see the wonder of wonders in the way of love and lasting affection between them, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And among them also, for the deliverance of a prisoner: write the noble sura and what is with it of the names of God, exalted is He, upon a pure garment; and let the recitation be three times, and say in the course of the recitation: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this noble sura, with the procuring of So-and-so son of So-and-so [f.], by the right it has over you and by its being obeyed among you. Then spread dust upon something clean, such as a napkin or the like, and lay the dust out flat; and let the prisoner pray upon that dust two rakʿas, in each rakʿa the Fātiḥa once and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣfourteen times. And when he has given the salām you say: O God, I ask You, O God, O Sublime, O Lord of seven heavens. And he says: Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him who gives release to every prisoner! Glory be to Him who knows every hidden thing! Glory be to Him whose command is between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He wills a thing, [His command is] only to say "Be", and it is! So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of everything, and to Him you shall be returned. Then let the dust be buried in a place that no foot treads upon; for the prisoner will be delivered speedily, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

And among the occult properties, for the repelling of diseases and ailments: write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water; and let it be dissolved with rainwater, and let the one who has the malady and the ailment drink it. And let him say when he drinks it: I have made the intention of healing by the mighty verses of God and His generous names. For God, exalted is He, heals him and gives him well-being from that malady and ailment, if God, glorified and exalted is He, wills. And it also benefits palpitation of the heart, and trembling from a sudden blow or from panic: he does that as we have mentioned at first.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties, for the prevention of sorcery and of harmful acts, and of what is feared and of what may befall him: if he wishes to prevent that, he writes the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass, with a pen of sweet basil (rayḥān); and the ink is what I shall mention — and it is a little rose-water, and water of sweet pomegranate, and myrtle-water, and jasmine-water, and water of vine-wood, and a little rainwater, and water of carrot leaves. A little of each thing is taken, and one writes with it; and it is dissolved with rainwater, and the bewitched man — or he who fears sorcery — bathes with it beside running water, or beside a channel that runs /fol. 211v./ toward the qibla. And he rubs the whole of his body except the front and the rear, for he must never touch them with his hand. And you recite, at his washing, His words, exalted is He: Moses said: What you have brought is sorcery; God will bring it to nothing. Truly God does not set right the work of those who work corruption (Q 10:81). O God, I ask You by the right of the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn that You repel from me the sorcery of the sorcerers and the guile of the guileful, by a thousand thousand "there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty". For God, exalted is He, takes away from him what he fears and what he guards against, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties, for the retention of the Qurʾān and of the rest of the sciences: you write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass, with musk-sukk, saffron and rose-water; and it is set out beneath the sky, and drunk on an empty stomach. He does that seven consecutive days, and avoids during them the eating of what is sour and salty. And he says when he drinks it: O God, I ask You, O God, by the blessing of this noble sura and the blessed, eminent names, that You cause me to retain the Mighty Qurʾān and the noble knowledge; and all that You have taught to those whom You love — make me one of them; and what You have taught them, teach me, O God, O All-Knowing, O Wise. For God, exalted is He, teaches him the Qurʾān and whatever he wishes of the sciences, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Faṣl. And among its occult properties: whoever desires high standing with kings and viziers and rulers, let him write the noble sura and what is with it in a bowl of glass with oil of zanbaq (lily), and jasmine oil, and oil of nasrīn (eglantine), and balsam oil; and if the oil is not to be had, then with the waters of them, and a little Palestinian oil. And there is recited together with the sura And when they saw him they magnified him, and they cut their hands, and they said: God forbid! This is no mortal; this is nothing but a noble angel (Q 12:31); and His words, exalted is He, and he was of high standing with God (Q 33:69); and the Throne Verse; and When the help of God comes, and the victory (Q 110:1); and Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, and the two suras of refuge-seeking (al-Muʿawwidhatān), and the Fātiḥa. Then put what you have written into a phial. And when you want to go in upon a king or a ruler or a vizier to ask a need, anoint your face with a little of the oil that is in the phial, and recite Sūrat Yā-Sīn and what you have written. Then you go in upon whom you wish of the rulers; and you will attain with him rank, and favour, and great standing; and he will accomplish for you all your interests and whatever you seek, without weariness and without hardship, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Faṣl. And among the occult properties of this noble sura: it is recited for the increase of provisions and of good things. Whoever recites it while thirsty is given to drink; and whoever is fearful is made secure and sufficed. And among its occult properties is what one of the righteous reported of it: that he had many sheep, and every night the man would go round with his staff and trace a line about the sheep while he recited Sūrat Yā-Sīn. And the thieves would come to steal something of the sheep, and they would find about the sheep a wall of iron, and they would go back disappointed. And when it had been so, on one of the nights he recited Yā-Sīn and did not complete it; and they came, and found in the wall an open door, and they were able to take one of the sheep. And when morning came, the man looked at the sheep and found a portion of them missing; and he reflected within himself that he had slept and had not completed the recitation of the noble Yā-Sīn. So thereafter /fol. 212r./ the man persevered in reciting it, and no evil ever befell him again.

And among its occult properties: if someone is on a journey and strays from the road and fears that he will lose his way in the wilderness, let him recite the noble Sūrat Yā-Sīn and say in the course of the recitation: O servant-spirits of this noble sura, guide me to the road! — and let him name the place he wants; for God will send to him one who will point him to his goal.

And among its occult properties: if you are fearful of a sultan or a ruler, and you want to be safe from his evil, then recite the noble sura; and whenever you reach His words, exalted is He, mubīn ("clear"), you say: O God, I ask You, O God of the heavens and the earth, and God of the earths, and God of Moses and Jesus and Abraham the Friend — and by the right of God, the majestic Lord — that You quench for me the anger of this king or this ruler, by the right of the noble, blessed Sūrat Yā-Sīn. And you say: Take charge, O servant-spirits of this sura, with the binding of his tongue away from me. And if you know his name and the name of his mother, then name him; and if you do not know his name, say: this ruler. For God, exalted is He, by His bounty and His generosity, quenches his anger and stills his heat, and nothing shall reach him from him but good, if God, glorified and exalted is He, wills. And its occult properties are many, not to be counted and not to be numbered. I have restricted myself to this much for fear of length and of wearying; so measure what is absent by what is present, and you will hit the mark, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And this is the noble invocation. You say: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, I ask You and I take refuge in You: You are God, other than whom there is no god, You alone, having no partner. O God, You are God, the King, the Real, the Evident. O God, You are God, firm in existence. O God, You are God, known for munificence. O God, You are God, the Manifest, and He is not seen. O God, You are God, the Hidden, and He shall never be concealed. O God, You are God, the Shaper, the Wondrous Originator. O God, You are God, the light of the heavens and the earth. O God, You are God, the light of this world and of the hereafter. O God, You are God, the One, the Unique. O God, You are God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. O God, You are God, the Mighty, the Tender. O God, You are God, who is singularly one in self-sufficiency (ṣamadāniyya). O God, You are God, the High, the Beneficent. O God, You are God, the Manifest through His words. O God, You are God, who is quit of every defect. O God, You are God, who did not beget and was not begotten, and to whom none is equal. O God,

You are God, who has no opposite and no like. O God, You are God, the First without term. O God, You are God, the Last without end. O God, You are God, the Everlasting without time. O God, You are God, the Enduring without limit. O God, You are God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, who never dies. O God, You are God, the Abiding, the Worshipped. O God, You are God, the Honourer, the Bestower of grace. O God, You are God, my Lord, Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour). O God, I ask You, by the sanctity of Sūrat Yā-Sīn and by the sanctity of this blessed, noble supplication, that You show me Your sacred precinct by Your generosity, and bring me to the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet /fol. 212v./ Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and make easy for me every hardship, and that You subject to me the servant-spirits of this noble sura, so that they may be a help unto what he wants of good. O God, subject to me Your creation and Your provision. O God, unite the hearts of Your servants toward me — male or female, free and slave, small and great — in love and affection and tenderness; and provide me with abundant fortune; and subject to me the hearts of Your servants in gentleness and mercy; and provide me with lawful, wholesome provision; and be for me a help and a helper unto what I want of good. O God, subject to me Your creation and Your provision. O God, unite the hearts of Your servants toward me, of male and female; and be for me a preserver and a supporter and a trustworthy guardian. Glory be to Him who gives release to every debtor! Glory be to Him who brings relief to every sorrowful one! Glory be to Him the treasuries of whose kingdom are between the kāf and the nūn! Glory be to Him who, when He decrees a matter, only says to it "Be", and it is! O Reliever — you say it seven times — O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, make light for me every hardship, by the blessing of Sūrat Yā-Sīn.

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾān (Q 36:1–2) — you say it seven times; and you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44), and you repeat it seven times; and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say truly you are among the messengers, upon a straight path — a sending-down from the Mighty, the Wise — that you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so that they are heedless. And you say: O Reliever — you repeat it seven times — and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say: O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, subject to me the servant-spirits of this noble sura, that they may obey me and comply with my command; and grant me as provision the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet /fol. 213r./ Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace; and make easy for me every hardship; and subject to me Your creation and Your provision. O God, I ask You, O God of the first and the last, that You subject to me the whole of Your creation in love and affection and tenderness, as You subjected the sea to Moses son of ʿImrān — peace be upon him — and that You soften for me their hearts and their spirits and their inmost hearts and their limbs and their members, as You softened iron for David — peace be upon him — so that they do not speak save by Your command. By Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful! I ask You, by the right of this noble sura, that You draw to me my provision, and the hearts of Your servants, upon love of me and affection for me and tenderness toward me, as the magnet draws iron. O God, and draw to me their spirits and their bodies and all their members, by Your right, and by the right of Your right, and the light of Your face; and by the right of Your prophets and the messengers and the angels brought near; and by the right of Sūrat Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾān (Q 36:1–2); and by the right of Alif-Lām-Mīm. That Book — there is no doubt in it — is a guidance for the God-fearing (Q 2:1–2); and by the right of Alif-Lām-Mīm. — Jibrāʾīl and Mīkāʾīl; and by the truth of Isrāfīl and ʿAzrāʾīl, and of the bearers of the Throne and the Footstool, and of the angels brought near; and by the sanctity of the heavens and the earths; and by the wandering planets; and by the heaven possessed of the constellations, and the promised Day, and a witness and a witnessed (Q 85:1–3); and by the heaven and the night-comer! And what will make you know what the night-comer is? The piercing star! Truly over every soul there is a guardian /fol. 213v./(Q 86:1–4); and by the truth of the dawn, and ten nights, and the even and the odd, and the night when it journeys on (Q 89:1–4); and by the truth of the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinai, and this secure land! Truly We created man in the fairest stature (Q 95:1–4); and by the sanctity of the Sacred House and the Holy House; and by the sanctity of Your prophets and Your elect and Your righteous servants —

O Lord of the worlds, O best of helpers, O Answerer of those who ask, O Fulfiller of needs, O Answerer of invocations, O Remitter of stumbles, O Patron of good deeds, O Repeller of afflictions, O Forgiver of evil deeds, O Remover of distresses: show me Your sacred precinct by Your generosity, and bring me to the visitation of Your Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace; and subject to me all Your creation, and soften for me their hearts and their spirits with love and affection and tenderness; and subject to me my provision, and make every hardship light for me, by the sanctity of Yā-Sīn. By the wise Qurʾān (Q 36:1–2); and relieve me of my debts, and dispel from me my anguish, and give me from Your ample treasuries. Your command, when You will a thing, is but to say to it "Be", and it is — by the truth of Sūrat Yā-Sīn.

And you repeat it seven times; and you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) — you repeat it seven times; and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say And strike for them a similitude: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it (Q 36:13), and you repeat it seven times; and you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) — you repeat it seven times; and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say When We sent to them two, and they denied them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said: Truly we are messengers to you. They said: You are only mortals like ourselves, and the All-Merciful has sent down nothing; you are only lying. They said: Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you, and upon us is only the clear delivery of the message (Q 36:14–17).

O God! Glory be to Him who gives respite to every debtor. And give relief to every one in distress, and give me from Your treasuries. O God, O Reliever, O God, O God of the first and the last: subject to me my provision, and make my affair easy for me, and make every hardship light for me, and make the hard easy for me; and endear me to all Your creation, and incline their hearts and their spirits and their eyes toward me, O Lord of the worlds, O Reliever — seven times. And you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44), repeating it seven times; and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say They said: We augur ill of you. If you do not desist, we shall surely stone you, and a painful torment from us shall touch you. They said: Your ill omen is with you. Is it because you have been reminded? Nay, you are a people transgressing all bounds. And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said: O my people, follow the messengers! Follow those who ask of you no wage, and who are rightly guided. And why should I not worship Him who originated me, and to whom you shall be returned? Shall I take gods apart from Him? If the All-Merciful should desire harm for me, their intercession would avail me nothing, nor would they deliver me. Truly I should then be in manifest error. Truly I have believed in your Lord, so hear me!(Q 36:18–25) /fol. 214r./

And you say: O God, I ask You, O God, O God of the first and the last — O God, I ask You to subject to me all Your creation, and to give respite to every debtor, and to give relief to every one who grieves, and to make all Your creation easy for me, and to make every hardship light for me. And you say And I commit my affair to God; truly God is All-Seeing of [His] servants (Q 40:44) seven times; and you invoke blessing upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — ten times; and you say Truly I have believed in your Lord, so hear me! It was said: Enter the Garden. He said: Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me one of the honoured! And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from heaven, nor were We sending down. It was but a single cry, and behold, they were extinguished. Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but that they mock him. Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them — that they do not return to them? And each and all shall be arraigned before Us. And a sign for them is the dead earth: We gave it life, and We brought forth from it grain, and of it they eat. And We placed in it gardens of date-palms and vines, and We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they might eat of its fruit — and their hands did not make it. Will they not then give thanks? Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth brings forth, and of themselves, and of what they do not know. And a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs to a resting-place appointed for it: that is the determining of the Mighty, the All-Knowing. And the moon — We have determined mansions for it, until it returns like an old palm-branch. It does not behove the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; and each swims in a sphere. And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship; and We created for them the like of it, in which they ride. And if We will, We drown them, and there is no crier for them, nor are they delivered — save by a mercy from Us and an enjoyment for a while. And when it is said to them: Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that you may receive mercy… And no sign of the signs of their Lord comes to them but that they turn away from it. And when it is said to them: Spend of that which God has provided you, those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Shall we feed one whom, if God willed, He would feed? You are in nothing but manifest error (Q 36:25–47).

O God, I ask You, O God of the first and the last — I ask You to discharge my debts, and to dispel my cares and my sorrows, and to give me from Your treasuries. O Reliever, subject to me my provision, and make every hardship light for me, and make the hearts of Your servants tender toward me, and soften for me their hearts and their inmost hearts as You softened iron for David — peace be upon him. O God, subject to me the servant-spirits (khuddām) of this sura, that they may accomplish my affairs; and provide me with the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace.

And you say And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful? They await only a single cry that will seize them while they are yet disputing; then they will not be able to make a bequest, nor /fol. 214v./ will they return to their families. And the trumpet is blown, and at once they are hastening forth from the graves to their Lord. They say: Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping-place? This is what the All-Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth. It was but a single cry, and behold, they were all arraigned before Us. So today no soul shall be wronged in anything, and you shall be recompensed only for what you used to do. Truly the companions of the Garden are today in an occupation, rejoicing — they and their spouses, in shades, reclining upon couches. Theirs therein is fruit, and theirs is whatever they call for. "Peace" — a word from a Compassionate Lord (Q 36:48–58). You repeat it 16 times.

And you say: My Master, peace be upon You from me. You are my Lord, and in Your hand are my hearing and my sight and my heart. You possess the whole of me; You have ennobled my lowliness, and raised my mention, and exalted my worth. Blessed are You, O Light of lights, O Bestower of lifetimes! You are exalted in Your loftiness above the marks of things originated in time, and Your rank is too high for imperfections and blemishes to find any way to it. The earths and the heavens bear witness to that. Yours is the most sublime glory, and the most spacious court, and the most impregnable might. All-Glorified, All-Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Illuminator of the darkened strongholds and of the glooms of night; Deliverer of the drowning from the seas of destruction and of terrors! I take refuge in You from the evil of the darkness when it gathers, and of an envier when he envies and lies in wait. My Master, I commune with You with the communing of a broken servant who knows that You hear and hopes that You answer; and I am one who asks, standing, waiting, finding no trustee apart from You. I ask You, O God, by the Name through which You caused good things to flow forth, and through which You sent down blessings, and through which You brought forth out of the darknesses, and through which You opened the thanksgiving of increase — I ask You to bless our master Muḥammad and the family of our master Muḥammad, and to pour upon me of the garments of Your lights that which turns back the eyes of the enviers in loss, and their hands in loss. And make my portion from You an illumination that polishes clear for me everything hidden, and discloses to me every secret that is closed upon me, O Light of everything — and every light is from Your light — O Unveiler of everything veiled, to whom the affairs return, and by whom evils are warded off! O Living, O Self-Subsisting! By Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful, I seek help; and from Your torment I seek protection. O God, I take refuge in You from their evils, and I ward them off by You at their throats. If We will, We shall send down upon them a sign from heaven, so that their necks remain humbled before it (Q 26:4).

O God, Sender-down of the clouds and Router of the confederates: rout my enemies and their host and their followers, and give me victory over them, and soften for me their hearts and their spirits. O God, show me Your sacred precinct by Your generosity, and let me visit the grave of Your Prophet Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace. O God, subject to me Your creation, and soften their hearts and their spirits toward love of me and affection for me; and be for me a helper, a guardian, a giver of victory, and a trustee. O God, make every hardship easy for me, and make the hard easy. O God —
