Having recited this, lie down on your right side facing the qibla, and by Allah's leave you will see, in a dream, the thing you had in mind.

I ask You, O) .(God, O He who is ever the sufficient, everlasting one
[II 178] Having said this, your requests will be accepted and you will succeed in all your affairs.
18. According to some of the righteous, the heart of the noble Surah Yā-Sīn is the following verse:

Merciful, the Compassionate. "Peace" — a word from a Merciful Lord.) This is verse 58, and it is made up of sixteen letters and four words. Of the sixteen letters, seven occur once and nine are repeated. The letters occurring once are Sin, Qāf, Wāw, Nun, Be, Ha, and Ye. Of the repeated letters, Alif occurs twice, Lam twice, Ra twice, and Mīm three times. The letters occurring once — sin, qāf, wāw, nun, be, ha, and ye — correspond to the seven planets, while the repeated letters alif, lam, ra, and mīm correspond to the nine celestial spheres. This verse contains six dots in all: three above, on the Qāf and Nun, and three below, on the Be and Ye. The two dots of the Qāf relate to fire and air; the two dots of the Ye relate to earth and water. The dot of the Nun relates to the sun, and the dot of the Be relates to the moon. The letters of this verse likewise embody the four elements: there are five letters of fire, four of earth, two of air, and five of water. The abjad (the numerical alphabet) value of this verse, taken as a sum, is 818.

Before beginning to recite this verse, one should start Surah Yā-Sīn from the beginning and, on reaching this verse, recite it 818 times, then continue reading the sūrah to its end; doing so hastens the expected benefit.

19. For someone paralyzed or ill, or afflicted with a spiritual illness, recite this verse 818 times over a glass of water, breathe upon it, and give the water to the patient to drink; if this is continued for seven days or more, he will find healing by Allah's leave.

Following this same order, if he recites Surah Yā-Sīn twice more to complete it, and then recites the noble salawat three times, he will be freed from hardship by Allah's leave. His provision will grow abundant and his earnings will increase.

22. For every kind of wish, sit facing the qibla toward dawn in a state of complete ritual purity and firm faith, and recite the verse "Selāmun kavlen mir rabbir Raḥīm" 1,479 times. Whoever, having recited it, humbly entreats the Almighty for his wish will have it granted in the shortest time, whatever it may be. This matter is sound and has been tested many times over.
23. If someone has a very important wish, let him write this verse's blessed fourfold wafq on a piece of paper, then carry what he has written as a ḥirz (protective amulet) upon his person.

Let him recite the verse "Selāmun kavlen mir rabbir Raḥīm" 818 times and the noble salawat 133 times, then turn to his need and ask it of Allah Almighty; Allah Almighty will grant that person's need. If someone, while wearing this wafq, takes this verse as his daily litany (wird) and recites it 818 times every day, he will find great benefit in it. This has been tested by those who live in fear of every danger. Whoever adopts this verse as a daily litany will, by Allah's leave, be kept safe from every material and spiritual, psychic, and contagious illness.
[II 181] There are several different ways of reciting the noble Surah Yā-Sīn.
One of them is this: begin Yā-Sīn and read up to the first "Mubin," then start again from the beginning and read up to the second Mubin.

Again start from the beginning of the sūrah and read up to the third Mubin, then start again from the beginning and read up to the fourth Mubin. Again start from the beginning of the sūrah and read up to the fifth Mubin. Start again from the beginning and read up to the sixth Mubin. Again start from the beginning of the sūrah and read up to the seventh Mubin. Then start once more from the beginning and read through to the end of the sūrah. In this way, returning to the beginning at every Mubin, you finish by reading through to the end of the sūrah. This is called the "Donmeli Yā-Sīn" (the Returning Yā-Sīn).

If you wish to draw the person who is the object of your working (maṭlūb, the object of the working) to you, prepare three candles made of pure white beeswax, about 12 centimeters long and 2 centimeters wide

[II 183] 2. Reciting the noble Surah Yā-Sīn (Yā-Sīn Sharif) by "returning" to fulfill a purpose is a well-tried method. After performing ablution (abdest), by night or by day, pray two rak'ahs. After the prayer, sit facing the qibla, and after the Euzu-Basmala (the formula of seeking refuge and the Basmala), begin reciting the noble Yā-Sīn. When you reach the word "Mubin" ("Clear," a word that recurs many times through the surah), go back to the beginning and read again up to the second occurrence of Mubin. In this way, at every occurrence of the word Mubin, return to the beginning and read all the way through to the end of the surah. Then recite Surah al-Ikhlāṣthree times, Surah al-Fātiḥa once, and the noble ṣalawāt (blessings on the Prophet) eleven times, and ask the Almighty (Jenāb-i Hak) for your need (ḥāja, the object of your request); by Allah's leave, your object and your purpose will come to pass.

Reciting Surah Yā-Sīn together with the azaim (ʿazīma, a binding conjuration formula recited at a fixed point in the text) of its occurrences of "Mubin" is a very effective and powerful method. Every Mubin in the noble Yā-Sīn has an ʿazīma of its own. Within these azaim are named the celestial and terrestrial angels belonging to the days [of the week], the angels of the Throne, the verses of the days (the Fātiḥa), and the seven Tahatil. Each of these azaim belongs to a particular day.

[II 202] The Exalted Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ) of Sūrat al-Wākia Know that Surat al-Wākia (the Qur'anic chapter al-Wāki'a, "The Event") possesses a sublime secret and wondrous properties. In particular, it holds a very great virtue for attracting wealth and repelling poverty.

Imam Ibn Abdilberr (may Allah be pleased with him), in his book called et-Temhīd, related a hadith of our Prophet Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, traced directly back to him. The Prophet Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said as follows:
-Whoever recites Surat al) .(Wākia every day will never be touched by poverty

Osman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) wished to give a certain amount of wealth to Abdullah ibn Mesud (may Allah be pleased with him). Abdullah ibn Mesud did not much welcome the idea of accepting it and was reluctant to take it. Osman ibn Affan said, "Take it, and accept it as provision for your daughters." Ibn Mesud replied, "Are you worried that they will remain in poverty? Yet I have commanded them to recite the noble Surat al-Wākia!" and he added: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, himself. He said: 'Whoever recites Surat al-Wākia every day will never be touched by poverty.'" This blessed sura holds a great secret and wondrous properties. Teach it to those who are worthy of it, for this sura contains the greatest of Allah's names, glorious and exalted is He.

1. If, every day after the morning prayer, one recites Surat al-Wākia once and follows it with the names Yā Kerīm, Yā Wedūd recited one thousand (1000) times, before a year has passed Allah Ta'ālā will make the reciter wealthier than all other people.

2. Whoever recites Surat al-Wākia forty-one (41) times in a single sitting and asks Allah Ta'ālā for their need will have that need fulfilled in the shortest time. Reciting it forty-one times has a particularly great effect where sustenance (rizq) is concerned.

3. Reciting Surat al-Wākia fourteen (14) times after the afternoon (ikindi) prayer is mujerreb (tried and tested) — it has been tried many times and positive results obtained. Whoever recites Surat al-Wākia continually will, by Allah Ta'ālā's leave, be granted sustenance and attain their desire.

[II 203] 4. Whoever recites Surat al-Wākia forty (40) times a day, for forty consecutive days without a break, Allah Ta'ālā will grant abundant sustenance to the reciter, and they will attain it without feeling any hardship or difficulty.

Treatments for the Illness of Epilepsy and Jinn-possession Epilepsy
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 267
Epilepsy is a cold and malignant humor concealed within the human body. Settling especially in the cavities of the brain, it is a grave illness, also called junūn (madness).

This illness of epilepsy is not always quiet; it grows more severe in rainy, cloudy, windy, and cold weather. Epilepsy begins in the feet and rises up to the brain. When it reaches the brain, the seizure takes hold of the patient, and if he happens to be standing at that moment, he falls to the ground. The patient senses this and strives not to fall, but he has not the strength [II 268] for it. Some epileptics, the instant they feel the seizure coming on, want to cover themselves at once, because their mental balance has been disturbed. You will see him speaking and answering without any awareness.

The treatment for this illness: the epileptic is kept in a house with clean air and no draft. You anoint the patient's head and entire body with a liquid oil. If he is fed rich, fatty and meaty foods of a moist and warm nature — such as walnuts, ewe's milk, clotted cream, butter, poultry meat, egg yolk, dried and fresh grapes, dates, bananas, and sweet pomegranate — and kept away from all other foods, the patient recovers, by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

Burning Jinn with Medicines and Herbs
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 283

1. If you wish to burn jinn with medicines, to treat with snuff and papers, and to overpower the afflicting jinn: take a quantity of meyatus sāile (a flowing aromatic resin), the same quantity of haltit (asafoetida), as much uzerlik (wild rue) as the two combined, as much sedef otu (rue) as the three combined, as much hanzal (colocynth) as the four combined, and as much [II 284] dried pomegranate rind as the five combined. Take all of these and pound them until soft, until they turn into something like flour. Add sharp vinegar to the mixture and work it into a paste. Put this paste into a bottle, bury it in warm manure, and leave it for forty days. After forty days the preparation inside the bottle turns into a cream. On the forty-first day, take the bottle out of the manure, add a little garlic to it, and mix well. If you wish to overpower the jinn and drive it out of the body, expelling it, drip a little of this mixture into the possessed patient's nose, and rub some of it over the patient's body as well. If you smear some of this cream onto a piece of paper, burn the paper, and have the patient inhale its smoke through the nose, the jinn will burn and, by the permission of Allah, glory be to Him, never return to that body again.

This working is even stronger and more effective against ferezdak, falic (paralysis), and hirab (names of nervous ailments). You will overcome these diseases, and torment the jinn afflicting the possessed, only by means of these burning names and medicines.

If a person fumigates his clothing with this cream (bakhūr — that is, perfumes it with smoke), no jinn will have the power to overcome him until he washes that clothing. That completes the treatment — after, of course, the prayers, the incantations, the recitations, and the fumigations have been carried out.

2. This working is sahih (sound) and mujerreb (tried-and-tested), and very beneficial. Take meyatus sāile, haltit, foul-smelling rue, wild rue, and sour pomegranate rind, and pound them thoroughly. After working them into a paste with vinegar, put the preparation into a glass bottle and bury the bottle in warm manure. Leave the bottle in the manure for twenty days. On the tenth and twentieth days, add a little olive oil into the bottle. On the twenty-first day this mixture becomes like tar. Take the bottle out of the manure, knead the preparation inside it with garlic juice, put it back into a glass bottle, and store the bottle carefully. When you wish to burn the jinn of a possessed patient, drip a little into the patient's nose and ear, and rub the patient's body with this ointment as well; by the permission of Allah, glory be to Him, the jinn will come forth and burn.

3. For a choking jinn: take an eagle's heart, cook this heart in honey, and if the possessed person eats it, he will, by Allah's permission, be healed. That choking jinn will leave the patient's body.

4. Knead meyatus sāile, haltit, rue, wild rue, and sour pomegranate rind together with garlic and vinegar, spread the paste on a piece of thin linen cloth, and wrap and tie this cloth around the possessed person's neck; for as long as this cloth remains on the possessed person's neck, that choking jinn cannot come near him.
[II 285] If you hang this cloth on a woman, the siḥr (sorcery) afflicting her is broken, and she is healed by the permission of Allah, glory be to
Him. If you fumigate a house with this cloth, no jinn can come near that house for as long as you remain in it.

5. For a jinn that lodges itself between the blood and the flesh and torments a person severely: take thirty-five grams of licorice root and put it into clean water without letting it dissolve. Leave it until morning, and if you drink it on an empty stomach in the morning, you will be delivered from the jinn lodged between your blood and flesh.
If you rub this water over your entire body, snakes and scorpions will not come near you. This is sahih and mujerreb.

6. The moment the possessed patient faints, if you have him smell haltit, or burn it and make him inhale the smoke, the possessed person will regain consciousness and come to his senses. No jinn can come near a person who carries haltit on him. Haltit is also beneficial for those who suffer bloating from yel (wind — a traditional humoral ailment).
7. If you drip a little of the juice of foul-smelling rue into the possessed person's nose, the afflicting jinn will leave that body, burning as it goes.

8. If you set a green emerald in the bezel of a ring and wear it on your finger, the disease of sara will stay away from you for as long as that ring is on your finger. The strength of your limbs will increase, and you will become someone loved and respected among people.
9. If you take a little from the right hoof of a donkey, shape it into something like a ring, and wear it on your finger, you will be delivered from the affliction of sara.

9. Whoever wishes to see jinn and speak with them: let him take the gall of a black cat and the gall of a black hen, mix the two galls with kohl stone, and apply it to his eyes like kohl — he will then see the jinn and speak with them.

2. Ahmed ibni Salih (may God be pleased with him) said: A jinn had taken possession of one of my slave-girls. I dismissed that slave-girl and took another in her place. The very same thing happened to her as well.
One day, as I sat in the place where I performed my prayers, I saw a tribe of jinn, and they greeted me with the salutation of peace.

Looking closely, I saw before me a vision like a bird. I returned their greeting and asked them, "Who are you?" One of them said, "I am a jinn named Abu Zakariya, and I have come to teach you a prayer. If you recite this prayer over the illnesses that befall your slave-girls, they will be delivered by God's leave." I at once tried to take up my inkwell, but I could not. He said to me, "The inkwell is under your bed." I took the inkwell from there and wrote down the prayer that the jinn named Zakariya recited. I asked that jinn how I should use this prayer. He told me, "Recite this prayer over water. If the sick person drinks some of this recited-over water and washes with the rest (gusul, ritual ablution), they will find healing by God's leave." I treated those two slave-girls with this prayer. Before a week had passed, both had recovered. After that, I recited this blessed prayer over everyone who was sick or afflicted, and by the leave of God, may He be exalted, they found healing and recovered.
This is the prayer that the jinn named Abu Zakariya taught:

Praise to God who raised up the sky and laid out the (earth, set the mountains firm, sent the winds, darkened the night and lit the day, creating what is seen and unseen without need of any helper among His creation — a supplication recalling how God restored Jacob's sight, saved Joseph from the well, and lifted Job's affliction, asking that the same mercy be shown to the person -named in this prayer's blank, "so-and-so, son/daughter of so-and so," delivering them from their pains, ailments, and sicknesses.)

For a moment there came a flash of light like lightning. When I raised my head I saw a black shadow. I drew near and touched it with my hand; its body was like the skin of a spine-covered hedgehog. At that very moment it hurled a spark at my face like a flying ember. The next day I described what had happened to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. He said: "O Ebū Dujāne! Set your house in good order." Then he called for pen and paper and commanded Alī, may God ennoble his countenance, to write down what follows. I took the amulet (nuskha) thus written and placed it beneath my head. That night I heard the jinn speaking these words: "O Ebū Dujāne! You have burned us! For the sake of your master, his holiness Muḥammad, peace be upon him, take this away from us, or there will be no deliverance for us. We shall never return to your house again, nor shall we ever set foot in any [II 300] place where this amulet is kept." That night felt very long to me; the droning of the jinn, their shouting and their wailing, would not let me sleep. After the morning prayer I told the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, what had happened. He said to me: "O Ebū Dujāne! Now take that amulet away from over them. I swear by God Most High that they will feel the pain of this torment until the Day of Resurrection." Wherever this prayer is kept, whether upon a person or in a place, the jinn can come neither into that place nor anywhere near it.

[II 313] To Undo the Baghli (a Binding Spell Causing Impotence)
Know that the treatment of those who are baghli (bound — rendered impotent by sorcery) is of five kinds: by plants, by plant roots, by Indian remedies, by medical remedies, and by written charms.

Binding is of three kinds. The first comes from a jinn, the second from human sorcery, and the third is where the man's himma (his vital disposition, his inner resolve) is simply "cold," so that his body does not arouse at all.

The sign of one bound by a jinn is that his semen is released the instant the organ enters, before it has properly entered. The sign of one bound by human sorcery is that the organ enters somewhat while still limp, and the semen is then released. The sign of one whose himma is cold is that the body does not arouse at all.
1. Treatment of those bound by a jinn: take three eggs, boil them thoroughly in water, and peel off the shells. Onto the first egg write the following verse, then feed the egg to the man.
Onto the second egg write the following verse:
(And the earth—We have spread it out, and how excellently We have smoothed it!)
and feed this egg to the woman as well.

2. For those bound by human sorcery: you use an Indian remedy. Binding by human sorcery is of two kinds — the first is a binding not yet a full year old, the second is one that has already passed a year.

Boil the pot thoroughly over the fire, then seat the patient over the pot until he sweats. God Almighty willing, the binding will be undone and he will find healing.
